# Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher — Transparency Coverage

This document is generated from the patch manifests. It is the project-level description of the differences the patcher can request; the per-output `VVFP Transparency Log.txt` is the authoritative record of the exact bytes and files used for one output.

## Automatic changes (every output)

Every output applies the selected population mode and the game's automatic physical-capacity safety. No Population Increase preserves the stock cap and progression; Collection Progression preserves the supported game's collection/bonus behavior while changing its declared maximum; Immediate Fixed keeps the fixed maximum. Safety only clamps physical allocation at the real record pool and applies in all three public modes. No game is launched by the patcher, so runtime/player confirmation remains pending.

Available population modes: No Population Increase, Collection Progression Max Pop, Immediate Fixed Max Pop.

## Optional-patch chooser catalog

The desktop chooser presents game-scoped optional patches under the five manifest titles in this fixed order: A New Home, The Lost Children, The Secret City, The Tree of Life, and New Believers. Within each title, entries sort by case-folded display name and then patch ID. Unknown or all-games entries appear under a final `Shared / All Games` header. Checkbox variables remain keyed by patch ID; Select All, Deselect All, dependency closure, and persisted selections operate on those same variables. This is presentation-only: it changes no executable bytes, save fields, companion DLLs, or game behavior.

## Origins doubler evidence boundary

Food Point Doubler changes only the positive food-source delta added to village stores. Tech Point Doubler changes only the positive earned-tech delta at its certified source boundary. Each eligible source value is doubled once; zero and negative deltas remain native, and native writers continue their normal storage/statistics updates using the doubled amount. No doubler changes deductions, initialization, ownership, counters, or unrelated resources. The explicit tech exclusions are Golden Child in VV1, Island Events in every game, Gong of Wonder in VV2, and Duplicate Collectibles wherever that route is present. VV5 stock-layout Tech and Food corrections are implemented with exact-build static proof. The current exact-build boundaries and pending/STOP statuses are recorded in `docs/doubler-composition-audit.md`; return-address checks alone are not treated as exhaustive provenance proof.

VV3 Magic Level-1 audit `4c588ffd36765d750533fe9694f8fda5c8e82736` exhaustively enumerates nine Magic-index reads and finds only one research consumer: sub_458DB0 case 26 getter call 0x4593DC. Magic level 1 or higher contributes a deterministic separate +1 tech writer call after the base and optional quarter-base awards and before timed and independent RNG additions. It changes no research speed, duration, base award, RNG probability/amount, or Research-skill gain. Ordinary and special/catch-up research converge before Magic; collection duplicates and Island Events are explicit Tech Doubler exclusions. The Tech Doubler changes only an eligible positive earned-tech source delta at the positive-writer boundary; separate Magic components and no-source paths remain native.

## Birth Control scope

The exact-build VV4/VV5 breeding audit confirms that both games already provide the requested Birth Control/Breeding behavior natively. Their literal contract is a native chooser score floor plus a 25% non-preference fallback, a candidate-only upper age bound for autonomous pairing, a female/carrier-only upper age bound for manual pairing, and native conception, pregnancy, and delivery. VV4 and VV5 are untouched no-patch references; no Birth Control runtime bytes are offered, applied, or reserved for either game. VV1, VV2, and VV3 now have separate exact-build records implementing or preserving that contract, with static verification complete and runtime/player confirmation pending.

Every current or future Birth Control, pregnancy, or Embracing patch is limited to the exact ordinary manual, autonomous, or catch-up route named by its game-specific evidence. Birth Control does not own Island Event pregnancy, birth, and child outcomes or VV2 Gong of Wonder outcomes. Their age, sex, preference, eligibility, conception, pregnancy, delivery, capacity, RNG, messages, statistics, and state writes remain outside that feature. Automatic physical-capacity safety is a separate layer applied in Stock, Collection Progression, and Immediate Fixed, so it may clamp physical allocation without being Birth Control behavior. These are control-flow/provenance exclusions, not result- or amount-based exceptions.

VV1 exact-build audit `c8d268d` rejects its former byte proposal: `0x3DBBE` is the stock food>=400 gate rather than an age predicate, `0x458D0` and `0x45930` are live instruction interiors, and `0x56740` is uncertified. The active `vv1_birth_control` record instead owns a `.vv1bc` executable page at raw `0x8E000` / VA `0x490000`, hooks the manual route at `0x3DD03`, the action-9 writer-reaching scans at `0x46E96` and `0x47084`, the planner at `0x477FA`, and the chooser tail at `0x39C80`/`0x39C83`. It preserves the stock lower bounds while adding only candidate upper bounds, and gives the chooser the literal VV4/VV5 score floor and 25% non-preference fallback. Catch-up reuses that route; conception, pregnancy, direct event births, and pending delivery remain outside Birth Control ownership, while automatic physical-capacity safety remains a separate layer in all three public modes.
VV3 exact-build feature `vv3_birth_control` changes only the five repeated initiator-age blocks at `0x5CE74`, `0x5CF35`, `0x5CFFC`, `0x5D0C0`, and `0x5D187`. Each native candidate `360..999` check remains; only the ordinary action-13 selector's duplicate initiator upper rejection is removed. The native VV4/VV5-style chooser floor/fallback and manual carrier gate remain unchanged by Birth Control, as do conception, pregnancy, pending delivery, direct event births, Island Events, clone paths, and other special producers; automatic physical-capacity safety separately guards their physical allocation in all three public modes.

VV2 exact-build feature `vv2_birth_control` is limited to the two complete 40-byte writer-reaching opcode-12 candidate scans at file offsets `0x6488D` and `0x64A8F`, based on disassembly commit `74778bd6a7d3a17dd990636cf6d4e769466800c6`. It preserves candidate sex in EDX and rejects an already-loaded candidate age in EAX at 1000 or above. Birth Control owns only those two age blocks. The native VV4/VV5-style chooser floor/fallback, stock manual carrier/female-only gate, lack of a male upper-age gate, conception roll, pregnancy writer, and delivery remain outside the feature and unchanged by Birth Control. Love Note call `0x22006`, Gong life-grant call `0x4EB3E`, Silver Mirror clone call `0x217F9`, planner, saves, RNG, resources, statistics, and all direct event/Gong routes are unchanged by Birth Control; automatic physical-capacity safety separately guards their physical allocation in all three public modes.

## Virtual Villagers - A New Home

### Automatic population and safety changes

Supported stock identity is the exact `Virtual Villagers - A New Home.exe` build recorded in `data/builds.json`. The automatic edits are the selected population mode plus 24 guarded safety edits. The modified output retains the untouched stock executable beside the modified executable. Stock modes preserve vanilla save format; expanded modes use the documented guarded compatibility/conversion path.

### Optional features

#### 2-10x Sickness (`vv1_sickness_multiplier`)

**Needs no other patch.** Makes the game harder; off by default. Villagers fall sick 2 to 10 times as often as they would: you choose how many times with the 2-10x Sickness slider in the patcher window (a whole number, 2 unless you move it). Every natural chance of falling sick is multiplied, at every Medicine level and difficulty, the old villagers' extra chance included, and it stacks with the other patches. Medicine, the fire, Easy's cures, healers, island events and everything that cures are unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The natural sickness roll's four moduli (Medicine 1, 2, 3 and the old villagers' roll) become round(stock / N), N the slider (2 to 10): each chance about N times as large.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The roll's thresholds, Medicine, the fire, the difficulty, Easy's cures, healers, events, the Hospital and every other health rule are unchanged; four immediates in place, written when the build is published.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; every multiplier on every site, stock and with Sickness works like VV1-3, is checked in tests/test_sickness_patches.py; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### 2-10x Tech Cost (`vv1_tech_cost_multiplier`)

Every technology level on the Tech screen costs 2 to 10 times its normal price in tech points: you choose the multiplier with the 2-10x Tech Cost slider in the patcher window (a whole number, 3 unless you move it). The normal prices are: Farming level 2 6,000, level 3 50,000; Fertility level 2 11,000, level 3 240,000; Science level 2 12,000, level 3 150,000; Medicine level 2 15,000, level 3 250,000; Construction level 2 2,500, level 3 80,000; Spirituality level 2 5,000, level 3 80,000. At x 3, for example, a 5,000-point level costs 15,000. The Tech screen shows the multiplied price, a purchase is refused (and nothing is spent) with fewer tech points than that, and buying takes exactly that many. Research, tech points from anywhere else, every other tech-point cost (such as clothes) and the patcher's own upgrades are unchanged. The higher you set it, the harder the game. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: Every technology price immediate in the Tech screen's hover label (0x434070), information box (0x4345E0) and buy handler (0x435AEF), each a price immediate, x N (the slider, 2 to 10; 3 by default): the shown price, the buy handler's refusal threshold (cmp / jb: too few tech points shows the game's message and spends nothing) and the amount it takes (sub) are the same multiplied number.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: Each price is changed in place, same length; no code is added and no executable space is claimed. Research, tech points from island events and duplicate collectibles, every other tech-point cost (such as 5,000 for clothes) and the patcher's Origins and Story / Cheat upgrades keep their stock numbers.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 35; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Birth Control (`vv1_birth_control`)

Matches the literal VV4/VV5 Birth Control boundary on the exact VV1 build. Manual pairing rejects only a category-2 carrier at internal age>=1000; the two action-9 writer-reaching scans and the planner reject only scanned candidates at internal age>=1000; the autonomous chooser uses the VV4/VV5 score floor and REQUIRES the parenting preference to be checked, rejecting an unchecked villager rather than applying the VV4/VV5 25% non-preference fallback; initiator males and older autonomous initiators retain no upper-age ceiling. Birth Control owns only its named ordinary-route checks; conception, pregnancy, delivery, direct event births, and pending delivery remain separate native paths, while automatic physical-capacity safety applies in every public mode.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

The action-9 writer-reaching scans at 0x46E96 and 0x47084 retain their stock candidate and initiator lower bounds while adding only a candidate upper bound. The planner scan at 0x477FA adds only a candidate upper bound before the stock initiator lower-bound check. The chooser's final score floor at 0x39C80 is raised from 1 to 5, and the tail at 0x39C83 requires a checked parenting preference for category 2: an unchecked villager is rejected instead of reaching the VV4/VV2/VV3 25% non-preference fallback, which this build does not apply.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No male upper-age gate is added. The existing candidate sex/category checks, writer calls, planner action dispatch, pregnancy writer, delivery, save format, fertility, capacity, messages, and statistics are unchanged by Birth Control; automatic physical-capacity safety separately guards their physical allocation in every public mode, and only the named chooser tail is redirected. Direct event-created births, pending delivery, and every route outside the named ordinary manual/planner/action-9 boundaries are unchanged by Birth Control; automatic physical-capacity safety separately guards their physical allocation in every public mode.

#### Builder Action Fixes (`vv1_builder_action_fixes`)

Villagers whose selected job is Building are more likely to try the stock construction dispatcher when food is plentiful: at 400 food or more, about three times in four each time the game chooses what such a villager does, they get the construction attempt the stock game gives only below 400; the rest of the time the game chooses exactly as it always has. What they build, and in what order, is the stock game's: a new population hut first (project IDs 9, 10, and 11, started from nothing as the stock game does), then the projects already under way; the project gates and the manual, existing-work, and repair routes remain stock. On its own this patch draws its roll from the processor's time-stamp counter, never the game's random numbers. With Builders Fix Huts When Idle also selected, that patch's companion takes over this gate so both share its one roll per choice. The new population huts also change. The normal game has a hidden rule here: it shows the scaffold of the second population hut (project 10) once the village has 15 villagers and of the third (project 11) at 28, but its builders will not work on the second hut until there are more than 22 villagers, nor on the third until there are more than 45 -- and above those numbers they start one on their own, while a hut they have already started is abandoned whenever the population falls back to 22 (or 45) or below. With this patch, at or below 22 (or 45) villagers builders only work on the second or third population hut once you have dropped a villager on it at least once, and from then on they finish it whatever the population; above that, as in the original game, they may start it themselves. This applies to every choice, at any food level.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

#### Builders and Healers Work First (`vv1_builders_and_healers_work_first`)

Builders and healers are more likely to do their own work first, at any food level -- about three times in four each time the game chooses what they do; the rest of the time the game chooses exactly as it always has, and the one roll is shared with Builders Fix Huts When Idle, so a choice is either all patched or all stock. When it steps in: whenever the game looks for something for a villager whose selected job is Building to do, it first tries building work (a project, or fixing a hut) while not every population hut is built -- and, in A New Home and The Lost Children below Building level 3, whenever any hut is built; for one whose selected job is Healing it always first tries healing and study, whenever there is a patient or they can study medicine (**in A New Home a healer with no patient studies the medical cactus only if you dropped them on it, unless Easier Healing Mastery is also selected, which makes every healer study it whenever no one is sick**). This comes before idling, farming or gathering. When there is nothing of their own to do, they do whatever the game would have had them do. This also applies during catch-up -- the time that passes while the game is closed, and Time Warp: each time catch-up chooses work for a builder or healer, about three times in four they are first given their own job (a builder only while it has hut work, as above), so they keep gaining skill while you are away; the rest of the time, and whenever there is nothing of theirs to do, catch-up's own choice stands. Villagers with any other job are untouched. An addendum to Builders Fix Huts When Idle. **Requires Builders Fix Huts When Idle**, whose DLL loads this one (in The Secret City, whose stub does); ticking this ticks it, and it brings with it the Origins-exclusive base, which adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens.

**Requires Builders Fix Huts When Idle: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this.**

- Behavior changes: Whenever the adult scheduler asks the work dispatcher to start a job for a villager whose selected job is Healing (job 5), or Building (job 4) while it has hut work (a population hut unbuilt, or in A New Home and The Lost Children below Building level 3 any hut built), the dispatcher is first asked for that villager's own job; if that starts something the scheduler sees it started, and if there is nothing of theirs to do the scheduler's own request runs unchanged. At any food level; at 250 food or less in The Secret City, The Tree of Life and New Believers this includes the scheduler's farming attempt. About three times in four, not always: the companion asks the decision's roll that Builders Fix Huts When Idle draws once per choice of the idle scheduler (VvfpFixHutsRoll, handed over through VvfpWorkFirstSetRoll, or looked up by module name in The Secret City); when it fails, the scheduler's own request runs alone, exactly as the stock game. Catch-up (time passed while the game was closed, and Time Warp) never runs the idle scheduler: the catch-up worker (0x42E790) dispatches the stock picker's job itself. Its pick dispatch (0x42E81C, returning to 0x42E821) is treated as the scheduler's calls are -- own job first, then the pick -- and its research pick (job 2), which never reaches the dispatcher, is tested at 0x42E7E0: for a builder or healer the own job is dispatched first and, if it starts something, the worker's own finish (its queue processor) runs instead of the stock research step. One 75% roll per catch-up decision: Builders Fix Huts When Idle wraps the worker as one decision, so VvfpFixHutsRoll gives every patch that decision reaches the same roll; when it fails, or there is nothing of theirs to do, the worker's stock code runs.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the fix-huts companion loads the DLL, which detours the work dispatcher and the catch-up worker's research-pick test at run time only after verifying the stock bytes; a different build of the game installs nothing. A builder or healer with nothing of their own to do does whatever the stock scheduler chose (farming, research, ...); the younger villagers' routine, every other caller of the dispatcher and every other selected job are untouched. A builder is put first only while it has hut work (a hut unbuilt, or in A New Home and The Lost Children below Building level 3 any hut built); a healer always. What the work does -- which project, which hut, which patient or study -- is the game's own dispatcher's choice. In catch-up, every pick other than research reaches the dispatcher hook only through the worker's own pick dispatch; nothing else in the worker changes. Nothing is written to a villager record, the save or any file.

#### Builders Fix Huts When Idle (`vv1_builders_fix_huts`)

Builders fix huts when no building projects are present, and build first. This makes builders more likely to do their building work, not certain: each time the game chooses what a builder does, the patch steps in about three times in four, and the rest of the time the game chooses exactly as it always has. A villager whose job checkmark on the Villager Details screen is not Building (any other job, or none) but whom the game gives building work anyway gets all of this only on 14% of those choices; otherwise the game chooses exactly as it always has. When it steps in, construction always comes first -- a builder goes straight into a new hut or building project the game would let it build, even when the game's own random roll would have skipped it this time, and never fixes a hut while there is one. When no building project is available to be worked on and at least one population hut stands -- while another is unbuilt, and below Building level 3 even once every one is built -- a builder with nothing to do examines and fixes one of the huts that already stands, the game's own "Examining hut" / "Fixing hut" job, which trains Building. It only makes that job able to be chosen autonomously; the job itself, its chance of a repair and its skill roll are the game's own. Whenever there is hut work to do, a builder also does this regardless of the food supply: plentiful food no longer skips the builder's work attempt (A New Home, The Lost Children), and scarce food no longer sends the builder to farm or gather first (The Secret City, The Tree of Life, New Believers). The new population huts also change. The normal game has a hidden rule here: it shows the scaffold of the second population hut once the village has 15 villagers and of the third at 28, but its builders will not work on the second hut until there are more than 22 villagers, nor on the third until there are more than 45 -- and above those numbers they start one on their own, while a hut they have already started is abandoned whenever the population falls back to 22 (or 45) or below. With this patch, at or below 22 (or 45) villagers builders only work on the second or third population hut once you have dropped a villager on it at least once, and from then on they finish it whatever the population; above that, as in the original game, they may start it themselves. This holds every time the game chooses, not only three times in four. Builder Action Fixes makes the same change in the executable. Builders and Healers Work First, Healers Study Plants Regardless of Food and Builder Action Fixes use the same roll when selected with it, so one choice is either all patched or all stock. Healers Study Plants Regardless of Food then adds its own two-in-three roll, so a studying healer carries on half the time. The food bypass acts only while you play. During catch-up (time passing while the game was closed, and Time Warp) each villager does the job the stock game picks, and when that job is building, the same build-first and hut-fixing rules apply, and so does the new-hut rule. **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. That base's companion loads this patch's DLL (in The Secret City, a small stub in the page the base appends does); if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock scheduler runs unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked; the Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically. Needed by Builders and Healers Work First: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: When the Building dispatcher finds no project to work on (every project check has failed) and at least one population hut is complete while another is not, the companion picks a random complete hut and starts the game's own 'Examining hut' job for it, in live play and in catch-up alike. Whenever a builder has hut work to do, its work attempt no longer depends on the food supply: at 400 food or more a villager whose selected job is Building still gets the preferred-job attempt the stock game gives below 400. Every other villager keeps the stock food behaviour. Below Building level 3 the stock Building branch gave up before the hut fix; now, at any food level, a builder fixes a built population hut whenever at least one is built and no other building project is available (every hut built included). And wherever A New Home's Building branch gives up (the 21% skip roll (rand(100) <= 20, 0x44772E), the level gate with no hut to fix, no hut standing) it reported 'started' with nothing started, leaving the builder on 'Nothing'; it now reports 'nothing started', so the villager goes on to other work. The Building branch's new-hut test (0x44754A) is extended: hut 10 and hut 11 are built while they are not complete and either their progress is 2 or more, at any population, or the population is above 22 / 45 as in the stock game (stock: only the population, whatever the progress). The village drawing routine marks a shown scaffold with progress 1 (0x414B0C, 0x414BF1); a villager the player drops on it works it past that. So at or below 22 / 45 builders never start one of these huts by themselves and always finish one the player has started; above, they may start it as the stock game does. Hut 9, the rest of the branch and the build itself are the game's own. This holds on every choice, whether or not the roll below passes. Construction always comes first: where the Building branch reaches the hut fix although it has a new hut to build (hut 9, or hut 10 or 11 once the player has worked on it or the population is above 22 / 45) or a started project open at this Building level -- after its 21% 'not this time' roll, or at the level-3 gate -- the builder goes straight into that construction through the branch's own code for it, and a hut is fixed only when there is nothing to build. Every change above happens about three times in four, not always: each time the game's idle scheduler chooses what a villager does (one run of 0x448220), one 75% roll from the companion's own generator -- never the game's random numbers -- decides whether the patches step in. If it passes, they act together; if it fails, every patched place runs the stock code for that choice, exactly as the unpatched game. The roll is drawn the first time a patched place asks and shared by every patch the choice reaches -- Builders and Healers Work First, Healers Study Plants Regardless of Food and Builder Action Fixes included. The new-hut test above is not part of the roll: it holds on every choice. Catch-up -- time that passed while the game was closed, and Time Warp -- never runs the idle scheduler; its worker (0x42E790) makes the choice instead, and one run of it is one decision too: the patches it reaches (this one's sites in the Building dispatcher, Builders and Healers Work First and Healers Study Plants Regardless of Food) share one 75% roll, never one each. Healers Study Plants Regardless of Food then adds its own two-in-three roll, so a studying healer carries on half the time. Not checked on the job: everything this companion makes a villager do trains Building -- construction first and the hut fix inside the Building dispatcher -- and the dispatcher is reached for anyone the game gives that job. For a villager whose job preference (village + index*0x3D8 + 0x3D0, Building 4; 0 or -1 is no checkmark) is not that job, the companion acts only when, after the decision's roll passes, one more roll of its own passes 14 times in 100 (NOT_PREFERRED_PERCENT, drawn once per decision like the decision's roll): about 10.5% of such decisions instead of 75%. A failed roll is the stock game's choice. A villager checked on the job is unchanged. 14 is the later games' own figure: their job chooser keeps a villager's checked job 86 times in 100.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: a companion that already runs every frame loads the DLL, which detours the dispatcher at run time only after verifying the stock bytes; a different build of the game installs nothing. Nothing about the examine/fix job itself changes: its route, its 70% repair chance, its Building practice roll and its messages are the game's own. A builder with a project available still takes the project. With no population hut built there is nothing to fix. With every hut built and no construction available, at Building level 3 or above (and in The Secret City, The Tree of Life and New Believers at any level) the hut choice is the stock fix-a-hut option; below level 3 in A New Home and The Lost Children a built population hut is fixed directly (never The Lost Children's building 5). Nothing is written to a villager record, the save or any file.

#### Checked Skill Preferences are listed as Jobs on Graves (`vv1_preferred_job_graves`)

A grave's Job line names the skill the villager had checked as their skill preference on the Villager Details screen (the one the game itself shows as their job there), with that skill's rank: "Untrained" below 20, else "Trainee", "Adept" or "Master" by the game's own values (and "Apprentice" for a child under 14 where Children's Graves Say Apprentice or the game does it). With no preference checked the grave shows the highest skill, as before. With Show Cause of Death and Age at Death on Graves, the epitaph it gives follows the same job. Titles still win: the game shows no title on a grave. Only graves made from now on change; for older graves, Repair Saves & Logs rewrites the grave and its Deaths log lines where the save still holds the villager's preference at death. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: A New Home's burial writer gives a villager with a skill preference checked the grave job of that preference and that skill's value (the grave dialog draws the rank, or Apprentice, from it as for any grave); without one the best-skill routine's job and value, as stock. The Cause of Death companion's epitaph and Deaths log Grave line read the grave, so they follow it.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The shared best-skill routine is not touched (its other callers, the Nursery lesson among them, are unchanged); only the burial writer's block is recoded in place, same length, no executable space claimed. The age is read and the record found once, the grave's fields reached from the age's address (value -8, job -4, name -0x24). The name copy's call at 0x448FF1 (which Fix Vanilla Bugs aims at strcpy) and the loop's end are untouched. Titles and the children's epitaphs are chosen before the job as stock; a grave already made is never changed by the exe (Repair Saves & Logs does it where the preference at death is known).

#### Children's Graves Say Apprentice (`vv1_apprentice_graves`)

A child's grave names the child's job as an "Apprentice", the way The Tree of Life does: a villager who died under 14 years old whose best skill was 20 or more (Trainee or better) shows "Apprentice Farmer", "Apprentice Scientist", "Apprentice Parent" and so on, instead of "Trainee", "Adept" or "Master"; below 20 it is "Untrained" as before. Adults' graves are unchanged. The word is the game's own "Apprentice" text, so it follows the game's language. Graves are read when shown, so graves made before you ticked this change too. With Show Cause of Death and Age at Death on Graves, the Deaths log writes the same line. **With Show Cause of Death and Age at Death on Graves ticked too,** the Golden Child's grave says "Golden Child" under Job (the game's own words, as his villager panel shows them) instead of a skill, and his Deaths log record says the same; that patch also gives him a child's epitaph. It knows his grave from his burial; for a Golden Child buried before both patches were installed, Repair Saves & Logs marks his grave from his Deaths log record (when its name and age at death match exactly one grave) and puts "Golden Child" in that record.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

Nothing is written to the save: the line is built each time the grave is shown.

#### Copy and Paste in Text Boxes (`vv1_copy_paste`)

Lets you copy and paste in the game's text boxes (the tribe name when a new village starts and the villager names on the Details screen, and every other box you type in). While a box has typing focus: Ctrl+V or Shift+Insert pastes the text on the Windows clipboard where you type (the boxes have no movable caret, so at the end of the text); Ctrl+C or Ctrl+Insert copies the box's whole text; Ctrl+X cuts it (copies it, then empties the box). Pasted text keeps the box's own rules: its own character filter (a numbers-only box takes only digits), and its own length limit, cut before the first character that does not fit, never inside a character. Line breaks and tabs become spaces; other control characters are dropped, and so is every character the game cannot show (never turned into '?'): **with Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts or Use Unicode Font on, every character those patches let you type is pasted (at least every Windows-1252 character: accented letters, curly quotes, €, ...); with neither, plain English letters, digits and signs only.** The keys never reach the game as letters or shortcuts. Ctrl+A does nothing: the game's boxes have no selection. When the clipboard is busy or holds no text, nothing happens. **On by default.** **Needs no other patch; works with or without Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts and Use Unicode Font.** **Not yet seen in a running game** (checked by emulation of each stock executable). The companion is "VVFP Copy and Paste.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; saves are never written by it.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The event pump's SDL_KEYDOWN case (0x4039D6) first asks the companion about the key: Ctrl+V, Shift+Insert, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Insert and Ctrl+X (no Alt, no Windows key), while a text box has typing focus, are handled and the pump goes on with the next event; every other key, and these keys while no box has focus, go on to the stock case exactly as before. The focused box is found the way the game types into it: the game's own keyboard listeners (event manager 0x48AEC8), in the game's order, the first whose keyboard handler is the text box's (0x40BE30) that has focus ([box+0x25]) on a screen that takes input. Paste: the clipboard's CF_UNICODETEXT, composed (NFC) and split into whole characters, CR/LF/Tab as spaces, other control characters and lone surrogates dropped, each character turned into the box's bytes (UTF-8 when the loaded Unicode companion -- VVFP Unicode Text.dll, else VVFP Unicode Font.dll -- answers VvfpGlyphsUtf8() == 1; every printable Windows-1252 character when it answers 0; printable ASCII when neither is loaded), a character the game cannot show dropped, a numbers-only box's filter applied, and the whole cut before the first character that does not fit the box's byte limit ([box+0x28]). UTF-8 text goes in through that companion's VvfpBoxInsertUtf8 (it inserts as typing does); otherwise the bytes are typed into the box through its own handler, one character message each. Copy: the box's text bytes, read back by the same rule, put on the clipboard as CF_UNICODETEXT; Cut: the same, then (only when the copy succeeded) the box's own Backspace for each byte.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces the SDL_KEYDOWN case's first ten bytes at run time, only after verifying their stock bytes, and installs nothing on a different build. Nothing is written but a focused box's text, through the box's own handler and its own rules: opening and closing a box without these keys leaves its bytes exactly as they were. Saves, villager records and the patcher's files are never written. The clipboard is opened and closed on the game thread and never waited for; busy or empty means nothing happens. A fault is abandoned and the key goes on to the stock code. The SDL_TEXTINPUT case (detoured by Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts) is not touched; both patches work together or alone.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Dropping an Adult on a Child Tells a Story (`vv1_storytelling`)

When you drop an adult (18 or older) on a child (under 18), the adult now tells the child a story instead of trying to embrace, as in the later Virtual Villagers games. The adult shows "Telling a story" and talks for a little while, and each story gives the adult one ordinary Breeding practice roll (A New Home's name for Parenting), with the game's own chance and amount. The child shows "Listening to a story" and waits where it is until the story is over, like a villager listening to a joke. Only your own drop does this: villagers never start a story by themselves, and dropping an adult on an adult, a child on anyone, or a 14-17 year old on a child works exactly as before. A dead child, or a sick one (who is sent for healing, as before), gets no story. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: In the drop handler's villager-on-villager case, where the stock game gives the villager under the mouse "Waiting for someone" (0x425291: 0x4454B0) and the dropped villager "Embracing" (0x4252B9: 0x445510), a drop of a villager aged 18 or older (age 360+) on a villager who is alive (health above 0) and under 18 (age below 360, age 0 included) tells a story instead, to that very villager; the handler then continues after its villager-on-villager case (0x4252BE). The child's steps are cleared and it gets the label "Listening to a story" (written in the game's language: English, German, Spanish or French) and two standing waits in place of 10-19 and 13-22, the lengths The Lost Children's listener (0x44A0E0) waits. #### Easier Healing Mastery (`vv1_easier_healing_mastery`)

Healers and villagers who prefer Healing study the Medical Cactus whenever the game gives them healing work and no sick villager needs treatment, including during catch-up (the time that passes while the game is closed, and Time Warp). A villager not checked on Healing (any other job, or none) studies there only 14% of the time; otherwise, as in the normal game, there is nothing to do. Without this patch only a villager you dropped on the cactus does that, and such a villager always studies. The study and its Healing practice are the game's own. **Needs no other patch. With Builders and Healers Work First also selected, healers are given healing work more often, so they study more.** The 14% roll lives in "VVFP VV1 Easier Healing.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if the DLL cannot be loaded, every villager studies as before.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

#### Enable Origins-Exclusive Features (includes the Heathen Mask mod) (`vv1_enable_origins_exclusive_features`)

Adds Origins-style Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. The Tech menu offers Food and Tech Point Doublers for 500,000 tech points each; only scientist tech production and farmer food production are doubled, while Island Events, story/puzzle discoveries (Whale, berries, mushroom, device), one-time milestone-dialog rewards, Duplicate Collectibles, and Golden Child gains remain unchanged. The Village-Wide menu adds Running, Full Mastery, and Make Villagers Young Adults. Equal Division of Labor (Includes Parenting / No Parenting, 1,000,000 tech points each) splits the village evenly across the jobs, with males and females balanced per job, and gives each villager the job whose skill they have made the most progress in while that job has room (then their next-best job); villagers with no progress, ties and anyone left over are placed at random in the remaining seats. Clear All Skill Preferences (500,000 tech points) unchecks every villager's skill preference (job checkmark) so each villager chooses their own work again, as in the stock game; skills are not changed. Check Highest Skill (Includes Parenting) / (No Parenting) (1,000,000 tech points each) sets each villager's skill preference to the skill they have the most progress in; the No Parenting version ignores Parenting, ties go to the first skill in the Skills list order (Farming, Building, Research, Healing, Parenting), and villagers with no progress yet keep their preference. The Golden Child is skipped by all three, as by Equal Division. This patch also contains the Heathen Mask mod: villagers can wear Heathen tribal masks, chosen per-villager via Change Appearance or across the whole village via Change Appearance for All, and rendered both on the Villager Details portrait and in the village view. Inspired by the Virtual Villagers 1 mobile port, where selected Origins-exclusive upgrades originated; this wording does not claim unsupported mobile parity.

Needed by Watering the Field Trains Building: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Builders Fix Huts When Idle: unticking this unticks it. Needed by School Lessons Stop at 50: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Healers Study Plants Regardless of Food: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Original Looks for Reset to Original: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Show Cause of Death and Epitaphs on Graves, and Log Every Death: unticking this unticks it.**

#### Fix Vanilla Bugs (`vv1_fix_vanilla_bugs`)

Fixes bugs in the base game. A Mysterious Vial (blue liquid): when a pregnant villager drinks it and turns back into a toddler, the pregnancy now ends completely, including the number of babies she was carrying; before, a villager who had been carrying twins or triplets kept that number and her next single pregnancy brought twins or triplets. Every default name can be chosen: the game numbers its 101 male and 101 female names from 0 but picks a number from 1, so Achak (male) and Aba (female) could never be given; now every name in each list can come up, for new villagers and twins alike. A "%" in a villager's name can no longer crash the game: the game showed some names by using them as formatting instructions; now it copies them as plain text, and its text boxes no longer accept a typed "%". The Likes and Dislikes on the Details screen are always shown correctly: the game read each word up to the next comma, but the last word of its list ("sleeping") has none, so a villager with that like or dislike showed stray characters and lost every word after it, and a number past the end of the list showed garbage. Now the last word shows like any other, a number that is not a word is left out, and the line can never run past the space the game keeps for it. A villager's name can no longer be given to another villager on the Details screen: when the arrows or Done are used, the game saves the name box into the selected villager, but it fills the box with the next villager's name only when the screen is next drawn, so two arrow clicks (or an arrow and then Done) taken in the same moment wrote one villager's whole name onto the next villager. Now the screen remembers which villager it filled the name box for, and the box is saved only into that samevillager; otherwise the box is dropped and the right name is shown. A name you type is still saved to that villager. Healers learn Healing while you are away: during catch-up -- the time that passes while the game is closed, and Time Warp -- the game skipped a healer's Healing practice (healing work, or studying the medical cactus) unless a small chance, the healer's Healing out of 1,500, made it look for a patient instead, so a healer learned almost no Healing while you were away, and one with no Healing learned none. Now that practice counts as it does while you play, whenever the search for a patient has not already given it; the search itself is unchanged. The Golden Child can't be picked by an island event that could kill him or make him disappear: he stays five and never heals, yet The Strange Berries, The Mysterious Face and The Book (always), and The Suspicious Monkey, The Wild Mushroom and the rotting and old fruit Mysterious Crates (whenever the most they could take from him is at least the health he has), could pick him like anyone else. Now they pick among the other villagers, each as likely as before; when he is the only villager such an event could be about, it does not happen, as in an empty village. The rotting crate's rats also pass over him (no bite, no sickness) when their bite would bring his health to 0. Every other island event, and every other villager, is the game's own. **Only the game's own random island events change: Pick Island Event and Custom Island Event (Story / Cheat Upgrades) can still choose any villager you wish, the Golden Child included.** Villagers keep what they carry when a walk is blocked: a villager with berries, crops, fish or a mushroom in its hands who could not get past an obstacle gave up the walk after fifteen sideways steps (or by walking off the edge of the map), and the game threw away the whole job -- the item was dropped and the food never paid. Now, instead of giving up, a villager who is carrying something looks for another way over the map (the cells the game itself lets a villager walk on), walks it, and goes on to the food bin and puts the food down as usual; it tries a new way up to four times, and only when there is no way at all does the walk end as it always did. A villager carrying nothing (or a baby), and every other walk, are exactly as before. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: A Mysterious Vial (blue liquid), "Drink the liquid", toddler result: the drinker's litter size (+0x35C) is cleared together with the pregnancy (+0x358), as the game's own delivery code does, so a later single conception brings one baby. A villager's default first name is picked from the whole of the game's male or female list (101 names each): name numbers 0 to 100 instead of 1 to the base game's limit. A villager's name (and in The Lost Children a grave's epitaph and the parents' names) is copied as plain text, never used as a printf format, and every text box refuses a typed "%". Details screen Likes/Dislikes (0x43BA20 / 0x43BAF0, called from 0x449140): each slot's word is found in the game's own word list without copying past its end, so the last word (index 46, "sleeping") is shown and the slots after it still show; a negative slot or one past the end of the list is skipped; the line is written straight into the caller's 256-byte buffer, bounded at 255 characters (4 slots of the longest word never reach it). Villager Details name box (0x44A700 Done/Next/Prev, refilled by the update 0x44A630 once per frame): the box is copied into the selected villager's name (+0x370) only when the screen's reload flag +0x24 is clear, i.e. when the box has been refilled for the villager now selected; a second arrow click, or an arrow and then Done, handled in the same frame no longer writes the previous villager's name onto the next one. Villager Details name box (A New Home): the screen remembers which villager it filled the box for -- the villager-name pointer (+0x370) and a fingerprint: the name's first dword XOR its second, the low byte also XOR the sex byte (+0x350), kept in 8 new bytes at the end of the screen object (+0xCC) -- whenever the box is filled (the update 0x44A630's strcpy(buf, name) at 0x44A66A (Fix Vanilla Bugs' own strcpy 0x44F380)); every write-back (getText 0x40BB70 (Done 0x44A748, right arrow 0x44A7A4, left arrow 0x44A859, all through the guard at 0x44A6F2)) goes ahead only when its destination is that same name and that villager still has the same fingerprint, otherwise the box is not saved (the next fill shows the right name). This covers any way the selected record could stop holding the villager shown (two clicks in one frame, a record reused or moved while the screen is open). Catch-up Healing practice (the catch-up step runner 0x446C70, step 6 = practice, skill 5 = Healing): live play completes a practice step with one call 0x43D440(index, skill) for every skill (0x448846); the catch-up runner instead rolled rand(1500) < Healing (0x446CCF) and, when it passed and the first-sickness hint (state +0x149) was clear, practised once per living villager it checked for a patient, and never made the plain call for skill 5 (0x446D92). Now the plain call 0x43D440(index, 5) is made at the join (0x446D97) when the roll fails (0x446CE4) and when the hint is still pending (the loop's hint test 0x446D0A now leaves the loop for the join instead of passing over every villager, which practised and cured nobody); when the loop has practised -- a cure (0x446D6D, re-encoded with the same writes and registers and ending in a jump past the join) or its end (0x446D6B) -- the step finishes at 0x446DA4 with no second practice. Golden Child and island events ("VVFP VV1 Golden Child Safe.dll", started by "VVFP Speed Change Timers.dll"): the villager picker 0x43BCD0, called from the setups of The Strange Berries (0x418AA3), The Mysterious Face (0x418BB1) and The Book (0x4191C8) -- always -- and of The Suspicious Monkey (0x418F25, -50 floored at 0, 0x419DB1), The Wild Mushroom (0x418FAC, -25..-49 floored at 0, 0x419F65), the rotting crate (0x42B22B, a bite of up to 20 at 0x42C1D8 then -15 with no floor at 0x42C2B0: 35) and the old fruit crate (0x42B391, -40/-70/-110 with no floor: 110) when that most is at least his health, leaves out the record whose +0x36C is 0xC7 and picks among the others exactly as the stock picker does (health +0x344 above 0, present +0x28, adults when asked, in record order, one rand(count) at the game's 0x402F10); with nobody else it returns -1, the stock answer for an empty village, and the setup returns 0 (0x41925F / 0x42B5D7). The rotting crate's bite 0x42AAA0 passes over him (0x42AAFC to the next villager, 0x42AB3E) when his health is at or below the bite (10/15/20 by level); its rand(100) is drawn first, so everyone else's rolls are unchanged. Keep what a villager carries ("VVFP Keep Carried.dll", started by "VVFP Startup.dll"): the three calls of the clear 0x439470 that end a walk -- the blocked handler's after fifteen nudges (0x43DFEE) and the walk's two map-edge clears (0x445F3B, 0x445F71) -- go to the companion. When the villager holds something (record +0x3C is not 0x13, not 3 the baby), the front steps are walks and other steps (the rest of the job: the release and the reward) are queued behind them, the nudges' leftover waypoints are dropped and a route over the game's own map read 0x414200 (cells 1 to 14 and 0x2A block) from the feet to the walk's target is queued as walks (0x4399F0, in front, at the walk's speed) and started (0x43DEF0, +0x40 = 0, +0x54 = 99); at most four routes per walk, none found: the stock clear runs and the item is lost as before.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: Catch-up's cure roll -- its rand(1500), its loop, its practice per villager checked and its cure -- and every other step and skill are the base game's own; skill 2 (Parenting, record +0x3BC), which the base catch-up runner also leaves out of plain practice, is not changed (no step 6 the game queues names it). The result text, the drinker's new age (80) and every other vial result are the base game's own. Conception, pregnancy and delivery are not changed; a villager who never drank the vial is not affected. No save data, villager record layout or art is changed. Which words a villager likes or dislikes, and how likes and dislikes affect behaviour, are the base game's own; only the Details screen's text changes. Renaming a villager on the Details screen works as before: a typed name is saved to the villager shown when the arrows or Done are used; which villager the arrows select (and the Sort By order) is unchanged. Renaming on the Details screen works as before: a typed name is saved to the villager shown by Done and the arrows; which villager the arrows select, the box's length and every other Details control are unchanged. A Pick Island Event or Custom Island Event may pick any villager the player wishes, the Golden Child included: an event Story / Cheat Upgrades delivered (VvfpStoryEventChosen) and every other caller of the picker (every other event, the Troubled Child's picker 0x43BE70, Fast Delivery) are the game's own; the Golden Child's own rules (age 100, never healing) are unchanged. A villager holding nothing or the baby, every other caller of the clear 0x439470, every walk that never meets an obstacle it cannot pass, and the game's own nudging before the fifteenth are the base game's own; with Improved Pathfinding installed its routing runs first and its "no route at all" give-up still ends the walk (no route can exist then).

#### Full Names on the Details Screen (`vv1_details_full_names`)

The Villager Details screen keeps a villager's whole name. In the base game its name box holds only 10 characters (fewer for wide letters) and, when the screen closes, writes what it holds back to the villager, so a longer name -- a last name, a numbered namesake -- was cut short for good. Now the box holds the 27 characters the game's name field has room for, is wide enough to show them, and copies the whole name back; typing a new name there allows 27 characters too. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts): unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: Villager Detail name box: setEditable max characters 10 -> 27 (heap buffer becomes 28 bytes). Villager Detail Done: getText copy length into villager+0x370 0x0B -> 0x1C (the full name field, NUL forced at +0x38B). Villager Detail Next: getText copy length into villager+0x370 0x0B -> 0x1C (the full name field, NUL forced at +0x38B). Villager Detail Prev: getText copy length into villager+0x370 0x0B -> 0x1C (the full name field, NUL forced at +0x38B). Villager Detail name box: size the box from the 53-char .rdata string at 0x4592A4 instead of 'wwwwwwwww' (0x482238), so the draw-time pixel cut (0x40C150) never trims a 27-char name.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The villager's name field is the base game's own 28-byte field; nothing is written past it, and the save's layout is unchanged. Names that already fitted are shown and kept exactly as before; no other screen changes.

#### Genetics: Babies Take After Their Parents (`vv1_genetics`)

Gives A New Home the head genetics of the later games. In the original game a baby's head is picked at random and neither parent's looks count; with this patch a baby's head comes from its parents, by The Lost Children, The Secret City, The Tree of Life and New Believers' own rule: the father's head and the mother's head added and halved (rounded down), then one row lower, the same or one row higher, one chance in three each; on 5 births in 100 any head instead, as the game rolls it. A boy's head stays within the boys' heads (0 to 18), so no boy is ever given head 19, which stays the Golden Child's; a girl's within 0 to 19. When the father is not known -- "Unknown", or a birth whose conception was not recorded -- the mother's head alone is used, with the same one-row step and the same 5 in 100. Twins and triplets share the first baby's head, as in every game. Bodies stay random, as in every game, and the Golden Child, new villages and island events' villagers are the game's own. **Needs Show Parents in Details Screen to know each baby's father; without it every baby takes after its mother.** **Works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Not yet tested in a running game.** The companion is "VVFP VV1 Genetics.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the game is stock.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The villager creator 0x43C350, when the pregnancy tick calls it for the first child of a birth (0x42EFD0, returning to 0x42EFD5), stores at 0x43C647 a head from the parents instead of the head it rolled: rand(100) < 5 keeps the rolled head (rand(19) for a boy, rand(20) for a girl, as stock); otherwise base + rand(3) - 1, made 0 below 0 and 18 (a boy) or 19 (a girl) above, from the game's own rand 0x402F10. base is (father's head + mother's head) / 2, rounded down, with the father VVFP VV1 Parentage.dll stashed against the mother at the conception (Vv1ParentageQueryExpectedFather); the mother's head alone when that DLL is not there, knows no father, or gives a head outside 0..19. Twins and triplets (0x43C840 at 0x42F021 and 0x42F06D) copy the first child's head, so they share the inherited head.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the DLL verifies the creator's head and body rolls (0x43C616..0x43C64C, but for the rand calls' targets and the name roll's bound) and the game's rand, and writes its one detour at run time through the shared all-or-none writer; a different build installs nothing. Bodies, sexes, names, likes and dislikes are rolled as in the stock game. The Golden Child (family 199: head and body 19 from the creator's own branch), the first villagers of a new village, and every villager an island event or Story / Cheat Upgrades makes are the game's own; only births from a pregnancy change. No save byte or file is written: the head is the record's own field, saved by the game.
- Dependencies: none

With this patch an A New Home villager of 55 years or more is drawn with a grey-haired version of the same head everywhere the game draws one -- in the village, on the map and in the Villager Details portrait -- and Change Appearance previews it the same way. Villagers already grey or bald look the same. #### Healers Study Plants Regardless of Food (`vv1_healers_study_regardless_of_food`)

Healers are more likely to keep studying plants regardless of the food supply. A villager who was studying the plant it was dropped on (the medical cactus) carries on studying when the village has 400 food or more, exactly as the stock game already does below 400 -- half the time (a 50% chance) each time the game chooses what the healer does; the rest of the time the game chooses exactly as it always has. A villager whose job checkmark on the Villager Details screen is not Healing (any other job, or none) carries on only on 14% of those checks, here and in catch-up, so farmers and other non-healers study noticeably less; when that roll fails the game chooses their work exactly as it always has. Below 400 food nothing changes. With Builders Fix Huts When Idle also selected, a choice that its roll leaves to the stock game is the stock game's for this patch too. During catch-up -- the time that passes while the game is closed, and Time Warp -- the normal game continues plant study only when it happens to give that villager healing work while no one is sick; with this patch a villager who was studying the cactus carries on there too, at any food level, half the time (a 50% chance) each time catch-up chooses what they do (otherwise catch-up's own choice stands). **Only a villager you dropped on the medical cactus is studying it; for every healer to study the cactus whenever no one is sick, also select Easier Healing Mastery.** **Without Fix Vanilla Bugs (on by default) that study teaches almost no Healing during catch-up.** **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. That base's companion loads this patch's DLL; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock scheduler runs unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked; the Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically.**

- Behavior changes: At 400 food or more, a villager in plant-study state 9 gets the stock continue-last-activity call 0x447CD0(index, 60) that the stock scheduler makes only below 400; if it starts a job, the scheduler's own done epilogue runs. A 50% chance per check, not always: without Builders Fix Huts When Idle this site -- reached at most once per run -- draws a 50% roll of its own; when that DLL is loaded the companion first asks its roll for the decision (VvfpFixHutsRoll, one 75% roll per run of the idle scheduler, shared by every patch the run reaches) and, only when that passes, draws a two-in-three roll of its own (3/4 x 2/3 = 1/2). Neither touches the game's random numbers. When the roll fails the continuation call is not made and the stock selection runs. Not checked on Healing: a villager whose job preference (record +0x3D0) is anything but Healing (5; 0 is no checkmark) needs one more roll of the companion's own, 14 in 100 (NOT_PREFERRED_PERCENT), drawn only after the 50% chance passes, at both sites -- so such a villager continues on 7% of checks, a villager checked on Healing on 50%. A failed roll is the stock selection: the picker, i.e. the villager's own work, never plant study from this patch. The owner (2026-10-20): villagers not checked on a skill do a patch's actions that train it 14% of the time; 14 is the later games' own figure (their job chooser keeps a villager's checked job 86 times in 100). Catch-up (time passed while the game was closed, and Time Warp) never runs the idle scheduler: the catch-up worker (0x42E790) dispatches the picked job, and the dispatcher's Healing case continues a state-9 villager's study (0x4478EF -> 0x443270) only when the pick is Healing and no one is sick. At the worker's pick dispatch (0x42E817, which Builders and Healers Work First's catch-up site also falls through to), a villager in state 9 gets 0x447CD0(index, 60) on the same 50% roll, at any food level; if it starts a job the worker's own finish (0x42E821, its queue processor) runs, otherwise the pick is dispatched exactly as the stock call would, with the stock return address, so Builders and Healers Work First still recognises it. The worker's research pick (job 2) never reaches this point and is unchanged.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the Origins companion loads the DLL, which detours the scheduler at run time only after verifying the stock bytes; a different build of the game installs nothing. Below 400 food nothing changes: the stock code has already made the call. The stock selection the failed roll runs is left as it is: when its pick starts nothing and the villager's best skill is under 50 and the five skills total under 70, it makes the continuation call itself (0x4483AB: 0x447CD0(index, 100)), so a low-skill villager in state 9 may still study there, as in the stock game. Only villagers already studying a plant (state 9, set only when the player drops a villager on the medical cactus; Easier Healing Mastery does not set it) are affected; every other villager's selection is the stock one. What the study does -- which plant, its animation, its Healing practice -- is the game's own. Nothing is written to a villager record, the save or any file.

#### Improved Pathfinding (`vv1_improved_pathfinding`)

Updates the pathfinding to resemble VV3-VV5. Hopefully villagers don't get stuck behind things anymore! When a villager's next step toward a task is blocked, a route round the obstacle is planned on the game's own walkability grid and followed, the way The Secret City does it, instead of the villager giving up and dropping the task. **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. That base's companion loads this patch's DLL; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock walk runs unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked; the Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically.**

- Behavior changes: When a villager walking to a task finds the next step blocked, the companion floods the game's own 168x168 walkability grid from the task and queues every corner of the way round as walk-tos in front of the current action (the same call the stock nudge makes, as many free queue entries as there are, up to twelve), so the villager walks leg to leg without meeting the obstacle again and then resumes the task. While a route exists the villager is never handed back to the stock handler's sideways nudges: bumping into a hut or the side of anything is routed round. Only a task that is truly unreachable -- its own cell on an obstacle, or walled off -- ends the action, at once through the game's own queue clear (0x439470), as The Secret City does; the fifteen nudges never run.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the Origins companion loads the DLL, which detours the handler at 0x43DFC0 at run time only after verifying its seven stock bytes; a different build of the game installs nothing. Wandering, running from danger and every other movement are untouched; only the walk toward a queued task consults the route. Nothing is written to a villager record beyond the same walk-to queue entry the stock nudge writes, and nothing to the save or any file.
- Dependencies: vv1_enable_origins_exclusive_features

#### Island Events Scale With Population (like The Lost Children) (`vv1_island_events_scale_with_population`)

Island events' food and tech-point gains and losses grow with the village, as in The Lost Children: each amount is multiplied by 1 with up to 25 villagers, by 2 with 26 to 50 and by 3 with more than 50 (living villagers plus the babies being carried, as the game counts its population). A New Home's island events already grow with the village (strength n); this patch scales the four encounters that give a fixed or rolled amount: The Trapped Whale (+1,000 food), The Troubled Child (+3,000 tech points), The Wild Mushroom (+300 to 499 food) and The Brass Compass (+2,000 to 4,999 tech points). The encounters' own result texts are fixed (for example the whale's "1000-point food bonus!"), so they still name the game's own amount while the scaled amount is what is given. Custom Island Events (Story / Cheat Upgrades) keep their own amounts. Nothing is saved, so the patch can be ticked or unticked at any time. **Needs no other patch.** **Cannot be ticked together with "Island Events Scale With Stored Food and Tech Points": the two scale the same amounts in different ways, so tick only one; with both ticked the patcher builds nothing.** Off by default; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.** The companion is "VVFP Island Events Scale.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if it cannot be loaded, the stock amounts are given.

A gain stays a gain and a loss a loss. The four amounts are gains; the game's food and tech writers add them as before. The Trapped Whale, "Harvest the whale for food.": +1,000 food (0x41944F). The Troubled Child, "Let him (her) try research.": +3,000 tech points (0x419C35). The Wild Mushroom, delicious: +300 to 499 food (rand(200) + 300) (0x419F09). The Brass Compass, "Let the researchers have it.": +2,000 to 4,999 tech points (rand(3000) + 2000) (0x41A367).

#### Keep the Game's Own Log (ldwLog.txt) (`vv1_game_log`)

Keeps the game's own log, 'ldwLog.txt' in the game's save folder (Documents\LDW\<game executable name>\). Every Virtual Villagers game has always had this log, but the base game starts the file afresh the first time it writes in each run (erasing the earlier runs' lines), holds what it writes in memory until the game closes (a crash loses it), and writes only when something goes wrong -- so most players never see the file. Now each time the game opens it adds a "---- Game started ----" line, and every line the game writes is added to the file at once and kept: a missing font picture, a missing picture and a missing sound. A New Home's code contains no other log line (no clock, text-file, healer, tip or path-finding line), so nothing else can be logged. A line repeated without a break is written once a minute with how many times it repeated, at most 1,000 lines are written a minute, and when the file reaches 4 MB it is renamed 'ldwLog 1.txt' (then 2, 3, ...) and a new one is started, so no file grows without limit; nothing is ever deleted. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The game's log writer (0x40a970) is replaced at run time by the companion's: the same "<date and time>: <line>" text with CR-LF line ends, to the same file, Documents\LDW\<executable name up to its first dot>\ldwLog.txt. The file is appended to (the base game opens it with "wt", which erases the earlier runs' lines), and each line is written to the file at once (the base game buffers until a clean exit). Each run starts with one "---- Game started ----" line, which also creates the file. A line that exactly repeats the one before it is written again only after a minute, preceded by "(the line above was repeated <n> more times)". At most 1,000 lines are written in a minute; the next line written says how many were left out. When ldwLog.txt would pass 4 MiB it is renamed "ldwLog <n>.txt" (n one more than the highest already there) and a new ldwLog.txt is started. Call at 0x4022e7 writes "Font Image not found: %s": a font picture is missing (the game then closes). Call at 0x40a715 writes " Missing Graphic -> %s": a picture file is missing. Call at 0x40af57 writes "ldwSoundFx Missing File ->%s": a sound file is missing.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces the writer's first instruction at run time, only after verifying its first 16 bytes, and installs nothing on a different build. Which lines the game writes, and when, is the game's own: every call site is unchanged, and no line the game's code does not contain is ever written (only the "Game started" line and the repeat and left-out counts are the companion's). No save, village or villager data is read or written; nothing else in the game changes. Older 'ldwLog <n>.txt' files and any other file in the folder are never changed or deleted.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static exact-build verification of the writer and every call to it in each executable (tests/test_game_log.py); the companion's writer is run by native/vvfp_game_log/game_log_harness.c
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Manual Drop-Breeding overrides Birth Control (`vv1_manual_drop_breeding_overrides_birth_control`)

**In A New Home this only changes anything when Birth Control is also ticked: A New Home itself never refuses a woman aged 50 or older on a manual drop. Birth Control adds that refusal, and with both ticked this patch takes it back out for manual drops only; the rest of Birth Control is unchanged.** When you drop an adult villager onto an adult of the opposite sex, a woman aged 50 or older is no longer refused. It is not a guarantee: the game's usual chances still decide whether the pair gets along and whether a baby is conceived, exactly as for any other couple, so a drop can still fail. Every other rule of the drop is unchanged: a man and a woman, both adults, both alive and well, the woman not already expecting or nursing, and the game's own food and population checks. The game never looks at the Parenting preference on a manual drop, and Parenting skill (the dropped villager's) only changes the chances without ever blocking a drop, so an unchecked preference or no skill never stopped one, with or without this patch. Only the manual drop is changed: villagers pairing up on their own, catch-up, events and Birth Control's own rules stay as they are. Off by default.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The block that picks the embrace duration just before the pairing handler's carrier branch (file 0x3DCD8..0x3DD02, VA 0x43DCD8, in the step-9 handler 0x43DAD0) is rewritten to compute the same duration with the same RNG(3)+5 re-roll rule and then test for the player's drop: when the drop's return address 0x4252BE sits at [esp+0x30] -- the depth the drop's own call chain (0x4252B9 -> 0x445510 -> 0x43DEF0 -> 0x43DAD0) puts it, because the drop queues step 9 on an emptied queue and the handler runs inside that call -- the block performs the stock category-2 comparison itself and continues at the stock push/branch at 0x43DD0A, so the drop never enters 0x43DD03. Every other entry continues into 0x43DD03 exactly as stock. The player's drop and villagers pairing up on their own both reach this handler through 0x445510. Autonomous pairing (0x447886) queues a walk to the partner before step 9, so its handler runs later from the walk's arrival (0x445C50) and never with the drop's call on the stack: it always passes through 0x43DD03. Without Birth Control, 0x43DD03 holds the stock comparison this block performs for the drop, so nothing changes: stock A New Home has no age limit on pairing. With Birth Control ticked, 0x43DD03 is Birth Control's hook into its .vv1bc page, which refuses a category-2 woman at internal age 1000 (50) or older; this patch steps around that hook for the player's drop only, so a manual drop is no longer refused for her age while villagers pairing up on their own are still refused by Birth Control. Birth Control's own bytes, its other five edits and its page are not touched.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: Birth Control's bytes are not modified: its hook at 0x3DD03, its action-9, planner and chooser hooks, and its .vv1bc page stay exactly as Birth Control writes them; only the manual drop stops reaching the 0x3DD03 hook. Every other stock manual-drop rule is unchanged and still refuses the drop: same sex, either villager under internal age 360 (18), either villager dead or ill, a woman already expecting or nursing, and the game's own food and population checks. The stock Parenting skill-attempt roll and the stock conception roll (RNG(300) against Parenting skill and technology) are unchanged and still decide; a drop can fail at either one. Autonomous pairing still goes through 0x43DD03 (Birth Control's refusal when it is ticked); the partner chooser and candidate scans, catch-up, Island Events and every other birth route, the conception and pregnancy writers, delivery, and automatic physical-capacity safety are unchanged.
