#### Translations (`vv1_translations`)

Plays the game in another language. Choose a language for each game in Tools > Translations... (or make your own there: the patcher writes a file with every English line of the game, its menus, events, tips, tech names and the patcher's own windows, and a built-in editor shows each line in the game's font). The game uses the chosen language from its next start, with no re-patching; lines a translation leaves out, or gets wrong, stay English. Gender and plural words follow the villager or the number (for example il / elle, 1 pomme / 2 pommes). **On by default, and English until you choose a language: with English chosen the game is exactly as without this patch.** **Letters beyond plain English (accents, Turkish ğ ş ı, Greek, Cyrillic, Chinese, Japanese, Cuneiform, emoji) need "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" or "Use Unicode Font"; without either, the game's own font draws only plain English letters and the rest show as "?".** **With one of those two rows a translated line never runs off the screen (it is cut with "…" at the window's edge, though it may run past its own box); without them the game draws it as it is.** **Words painted into pictures (buttons, the title screen, help pages) stay English.** **Every patch's own text is translated too: its windows and messages, Custom Island Event popups, Cause of Death words and epitaphs, Son/Daughter, and the text the exe patches write; log files stay English.** **Works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Not yet seen in a running game.** The companion is "VVFP Translations.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if it cannot be loaded, or the game's text is not the version a translation was made from, those lines stay English.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: At game start the companion reads "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Files\Translation\Translation.txt" (written by the patcher's Translations window; docs/translation-file-format.md). With no such file it returns at once and writes nothing. Each translated line replaces the English where the game looks it up: the string table at 0x487208 (629 rows): each translated row's English pointer (+4); the visible literals outside the table by the address their loading instruction pushes (data/translations/vv1_strings.json).  A line is used only when the English it was made from is the English this game shows (the key's SHA-256), its placeholders match and its selects are well formed. The patcher's own windows (Origins, Story / Cheat Upgrades, Custom Island Event) are translated as they open (a WH_CALLWNDPROCRET hook on the game's own thread, only when the file translates any of them); a message put together from several lines is translated line by line. The companions that build a text the game shows (Cause of Death's words and epitaphs, Story / Cheat Upgrades' island event lines and Time Skip notice, Show Parents' Son / Daughter, Storytelling, Both Factions) ask for it by its line's key (VvfpTranslateKey / VvfpTranslateKeyText, native/shared/vvfp_translate.h): the translation is used only when the English is the line's and it fits the companion's own buffer, else the English. Text an exe patch wrote ("patch/0x<va>" lines, data/translations/exe_patch_strings.json) is written over in place when the translation fits the English's own bytes (through the same all-or-none writer, after checking the live text is the line's English); a longer one is left English there. Without "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" or "Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts)" (their companion's VvfpGlyphsUtf8; Use Unicode Font's, which starts later, is loaded and started on first use), translations are given to the game in Windows-1252, '?' for what it cannot write.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the companion checks each site's stock bytes and writes them at run time through the shared all-or-none writer, and writes only the ones the chosen file needs; if any check fails it writes nothing, not even a table pointer, and the game stays English. No save, record or game file is written; the game's own English text stays in memory unchanged. With English chosen (no Translation.txt), nothing at all is written.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts) (`vv1_unicode_font`)

Draws ALL of the game's text in a Windows typeface instead of the game's own bitmap fonts: Segoe UI unless you choose another in the patcher (the Unicode Font box, or the Tools tab's Unicode Font... window: any installed family, or a .ttf, .otf or .ttc file; the choice is written next to the game as "VVFP Unicode Font.txt"), with Windows' fallback chain for every character it lacks (Segoe UI, Segoe UI Historic, Segoe UI Symbol, Segoe UI Emoji (in colour), the CJK fonts, Nirmala UI, Ebrima ..., Noto if installed, then the bundled open fonts: Noto Sans Cuneiform, Noto Serif Tangut, GNU Unifont, Unifont Upper and last Last Resort). Each of the game's two fonts keeps its line height, baseline and weight, and its size is fitted so a line is as wide as the game's own, so every screen keeps its layout; every character works, as with "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts". **Text and translations never run off the screen:** a line this patch, a long name or a translation draws that would cross the edge of the game's 800-pixel-wide window is cut there with "…" (whole letters only; a justified paragraph wraps at the edge instead), and one that would start left of the window starts at its edge; it may still run past its own box. Without a translation, the game's own English is drawn exactly as before. This needs this row: with Translations alone (no Unicode row) the game draws by itself and nothing is fitted. Where Windows has no icu.dll (before Windows 10 1903), Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between words by ICU's own word lists (ICU 77.1, Unicode License; about 4.4 MB in "Word Lists", read only when such a line is broken). Typing: every text box -- the tribe name, villager names on the Details screen, epitaphs -- takes any character Windows sends (dead keys, Alt codes, the Windows emoji panel, an input method for Japanese or Chinese), each stored whole or not at all, and Backspace erases a whole character (a whole emoji, flag or accented letter). Long names, everywhere: every name box takes names up to 1,200 bytes (up to 1,200 plain letters; fewer when letters need more bytes): the tribe name, villager names on the Details screen, epitaphs; Rename Tribe takes the same. It is one limit, shared with the other Fun Patchers. Characters are counted as you see them (a letter with its accents, an emoji with its skin tone or a flag is one), and Backspace removes one whole character. A long name scrolls in its box while you type it. The save itself is not changed: a name that fits its field (a villager's name 27 bytes, the tribe name 31) is kept there exactly as before; a longer one is kept there as its short form (its start and a mark, with a number when two would start alike) and the whole name is kept beside the save, in Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Long Names. The game shows the whole name wherever it shows that name. Back Up Saves, Restore Saves and Copy Player Slot carry the Long Names files with the saves. With both settings off the game still loads and plays such a save and shows the short form. Characters are stored as UTF-8 (a Western European letter keeps its one Windows-1252 byte), so every older name reads as before; the base game and older patchers show other characters as odd letters but never break. **Off by default and in Owner's Defaults.** **Cannot be used with "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" (ticking one unticks the other).** **Needs "Full Names on the Details Screen" (ticked with it): its Details box keeps the whole stored name, so opening a villager's Details and closing it never changes a name.** **Not yet seen in a running game** (checked by emulation of each stock executable). The companion is "VVFP Unicode Font.dll" (the same code as "VVFP Unicode Text.dll"), started by VVFP Startup.dll; the game's own pictures and saves are never changed, and no Windows font is shipped. **Bundles four open fonts, loaded privately by the game (never installed in Windows): GNU Unifont 18.0.01 (GPL-2.0-or-later with the font exception, or OFL-1.1) and Unifont Upper for nearly every assigned character, Noto Sans Cuneiform and Noto Serif Tangut (OFL-1.1), and Last Resort 18.000 (OFL-1.1), a placeholder block for anything still without a glyph; about 14 MB of fonts (in the patcher's files folder, in "Unicode Fonts", with their licence texts and sources), copied once per game folder, and not again when the folder already has identical files.**

**Requires Full Names on the Details Screen: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this.**

- Behavior changes: The font constructor (0x402240) runs unchanged; for the game's two fonts -- ldwBurweed27 (stock glyph table 0x4862A0) and ldwarialbold (0x486888) -- the companion records the font's line height, baseline, capital height and pixel format. Their own letters are not used: every letter is made from the chosen Windows typeface. Text is read by one rule (src/vv_game_text.py, native/vvfp_unicode_text/text_utf8.h): a well-formed UTF-8 sequence is its character, every other byte its Windows-1252 character, so every existing name reads as before. The width, draw, line-fitting, counted-draw and justified-paragraph routines are detoured: text without a multi-byte sequence goes to the game's own routine unchanged (with this patch, every text is drawn by the companion); other text is cut into whole units (grapheme clusters; shaped runs of Arabic, Hebrew, Indic and other scripts) and drawn in runs by the game's own draw and width routines, from the font's own letters or from pages of letters made at run time (Uniscribe shaping, GDI glyphs, COLR colour layers for emoji) in the font's size and baseline. Each detoured text routine first offers the text to VvfpTranslateText of "VVFP Translations.dll" when that companion is loaded (fails open), and shows a long name's short form as the whole name. Line breaking follows UAX #14 by Windows' own icu.dll (loaded from System32 only; a built-in table where Windows has none): a text with Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar or emoji breaks between whole characters where the rules allow (never before a closing mark or small kana, never after an opening one; Thai and the others at their words, inside a shaped run too), other text at spaces, and a word wider than the line after its longest start of whole characters that fits. Without icu.dll, Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between the words of ICU's own word lists ("Word Lists" beside the companion, read the first time a line of that script is broken; a missing list leaves the built-in table). The screen edge: a text drawn by the companion, expanded from a long name's short form, or drawn while a translation is in use is measured where the game draws it (x is its left edge after the game's own alignment); a line that would cross the right edge of the 800-pixel window (or of a narrower surface) is drawn as its longest start of whole units that fits with "…" after it, a text partly left of the window is drawn from its left edge, a justified paragraph is laid out no wider than the room to the edge, and when not even one unit fits the game's English is drawn. The widths the game is told are unchanged. The SDL_TEXTINPUT case (0x403B9B) posts a typed ASCII character exactly as before; any other well-formed text is handed whole to the focused text box, which stores each character whole (a Windows-1252 character as its one byte, any other as UTF-8) while it fits the box's limit. Backspace erases a whole unit. A box never cuts its text by pixels. Every box's limit is 1200 bytes; a text longer than the field GetText copies it to leaves as a short form: its longest start of whole characters, then "..." ("2...", "3...", the number first, when another long name has it; the older short forms ending in … stay readable), whose whole text is appended to the save's Long Names file and given back when the game puts the short form into a box.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces each routine's first instructions at run time, all of them or none, only after verifying their stock bytes, and installs nothing on a different build. The game's pictures (Images\ldwBurweed27.png, Images\ldwarialbold.png) are never changed and nothing of the game's art is shipped; letters are made in memory from the player's own Windows fonts and, for what they lack, from the bundled open fonts (Unicode Fonts folder), which are added to the game's process only (FR_PRIVATE) and never installed in Windows; a missing or unreadable font file only leaves its step out. A save's records only ever hold what fits their fields: every stock copy of a name sees the short form, never more bytes than the stock game wrote. Nothing is cut inside a character. A fault in any detour falls back to the game's own routine with the game's own text.
- Dependencies: vv1_details_full_names
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Villagers Have Last Names (`vv1_last_names`)

Babies born in the village and the village's founders get a last name after their first name, from the game's own list of 50 last names (Akikai, Alosaka, Awanata ... Wikimak) -- a list the game has always carried but never used, and the one Virtual Villagers 6 and 7 later used for villagers' last names. A baby takes its father's or its mother's last name by the rule chosen in Repair Saves & Logs (Last names come from: from the father, from the mother, 50:50, or a random one of the last names the village has ever used); without a rule recorded, a baby takes its father's last name (the village's default is from the father). A villager can also have a rule of their own for their children (Each villager's own rule): from the father, from the mother, 50:50, a random last name from the list, which gives each child -- twins and triplets too -- its own random draw from the game's list, every name equally likely, or a random one of the village's existing last names. A villager's own rule always beats the village's; when both parents have one and they disagree, a coin toss for each child picks whose. Villagers who arrive through an island event get no last name, because theirs would not be their family's. Only villagers named from now on get one: villagers who already have names keep them. The last name is part of the name the game stores, so it shows wherever the name does and stays in the save even if this patch is later removed. The Golden Child, whose family is not one of the 50, gets no last name. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: A baby born in the village from now on (a mother's delivery: the first child, a twin or a triplet) and a new village's founders are called "<first name> <last name>": the first name is the game's own pick, and the last name is name number <family - 1> of the game's unused third list (0X481BA0), read from the running executable. A villager the game creates any other way -- brought by an island event, a cheat or the Origins page -- keeps the game's own first name only: the companion tells a birth or a founder by the callers' return addresses on the stack, at fixed places. A villager whose family is outside 1-50 gets no last name. At a birth, the rule recorded by Repair Saves & Logs decides the last name (VvfpRuleLastName2): the father's, the mother's, either at random (50:50), or -- a parent's own rule "Random last name from the list" -- a name drawn at random from the game's list, or -- "Random from the existing Village Names", the village's rule or a parent's own -- one of the last names the village has ever used (the record's "used" lines, the villagers in the game at the birth, VvfpRuleLastName3, and the parents'; the game's list when there are none); every random draw is a fresh, unbiased one for each child. Each such birth adds the names it saw that the record lacks as "used" lines (only adding, through a temporary file, never for a slot it cannot tell), so a name stays ever used after its last bearer is gone. A parent's own rule always beats the village's; parents whose own rules disagree: a fresh coin toss for each child picks the father's or the mother's. The whole name always fits the game's own name field: the longest pairing is far below its 27 characters.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion detours the naming routine's first instruction at run time, after verifying it, the routine's push of the list and the creators' calls to it, and changes nothing if any differs. Villagers who already have names keep them; nothing is renamed when a village is loaded. The first names, sexes, looks and families are the game's own; the save format is unchanged.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static exact-build verification of the naming routines, their callers and the unused list in each executable; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Watering the Field Trains Building (`vv1_watering_trains_building`)

"Watering the field" now gives Building skill, but only when it makes progress towards the garden puzzle (after the lagoon puzzle is complete). Each watering that advances the garden ends with one ordinary Building practice roll, exactly like every other Building job; once the garden is restored, watering gives nothing extra. Because watering now trains Building, a villager whose job checkmark on the Villager Details screen is not Building (any other job, or none) waters the field only 14% of the times the game would send them to it; otherwise the game gives them its next choice of work instead. Villagers checked on Building water exactly as before, and your own drop on the field is never restricted. "Watering crops" and "Trying to water strange patch" are unchanged. **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. That base's companion loads this patch's DLL; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock game runs unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked; the Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically.**

- Behavior changes: When a villager's "Watering the field" job reaches its garden progress step (0x43B1E6) while the garden is not yet restored, one practice-Building action (type 6, skill 4) is appended to the end of that villager's job -- the same action every stock Building job queues last, with the stock chance, amount and failure handling. The last watering that completes the garden counts. Not checked on Building: the game sends a villager to water the field only from the work dispatcher's Building case (0x4472C0 case 4, the garden block 0x447635: garden not restored and progress above 0, then 0x43FC20), reached from the idle scheduler and the catch-up worker. The companion replaces the block's first twelve bytes: the same two tests, then, for a villager whose job preference (record +0x3D0) is not Building (4; 0 is no checkmark), one roll of its own (never the game's random numbers) that passes 14 times in 100 (NOT_PREFERRED_PERCENT). A failed roll continues at 0x44765E, where the stock block goes when the garden is not available: the Building branch's next choice, with watering excluded. A villager checked on Building is unchanged; the player's drops (0x4244A0, 0x424BAE) call 0x43FC20 directly and are never gated. The owner (2026-10-20).
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the Origins companion loads the DLL, which detours 0x43B1E6 at run time only after verifying its twelve stock bytes; a different build of the game installs nothing. The garden progress itself, its 200-step goal, the lagoon and well requirements, "Watering crops" (Farming) and "Trying to water strange patch" are unchanged. Once the garden is restored, watering the field queues no extra practice action.
- Dependencies: vv1_enable_origins_exclusive_features
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File (`vv1_write_parentage_log`)

Keeps a plain-text log of the village's conceptions and births in 'Virtual Villagers 1 Births and Conceptions Log <n>.txt', in the save slot's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Births and Conceptions' folder beside the game's saves (Documents\LDW\<game executable name>\); a shared 'Births and Conceptions' folder an older patcher wrote is kept as it was and still read. Each Conception record gives both parents' names, both parents' ages at conception, both head and body values, both parents' likes and dislikes, and the number of babies; the mother's age determines the child's age. Each Birth record, numbered like the Conceptions ("Birth 1", "Birth 2", ...), gives the child's name, head, body, likes, dislikes and skills, and its mother's and father's names, heads and bodies; Repair Saves & Logs can number the Birth records an older patcher wrote without one. A new numbered file is started after every 256 Conception records; Birth records go into the file holding the latest conceptions and do not count toward that limit. Each Arrived record, numbered on its own, gives a villager who joined the village without being born into it -- a new village's founders, an island event's newcomers, the Barrel of Babies, the Custom Island Event's new villagers (never a birth): their name, age when they arrived, sex, head, body, likes, dislikes and skills, and how they came ("Founder", the event's title, "Barrel of Babies", "Custom Island Event", or "unknown"); villagers who arrived before this record existed get one, marked "Recorded afterwards", only once the player chooses Repair when the village is loaded. **The Arrived records are found by the Cause of Death patch ("Log Every Death ..."): with it off, none is written.** A New Home stores no parents on any villager record, so both parents are captured at conception; they cannot be recovered from the child afterwards. VV1 stores nothing about the father in the mother's record -- not his name, and no id that could find him -- so his details, his age included, are captured from his own record at the six conception call sites, where the game holds it briefly. A birth that reaches delivery without such a capture reports the father as not captured for that birth, rather than naming the wrong villager. **The Birth records are written by Show Parents in Details Screen, which sees every birth; with it off, only Conception records are written.**

**Needs Write Village Statistics to Text File or Show Cause of Death and Epitaphs on Graves, and Log Every Death on for the village and savegame header at the top of the log, and for creating the log at a village's first save -- a new village, or one restarted with Start Over -- before anything is recorded (without either, records are still written correctly, just unlabelled, and the log first appears with its first record; Cause of Death names the village at each save itself). Needs Show Parents in Details Screen on for the "Birth" records (conceptions are logged without it). Needed by Show Cause of Death and Epitaphs on Graves, and Log Every Death for the Deaths and Unaccounted Villagers logs, which that patch's DLL writes (without it neither is written). Needed by Write Island Events Log to Text File for the Island Events log, which that patch's DLL writes (without it nothing is written).**

- Behavior changes: Keeps a plain-text log of the village's conceptions and births in 'Virtual Villagers 1 Births and Conceptions Log <n>.txt', in the save slot's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Births and Conceptions' folder beside the game's saves (Documents\LDW\<game executable name>\); a shared 'Births and Conceptions' folder an older patcher wrote is kept as it was and still read. Each Conception record gives both parents' names, both parents' ages at conception, both head and body values, both parents' likes and dislikes, and the number of babies; the mother's age determines the child's age. Each Birth record, numbered like the Conceptions ("Birth 1", "Birth 2", ...), gives the child's name, head, body, likes, dislikes and skills, and its mother's and father's names, heads and bodies; Repair Saves & Logs can number the Birth records an older patcher wrote without one. #### Write Island Events Log to Text File (`vv1_island_events`)

Every change an island event makes to a villager is written to a new log, the Island Events log ("Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Island Events\Virtual Villagers 1 Island Events Log 1.txt"): one numbered record per villager it changed, with the event's title as the game shows it, the answer you picked when it asked, and each change as old -> new -- health, age, sickness, pregnancy, head, body, name, likes, dislikes, every skill, parents, custom title, mask and Special villager title -- "Gone" for a villager the event took away, and the sex and age of a villager it brought. What an event changes in the village as a whole -- food, tech points, the berries and crops, puzzles solved or unsolved -- is one record of its own, a "Village:" list of old -> new, and an event that changes nothing still gets its record, "Changes: none". A villager whose head or body an event changed also gets an "Appearance changed" record naming the event, so the Family Tree Maker knows the old and the new look are the same villager. A branching Custom Island Event from the library (Story / Cheat Upgrades), whose effects come page by page, is ONE record: its title, the answer picked, then every change in page order as "<name>: <change> <old> -> <new>"; at every save during it the log already holds the entry so far, and later pages continue that same entry, across a quit too, nothing twice. The records are written when the game saves, like the other logs. **Needs Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File: that patch's DLL writes the records.** **A New Home keeps a villager's parents only with Show Parents in Details Screen on: without it, parents are not logged.**

**Needs Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File on for the Island Events log, which that patch's DLL writes (without it nothing is written).**

- Behavior changes: When an island event runs, every villager is copied just before the game applies it and compared just after; each difference is one line of the villager's "Island event <n>" record. The village's food, tech points, food stores, puzzles and (where the game has one) weather are read just before and just after too; what changed is one "Island event <n>" record with a "Village:" list, and an event that changes nothing is one record ending "Changes: none". A villager the event brings is named with its sex and its age, in game units and years ("Age: 340 (17 years old)"). A head or body change is also an "Appearance changed" record in the Births and Conceptions log, ending "Changed by: <event> (island event)". A new village gets its Island Events log when it is made, like the other logs. A branching Custom Island Event (Story / Cheat Upgrades, story_graph.inc) brackets each page's own effects through this comparison (VvfpIslandEventsGraphBegin / End) and hands the event's one entry so far to the log after each page (VvfpIslandEventsGraphWrite -> the Parentage Export's WriteVillageEventEntry): "Event:", "Choice:", then each change as "<name>: <Label> <old> -> <new>" in page order. Its held record is replaced each time and each save writes what it has gained onto the same entry, append-only (a numbered first part left open, then only new lines, or a marked "(continued) Island event <n>" when another record came between), closed when the event is over; the game's own bracket around its popups writes nothing for them (VvfpStoryGraphLogged).
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion detours the routines' first instructions at run time, after verifying them, and installs nothing if any differs. The game's own routine runs unchanged, with the same registers and stack; the events, their odds and their effects are the game's own. Nothing is written without Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static exact-build verification of the event routines and the villager records in each executable; live-tested per game before release
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Write Village Statistics to Text File (`vv1_write_village_statistics`)

After each successful save of slots 1 through 5, writes the save's local lifetime statistics to 'Village Statistics v2 - Save N.txt' in the save slot's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Village Statistics' folder beside the game's saves (an earlier 'Village Statistics - Save N.txt' is kept unchanged). Counts the game does not keep are stored in per-save .dat files in each save's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save N\Data' folder. Later games retain the inherited per-save statistics block even where no Statistics screen is reachable; omitted stock bookkeeping is restored by exact gameplay hooks. Puzzle totals are read from the current save state during export so existing saves are reported accurately. These files are checked against what the save and the patcher's own logs prove -- Village Elders the Village History log shows with Master in three or more skills who are missing from the list, Villagers Buried below the Deaths log's burials or the graves -- and are changed only when the player says so -- Repair Saves & Logs in the patcher window, or Repair when the game asks as it closes (with "Check logs automatically" on, and only if something is wrong); nothing is ever asked while the village is played. Each file is backed up first (a copy '<file>.before-v1.35.58-repair' in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Data\Copies Made Before Repairs', at the file's own place), every change is listed in the Repairs log ('Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Repairs Made'; the shared 'Repairs Made' or 'Repairs' folder an older version made is kept as it was: nothing is moved), and a count is only ever raised and an elder never removed. The original save result is preserved, and text-export failure does not turn a successful game save into a failure. Start Over wipes everything the Fun Patcher kept for that save: all its logs (the Village History too), all its data (ElderTotems.dat too) and its family tree files. It keeps Backups, Copies Made Before Repairs and exported family tree pictures. Other saves are not touched.

**Needs Show Parents in Details Screen on for the "Parents:" lines in the Village Population roster. Needed by Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File for the village and savegame header at the top of the log, and for creating the log at a village's first save -- a new village, or one restarted with Start Over -- before anything is recorded (without either, records are still written correctly, just unlabelled, and the log first appears with its first record; Cause of Death names the village at each save itself).**

## Virtual Villagers - The Lost Children

### Automatic population and safety changes

Supported stock identity is the exact `Virtual Villagers - The Lost Children.exe` build recorded in `data/builds.json`. The automatic edits are the selected population mode plus 29 guarded safety edits. The modified output retains the untouched stock executable beside the modified executable. Stock modes preserve vanilla save format; expanded modes use the documented guarded compatibility/conversion path.

### Optional features

#### 2-10x Sickness (`vv2_sickness_multiplier`)

**Needs no other patch.** Makes the game harder; off by default. Villagers fall sick 2 to 10 times as often as they would: you choose how many times with the 2-10x Sickness slider in the patcher window (a whole number, 2 unless you move it). Every natural chance of falling sick is multiplied, at every Medicine level and difficulty, the old villagers' extra chance included, and it stacks with the other patches. Medicine, the fire, Easy's cures, healers, island events and everything that cures are unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The natural sickness roll's four moduli (Medicine 1, 2, 3 and the old villagers' roll) become round(stock / N), N the slider (2 to 10): each chance about N times as large.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The roll's thresholds, Medicine, the fire, the difficulty, Easy's cures, healers, events, the Hospital and every other health rule are unchanged; four immediates in place, written when the build is published.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; every multiplier on every site, stock and with Sickness works like VV1-3, is checked in tests/test_sickness_patches.py; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### 2-10x Tech Cost (`vv2_tech_cost_multiplier`)

Every technology level on the Tech screen costs 2 to 10 times its normal price in tech points: you choose the multiplier with the 2-10x Tech Cost slider in the patcher window (a whole number, 3 unless you move it). The normal prices are: Farming level 2 1,500, level 3 90,000; Exploration level 2 10,000, level 3 160,000; Science level 2 16,000, level 3 150,000; Medicine level 2 20,000, level 3 65,000; Engineering level 2 5,000, level 3 75,000; Culture level 2 20,000, level 3 85,000. At x 3, for example, a 5,000-point level costs 15,000. The Tech screen shows the multiplied price, a purchase is refused (and nothing is spent) with fewer tech points than that, and buying takes exactly that many. Research, tech points from anywhere else, every other tech-point cost (such as clothes) and the patcher's own upgrades are unchanged. The higher you set it, the harder the game. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: Every technology price immediate in the Tech screen's hover label (0x441D80), information box (0x4422F0) and buy handler (0x4437FF), each a price immediate, x N (the slider, 2 to 10; 3 by default): the shown price, the buy handler's refusal threshold (cmp / jb: too few tech points shows the game's message and spends nothing) and the amount it takes (sub) are the same multiplied number.

#### Birth Control (`vv2_birth_control`)

Matches the VV4/VV5 Birth Control boundary on the exact VV2 ordinary routes: the native chooser's score floor remains in force while its 25% non-preference fallback is removed so an unchecked preference is rejected outright, the two writer-reaching opcode-12 candidate scans reject candidates at internal age 1000 or greater, and the stock manual carrier/female-only gate rejects older carriers without adding a male upper-age gate. Birth Control owns only those two candidate scans; the conception roll, pregnancy writer, pregnancy, delivery, and automatic physical-capacity safety remain separate native/automatic paths in every public mode.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The writer-reaching opcode-12 candidate scans at file offsets 0x6488D and 0x64A8F reject candidates whose already-loaded internal age in EAX is at least 1000. The chooser at 0x449C60 no longer rolls RNG(100) for a villager whose parenting preference is unchecked. File offset 0x49E36 replaces that roll with a jump to the routine's own reject path at 0x449E55, which returns 0. Stock tests the selected category at 0x449E29 (cmp eax,2 / jne 0x449E57) before this point, so Farming, Building, Research and Healing never reach the patched bytes. Both complete 40-byte guarded blocks are one atomic VV2-only optional feature.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The stock manual carrier/female-only age<1000 gate is unchanged, and no male upper-age gate is added. The native VV4/VV5-style chooser score floor, token 43 exact string work, willingness token 39 learning, planner logic, conception roll, pregnancy writer, delivery, save format, RNG, food, fertility, messages, and statistics are unchanged by Birth Control; automatic physical-capacity safety remains separately owned and applies in every public mode. The chooser's 25% non-preference fallback is removed for the Parenting category, which is the one change this feature adds there. Love Note event, Gong grant, Silver Mirror clone, direct/event births, and every path outside the two writer-reaching opcode-12 candidate scans are unchanged by Birth Control; automatic physical-capacity safety separately guards their physical allocation in every public mode.

#### Builders and Healers Work First (`vv2_builders_and_healers_work_first`)

Builders and healers are more likely to do their own work first, at any food level -- about three times in four each time the game chooses what they do; the rest of the time the game chooses exactly as it always has, and the one roll is shared with Builders Fix Huts When Idle, so a choice is either all patched or all stock. When it steps in: whenever the game looks for something for a villager whose selected job is Building to do, it first tries building work (a project, or fixing a hut) while not every population hut is built -- and, in A New Home and The Lost Children below Building level 3, whenever any hut is built; for one whose selected job is Healing it always first tries healing and study, whenever there is a patient or they can study medicine (**in The Lost Children a healer with no patient studies a plant only if you dropped them on one, unless Easier Healing Mastery is also selected, which makes every healer study whenever no one is sick**). This comes before idling, farming or gathering. When there is nothing of their own to do, they do whatever the game would have had them do. This also applies during catch-up -- the time that passes while the game is closed, and Time Warp: each time catch-up chooses work for a builder or healer, about three times in four they are first given their own job (a builder only while it has hut work, as above), so they keep gaining skill while you are away; the rest of the time, and whenever there is nothing of theirs to do, catch-up's own choice stands. Villagers with any other job are untouched. An addendum to Builders Fix Huts When Idle. **Requires Builders Fix Huts When Idle**, whose DLL loads this one (in The Secret City, whose stub does); ticking this ticks it, and it brings with it the Origins-exclusive base, which adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens.

**Requires Builders Fix Huts When Idle: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this.**

- Behavior changes: Whenever the adult scheduler asks the work dispatcher to start a job for a villager whose selected job is Healing (job 3), or Building (job 5) while it has hut work (a population hut unbuilt, or in A New Home and The Lost Children below Building level 3 any hut built), the dispatcher is first asked for that villager's own job; if that starts something the scheduler sees it started, and if there is nothing of theirs to do the scheduler's own request runs unchanged. At any food level; at 250 food or less in The Secret City, The Tree of Life and New Believers this includes the scheduler's farming attempt. About three times in four, not always: the companion asks the decision's roll that Builders Fix Huts When Idle draws once per choice of the idle scheduler (VvfpFixHutsRoll, handed over through VvfpWorkFirstSetRoll, or looked up by module name in The Secret City); when it fails, the scheduler's own request runs alone, exactly as the stock game. Catch-up (time passed while the game was closed, and Time Warp) never runs the idle scheduler: the catch-up worker (0x43B4D0) dispatches the stock picker's job itself. Its pick dispatch (0x43B583, returning to 0x43B588) is treated as the scheduler's calls are -- own job first, then the pick -- and its research pick (job 2), which never reaches the dispatcher, is tested at 0x43B52D: for a builder or healer the own job is dispatched first and, if it starts something, the worker's own finish (its queue processor) runs instead of the stock research step. One 75% roll per catch-up decision: Builders Fix Huts When Idle wraps the worker as one decision, so VvfpFixHutsRoll gives every patch that decision reaches the same roll; when it fails, or there is nothing of theirs to do, the worker's stock code runs.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the fix-huts companion loads the DLL, which detours the work dispatcher and the catch-up worker's research-pick test at run time only after verifying the stock bytes; a different build of the game installs nothing. A builder or healer with nothing of their own to do does whatever the stock scheduler chose (farming, research, ...); the younger villagers' routine, every other caller of the dispatcher and every other selected job are untouched. A builder is put first only while it has hut work (a hut unbuilt, or in A New Home and The Lost Children below Building level 3 any hut built); a healer always. What the work does -- which project, which hut, which patient or study -- is the game's own dispatcher's choice. In catch-up, every pick other than research reaches the dispatcher hook only through the worker's own pick dispatch; nothing else in the worker changes. Nothing is written to a villager record, the save or any file.

#### Builders Fix Huts When Idle (`vv2_builders_fix_huts`)

Builders fix huts when no building projects are present, and build first. This makes builders more likely to do their building work, not certain: each time the game chooses what a builder does, the patch steps in about three times in four, and the rest of the time the game chooses exactly as it always has. A villager whose job checkmark on the Villager Details screen is not Building (any other job, or none) but whom the game gives building work anyway gets all of this only on 14% of those choices; otherwise the game chooses exactly as it always has. When it steps in, construction always comes first -- a builder goes straight into a new hut or building project the game would let it build, even when the game's own random roll would have skipped it this time, and never fixes a hut while there is one. When no building project is available to be worked on and at least one population hut stands -- while another is unbuilt, and below Building level 3 even once every one is built -- a builder with nothing to do examines and fixes one of the huts that already stands, the game's own "Examining hut" / "Fixing hut" job, which trains Building. It only makes that job able to be chosen autonomously; the job itself, its chance of a repair and its skill roll are the game's own. Whenever there is hut work to do, a builder also does this regardless of the food supply: plentiful food no longer skips the builder's work attempt (A New Home, The Lost Children), and scarce food no longer sends the builder to farm or gather first (The Secret City, The Tree of Life, New Believers). The new population huts also change. The normal game has a hidden rule here: it shows the scaffold of the second population hut once the village has 21 villagers and of the third at 46, but its builders will not work on the second hut until there are more than 22 villagers, nor on the third until there are more than 45, and then only on a hut someone has already worked on -- and a hut they have already started is abandoned whenever the population falls back to 22 (or 45) or below. With this patch builders start the second or third population hut only after you have dropped a villager on it at least once, and from then on they finish it whatever the population. This holds every time the game chooses, not only three times in four. Builders and Healers Work First and Healers Study Plants Regardless of Food use the same roll when selected with it, so one choice is either all patched or all stock. Healers Study Plants Regardless of Food then adds its own two-in-three roll, so a studying healer carries on half the time. The food bypass acts only while you play. During catch-up (time passing while the game was closed, and Time Warp) each villager does the job the stock game picks, and when that job is building, the same build-first and hut-fixing rules apply, and so does the new-hut rule. **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. That base's companion loads this patch's DLL (in The Secret City, a small stub in the page the base appends does); if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock scheduler runs unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked; the Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically. Needed by Builders and Healers Work First: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: When the Building dispatcher finds no project to work on (every project check has failed) and at least one population hut is complete while another is not, the companion picks a random complete hut and starts the game's own 'Examining hut' job for it, in live play and in catch-up alike. Whenever a builder has hut work to do, its work attempt no longer depends on the food supply: at 300 food or more a villager whose selected job is Building still gets the preferred-job attempt the stock game gives below 300. Every other villager keeps the stock food behaviour. Below Building level 3 the stock Building branch gave up before the hut fix; now, at any food level, a builder fixes a built population hut (never building 5) whenever at least one is built and no other building project is available (every hut built included). The Building branch's new-hut test (0x4600DE) is replaced: hut 25 and hut 26 are built while they are not complete and their progress is 2 or more, whatever the population (stock: also more than 22 / more than 45 villagers). The village drawing routine marks a shown scaffold with progress 1 (0x419702, 0x41977D); a villager the player drops on it works it past that. So builders never start one of these huts by themselves and always finish one the player has started. Hut 24, the rest of the branch and the build itself are the game's own. This holds on every choice, whether or not the roll below passes. Construction always comes first: while the Building branch has a new hut to build or a project to start or continue -- the villager's own build task, project 1, hut 24, hut 25 or 26 once the player has worked on it, and the level-2 and level-3 projects -- with only its 79% rolls (rand(100) > 20) against it, a failed roll no longer leads to a hut fix (the companion's or the stock one): the builder goes straight into the first of them, in the branch's own order, through the branch's own code for it. Every change above happens about three times in four, not always: each time the game's idle scheduler chooses what a villager does (one run of 0x461850), one 75% roll from the companion's own generator -- never the game's random numbers -- decides whether the patches step in. If it passes, they act together; if it fails, every patched place runs the stock code for that choice, exactly as the unpatched game. The roll is drawn the first time a patched place asks and shared by every patch the choice reaches -- Builders and Healers Work First and Healers Study Plants Regardless of Food included. The new-hut test above is not part of the roll: it holds on every choice. Catch-up -- time that passed while the game was closed, and Time Warp -- never runs the idle scheduler; its worker (0x43B4D0) makes the choice instead, and one run of it is one decision too: the patches it reaches (this one's sites in the Building dispatcher, Builders and Healers Work First and Healers Study Plants Regardless of Food) share one 75% roll, never one each. Healers Study Plants Regardless of Food then adds its own two-in-three roll, so a studying healer carries on half the time. Not checked on the job: everything this companion makes a villager do trains Building -- construction first and the hut fix inside the Building dispatcher -- and the dispatcher is reached for anyone the game gives that job. For a villager whose job preference (village + index*0xE48C + 0x7F8, Building 5; 0 or -1 is no checkmark) is not that job, the companion acts only when, after the decision's roll passes, one more roll of its own passes 14 times in 100 (NOT_PREFERRED_PERCENT, drawn once per decision like the decision's roll): about 10.5% of such decisions instead of 75%. A failed roll is the stock game's choice. A villager checked on the job is unchanged. 14 is the later games' own figure: their job chooser keeps a villager's checked job 86 times in 100.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes one test in the executable, the Building branch's new-hut test, so it holds from the first catch-up of a session; everything else is detoured at run time by the DLL, which a companion that already runs every frame loads and which installs only after verifying the stock bytes; a different build of the game installs nothing. Nothing about the examine/fix job itself changes: its route, its 70% repair chance, its Building practice roll and its messages are the game's own. A builder with a project available still takes the project. With no population hut built there is nothing to fix. With every hut built and no construction available, at Building level 3 or above (and in The Secret City, The Tree of Life and New Believers at any level) the hut choice is the stock fix-a-hut option; below level 3 in A New Home and The Lost Children a built population hut is fixed directly (never The Lost Children's building 5). Nothing is written to a villager record, the save or any file.

#### Copy and Paste in Text Boxes (`vv2_copy_paste`)

Lets you copy and paste in the game's text boxes (the tribe name when a new village starts and the villager names on the Details screen, and every other box you type in). While a box has typing focus: Ctrl+V or Shift+Insert pastes the text on the Windows clipboard where you type (the boxes have no movable caret, so at the end of the text); Ctrl+C or Ctrl+Insert copies the box's whole text; Ctrl+X cuts it (copies it, then empties the box). Pasted text keeps the box's own rules: its own character filter (a numbers-only box takes only digits), and its own length limit, cut before the first character that does not fit, never inside a character. Line breaks and tabs become spaces; other control characters are dropped, and so is every character the game cannot show (never turned into '?'): **with Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts or Use Unicode Font on, every character those patches let you type is pasted (at least every Windows-1252 character: accented letters, curly quotes, €, ...); with neither, plain English letters, digits and signs only.** The keys never reach the game as letters or shortcuts. Ctrl+A does nothing: the game's boxes have no selection. When the clipboard is busy or holds no text, nothing happens. **On by default.** **Needs no other patch; works with or without Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts and Use Unicode Font.** **Not yet seen in a running game** (checked by emulation of each stock executable). The companion is "VVFP Copy and Paste.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; saves are never written by it.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The event pump's SDL_KEYDOWN case (0x403C66) first asks the companion about the key: Ctrl+V, Shift+Insert, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Insert and Ctrl+X (no Alt, no Windows key), while a text box has typing focus, are handled and the pump goes on with the next event; every other key, and these keys while no box has focus, go on to the stock case exactly as before. The focused box is found the way the game types into it: the game's own keyboard listeners (event manager 0x4997A8), in the game's order, the first whose keyboard handler is the text box's (0x40C810) that has focus ([box+0x25]) on a screen that takes input. Paste: the clipboard's CF_UNICODETEXT, composed (NFC) and split into whole characters, CR/LF/Tab as spaces, other control characters and lone surrogates dropped, each character turned into the box's bytes (UTF-8 when the loaded Unicode companion -- VVFP Unicode Text.dll, else VVFP Unicode Font.dll -- answers VvfpGlyphsUtf8() == 1; every printable Windows-1252 character when it answers 0; printable ASCII when neither is loaded), a character the game cannot show dropped, a numbers-only box's filter applied, and the whole cut before the first character that does not fit the box's byte limit ([box+0x28]). UTF-8 text goes in through that companion's VvfpBoxInsertUtf8 (it inserts as typing does); otherwise the bytes are typed into the box through its own handler, one character message each. Copy: the box's text bytes, read back by the same rule, put on the clipboard as CF_UNICODETEXT; Cut: the same, then (only when the copy succeeded) the box's own Backspace for each byte.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces the SDL_KEYDOWN case's first ten bytes at run time, only after verifying their stock bytes, and installs nothing on a different build. Nothing is written but a focused box's text, through the box's own handler and its own rules: opening and closing a box without these keys leaves its bytes exactly as they were. Saves, villager records and the patcher's files are never written. The clipboard is opened and closed on the game thread and never waited for; busy or empty means nothing happens. A fault is abandoned and the key goes on to the stock code. The SDL_TEXTINPUT case (detoured by Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts) is not touched; both patches work together or alone.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

When you drop an adult (18 or older) on a child (under 18), the adult now always tells that child a story, as in the later Virtual Villagers games. The Lost Children has storytelling of its own, but its drop starts an embrace and only finds its way to the story when the embrace's own second search happens to find the same child, so dropping usually just embraced. Now the adult shows "Telling a story" and each story gives one ordinary Parenting practice roll; the child shows "Listening to a story", and a playing child nearby may join in -- all of it the game's own storytelling. A dead child, or a sick one (who is sent for healing, as before), gets no story. **Needs no other patch.**

The story, listening and teaching routines, their walks, waits, practice roll and the dislike of children are the game's own and unchanged. Every other drop keeps its stock result, refusal messages included: adult on adult (embracing, conception and every Birth Control or Manual Drop-Breeding rule), a 14-17 year old dropped on a child, a child dropped on anyone, a dead villager, and a sick one (healing). #### Enable Origins-Exclusive Features and Heathen Masks (`vv2_enable_origins_exclusive_features`)

Adds Origins-style Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. The Tech menu offers Time Warp, Island Event, Barrel of Babies, Tech and Food Point Doublers, and Cure All Villagers; eligible positive gains are doubled, while Island Events, Duplicate Collectibles, and Gong of Wonder tech gains remain unchanged. Island Event and Barrel of Babies are queued rather than fired at once: each waits a few real seconds after the Tech screen closes, so the purchase confirmation is readable first and a natural island event falling due at the same moment cannot consume the purchased one. While either is still pending its row reads 'Why not?' instead of offering a second purchase; clicking it explains that one is already on its way and closes nothing, so it cannot be bought twice or charged for twice. The same applies when the village has no room for the children a barrel would bring, where the message says so and notes that a villager who has died still occupies a slot until buried. The Villager Details menu grants Youth, Full Mastery, Running, and Set Age to 18 to the selected villager. Equal Division of Labor (Includes Parenting / No Parenting, 1,000,000 tech points each) splits the village evenly across the jobs, with males and females balanced per job, and gives each villager the job whose skill they have made the most progress in while that job has room (then their next-best job); villagers with no progress, ties and anyone left over are placed at random in the remaining seats. Clear All Skill Preferences (500,000 tech points) unchecks every villager's skill preference (job checkmark) so each villager chooses their own work again, as in the stock game; skills are not changed. Check Highest Skill (Includes Parenting) / (No Parenting) (1,000,000 tech points each) sets each villager's skill preference to the skill they have the most progress in; the No Parenting version ignores Parenting, ties go to the first skill in the Skills list order (Farming, Building, Research, Healing, Parenting), and villagers with no progress yet keep their preference. Also includes the Heathen mask mod: a cosmetic mask (Blue, Orange, Red, Purple, or Chief) can be given to any villager from the Change Appearance picker on the Villager Details screen, or to the whole village at once from the Change Appearance for All tech upgrade. Masks render on villagers in the village view and on the Details screen portrait, and persist across save and reload. The mask artwork ships inside the companion DLL and is written out automatically on first run, including migration of an exact obsolete bundled 320x440 atlas while preserving current/custom art. Inspired by the Virtual Villagers 1 mobile port, where selected Origins-exclusive upgrades originated; this wording does not claim unsupported mobile parity.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Enable Origins Tech, Details, and Village-Wide Upgrades: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Improved Pathfinding: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Builders Fix Huts When Idle: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Teaching Children Stops at 50: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Healers Study Plants Regardless of Food: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Original Looks for Reset to Original: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Show Cause of Death on Graves, and Log Every Death: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File: unticking this unticks it.**

#### Esteemed Elders' Totems Use No Villager Records (`vv2_totems_out_of_entries`)

In the stock game every Esteemed Elder's totem statue takes one of the village's 256 villager records for good, so in a big village the statues crowd out babies waiting to be born. With this patch the totems are kept apart, in a file beside each save ('Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Elder Totems\ElderTotems.dat'), and take no villager record: when a village loads, every totem in it moves into that file and its record is free for a villager. The totems look, sort, show their "<name>`s totem" label and can be dragged and placed exactly as before, on the village and on the Map. There is no longer a limit of 50 Esteemed Elders. **The stock game never reads ElderTotems.dat: before removing this patch, use Repair Saves & Logs > "Put Totems Back Into the Save" (with the game closed), or the village shows no totems (nothing else changes).** Repair Saves & Logs can also move totems out with the game closed ("Move Totems Out of the Save") and change an elder's totem colour. With the village's "Give Esteemed Elders their totems automatically" setting on (Repair Saves & Logs), an Esteemed Elder without a totem is given one automatically, during play -- when the village loads and after every elder check the game makes -- and so is an elder who has passed away without one (listed by Check or Repair Saves & Logs, given at the next load); an elder who may already have a totem (the same looks, or the same first name) is left for Repair Saves & Logs to ask about. **Unverified in play: this has not been tested in the running game yet.** **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: A totem statue record in a loaded village (Is Totem +0x558 set and health 0 or less) is moved into ElderTotems.dat and its record freed; a villager with the mark but health above 0 is never moved. A new Esteemed Elder's totem (0x44D190) is kept in ElderTotems.dat with everything the game copies onto it; the elder is marked and counted by the game's own pass, as before. No limit of 50 totems: the elder pass's two checks (0x44D4D1, 0x44D54C) never wait while the store works; the full-village guard's wait no longer applies to totems, which need no record. Store totems are drawn with the game's own calls in the game's own y order, on the village and on the Map; a click picks one in front of the villager the game found; the name panel shows "<name>`s totem"; dragging, the dust, the totem puzzle spot (terrain 0x42), the nudge off unfit ground and the stored home x/y are as the game does them for a totem record. ElderTotems.dat is written before each save of the slot and read after each load; one bound to another village is moved aside, never used or overwritten. With the village's give-automatically setting on (Elder Totem Settings.dat), after each load and each elder pass (0x44D4C0, detoured at its entry) every Esteemed Elder record (+0x7FC) with no totem of the same name and looks, or of a recorded rename, is given one as 0x44D190 makes it; the passed-away elders the patcher lists in PendingElderTotems.dat are given one at the next load and taken off the list. A near match (the same looks, or the same first name) makes nothing.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion verifies every site's stock bytes and installs all of them or none; a different build of the game installs nothing. The .ldw save stays the stock game's own format: it simply holds no totem records. If ElderTotems.dat exists but cannot be opened, that session runs as the stock game (nothing is moved, and the game's own 50-totem limit stands). Village Statistics, the logs and the family tree never counted totems as villagers and still do not.

#### Fix Vanilla Bugs (`vv2_fix_vanilla_bugs`)

Fixes bugs in the base game. The Crystal Ball: the island event is only offered when at least one other living villager besides the one who finds the ball is there to trade places with, and if "Keep it" is ever chosen with nobody else living (for example through Pick Island Event), nothing is swapped and the game carries on instead of closing. Every default name can be chosen: the game numbers its 125 male and 125 female names from 0 but picks a number from 1 (and never the last one), so Achak and Zuri (male) and Aba and Zuna (female) could never be given; now every name in each list can come up, for new villagers and twins alike. A "%" in a villager's name can no longer crash the game: the game showed some names by using them as formatting instructions; now it copies them as plain text, and its text boxes no longer accept a typed "%". The Likes and Dislikes on the Details screen are always shown correctly: the game read each word up to the next comma, but the last word of its list ("dirt") has none, so a villager with that like or dislike showed stray characters and lost every word after it, a number past the end of the list showed garbage, and a villager with a great many likes or dislikes overflowed the game's 256-character line, damaging memory. Now the last word shows like any other, a number that is not a word is left out, and a line too long for its space ends in "..." instead of overflowing. A villager's name is saved only to the villager it belongs to on the Details screen: the screen remembers which villager it filled the name box for, and Done or the arrows save the box only into that same villager; if the selected villager is not the one the box was filled for, the box is dropped and the right name is shown. A name you type is still saved to the villager shown. Villagers never turn into totems: the game could bury an Esteemed Elder's totem as if it were a body, leaving its record marked as a totem (starting a new village or Start Over also left the last village's totem records marked), and a twin, triplet or the Silver Mirror's double born into that record became an immortal totem that still had a villager's Details screen. Now a totem is never buried and a twin, triplet or double never inherits the mark. Healers learn Healing while you are away: during catch-up -- the time that passes while the game is closed, and Time Warp -- the game skipped a healer's Healing practice (healing work, or studying a plant) unless a small chance, the healer's Healing out of 1,500, made it look for a patient instead, so a healer learned almost no Healing while you were away, and one with no Healing learned none. Now that practice counts as it does while you play, whenever the search for a patient has not already given it; the search itself is unchanged. A man who drinks A Mysterious Vial (green) can get any of the 30 men's heads: the game rolled a man's new head from 0 to 28 only, so head 29 never came from the drink (a woman's was already any of 0 to 29). Villagers no longer get stuck walking to the shore in the south-east sand (for example a healer dropped on the herb there): the game turned a villager back from the shoreline to a fixed spot, and from there the villager walked into the same shoreline again, forever, and never did anything else. Now, once the game has turned a villager back from the same place twice, the villager tries other nearby spots it can walk to and goes on from there; if there is none, it gives up that walk the normal stock way, dropping what it is carrying, and the game gives it something else to do. The Overview Map's fire looks like the village's own fire: the game drew only its first picture, never moving, once for every object on the map, so its soft glow piled up into a solid yellow blob. Now it is drawn once, in the same place in the stone fire pit, flickering through the village fire's own pictures at the same speed. Island events that show one result now double their food and tech amounts above 25 villagers, as the two-choice events do: the game meant 1, 2 or 3 times the amount (up to 25, up to 50, above 50 villagers), but the single-result events tested 50 twice, so they went from 1 to 3 times with no 2 (the owner, 2026-11-12). A word too wide for its line (a long name or an unbroken word in a translation) is no longer cut: the game's line layout (the story tips) dropped its letters one empty line each until the rest fitted. Now such a word gets a line of its own, at its full width (wider than its box), and the text goes on; text without such a word is laid out exactly as before ("VVFP Long Words.dll"). **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The Crystal Ball (two-choice island event) is offered only when the base game's own condition holds (a living villager aged 14 or over) and at least two villagers are living, so the finder always has someone to trade places with. If "Keep it" is resolved while no other villager is living, the swap is skipped: nothing about any villager changes and the game does not read an unset list entry. With at least one other living villager, keeping the ball trades the same skills, likes, dislikes and +0x564 text with the same randomly chosen villager as the base game. A villager's default first name is picked from the whole of the game's male or female list (125 names each): name numbers 0 to 124 instead of 1 to the base game's limit. A villager's name (and in The Lost Children a grave's epitaph and the parents' names) is copied as plain text, never used as a printf format, and every text box refuses a typed "%". Details screen Likes/Dislikes (0x44B7E0 / 0x44B8B0, called from 0x4654B0): each slot's word is found in the game's own word list without copying past its end, so the last word (index 61, "dirt") is shown and the slots after it still show; a negative slot or one past the end of the list is skipped; the line is written straight into the caller's 256-byte buffer, bounded at 255 characters, and a line that does not fit ends in "..." (the label draws a single unwrapped line, so text past 255 characters could never be seen on an 800-pixel screen anyway). Villager Details name box (The Lost Children): the screen remembers which villager it filled the box for -- the villager-name pointer (+0x564) and a fingerprint: the name's first dword XOR its second, the low byte also XOR the sex byte (+0x538), kept in 8 new bytes at the end of the screen object (+0x54C) -- whenever the box is filled (setText 0x40C510 (shown 0x4663A6, after an arrow 0x467945)); every write-back (getText 0x40C550 (Done 0x467767, right arrow 0x4677F8, left arrow 0x4678C6)) goes ahead only when its destination is that same name and that villager still has the same fingerprint, otherwise the box is not saved (the next fill shows the right name). This covers any way the selected record could stop holding the villager shown (two clicks in one frame, a record reused or moved while the screen is open). Catch-up Healing practice (the catch-up step runner 0x464680, step 6 = practice, skill 3 = Healing): live play completes a practice step with one call 0x44E170(index, skill) for every skill (0x464F15); the catch-up runner instead rolled rand(1500) < Healing (0x4646D7) and, when it passed and the first-sickness hint (state +0x1D4) was clear, practised once per living villager it checked for a patient, and never made the plain call for skill 3 (0x464788). Now the plain call 0x44E170(index, 3) is made at the join (0x46478D) when the roll fails (0x4646EC) and when the hint is still pending (the loop's hint test 0x464718 now leaves the loop for the join instead of passing over every villager, which practised and cured nobody); when the loop has practised -- a cure (0x464763, re-encoded with the same writes and registers and ending in a jump past the join) or its end (0x464761) -- the step finishes at 0x46479A with no second practice. A Mysterious Vial (green), drunk by a man: his new head is rand(30), heads 0 to 29 each 1 in 30, instead of rand(29) (0x4395ED and 0x43968F, the drink's two texts); a woman's roll, rand(30), is unchanged. The shoreline band handler 0x44FCB0 (a map cell of 76 to 79 ahead of a walking villager; entered from 0x45EB1A and 0x45ECF5) is detoured by VVFP Stuck Walks.dll: it runs exactly as before unless the same villager's walk to the same target (a type-3 step that is not one of the handler's twelve waypoints) has met the band within 8 pixels of the same place twice before; then, instead of the stock waypoint, the nearest walkable point on rings of 12 to 80 pixels round the feet (16 directions; walkable by the game's map read 0x4181D0 and the walk's rule: cell 0 or above 23, 24 only for an adult, never 75 to 80) with a walkable straight line to it and from it to the target is queued as the stock handler queues a waypoint (3, x, y, 0, front, 100) and the step restarted (0x44FBB0); each point is tried once, at most 16; with none left the villager gives up the normal stock way: the game's own queue clear 0x4492A0 runs, as the stock give-up runs it (the step queue is emptied, what the villager carries is dropped, and the scheduler gives it a new job). Overview Map fire (the map objects routine 0x41BAD0, called by the map's draw 0x436C30): drawn once after the map's objects, while the fire burns, as frame (SDL_GetTicks / 231) mod 7 of firestrip.png -- the 7 frames the village view's fire effect 11 plays (0x42301D), one every 7 game frames as there and in The Secret City -- at the stock place and size ((315, 205), 25%, centred: on screen (363, 253), the stone fire pit); stock drew frame 0 there once per map object, so its glow piled up. Island events' single-result amount factor 0x4335A0: its second test (0x4335C9 cmp eax,0x32) compares the population (0x425860) with 25 (0x19), so the factor is 1 up to 25 people, 2 up to 50, 3 above, as the two-choice factor 0x41F720 (0x41F749 cmp eax,0x19); stock it was 1 or 3. The line fit 0x4022B0 (the tips' line loops and the wrapped-height measures): at 0x4023E5 (`cmp byte [esi], ' '`, where a line too wide backs off to its last space) a line with no space keeps its letters and takes the rest of the word (to the next space, line break or end, within the caller's letter limit less one), where the stock code backed off to nothing and returned one letter on, so the word lost its letters one empty line each until the rest fitted; a line with a space backs off as before.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: Catch-up's cure roll -- its rand(1500), its loop, its practice per villager checked and its cure -- and every other step and skill are the base game's own; skill 2 (Parenting, record +0x7E4), which the base catch-up runner also leaves out of plain practice, is not changed. The result text, the "give it to the children" choice, every other island event and the event's chance of being chosen are the base game's own. No save data, villager record layout or art is changed. Which words a villager likes or dislikes, and how likes and dislikes affect behaviour, are the base game's own; only the Details screen's text changes. Renaming on the Details screen works as before: a typed name is saved to the villager shown by Done and the arrows; which villager the arrows select, the box's length and every other Details control are unchanged. Every other head and body roll is the base game's own (a newborn's inherited head and its 0 to 29 clamp, the 5-in-100 random head rand(30), the body rand(30), a new village's fixed lists); only the drink's pushed bound changes, and the call to the game's rand routine after it is not touched. A walk the stock band handler gets past (no third approach from the same place) runs exactly as before, frame for frame; the handler's waypoints, the walk, the router (and Improved Pathfinding's flood and descent, 0x41A700 and 0x41A9B0) and every other step are the game's own; no executable byte is patched by the row for this fix, and nothing is written to the save or any file (the companion's memory of each walk is kept only while the game runs). The fire's place and size on the map, its timer, how long it burns, its art (The Lost Children's own firestrip.png), every other picture on the Overview Map and the village view's fire are the base game's own.

#### Full Names on the Details Screen (`vv2_details_full_names`)

The Villager Details screen keeps a villager's whole name. In the base game its name box holds only 18 characters (fewer for wide letters) and, when the screen closes, writes what it holds back to the villager, so a longer name -- a last name, a numbered namesake -- was cut short for good. Now the box holds the 23 characters the game's name field has room for, is wide enough to show them, and copies the whole name back; typing a new name there allows 23 characters too. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts): unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: Villager Detail name box: SetEditable max characters 18 -> 23 Villager Detail name box initial text: 15 'w' -> existing 26 'W' string at 0x00476C10 so the box is wide enough that the draw routine never NUL-truncates a 23-character name Villager Detail OK: GetText(&rec+0x564, 0x13 -> 0x18) keeps 23 characters + NUL Villager Detail next villager: GetText(&rec+0x564, 0x13 -> 0x18) keeps 23 characters + NUL Villager Detail previous villager: GetText(&rec+0x564, 0x13 -> 0x18) keeps 23 characters + NUL
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The villager's name field is the base game's own 24-byte field; nothing is written past it, and the save's layout is unchanged. Names that already fitted are shown and kept exactly as before; no other screen changes.
- Dependencies: none
