#### Healers Study Plants Regardless of Food (`vv2_healers_study_regardless_of_food`)

Healers are more likely to keep studying plants regardless of the food supply. A villager who was studying a plant (the same four-plant roll the stock game makes) carries on studying when the village has 300 food or more, exactly as the stock game already does below 300 -- half the time (a 50% chance) each time the game chooses what the healer does; the rest of the time the game chooses exactly as it always has. A villager whose job checkmark on the Villager Details screen is not Healing (any other job, or none) carries on only on 14% of those checks, here and in catch-up, so farmers and other non-healers study noticeably less; when that roll fails the game chooses their work exactly as it always has. Below 300 food nothing changes. With Builders Fix Huts When Idle also selected, a choice that its roll leaves to the stock game is the stock game's for this patch too. During catch-up -- the time that passes while the game is closed, and Time Warp -- the normal game never continues plant study at all; with this patch a villager who was studying a plant carries on there too, at any food level, half the time (a 50% chance) each time catch-up chooses what they do (otherwise catch-up's own choice stands). **Only a villager studying a plant carries on (one you dropped on a plant, or a healer Easier Healing Mastery sent to study); for every healer to study whenever no one is sick, also select Easier Healing Mastery.** **Without Fix Vanilla Bugs (on by default) that study teaches almost no Healing during catch-up.** **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. That base's companion loads this patch's DLL; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock scheduler runs unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked; the Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically.**

- Behavior changes: At 300 food or more, a villager in plant-study state 9 gets the stock continue-last-activity call 0x460590(index, 40) that the stock scheduler makes only below 300; if it starts a job, the scheduler's own done epilogue runs. A 50% chance per check, not always: without Builders Fix Huts When Idle this site -- reached at most once per run -- draws a 50% roll of its own; when that DLL is loaded the companion first asks its roll for the decision (VvfpFixHutsRoll, one 75% roll per run of the idle scheduler, shared by every patch the run reaches) and, only when that passes, draws a two-in-three roll of its own (3/4 x 2/3 = 1/2). Neither touches the game's random numbers. When the roll fails the continuation call is not made and the stock selection runs. Not checked on Healing: a villager whose job preference (record +0x7F8) is anything but Healing (3; 0 is no checkmark) needs one more roll of the companion's own, 14 in 100 (NOT_PREFERRED_PERCENT), drawn only after the 50% chance passes, at both sites -- so such a villager continues on 7% of checks, a villager checked on Healing on 50%. A failed roll is the stock selection: the picker, i.e. the villager's own work, never plant study from this patch. The owner (2026-10-20): villagers not checked on a skill do a patch's actions that train it 14% of the time; 14 is the later games' own figure (their job chooser keeps a villager's checked job 86 times in 100). Catch-up (time passed while the game was closed, and Time Warp) never runs the idle scheduler: the catch-up worker (0x43B4D0) runs the task-state continuation 0x461580, whose plant-study case starts nothing, and then dispatches the picked job, whose Healing case does nothing when no one is sick (unless Easier Healing Mastery is selected). At the worker's pick dispatch (0x43B581, reached after 0x461580 as in the live scheduler), a villager in state 9 gets 0x460590(index, 40) on the same 50% roll, at any food level; if it starts a job the worker's own finish (0x43B588) runs, otherwise the pick is dispatched exactly as the stock call would, with the stock return address, so Builders and Healers Work First still recognises it. The worker's research pick (job 2) never reaches this point and is unchanged.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the Origins companion loads the DLL, which detours the scheduler at run time only after verifying the stock bytes; a different build of the game installs nothing. Below 300 food nothing changes: the stock code has already made the call. The stock selection the failed roll runs is left as it is: when its pick starts nothing and the villager's best skill is under 50 and the five skills total under 70, it makes the continuation call itself (0x461A5E: 0x460590(index, 100)), so a low-skill villager in state 9 may still study there, as in the stock game. Only villagers already studying a plant (state 9, set when the player drops a villager on a plant, or by Easier Healing Mastery when a healer has no one to treat) are affected; every other villager's selection is the stock one. What the study does -- which plant, its animation, its Healing practice -- is the game's own. Nothing is written to a villager record, the save or any file.
- Dependencies: vv2_enable_origins_exclusive_features
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Improved Pathfinding (`vv2_improved_pathfinding`)

Updates the pathfinding to resemble VV3-VV5. Hopefully villagers don't get stuck behind things anymore! When a villager's next step toward a task is blocked, a route round the obstacle is planned on the game's own walkability grid and followed, the way The Secret City does it, instead of the villager giving up and dropping the task. **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. That base's companion loads this patch's DLL; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock walk runs unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked; the Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically.**

- Behavior changes: The route flood keeps the game's (and The Secret City's) rule that a task on a blocked cell is unreachable, but writes the field with the shared flood so the descent below has it. The route descent takes the neighbour nearest the task rather than the first smaller one in a fixed order, never cuts the corner between two blocked cells, and from an unreached or blocked cell heads for the nearest reached one; the field it writes and reads is laid out exactly as the game's own follower expects.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the Origins companion loads the DLL, which detours the flood at 0x41A700 and the descent at 0x41A9B0 at run time only after verifying their stock bytes; a different build of the game installs nothing. The follower, the arrival test, the goal-on-24 rule and the child rule for 24 cells are the game's own and are unchanged. Nothing is written to the save or any file.
- Dependencies: vv2_enable_origins_exclusive_features

#### Keep the Game's Own Log (ldwLog.txt) (`vv2_game_log`)

Keeps the game's own log, 'ldwLog.txt' in the game's save folder (Documents\LDW\<game executable name>\). Every Virtual Villagers game has always had this log, but the base game starts the file afresh the first time it writes in each run (erasing the earlier runs' lines), holds what it writes in memory until the game closes (a crash loses it), and writes only when something goes wrong -- so most players never see the file. Now each time the game opens it adds a "---- Game started ----" line, and every line the game writes is added to the file at once and kept: a missing font picture, a missing picture, a missing sound, "Seconds Timer out of bounds!" (the computer's clock was set back, so the game's one-second timer is ahead of it) and each tutorial tip shown. The Lost Children's code contains no text-file, healer or path-finding line, so those cannot be logged. A line repeated without a break is written once a minute with how many times it repeated, at most 1,000 lines are written a minute, and when the file reaches 4 MB it is renamed 'ldwLog 1.txt' (then 2, 3, ...) and a new one is started, so no file grows without limit; nothing is ever deleted. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The game's log writer (0x40ab70) is replaced at run time by the companion's: the same "<date and time>: <line>" text with CR-LF line ends, to the same file, Documents\LDW\<executable name up to its first dot>\ldwLog.txt. The file is appended to (the base game opens it with "wt", which erases the earlier runs' lines), and each line is written to the file at once (the base game buffers until a clean exit). Each run starts with one "---- Game started ----" line, which also creates the file. A line that exactly repeats the one before it is written again only after a minute, preceded by "(the line above was repeated <n> more times)". At most 1,000 lines are written in a minute; the next line written says how many were left out. When ldwLog.txt would pass 4 MiB it is renamed "ldwLog <n>.txt" (n one more than the highest already there) and a new ldwLog.txt is started. Call at 0x402577 writes "Font Image not found: %s": a font picture is missing (the game then closes). Call at 0x40a915 writes " Missing Graphic -> %s": a picture file is missing. Call at 0x40b937 writes "ldwSoundFx Missing File ->%s": a sound file is missing. Call at 0x42f1f1 writes "Seconds Timer out of bounds!": the game's one-second timer is more than 3 seconds ahead of the computer's clock, as when the clock is set back (checked every frame). Call at 0x42f37b writes "Displaying Tip (%d) message!": a tutorial tip is shown.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces the writer's first instruction at run time, only after verifying its first 16 bytes, and installs nothing on a different build. Which lines the game writes, and when, is the game's own: every call site is unchanged, and no line the game's code does not contain is ever written (only the "Game started" line and the repeat and left-out counts are the companion's). No save, village or villager data is read or written; nothing else in the game changes. Older 'ldwLog <n>.txt' files and any other file in the folder are never changed or deleted.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static exact-build verification of the writer and every call to it in each executable (tests/test_game_log.py); the companion's writer is run by native/vvfp_game_log/game_log_harness.c
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Manual Drop-Breeding overrides Birth Control (`vv2_manual_drop_breeding_overrides_birth_control`)

**Works the same with or without Birth Control: the 50-and-over refusal it lifts is The Lost Children's own, which Birth Control does not change.** When you drop an adult villager onto an adult of the opposite sex, a woman aged 50 or older is no longer refused. It is not a guarantee: the game's usual chances still decide whether the pair gets along and whether a baby is conceived, exactly as for any other couple, so a drop can still fail. Every other rule of the drop is unchanged: a man and a woman, both adults, both alive and well, the woman not already expecting or nursing, and the game's own food and population checks. The game never looks at the Parenting preference on a manual drop, and Parenting skill (the dropped villager's) only changes the chances without ever blocking a drop, so an unchecked preference or no skill never stopped one, with or without this patch. Only the manual drop is changed: villagers pairing up on their own, catch-up, events and Birth Control's own rules stay as they are. Off by default.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: After the stock conception roll succeeds, the pairing handler at VA 0x44F610 (step 12) checks the woman: it returns without calling the pregnancy writer when she is at internal age 1000 (50) or older. The player's drop and villagers pairing up on their own both reach this handler through 0x45D510, so the refusal block at file 0x4F7C8 is re-encoded to skip it only for the drop: when the drop's return address 0x430F63 sits at [esp+0x30] -- the depth the drop's own call chain (0x430F5E -> 0x45D510 -> 0x44FBB0 -> 0x44F610) puts it, because the drop queues step 12 on an emptied queue and the handler runs inside that call -- it continues at the stock accept 0x44F7FF, so she conceives on a passing roll like any other woman. Every other entry runs the stock check unchanged. Autonomous pairing (0x46044C) queues a walk to the partner before step 12, so its handler runs later from the walk's arrival (0x449380) and never with the drop's call on the stack: an initiating woman of 50 or older is still refused after the stock roll, exactly as stock.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: Birth Control's two candidate-scan blocks and its chooser change are not touched and do not overlap this patch. Every other stock manual-drop rule is unchanged and still refuses the drop: same sex, either villager under internal age 360 (18), either villager dead or ill, a woman already expecting or nursing, and the game's own food and population checks. The stock Parenting skill-attempt roll and the stock conception roll (RNG(300) against Parenting skill and technology) are unchanged and still decide; a drop can fail at either one. Autonomous pairing keeps the stock woman-aged-50-or-older refusal in the shared handler; the partner chooser and candidate scans, catch-up, Island Events and every other birth route, the conception and pregnancy writers, delivery, and automatic physical-capacity safety are unchanged.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the player's drop and autonomous pairing are each emulated from their real call sites through the game's own step queue and dispatcher into the handler in tests/test_manual_drop_breeding.py; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 1; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### More Island Events (`vv2_more_island_events`)

Adds new island events, written by the owner, to the ones the game draws from (more come in later versions). Four here: The Aspiring Adventurer -- a villager who loves to explore sees something glinting off the safe path. "Go investigate!" finds a pile of dirt, a stack of meat (food) or a golden chest of artifacts (tech points); half the time the adventurer gets home (with the find, or with a friend's help), half the time a trap leads to death (a grave) or a disappearance (no grave). "Stay on the safe path" brings them home 9 times in 10; otherwise they are lost: hurt, healed or disabled, a skilled survivalist, killed, gone, or they join another tribe. The event is one more of the game's two-choice island events (family A) with its own slot in the draw, 1 in 23 a draw like each of them (the draw is one wider for The Climb), never the village's first island event; it needs two villagers of 14 or more who are not nursing a baby and not an Esteemed Elder's totem statue, and the adventurer and the friend who may come to help are drawn from them. The reward is a random amount from the smallest to the largest food or tech-point gain of the game's own island events (100 to 1,500 food for the meat, 500 to 3,000 tech points for the chest) times the game's own factor for its two-choice events (1 up to 25 villagers, 2 up to 50, 3 above). Deaths are the game's own ("Unknown causes", with a grave); a disappearance is logged as one in the Deaths log. The popups show the owner's text in pages that fit the screen (OK shows the next); the effects wait for the page that tells them, and the Island Events log keeps one entry for each event. And The Climb (The Lost Children only): a villager of 18 or more who is at least a Trainee in Research (20 or more) wants to climb the Great Falls. "Go with the plan": half the time they fall and die (a grave); half the time they reach the top -- their Research becomes the game's maximum (100), the village gains a large tech award (twice a normal one: 1,000 to 6,000 tech points, then the game's own factor) and everyone celebrates. "Follow the scientists' advice": +10 to 20 Research (at most 100). One villager who may go is enough; it has its own slot among the two-choice events. And The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings (all five games; one popup each, OK only). The Remembrance Ceremony needs at least one grave: everyone joins in -- children, nursing mothers and fathers, everyone -- each at the memorial, "Honoring the Dead" or "Reflecting" (half the time each), and the feast quietly uses 10 food for every villager (never below 0). The Rumblings needs every puzzle solved and a finished hut: an earthquake damages each of the three population huts (the Lovely Hut, the Hospital and the Sewing Hut are puzzles and are never damaged) one time in four (at least one always), each losing 10 to 100% of its building work; the builders must build it again (at 100% it is unbuilt again, as in a new village). Nobody is hurt; a village over its limit keeps everyone and has no new births until it is rebuilt. Each has its own share of the draw and can come again. Off by default; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Needs no other patch.** **Unverified in play: the event has not been seen in a running game** (emulated on the stock executable). The companion is "VVFP More Island Events.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; nothing is saved by it.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The event is one more of the game's two-choice island events (family A) with its own slot in the draw, 1 in 23 a draw like each of them (the draw is one wider for The Climb), never the village's first island event. It can happen only while at least two villagers may go: 14 or more (280 age units), alive and present, not carrying a baby, and not an Esteemed Elder's totem statue; the adventurer and the friend of ending A8 are drawn from them, the friend never the adventurer. Choice A, "Go investigate!": the find 50% a pile of dirt, 25% meat (a food award: 100 to 1,500 food), 25% a golden chest (a tech award: 500 to 3,000 tech points); then 50% a surviving ending (after the dirt A7 or A9; after a find A1, A5 or A8, which give the reward) and 50% a deadly one (A2 and A4 die, the game's own death with cause -1 and a grave; A3 and A6 disappear, no body), each equally likely within its half. Choice B, "Stay on the safe path": 90% home safe; 10% lost, then 1 in 6 each: the healers (1 in 3 each: dies; a full recovery; health set to 10-50 and running disliked), joins another tribe (gone for good, no grave), a survivalist (+20 to 30 in Farming, Building, Research or Healing, at most 100), dies under a fallen tree, dies at the bottom of a cliff, disappears. The reward is drawn, each amount equally likely, from the game's smallest to its largest stock island-event gain of that kind (src/vv_aspiring_adventurer.py AWARD_RANGES), and goes through the game's own food or tech writer, times the game's own factor for its two-choice events (1 up to 25 villagers, 2 up to 50, 3 above). The effects wait for their own page (the page that ends the ending's text), and the event writes its own one Island Events log entry; a disappearance is told to the Cause of Death companion (VvfpCauseVanishedBy), so its Deaths log records it as one. The owner's words, by translation key (the event's popup shows the player's language when a translation has them), are laid out in pages that fit the game's popup -- whole paragraphs, else whole sentences -- each shown in turn with OK. The Climb (The Lost Children): its own slot in family A's draw, 22 of rand(23) (The Aspiring Adventurer 21; each 1 in 23 a draw, like each stock event), kept only while a villager who may go on The Aspiring Adventurer is 18 or more (360 age units) with Research +0x7F4 of 20 or more (the game's own "Trainee" level, 0x429C3D); the villager is drawn among them. "Go with the plan": 50% the fall (health 0: a body and a grave), 50% the summit (Research set to the game's cap 100, 0x4212F4; a large tech award, twice a normal one, through the family-A tech writer 0x426290 after the two-choice factor 0x41F720; the game's own village celebration 0x45D7D0 with Old Friends' place 0x18). "Follow the scientists' advice": +10 to 20 Research, at most 100. The effects wait for their own page: they are made when the page that ends the ending's text is shown, and the event writes its own one Island Events log entry (VvfpIslandEventsGraphBegin / End / Write). The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings (ceremony_core.inc, ceremony_games.inc): each its own case in the single-result events' draw (rand(28) one wider for each of the two that can happen), through two sites of its own; the game's own single-result popup shows the owner's words, the effects are made as it is built, with the event's one Island Events log entry. The Remembrance Ceremony: needs at least one grave (the game's own grave count); every living, present villager is started on its own through the game's own stop and action starter, as its Day of Honor starts each one (so no group filter leaves anyone out), at the memorial, "Honoring the Dead" or "Reflecting" (half the time each); the feast uses 10 food for every villager the game counts, never below 0 (Blessings Day's own rule). The Rumblings: needs every puzzle of the game's Puzzles screen solved and one of the three population huts (the Lovely Hut, the Hospital and the Sewing Hut are puzzles and are never damaged) finished; each finished one rand(100) < 25 (none: one of them at random), each losing 10 + rand(91) percent of its building work, written as the states the game's own construction passes through (at 100% the new village's state).
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion writes each site at run time, only after verifying every site's stock bytes (all of them, or none); without it the event does not exist. Every stock event, its odds, the island-event timer and counting, the rescue rules and Custom Island Events are unchanged; nothing is saved by the companion.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the draw, the popup pages, both choices' effects and the install with every other patch emulated on the stock executable in tests/test_aspiring_adventurer.py (The Climb: who may climb, both answers, both climbs, every effect and its pages, in tests/test_the_climb.py); The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings: the conditions, the draw, everyone sent and where, the feast, the damage and its states, the log entry and the words, in tests/test_ceremony_and_rumblings.py; runtime/player confirmation pending
