#### Original Looks for Reset to Original (`vv2_original_look`)

Remembers each villager's original look -- the head, body and mask they had before any Change Appearance or island event changed them -- so Change Appearance and Change Appearance for All can put them back with Reset to original (the head look goes back to Auto too). A look the game itself gives a villager stays: The Secret City's robe for a new Tribal Chief, and the outfit the game's own clothing dialog puts on (The Lost Children to New Believers), become part of the original. Each villager's look is noted the first time the patcher sees them: when they are born or arrive, or, for a village you already have, the first time you play it with this patch; a look noted is never written over. For villagers changed before this patch, Repair Saves & Logs adds the original the patcher's logs prove -- the look before their earliest "Appearance changed" record -- and never guesses: when the logs cannot prove it, Change Appearance says the original look is not known. The looks are kept in the save's own Original Looks file, follow each villager (through deaths, reloads and renames) and are copied by Back Up Saves; Start Over clears them. **On by default.** Change Appearance is in the Origins upgrades: **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. **Works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Not yet seen in a running game.** The companion is "VVFP Original Look.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; it changes nothing the game does. If it cannot be loaded, Change Appearance says the original look is not known.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked; the Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically.**

- Behavior changes: Each villager's head, body and mask (the mask the Origins companion keeps, its VvfpMaskOf) are noted the first time the companion sees them, in the save's own "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <S>\Data\Original Looks\Original Looks - Save <S>.dat" (native/vvfp_original_look/original_look_store.inc), and never written over. The companion looks at the villager records from the game's own thread between frames (a WH_GETMESSAGE hook on that thread and a thread timer, at most every 250 ms): a villager present when a village is bound is a first-run original, one who appears after is a born / arrived one. A village is bound only once its records have held still for 1.5 s; one whose file is missing or belongs to another village is kept in memory only until the game itself saves that slot again (so the title screen's seeded records are never written into a slot's file). Repair Saves & Logs (game closed) adds the originals the logs prove (src/vv_original_look.py): the Old head and Old body of each villager's earliest "Appearance changed" record, the mask before it when logged; where a change is seen with no record, the original is marked not known. Change Appearance's Reset to original reads it through VvfpOriginalLookGet (native/shared/original_look.h). The game's own changes are kept: each instruction by which the game itself writes a villager's body outside Change Appearance and island events -- The Secret City's robe (0x45FBDE in the robing 0x45FBC0) and the clothing dialog's OK (The Lost Children 0x4228E4, The Secret City 0x41BF89, The Tree of Life 0x41961D, New Believers 0x419D68 and 0x419E8E) -- tells the companion the body first, which becomes part of that villager's original; the game's write then happens exactly as before. A New Home's stock game has no such writer.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the companion splices the game's own body writers listed above at run time, after checking their stock bytes, through the shared all-or-none writer (a different build installs none, and then the game's own changes are not kept); it writes no record byte of its own -- the splice makes the very write the game makes. Change Appearance and island events are never folded in: neither reaches those instructions. The save is never written; the Original Looks file is the patcher's own. A corrupt Original Looks file is moved aside intact and never read or written over; another village's file is never replaced on what is on screen alone.
- Dependencies: vv2_enable_origins_exclusive_features
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Picked Up Collectibles Stay Collected When Dropped (`vv2_collectibles_stay_collected`)

A mushroom or collectible counts the moment a child picks it up: the mushroom's food and Mushrooms Found, or the collection piece (tech points for a piece already found) with its tips and completion messages, come right then, exactly once, so a child who is picked up and dropped somewhere else, or stops on the way, no longer loses it. In the normal game it counts only at the end of the child's trip (the food bin for a mushroom), and one that never gets there is lost. The child still carries it there, as before. Nothing new is saved, so without the patch the game simply goes back to its own rule. **Needs no other patch.** Off by default; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.** The companion is "VVFP Collectibles Stay Collected.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if it cannot be loaded, the game keeps its own rule.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The mushroom job (0x45BCA0): its call at 0x45BE4D, which appends the award step (job step 17 with callback 39 brown / 40 red) to the child's queue at the end of the trip, calls VVFP Collectibles Stay Collected.dll instead, which makes the same call to the queue push 0x449B70 and then moves that new entry to right after the step that puts the mushroom in the child's hands (step 15, queued at 0x45BD49); the steps in between (the pose, the walks, the waits and the sparkle) follow it in their order, then the stock 'hands empty' step 16. The collectible job (0x45BF10) does the same at its call 0x45C09A (step 17 with callback 41): the award comes right after step 15 (queued at 0x45BFE4), and the walk and the rest follow. The child's queue is the game's own (villager record +0x4C, 49 entries of 24 bytes, emptied by the job first at 0x4492A0); the entry moved is the one the game's push just added (step 17 with the job's own callback), so whatever callback the job computed is the one queued. A queue the game left full (the push added nothing) is left as it is. The callbacks read the carried item (record +0x44), which step 15 has already set, so a piece is credited as the same piece.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion writes both call sites at run time, only after verifying their stock bytes and the pushes before them -- all of them, or none. The pickup callbacks (62, 63), the awards themselves (0x4633C5, 0x463422, 0x463426), the trip's walks and waits, catch-up's step simulator and the save are unchanged. Interrupting a child after the pick now keeps the award; before the pick nothing is taken, as before.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the shipped companion is emulated on the stock executable (and with every other patch, in every mode) in tests/test_collectibles_stay_collected.py: both jobs' queues built by the game's own push and played with the real callbacks, dropped away from the bin and delivered; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts (`vv2_unicode_text`)

Lets the game draw, measure and accept ANY character -- accented letters, Greek, Cyrillic, Turkish, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic and Hebrew (joined and right to left), Indian scripts, cuneiform, symbols and colour emoji -- in the game's own two fonts (the big Burweed story font and the small Arial Bold font). The Lost Children's two fonts hold only A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and ! " ' , . ? / ` : -; every other Windows-1252 character is added to the fonts in their own style when the game starts (from the font's own plain letter with the accent added, or drawn by Windows in the font's own typeface: Arial Bold is part of Windows; **for Burweed, install the Burweed ICG font for the best-matching letters** -- the patcher never ships it -- otherwise Comic Sans MS stands in), and every other character is made the first time it is shown, in the font's size, baseline and weight, from the fonts Windows has (Segoe UI, Segoe UI Historic, Segoe UI Symbol, Segoe UI Emoji (in colour), the CJK fonts, Nirmala UI, Ebrima ..., Noto if installed, then the bundled open fonts: Noto Sans Cuneiform, Noto Serif Tangut, GNU Unifont and Unifont Upper, and last Last Resort, so every one of Unicode 18.0's assigned characters draws, even ones no Windows font has). Names, the Details screen, popups, dialogs and every other text use them with their real widths, so centring and line breaks stay right; Chinese and Japanese break between characters. **Text and translations never run off the screen:** a line this patch, a long name or a translation draws that would cross the edge of the game's 800-pixel-wide window is cut there with "…" (whole letters only; a justified paragraph wraps at the edge instead), and one that would start left of the window starts at its edge; it may still run past its own box. Without a translation, the game's own English is drawn exactly as before. This needs this row: with Translations alone (no Unicode row) the game draws by itself and nothing is fitted. Where Windows has no icu.dll (before Windows 10 1903), Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between words by ICU's own word lists (ICU 77.1, Unicode License; about 4.4 MB in "Word Lists", read only when such a line is broken). Typing: every text box -- the tribe name, villager names on the Details screen, epitaphs -- takes any character Windows sends (dead keys, Alt codes, the Windows emoji panel, an input method for Japanese or Chinese), each stored whole or not at all, and Backspace erases a whole character (a whole emoji, flag or accented letter). Long names, everywhere: every name box takes names up to 1,200 bytes (up to 1,200 plain letters; fewer when letters need more bytes): the tribe name, villager names on the Details screen, epitaphs; Rename Tribe takes the same. It is one limit, shared with the other Fun Patchers. Characters are counted as you see them (a letter with its accents, an emoji with its skin tone or a flag is one), and Backspace removes one whole character. A long name scrolls in its box while you type it. The save itself is not changed: a name that fits its field (a villager's name 23 bytes, the tribe name 31) is kept there exactly as before; a longer one is kept there as its short form (its start and a mark, with a number when two would start alike) and the whole name is kept beside the save, in Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Long Names. The game shows the whole name wherever it shows that name. Back Up Saves, Restore Saves and Copy Player Slot carry the Long Names files with the saves. With both settings off the game still loads and plays such a save and shows the short form. Characters are stored as UTF-8 (a Western European letter keeps its one Windows-1252 byte), so every older name reads as before; the base game and older patchers show other characters as odd letters but never break. **On by default and in Owner's Defaults.** **Cannot be used with "Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts)" (ticking one unticks the other).** **Needs "Full Names on the Details Screen" (ticked with it): its Details box keeps the whole stored name, so opening a villager's Details and closing it never changes a name.** **Not yet seen in a running game** (checked by emulation of each stock executable). The companion is "VVFP Unicode Text.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; the game's own pictures and saves are never changed. **Bundles four open fonts, loaded privately by the game (never installed in Windows): GNU Unifont 18.0.01 (GPL-2.0-or-later with the font exception, or OFL-1.1) and Unifont Upper for nearly every assigned character, Noto Sans Cuneiform and Noto Serif Tangut (OFL-1.1), and Last Resort 18.000 (OFL-1.1), a placeholder block for anything still without a glyph; about 14 MB of fonts (in the patcher's files folder, in "Unicode Fonts", with their licence texts and sources), copied once per game folder, and not again when the folder already has identical files.**

**Requires Full Names on the Details Screen: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this.**

- Behavior changes: The font constructor (0x4024D0) runs unchanged; for the game's two fonts -- ldwBurweed27 (stock glyph table 0x4952C0) and ldwarialbold (0x4958A8) -- the companion records the font's line height, baseline, capital height and pixel format, then adds every printable Windows-1252 character the font lacks (src/vv_font_glyphs.py, run in C by native/vvfp_unicode_text/glyphs.inc) as new rows under the loaded picture and new entries in a copy of the glyph table. Text is read by one rule (src/vv_game_text.py, native/vvfp_unicode_text/text_utf8.h): a well-formed UTF-8 sequence is its character, every other byte its Windows-1252 character, so every existing name reads as before. The width, draw, line-fitting, counted-draw and justified-paragraph routines are detoured: text without a multi-byte sequence goes to the game's own routine unchanged; other text is cut into whole units (grapheme clusters; shaped runs of Arabic, Hebrew, Indic and other scripts) and drawn in runs by the game's own draw and width routines, from the font's own letters or from pages of letters made at run time (Uniscribe shaping, GDI glyphs, COLR colour layers for emoji) in the font's size and baseline. Each detoured text routine first offers the text to VvfpTranslateText of "VVFP Translations.dll" when that companion is loaded (fails open), and shows a long name's short form as the whole name. Line breaking follows UAX #14 by Windows' own icu.dll (loaded from System32 only; a built-in table where Windows has none): a text with Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar or emoji breaks between whole characters where the rules allow (never before a closing mark or small kana, never after an opening one; Thai and the others at their words, inside a shaped run too), other text at spaces, and a word wider than the line after its longest start of whole characters that fits. Without icu.dll, Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between the words of ICU's own word lists ("Word Lists" beside the companion, read the first time a line of that script is broken; a missing list leaves the built-in table). The screen edge: a text drawn by the companion, expanded from a long name's short form, or drawn while a translation is in use is measured where the game draws it (x is its left edge after the game's own alignment); a line that would cross the right edge of the 800-pixel window (or of a narrower surface) is drawn as its longest start of whole units that fits with "…" after it, a text partly left of the window is drawn from its left edge, a justified paragraph is laid out no wider than the room to the edge, and when not even one unit fits the game's English is drawn. The widths the game is told are unchanged. The SDL_TEXTINPUT case (0x403E2B) posts a typed ASCII character exactly as before; any other well-formed text is handed whole to the focused text box, which stores each character whole (a Windows-1252 character as its one byte, any other as UTF-8) while it fits the box's limit. Backspace erases a whole unit. A box never cuts its text by pixels. Every box's limit is 1200 bytes; a text longer than the field GetText copies it to leaves as a short form: its longest start of whole characters, then "..." ("2...", "3...", the number first, when another long name has it; the older short forms ending in … stay readable), whose whole text is appended to the save's Long Names file and given back when the game puts the short form into a box.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces each routine's first instructions at run time, all of them or none, only after verifying their stock bytes, and installs nothing on a different build. The game's pictures (Images\ldwBurweed27.png, Images\ldwarialbold.png) are never changed and nothing of the game's art is shipped; letters are made in memory from the player's own Windows fonts and, for what they lack, from the bundled open fonts (Unicode Fonts folder), which are added to the game's process only (FR_PRIVATE) and never installed in Windows; a missing or unreadable font file only leaves its step out. A save's records only ever hold what fits their fields: every stock copy of a name sees the short form, never more bytes than the stock game wrote. Nothing is cut inside a character. A fault in any detour falls back to the game's own routine with the game's own text.
- Dependencies: vv2_details_full_names
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Restore Missing Island Events (`vv2_restore_missing_island_events`)

Lets the island events the original game contains but never runs happen. The Mosquito Swarm (some villagers fall ill and the adults take refuge in the water), The Dragonfly Migration (every villager is restored to full health and cured) and Science Awareness Day (the children gain research skill) join the game's own random island-event roll with the same chance as a typical event. Three events whose text the game ships but never shows are added as rarer no-choice events, each a third as likely as a typical event: The Tattered Diary, The Doctrine of Magicians and The Doctrine of Naturalists, pages of Isola's lore a villager finds; they change nothing else. **Needs no other patch.** With Story / Cheat Upgrades, Pick Island Event also offers the three new events.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The single-result island-event chooser (0x434570) accepts cases 18, 20 and 26 like every unconditional case: each is drawn 1 time in 28, as The Heat Wave or The West Wind are. The Mosquito Swarm runs the game's own case 18: each living villager has a 20% chance to fall sick, and every adult who is not pregnant stops what they are doing and goes to the pond ("Enjoying the pond", the game's swim). The Dragonfly Migration runs the game's own case 20: every living villager's health becomes 100 and their sickness is cured. Science Awareness Day runs the game's own case 26: every living child gains 3 to 7 Research skill points (capped at 100). Case 4 (no body or text in the original game) is drawn 1 time in 28 and shows one of The Tattered Diary, The Doctrine of Magicians or The Doctrine of Naturalists (rand(3)), the game's own English texts 698-700, in the ordinary single-result popup.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The lore pages change nothing but the popup: no food, tech, villager, skill or save value. The Mosquito Swarm and The Dragonfly Migration stay independent, as in the game's own code: neither sets or reads anything the other uses. Every other island event, the family weights, the 10-draw retry, the event timer and the Island Events Seen counter are the base game's own. No executable space is claimed: the lore-page body replaces stock code that can never run, and the five other edits are entries of the game's own jump tables.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static exact-build evidence; emulation of the real chooser, runner and trigger code proving each event's odds and effects; and a live test (v1.35.58 test build, 2026-10-04, every public VV2 patch): all six events picked through Pick Island Event and clicked through, each popup showing the game's own text, with the Swarm's sickness and pond, the Migration's heal and cure and Science Day's child Research read back from memory, and the three pages changing nothing but the Island Events Seen counter
- Guarded executable edits: 6; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Scrolling Popups (`vv2_scrolling_popups`)

Popups get scrollbars when their text does not fit: a popup is never taller or wider than the screen (its buttons stay at its bottom, where they always are), and when its text is taller than the room left, or wider than the box (a long line, or one very long word), a vertical and/or a horizontal scrollbar appears, drawn with the game's own scrollbar pictures. A New Home and The Lost Children have no up/down scrollbar pictures of their own, so they borrow The Secret City's (shipped as new picture files; no game file is replaced). Scroll with the mouse wheel over the popup, the arrows, by dragging the knob or by clicking the bar; the text starts at the top and starts over when it changes. A popup whose text fits looks and works exactly as before. This covers the island-event popups (plain, two-choice and visitor events, and Custom Island Events from Story / Cheat Upgrades; also when the result replaces the question in a popup sized for the question), message boxes (tech and puzzle results, confirmations), tips (the tutorial and notices), the tombstone (a long name or cause of death scrolls sideways) and Statistics and Create Nickname (a long translation or name scrolls sideways). The Options panel (each label sits beside its slider or button, which cannot scroll with it), the few-second online-statistics notice, and the panels with no text body (Change Player, the outfit chooser) are as the game draws them. There is no keyboard scrolling. Nothing is saved, so the patch can be ticked or unticked at any time. **Needs no other patch.** Off by default; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.** The companion is "VVFP Scrolling Popups.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if it cannot be loaded, the popups are as the game draws them.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The message box (vtable 0x476DC4, laid out by 0x432C90): its `call 0x40D140` sizing the panel (0x432EE8) calls the companion, which keeps the size asked for and caps the width and the height to the screen's (800 x 600, read from the drawing context) less 16 px on each side; the game then centres the panel and places its text and buttons as always. The text control draw's `call 0x4096A0` drawing a control's text (0x40CB77) calls the companion: the text of a message box whose panel was capped (the control's parent has the message box's vtable and asked for more than the screen holds) is drawn under a clip rectangle set to the room the box keeps for it (0x14 below the panel's top, 0x1E from its sides, above its buttons), moved by the scroll position, with the scrollbars beside it; every other text, and a message box's text that fits, is the stock call unchanged. The tip (vtable 0x48FAC8): its `call 0x40D140` sizing the panel (0x443D86) is capped the same way. The frame draw's tail (0x40D383, `mov edx, [esi]` to the `jmp` into the dialog's body draw) jumps to the companion, which makes the same pops and calls the body draw: a tip that asked for more than the screen holds has its body drawn with its panel rectangle (+0x14..+0x20, which the body draw places everything by) moved by the scroll position and by what the capped panel moved its centred contents, under a clip set to the box (0x24 from the sides, 0x0A below the top, above twice the OK button's height), the rectangle put back after, with the scrollbars; every other dialog's body is called exactly as before. The island-event dialog (plain, vtable 0x476DF8): its `call 0x40D140` (0x434A6B) is capped the same way, and the room it asks for below its text is kept. The island-event dialog (two choices, vtable 0x476714): its `call 0x40D140` (0x42255F) is capped the same way, and the room it asks for below its text is kept. The island-event dialog (sacks and vials / two choices, vtable 0x476F30): its `call 0x40D140` (0x439FA4) is capped the same way, and the room it asks for below its text is kept. Through the frame draw's tail, an island-event dialog whose text shown now (measured with the game's own text height and width; the result when it has replaced the question) does not fit above that room, or is wider than the panel, has its body drawn with the y its constructor keeps (+0x64 / +0x6C) and, for a wide text, the panel's sides moved by the scroll position, under a clip, with the scrollbars. The tombstone (vtable 0x48FB48, a fixed panel): its body draw draws every line with the centred-block draw, whose call of the core draw (0x4096F1) calls the companion. Through the frame draw's tail the body is drawn once measuring (each line's extent recorded, nothing drawn, the clip empty), and when a line runs past the panel's sides (a long name, Cause of Death's cause line, a translation) the body is drawn with the panel rectangle (which the body draw and Cause of Death's line place everything by) moved by the scroll position, under a clip 16 px in from the sides and above the OK button, with a horizontal bar below the lines; otherwise exactly as before. The same for Statistics (vtable 0x477640), Create Nickname (vtable 0x47647C): at the text control draw's call (0x40CB77) a line of one of these panels is measured with all the panel's lines (its window's text controls); when one runs past the panel's sides, every line is drawn moved by the scroll position under a clip 16 px in from the sides, above the controls in the panel's lower half (its buttons, a text box), with a horizontal bar below the lines; text boxes, buttons and every panel that fits are drawn exactly as before. The event pump's `call 0x402070` handing a mouse event to the game (0x403EFE) calls the companion first: a press on a scrollbar of the popup drawn this moment, a knob drag and its release are used by the companion and not passed on; every other event goes to the game unchanged. The wheel is read by an SDL event watch (SDL_AddEventWatch, SDL_MOUSEWHEEL). The scrollbars are the game's own pictures (WideSlider2.png and sliderhandle.png (its own) and Images\vvfp_scroll_up/down/track/knob.png (The Secret City's UpArrowButton, DownArrowButton, VerticalScrollTrack and VerticalScrollKnob, borrowed)): Up/DownArrowButton, VerticalScrollTrack fitted to the bar's height, VerticalScrollKnob; the horizontal bar is WideSlider2 fitted to the vertical track's width (18 px) with sliderhandle fitted to the knob's size turned sideways.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion writes its sites at run time, only after verifying their stock bytes and the instructions before them (all of them, or none). A popup whose text fits is drawn by the very same call as in the stock game; the popups' text fields keep their sizes; keys, the buttons, the events and the save are unchanged. No game picture is replaced: the borrowed pictures are new files.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the companion emulated on the published executable's own popup code with the game's own fonts and pictures (tests/test_scrolling_popups.py: the panel capped, the clip set and restored, wheel, arrows, knob drag and track clicks moving the drawn lines, the buttons at the panel's bottom, a fitting text drawn exactly as the stock game draws it); runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Show Cause of Death on Graves, and Log Every Death (`vv2_cause_of_death`)

Shows each dead villager's cause of death on their grave, the way The Secret City, The Tree of Life and New Believers do: clicking a gravestone shows the cause under the age, in those games' own words (Old age, Disease, Starvation, Work accident, or Unknown causes). The cause is the one that killed them -- old age, sickness, hunger or an empty food bin, an injury at work -- and "Unknown causes" for an island event and anything else, which is how those games word an island-event death; a Custom Island Event's "dies" is "Died in a custom island event". The Lost Children keeps no cause, so it is kept for each save slot in a file beside the saves ('Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Graves\Virtual Villagers 2 Graves - Save <n>.dat'); Start Over deletes it. The game's own epitaphs are unchanged. With Children's Graves Say Apprentice ticked, a child's grave -- a villager who died before the age of 14 -- names their job the way The Tree of Life words a child's grave: "Apprentice Farmer" rather than Trainee, Adept or Master, and the Deaths log says the same. **Graves dug before this patch was installed, and bodies that were already lying when it was, show no cause: how they died was never recorded.** Every death that leaves a body is written to the Deaths log ('Virtual Villagers 2 Deaths Log <n>.txt' in the save slot's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Deaths and Disappearances' folder beside the game's saves, or 'Deaths' in a save an older version made: nothing is moved) when it is final: when the body is buried, with the skill line and epitaph the grave was given, or when the game removes a body nobody buried ("no grave"). Each Death record gives the villager's name, head, body, likes and dislikes, their age at death in the game's own units (20 per year, as the Village Population log prints Age), the cause, the grave and the epitaph. A villager brought back to life gets no Death record. A villager taken with no skeleton (A Dangerous Mission and The Voices In The Brush, or the Custom Island Event's "Disappears") gets a "Disappeared" record saying what took them, and editing a grave's epitaph adds an "Epitaph changed" record with the old and new text. A grave the Deaths log has no record for -- dug before the log was kept, or while the game was catching up on time away -- is given a Death record only when the player says so -- Repair Logs in the patcher window, or Repair when the game asks as it closes (with "Check logs automatically" on, and only if something is wrong); nothing is ever asked while the village is played. The record is made from the grave (name, age at death, skill line, epitaph, and the cause where the game or this patch knows it) with the head, body, likes and dislikes of the villager's last Village History snapshot ("(unknown)" when that does not settle who it was), and marked "Recorded from the grave". Which graves have their record is kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Deaths\Virtual Villagers 2 Graves Logged - Save <n>.dat', so no grave is recorded twice; Start Over deletes it. Every villager who joins the village without being born into it -- a new village's founders, an island event's newcomer, the Barrel of Babies, the Custom Island Event's new villagers -- gets an "Arrived" record in the Births and Conceptions log ('Virtual Villagers 2 Births and Conceptions Log <n>.txt'), written at the next save: the name, the age when they arrived, sex, head, body, likes, dislikes, skills, and how they came ("Founder", the island event's title, "Barrel of Babies", "Custom Island Event", or "unknown"). A birth is never an arrival. A mother who dies or disappears while nursing (the game's own word for a mother whose babies are not yet born) loses them with her: they never become villagers and get no grave, so her Death or Disappeared record says "Nursing: yes, <n> babies (never born: lost with their mother)", and a "Lost before birth" record in the Births and Conceptions log closes her Conception (the mother, the expected father, the babies). Repair Saves & Logs adds both to older records where her Conception has no Birth and her one Death or Disappeared record came before the babies were due, and asks the player where the records cannot settle it. Villagers already in a village who arrived before this record existed (no Birth or Arrived record with their name, head and body) each get one the same way, only when the player says so, marked "Recorded afterwards (arrived before this log existed)", as "Founder" when the village's first Village History snapshot lists them and otherwise with how they came unknown -- exactly once: 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Data\Arrivals\Virtual Villagers 2 Arrivals Recorded - Save <n>.dat' then says it is done; Start Over deletes it. A villager the save says was born here (their record keeps their parents) who has no Birth or Arrived record -- born before the log existed -- gets, the same way and only when the player says so, a Birth record written from the save, with their parents as the save keeps them, marked "Recorded afterwards (born before this log existed)" -- exactly once: 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Births\Virtual Villagers 2 Births Recorded - Save <n>.dat' then says it is done; Start Over deletes it. At every save, the village is checked against the one saved before, villager by villager by who they are (name, sex, looks, likes and dislikes, and an age that fits; never by record number, which every load, a full village and the Elder Totems move change): a villager who left with no Death or Disappeared record, or arrived with no birth or known arrival, is written with everything known about them to the Unaccounted Villagers log ('Virtual Villagers 2 Unaccounted Villagers Log <n>.txt' in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Unaccounted Villagers'). Both logs are headed with the village and its save slot, are created when a village is started and again after Start Over (which deletes them with the village), only ever grow, and start a new numbered file after every 256 records. The village as it was at each save is kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Unaccounted Villagers\Virtual Villagers 2 Villagers at Last Save - Save <n>.dat' ('... Village Roster ...' in a save an older version made); Start Over deletes it. A villager who is in the village at both saves with another head or body (an island event the Island Events log did not see, or any other change the game made) is written to the Births and Conceptions log as an 'Appearance changed' record, 'Changed by: the game', unless Change Appearance or the Island Events log already wrote one for that look; a newcomer never is. **The first save after this patch is installed only starts the check: nothing is reported about anything that happened before it.** **The patch's DLL is loaded and its hooks installed as soon as the game is opened, before any village is loaded, so the deaths, burials, disappearances and arrivals of the catch-up on time away (and of a Time Warp) are recorded as they happen, like any others.** **The logs are written by Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File's DLL: with that patch off, none of them is written.** **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. That base's companion loads this patch's DLL; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the game runs unchanged.

**Needs Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File on for the Deaths and Unaccounted Villagers logs, which that patch's DLL writes (without it neither is written). The Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically.**

- Behavior changes: At each site that can kill (the aging step's old-age store and its sickness, hunger and no-food drains; every work injury), a check made before the site's own instructions records the cause when that change takes a living villager's health to 0 or below; the site's instructions then run unchanged. Every frame, a villager seen alive on an earlier frame who is now a body, with no site having reported the death, is recorded with "Unknown causes" (island events, the Gong of Wonder, an edited save); the Custom Island Event's "dies" is reported by the Story / Cheat Upgrades companion and recorded as "Died in a custom island event". After the burial's grave loop, the cause recorded for that body is carried to the grave it was given, and the Death record is written. The grave popup draws the cause at the later games' height (+0xD7). With Children's Graves Say Apprentice in the exe (its recoded rank pick, checked by cod_apprentice_patched), a child's grave (the age at death the grave keeps under 280 age units, 14 years) whose best skill is 20 or more shows "Apprentice <job>" (that row draws it; right after the popup prints the rank this companion puts the game's own "Apprentice " string (0x83) in the line too, the same words), and the Death, Epitaph changed and Recorded from the grave records' Grave line says "Apprentice <job>" for the same graves. Without that row the grave and the records show the rank. Kept per save slot in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Graves\Virtual Villagers 2 Graves - Save <n>.dat' (written atomically; an unreadable file is set aside, never overwritten; deleted by Start Over). The listed removals of a living villager write a Disappeared record before the game takes them; the Custom Island Event's "Disappears" is reported by the Story / Cheat Upgrades DLL. Graves with no Death record: VvfpCauseScanGraves counts, writing nothing, the graves the village's Deaths log has no record for (the first-load check lists them for the player); VvfpCauseRepairGraves records the player's answer. Only after Repair, at each save of that village in the session, each such grave gets a Death record from the grave, filed by RecordGravesMissingFromLog in "VVFP Parentage Export.dll" (which counts the log's own and held records first, and takes the head, body, likes and dislikes from the Village History log); a villager the previous save held who was buried unseen is then not an Unaccounted record. The graves whose record is in the log are kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Deaths\Virtual Villagers 2 Graves Logged - Save <n>.dat' (written atomically; deleted by Start Over). The grave's Done writes an Epitaph changed record when the epitaph's text changed; spaces typed before or after the same words are not a change. Every villager the game's own creators make is noted as an arrival; after each save the village is compared with the roster kept at the save before, and any departure with no Death or Disappeared record, or arrival with no known arrival, is written to the Unaccounted Villagers log. The comparison follows each villager by identity, never by record number (v1.35.80): each villager of the last save is matched one to one to a villager now by name, sex, head, body, likes and dislikes with the age gone on by the time every matched villager aged, then by name, sex and looks, then -- only when one villager on each side is such -- through a changed head, a rename or a rejuvenation; a departure the game reported (a burial, a body's removal, a disappearance) accounts for the villager it names, by name, sex and looks, before any matching; a villager who only moved to another record is neither Left nor Arrived, and one with a Death or Disappeared record is never Left. Statues, totems and look-alikes are no villagers. The roster is kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Unaccounted Villagers\Virtual Villagers 2 Villagers at Last Save - Save <n>.dat', or '... Village Roster ...' in a save an older version made, never renamed; under both names the one written last (written atomically; deleted by Start Over). Arrivals: a villager a creator made that is neither a birth (the path's own return addresses, read at fixed places on the stack, or the Births and Conceptions log's note) nor a record the game takes away again is decided at the next tick, named by its path (Founder, the island event, Barrel of Babies, the developer F7 command in The Tree of Life), or "added outside a recorded event" when no listed path made it, and gets an Arrived record at the next save of that village (at its departure if it leaves first); the Story / Cheat Upgrades DLL names the Custom Island Event's (VvfpCauseArrivedBy). A founder is written only at a save with no village saved in the slot before. Arrivals before this record existed: VvfpCauseScanArrivals counts, writing nothing, the villagers (believers, with no parents on their record) the village's Births and Conceptions log has no Birth or Arrived record for (name, head and body), for the first-load check; VvfpCauseRepairArrivals records the answer. Only after Repair, at the next save, each gets an Arrived record filed by RecordArrivalsMissingFromLog in "VVFP Parentage Export.dll", and none is an Unaccounted record; once all are on disk 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Arrivals\Virtual Villagers 2 Arrivals Recorded - Save <n>.dat' (deleted by Start Over) ends the backfill for good. All records are written through WriteVillageRecord in "VVFP Parentage Export.dll".
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the Origins companion loads the DLL, which detours the listed sites at run time only after verifying every site's stock bytes; any other build installs nothing. No game value is changed: health, age, the graves, the Roster of the Dead and the save are only read; each detoured site's own instructions run unchanged after the check. Nothing is written into the game's grave table or a villager record; the cause lives only in the patcher's .dat file.
- Dependencies: vv2_enable_origins_exclusive_features
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Skip All on the Intro Story (`vv2_skip_all_intro`)

Adds a "Skip All" button to the story shown when a new village starts, as The Secret City has. The story is three pages (the third asks the help question); on every page before the question, a Skip All button sits at the bottom right, in the game's own button style and font. Clicking it ends the story at once: the page fades out as it always does and you land straight on the help question, "Would you like tutorial tips turned on?", with its Yes and No buttons already showing. Yes and No are the game's own and do exactly what they do at the end of the story read to the end. Without a click on Skip All the story is unchanged (a click anywhere else still turns the page). The button's word is translatable. **On by default.** **Needs no other patch.** **Not yet seen in a running game** (checked by emulation of the stock executable). The companion is "VVFP Skip Intro.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; saves are never written by it.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: When a story page before the last is activated, a button is built once for it as the last page builds its Yes button -- the game's allocator, button constructor and label call, with the art name pointer the Yes button uses -- at the Yes/No row (640, 550), drawn with popup_button1.png, the art of the help question's own Yes and No, labelled "Skip All" (asked of VVFP Translations.dll by key), id 0x5C1A, and added to the page as a child: the page draws it and the game's event manager hands it the mouse. Its click (message 8, id 0x5C1A, to the page's button slot) sets skip pending and calls the page's own event slot with event 2 -- the stock code a click anywhere runs -- so the page fades out and moves on as it always does. When the first page's stock update has just moved the game to page 2's state (0x17) while skip is pending, the game goes to page 3's state (0x18) instead; page 3 was built with page 1. On the first frame of the page 3 (the help question) while skip is pending, its frame count is put past its 50-frame (25 fast) wait before the stock update runs, so the stock update adds its Yes and No buttons on that frame; skip pending is then cleared (and is cleared whenever page 1 is activated). The answer is the stock last page's own: Yes: the tutorial-tip flags [game+0x31+i] cleared and set from 0x186, the help flags +0x1F4..+0x1F7, +0x1FA, +0x1FB set, [game+0x2E4F8] = the clock, sound 0x4A. No: the same, then tips 0x186..0x1BE cleared, [game+0x1D8] = 1, sound 0x49 (the last page's button slot 0x428B30).
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces vtable slots of the story page classes at run time, only after verifying every stock pointer, and installs nothing on a different build. Without a click on Skip All every replaced slot runs the stock one with the same arguments; only the button is added. The pages' text, timing, the help question, its Yes and No buttons and what they set are the game's own. The F1 key and the typed-character page turn are untouched. No game art or font ships: the game draws its own button image with its own font. Nothing is written to a save, a villager record or a file.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Story / Cheat Upgrades (`vv2_story_cheat_upgrades`)

Adds optional tools intended for custom stories, experiments, sandbox play, and cheats. These features deliberately allow the player to bypass normal game progression and random-event behavior. When enabled, all Origins Upgrades cost 0 Tech Points. Also adds the following Origins Upgrades: Pick Island Event -- Allows the player to directly choose which stock Island Event occurs instead of relying on random selection. Opening this upgrade displays a list of the game's official Island Event titles, each with a brief description. Selecting an event causes that specific event to occur through the game's Island Event system. Custom Island Event -- Allows the player to create and trigger a custom Island Event for storytelling, testing, sandbox play, or cheats. The player may customize supported event properties, including: Title and description; Food gained or lost; Tech Points gained or lost; Villagers spawned; Spawned-villager details, including supported appearance, age, sex, name, likes/dislikes, skills, and other valid villager attributes; Villager behavior or state changes; Village-state changes; Puzzle-state changes; Other game-specific values that can be safely and reliably manipulated. Custom events should appear and behave as closely as practical to ordinary Island Events, while clearly allowing player-defined outcomes. Only what this game's own code supports is offered; the rest is shown as not available in this game. A custom title is kept per save slot in a file beside the saves and is removed by Start Over. Bought island events don't change when the game's own island events come. A Custom Island Event can also be bought and delivered when everyone in the village has died (the game's own island events wait for a living villager), so new villagers, food, Tech Points, refills and revived skeletons can bring the village back; what needs a living villager is simply not there to choose, and a question with two choices is refused until someone lives. In A New Home and The Lost Children a village that died before its first island event gets it too, uncounted, so its first island event is still the game's own visitor once someone lives. A custom event can also ask a question with two choices: the player writes the question, the two button labels and, for each button, one to four outcomes, each with its own chance, result text and changes (everything the event itself can change); clicking a button rolls one of its outcomes by those chances and makes only that outcome's changes. **A question with two choices can be queued only in a game whose own two-button island-event popup the companion hooks; in any other game the option is shown as not available yet.** Pick Island Event also lets the player set how the picked event turns out. Each setting starts at "Random (original game)" and offers only what that event's own code can produce in this game: its result (for a two-choice event, the result of each choice -- the popup still appears and the player still clicks), every amount it can roll, who a roll it makes for each villager hits (nobody, everyone, or the villagers chosen), which villager it is about, and each baby's details; in A New Home and The Lost Children also its strength (normally a third of the population, 1 to 10). A setting whose condition does not hold right now can not be bought. An event whose own condition is only a matter of timing or story can be picked anyway, and developer-dead events proven to work are offered as never happening in the original game; events that need something the village lacks, or room for new villagers, stay locked with the reason. On by default, with Story / Cheat Upgrades cost Tech Points ticked too, so the upgrades keep their normal tech-point prices until that row is unticked. **Requires Enable Origins Tech, Details, and Village-Wide Upgrades: ticking this ticks it, and without it there are no Origins Upgrades to make free and no Pick Island Event or Custom Island Event.** **A pregnancy a custom event starts is written to the Births and Conceptions log only with Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File ticked.** Also adds Pick Gong of Wonder Outcome (0 Tech Points): the player picks what the next ring of the Gong of Wonder does -- any of the 23 results the Gong can give (also the ones the game keeps for after a village's first ring), with its amounts, who falls sick, the skill, the babies and the villager the ringer's results act on -- each defaulting to "Random (original game)". Buying it makes a whole Gong ready to ring at once (refused, and nothing spent, while the Gong is not whole); the choice is used for one ring, in this save slot, within ten minutes. Also adds Choose Time Skip Amount (0 Tech Points, the same as Time Warp): the player types how many years to skip, from 1 to 72, and the village moves forward that many villager years as a run of the Time Warp upgrade's own advance -- one Time Warp at a time (3 years on slow, 6 on normal, 12 on fast, the last one only what is left), each caught up by the game before the next -- so villagers work, eat, have babies, grow up and die of old age through the skipped years just as after a Time Warp. **Keep the game running until the skip is done: it pauses while the game is paused, and loading another village, Start Over or deleting the tribe drops the rest.** Cancel charges nothing.

**Requires Enable Origins Tech, Details, and Village-Wide Upgrades: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this. Needed by Story / Cheat Upgrades cost Tech Points: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: Every Origins upgrade on the Tech screen and the Villager Details screen costs 0 tech points: each price the Origins payload compares, deducts, refunds or shows is set to 0 at run time, and the Origins companion shows and charges 0. Every existing refusal stays: one pending Island Event or Barrel of Babies at a time, room for the Barrel's children, and every "nothing to change" check. A bought island event (the Origins Island Event, Pick Island Event, Custom Island Event) counts as pending until the game's own island-event trigger runs it -- the Origins companion's keeper of the island timer knows it from the purchase's write until the trigger's own (native/shared/island_timer_keep.h) -- not only while the timer is due within the purchase's five seconds, which the paused Tech screen outlasts.  A Custom Island Event is never held by it: it is delivered first and the bought or picked event it went ahead of is made due again right after it, each charged once; a waiting Barrel of Babies is never replaced (it comes first).  With nobody the trigger accepts (a count of 0, or no villager its own draw takes), the custom event is delivered all the same, so its new villagers always arrive; changes for villagers who are not there are skipped and the popup says so.  It is never held for a new village's two opening island events: it comes first, uncounted, and they still come after it as the game makes them. Adds a Choose Time Skip Amount upgrade (the Time Warp's price: 0 tech points, or 50,000 with Story / Cheat Upgrades cost Tech Points) to the Origins Tech menu: a plain Windows dialog takes 1-72 years (20 age units a year), and the Origins companion's own Time Warp advance runs in steps of at most one Time Warp at the current speed, the next step only once the game's villager tick has replayed the last (its catch-up), so no jump is bigger than a Time Warp.  Charged once, when the first step is made; Cancel, a paused game or an empty village charge nothing. Adds a Pick Island Event upgrade (0 tech points) to the Origins Tech menu: a plain Windows list of this game's island events by their official titles, each with a one-line description.  The pick makes the island event due exactly as the Island Event upgrade does (the same pending lock), and when the game's own scheduler fires it, the game's own chooser runs the picked event -- only if that event's own condition holds -- with its own text, choices, random outcomes and amounts. Offers 59 island events; events that can never run in this game are not offered. Adds a Custom Island Event upgrade (0 tech points): plain Windows dialogs build an event (title, description, village changes, new villagers, per-villager changes for a list with extended selection and the group toggles All Adult Women, All Adult Men, All Females, All Males and All Children, plus in New Believers All Heathens and one toggle for each Heathen type; each villager's row names the role the game keeps for them, such as the Golden Child or the Tribal Chief).  It is queued exactly as the Island Event upgrade queues one (the same lock), and when the game's own scheduler fires it, the game's own island-event popup shows the custom title and description and the changes are made through the game's own routines. Its amounts list shows each amount the game keeps as it is now, below 0 included (The Lost Children's fish and the field's protection fall below 0 in the original game), and the event replaces it; only a store that is not there yet, such as a farm not yet built, reads "not there yet" and is refused. Villager Changes offers every villager action the game's own code can start for one villager, Celebrating included, grouped (work, leisure, celebration and dance, devotion, family, children, health, curiosity, moods, puzzles and story) and sorted, each labelled with the text the Details screen then shows; the villager is stopped first and the game's own starter runs.  An action that may harm the game or the save ends "(Unsafe)": choosing it shows the reason and advises backing up the save (OK / Cancel), and one that would need a missing object is refused when the event happens instead of crashing. New villagers and babies are made only while the game's own room predicate says the village has room, so the population cap of the installed mode is never passed. A new tribe's first two island events are always the game's own (each game's village start sets its island-event counter to 0): a custom event queued before the second of them stays queued -- the same lock, nothing charged again -- without making the island event due, and is made due exactly as the Island Event upgrade does once the game has made both, so it is the third. A village where everyone has died (the game's own population count is 0; in New Believers the believers): the game keeps running but its island-event trigger does nothing while that count is 0.  The trigger's call of the count is retargeted to a stub that runs it unchanged; only when it answers 0 and a plain Custom Island Event is queued for this village does the trigger go on past its villager draw (as if one had been drawn), so the game reschedules, plays its sound, counts the event, builds it and shows its own popup with the custom event.  New Believers' selector, when no stock event is possible, goes to its delivery site with the custom event the same way (its two stock trophy calls first).  The purchase allows an empty village (a question with two choices is refused: it needs a living villager), an empty village does not wait for the two opening island events.  A New Home's and The Lost Children's trigger makes a village's first island event the game's visitor: an empty village that has had none resumes past that check too, and the delivery takes the trigger's count of it back (as for the time skip's notice), so Island Events Seen stays 0 and the visitor is still its first island event once someone lives. Pick Island Event's settings: each offered event can carry its result, every amount it rolls, who a per-villager roll hits, which villager it is about and each baby's details (A New Home and The Lost Children: also its strength), each defaulting to Random (original game).  The companion points the event's own rand() calls at a stub that answers the chosen value only in that roll's phase (before the popup, the popup, or the event's apply), for the clicked choice, and -- in a routine other code shares -- only inside the event's own call to it; the outcome ends when the event's apply returns, on refusal and on lapse, so no chosen value reaches a natural event. Unlocked picks: an event whose own condition is only timing or story (proven by running its popup and apply with the condition false) can be picked anyway; its condition is passed for that one delivery only.  Developer-dead events proven to work are offered as never happening in the original game. A custom title replaces a villager's title in the villager panel and is printed in the Village Population and Village History logs; it is kept per save slot in Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save N\Data\Custom Titles\Custom Titles - Save N.dat and deleted by Start Over.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched; the companion writes the listed sites at run time after verifying every one of them, and writes nothing if any differs. No stock event is emulated: a picked event is created, shown and resolved by the game's own code; a custom event is shown by the game's own island-event popup. Pick Island Event adds no tech points and writes nothing to the save; a custom event changes only what the player chose, through the game's own routines and fields, and the game saves the village as usual. No custom title is written into a villager record. An empty village with nothing queued, and every village with anyone alive, runs the island-event trigger exactly as stock; the game's own "Your tribe has been lost! Game over." status line and its tips are left as they are. Pick Gong of Wonder Outcome writes one value at the purchase: the Gong's rest (village +0x2EAC8) is set to 1, the value the game itself writes when the Gong becomes whole, only when the Gong is whole and resting.  A chosen result the game keeps for after a village's first ring sets the Gong's tier byte (village +0x2E910) to 1, the game's own value, for that ring only, and puts 0 back when the ring's outcome routine returns.  'Takes youth' / 'Grants youth' write the fixed records 6 and 15 in the game; with a villager chosen they write that villager's age instead, through the game's own stores (Random keeps records 6 and 15).
- Dependencies: vv2_origins_village_wide_upgrades
- Evidence status: static exact-build verification and emulation of the rendered executables and the companion; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Teaching Children Stops at 50 (`vv2_teaching_children_cap_50`)

Each child who finishes a Teaching Children lesson (Attending lessons) still gains 7 to 9 points in one random skill, but only a skill still below 50 can be chosen, and the gain stops at exactly 50; a skill already at 50 or above is never chosen and never lowered. When every skill is at 50 the lesson awards nothing. This matches the Nursery Schools of the later games, which skip any skill at 50. **Requires Teaching Children Grants Skill** (the lesson it caps). **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. That base's companion loads this patch's DLL.

**Requires Teaching Children Grants Skill: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this. The Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically.**

- Behavior changes: When the lesson's completion callback 127 runs, the companion counts the child's skills below 50, asks the game's own RNG for one of them and for the stock 7 to 9 points, adds them and stops at exactly 50. With every skill at 50 or above the lesson awards nothing.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the Origins companion loads the DLL, which detours the lesson row's own callback cave at run time only after verifying its bytes; the lesson row not applied, or a different build, installs nothing. A skill at or above 50 is never lowered; work-task training past 50 is untouched. The lesson itself -- who teaches, who attends, its length, its animation and its messages -- is the game's own; only the award at its end changes. Nothing is written to a villager record beyond the skill the lesson would have written, nor to the save or any file.

#### Translations (`vv2_translations`)

Plays the game in another language. Choose a language for each game in Tools > Translations... (or make your own there: the patcher writes a file with every English line of the game, its menus, events, tips, tech names and the patcher's own windows, and a built-in editor shows each line in the game's font). The game uses the chosen language from its next start, with no re-patching; lines a translation leaves out, or gets wrong, stay English. Gender and plural words follow the villager or the number (for example il / elle, 1 pomme / 2 pommes). **On by default, and English until you choose a language: with English chosen the game is exactly as without this patch.** **Letters beyond plain English (accents, Turkish ğ ş ı, Greek, Cyrillic, Chinese, Japanese, Cuneiform, emoji) need "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" or "Use Unicode Font"; without either, the game's own font draws only plain English letters and the rest show as "?".** **With one of those two rows a translated line never runs off the screen (it is cut with "…" at the window's edge, though it may run past its own box); without them the game draws it as it is.** **Words painted into pictures (buttons, the title screen, help pages) stay English.** **Every patch's own text is translated too: its windows and messages, Custom Island Event popups, Cause of Death words and epitaphs, Son/Daughter, and the text the exe patches write; log files stay English.** **Works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Not yet seen in a running game.** The companion is "VVFP Translations.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if it cannot be loaded, or the game's text is not the version a translation was made from, those lines stay English.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: At game start the companion reads "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Files\Translation\Translation.txt" (written by the patcher's Translations window; docs/translation-file-format.md). With no such file it returns at once and writes nothing. Each translated line replaces the English where the game looks it up: the string table at 0x496300 (876 rows): each translated row's English pointer (+4); the visible literals outside the table by the address their loading instruction pushes (data/translations/vv2_strings.json).  A line is used only when the English it was made from is the English this game shows (the key's SHA-256), its placeholders match and its selects are well formed. The patcher's own windows (Origins, Story / Cheat Upgrades, Custom Island Event) are translated as they open (a WH_CALLWNDPROCRET hook on the game's own thread, only when the file translates any of them); a message put together from several lines is translated line by line. The companions that build a text the game shows (Cause of Death's words and epitaphs, Story / Cheat Upgrades' island event lines and Time Skip notice, Show Parents' Son / Daughter, Storytelling, Both Factions) ask for it by its line's key (VvfpTranslateKey / VvfpTranslateKeyText, native/shared/vvfp_translate.h): the translation is used only when the English is the line's and it fits the companion's own buffer, else the English. Text an exe patch wrote ("patch/0x<va>" lines, data/translations/exe_patch_strings.json) is written over in place when the translation fits the English's own bytes (through the same all-or-none writer, after checking the live text is the line's English); a longer one is left English there. Without "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" or "Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts)" (their companion's VvfpGlyphsUtf8; Use Unicode Font's, which starts later, is loaded and started on first use), translations are given to the game in Windows-1252, '?' for what it cannot write.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the companion checks each site's stock bytes and writes them at run time through the shared all-or-none writer, and writes only the ones the chosen file needs; if any check fails it writes nothing, not even a table pointer, and the game stays English. No save, record or game file is written; the game's own English text stays in memory unchanged. With English chosen (no Translation.txt), nothing at all is written.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts) (`vv2_unicode_font`)

Draws ALL of the game's text in a Windows typeface instead of the game's own bitmap fonts: Segoe UI unless you choose another in the patcher (the Unicode Font box, or the Tools tab's Unicode Font... window: any installed family, or a .ttf, .otf or .ttc file; the choice is written next to the game as "VVFP Unicode Font.txt"), with Windows' fallback chain for every character it lacks (Segoe UI, Segoe UI Historic, Segoe UI Symbol, Segoe UI Emoji (in colour), the CJK fonts, Nirmala UI, Ebrima ..., Noto if installed, then the bundled open fonts: Noto Sans Cuneiform, Noto Serif Tangut, GNU Unifont, Unifont Upper and last Last Resort). Each of the game's two fonts keeps its line height, baseline and weight, and its size is fitted so a line is as wide as the game's own, so every screen keeps its layout; every character works, as with "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts". **Text and translations never run off the screen:** a line this patch, a long name or a translation draws that would cross the edge of the game's 800-pixel-wide window is cut there with "…" (whole letters only; a justified paragraph wraps at the edge instead), and one that would start left of the window starts at its edge; it may still run past its own box. Without a translation, the game's own English is drawn exactly as before. This needs this row: with Translations alone (no Unicode row) the game draws by itself and nothing is fitted. Where Windows has no icu.dll (before Windows 10 1903), Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between words by ICU's own word lists (ICU 77.1, Unicode License; about 4.4 MB in "Word Lists", read only when such a line is broken). Typing: every text box -- the tribe name, villager names on the Details screen, epitaphs -- takes any character Windows sends (dead keys, Alt codes, the Windows emoji panel, an input method for Japanese or Chinese), each stored whole or not at all, and Backspace erases a whole character (a whole emoji, flag or accented letter). Long names, everywhere: every name box takes names up to 1,200 bytes (up to 1,200 plain letters; fewer when letters need more bytes): the tribe name, villager names on the Details screen, epitaphs; Rename Tribe takes the same. It is one limit, shared with the other Fun Patchers. Characters are counted as you see them (a letter with its accents, an emoji with its skin tone or a flag is one), and Backspace removes one whole character. A long name scrolls in its box while you type it. The save itself is not changed: a name that fits its field (a villager's name 23 bytes, the tribe name 31) is kept there exactly as before; a longer one is kept there as its short form (its start and a mark, with a number when two would start alike) and the whole name is kept beside the save, in Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Long Names. The game shows the whole name wherever it shows that name. Back Up Saves, Restore Saves and Copy Player Slot carry the Long Names files with the saves. With both settings off the game still loads and plays such a save and shows the short form. Characters are stored as UTF-8 (a Western European letter keeps its one Windows-1252 byte), so every older name reads as before; the base game and older patchers show other characters as odd letters but never break. **Off by default and in Owner's Defaults.** **Cannot be used with "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" (ticking one unticks the other).** **Needs "Full Names on the Details Screen" (ticked with it): its Details box keeps the whole stored name, so opening a villager's Details and closing it never changes a name.** **Not yet seen in a running game** (checked by emulation of each stock executable). The companion is "VVFP Unicode Font.dll" (the same code as "VVFP Unicode Text.dll"), started by VVFP Startup.dll; the game's own pictures and saves are never changed, and no Windows font is shipped. **Bundles four open fonts, loaded privately by the game (never installed in Windows): GNU Unifont 18.0.01 (GPL-2.0-or-later with the font exception, or OFL-1.1) and Unifont Upper for nearly every assigned character, Noto Sans Cuneiform and Noto Serif Tangut (OFL-1.1), and Last Resort 18.000 (OFL-1.1), a placeholder block for anything still without a glyph; about 14 MB of fonts (in the patcher's files folder, in "Unicode Fonts", with their licence texts and sources), copied once per game folder, and not again when the folder already has identical files.**

**Requires Full Names on the Details Screen: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this.**

- Behavior changes: The font constructor (0x4024D0) runs unchanged; for the game's two fonts -- ldwBurweed27 (stock glyph table 0x4952C0) and ldwarialbold (0x4958A8) -- the companion records the font's line height, baseline, capital height and pixel format. Their own letters are not used: every letter is made from the chosen Windows typeface. Text is read by one rule (src/vv_game_text.py, native/vvfp_unicode_text/text_utf8.h): a well-formed UTF-8 sequence is its character, every other byte its Windows-1252 character, so every existing name reads as before. The width, draw, line-fitting, counted-draw and justified-paragraph routines are detoured: text without a multi-byte sequence goes to the game's own routine unchanged (with this patch, every text is drawn by the companion); other text is cut into whole units (grapheme clusters; shaped runs of Arabic, Hebrew, Indic and other scripts) and drawn in runs by the game's own draw and width routines, from the font's own letters or from pages of letters made at run time (Uniscribe shaping, GDI glyphs, COLR colour layers for emoji) in the font's size and baseline. Each detoured text routine first offers the text to VvfpTranslateText of "VVFP Translations.dll" when that companion is loaded (fails open), and shows a long name's short form as the whole name. Line breaking follows UAX #14 by Windows' own icu.dll (loaded from System32 only; a built-in table where Windows has none): a text with Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar or emoji breaks between whole characters where the rules allow (never before a closing mark or small kana, never after an opening one; Thai and the others at their words, inside a shaped run too), other text at spaces, and a word wider than the line after its longest start of whole characters that fits. Without icu.dll, Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between the words of ICU's own word lists ("Word Lists" beside the companion, read the first time a line of that script is broken; a missing list leaves the built-in table). The screen edge: a text drawn by the companion, expanded from a long name's short form, or drawn while a translation is in use is measured where the game draws it (x is its left edge after the game's own alignment); a line that would cross the right edge of the 800-pixel window (or of a narrower surface) is drawn as its longest start of whole units that fits with "…" after it, a text partly left of the window is drawn from its left edge, a justified paragraph is laid out no wider than the room to the edge, and when not even one unit fits the game's English is drawn. The widths the game is told are unchanged. The SDL_TEXTINPUT case (0x403E2B) posts a typed ASCII character exactly as before; any other well-formed text is handed whole to the focused text box, which stores each character whole (a Windows-1252 character as its one byte, any other as UTF-8) while it fits the box's limit. Backspace erases a whole unit. A box never cuts its text by pixels. Every box's limit is 1200 bytes; a text longer than the field GetText copies it to leaves as a short form: its longest start of whole characters, then "..." ("2...", "3...", the number first, when another long name has it; the older short forms ending in … stay readable), whose whole text is appended to the save's Long Names file and given back when the game puts the short form into a box.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces each routine's first instructions at run time, all of them or none, only after verifying their stock bytes, and installs nothing on a different build. The game's pictures (Images\ldwBurweed27.png, Images\ldwarialbold.png) are never changed and nothing of the game's art is shipped; letters are made in memory from the player's own Windows fonts and, for what they lack, from the bundled open fonts (Unicode Fonts folder), which are added to the game's process only (FR_PRIVATE) and never installed in Windows; a missing or unreadable font file only leaves its step out. A save's records only ever hold what fits their fields: every stock copy of a name sees the short form, never more bytes than the stock game wrote. Nothing is cut inside a character. A fault in any detour falls back to the game's own routine with the game's own text.
- Dependencies: vv2_details_full_names
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Villagers Have Last Names (`vv2_last_names`)

Babies born in the village and the village's founders get a last name after their first name, from the game's own list of 50 last names (Akikai, Alosaka, Awanata ... Wikimak) -- a list the game has always carried but never used, and the one Virtual Villagers 6 and 7 later used for villagers' last names. A baby takes its father's or its mother's last name by the rule chosen in Repair Saves & Logs (Last names come from: from the father, from the mother, 50:50, or a random one of the last names the village has ever used); without a rule recorded, a baby takes its father's last name (the village's default is from the father). A villager can also have a rule of their own for their children (Each villager's own rule): from the father, from the mother, 50:50, a random last name from the list, which gives each child -- twins and triplets too -- its own random draw from the game's list, every name equally likely, or a random one of the village's existing last names. A villager's own rule always beats the village's; when both parents have one and they disagree, a coin toss for each child picks whose. Villagers who arrive through an island event get no last name, because theirs would not be their family's. Only villagers named from now on get one: villagers who already have names keep them. The last name is part of the name the game stores, so it shows wherever the name does and stays in the save even if this patch is later removed. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: A baby born in the village from now on (a mother's delivery: the first child, a twin or a triplet) and a new village's founders are called "<first name> <last name>": the first name is the game's own pick, and the last name is name number <family - 1> of the game's unused third list (0X48FB98), read from the running executable. A villager the game creates any other way -- brought by an island event, a cheat or the Origins page -- keeps the game's own first name only: the companion tells a birth or a founder by the callers' return addresses on the stack, at fixed places. A villager whose family is outside 1-50 gets no last name. At a birth, the rule recorded by Repair Saves & Logs decides the last name (VvfpRuleLastName2): the father's, the mother's, either at random (50:50), or -- a parent's own rule "Random last name from the list" -- a name drawn at random from the game's list, or -- "Random from the existing Village Names", the village's rule or a parent's own -- one of the last names the village has ever used (the record's "used" lines, the villagers in the game at the birth, VvfpRuleLastName3, and the parents'; the game's list when there are none); every random draw is a fresh, unbiased one for each child. Each such birth adds the names it saw that the record lacks as "used" lines (only adding, through a temporary file, never for a slot it cannot tell), so a name stays ever used after its last bearer is gone. A parent's own rule always beats the village's; parents whose own rules disagree: a fresh coin toss for each child picks the father's or the mother's. The whole name always fits the game's own name field: the longest pairing is far below its 23 characters.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion detours the naming routine's first instruction at run time, after verifying it, the routine's push of the list and the creators' calls to it, and changes nothing if any differs. Villagers who already have names keep them; nothing is renamed when a village is loaded. The first names, sexes, looks and families are the game's own; the save format is unchanged.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static exact-build verification of the naming routines, their callers and the unused list in each executable; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.
