**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: Multiple children can be dropped onto a single mushroom (and collectible) and it will be multiplied.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: none declared

#### Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File (`vv2_write_parentage_log`)

Keeps a plain-text log of the village's conceptions and births in 'Virtual Villagers 2 Births and Conceptions Log <n>.txt', in the save slot's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Births and Conceptions' folder beside the game's saves (Documents\LDW\<game executable name>\); a shared 'Births and Conceptions' folder an older patcher wrote is kept as it was and still read. Each Conception record gives both parents' names, both parents' ages at conception, both head and body values, both parents' likes and dislikes, and the number of babies; the mother's age determines the child's age. Each Birth record, numbered like the Conceptions ("Birth 1", "Birth 2", ...), gives the child's name, head, body, likes, dislikes and skills, and its mother's and father's names, heads and bodies; Repair Saves & Logs can number the Birth records an older patcher wrote without one. A new numbered file is started after every 256 Conception records; Birth records go into the file holding the latest conceptions and do not count toward that limit. Each Arrived record, numbered on its own, gives a villager who joined the village without being born into it -- a new village's founders, an island event's newcomers, the Barrel of Babies, the Custom Island Event's new villagers (never a birth): their name, age when they arrived, sex, head, body, likes, dislikes and skills, and how they came ("Founder", the event's title, "Barrel of Babies", "Custom Island Event", or "unknown"); villagers who arrived before this record existed get one, marked "Recorded afterwards", only once the player chooses Repair when the village is loaded. **The Arrived records are found by the Cause of Death patch ("Log Every Death ..."): with it off, none is written.** A baby born with the full name of a living villager is numbered at its birth, before its Birth record is written ("Chip Kenobi" is born "Chip Kenobi II"; a number a dead or gone namesake had is never given again), while the village's "Number villagers who share a name automatically" is on (Repair Saves & Logs; on by default); the villager who already had the name becomes "I" -- with the dead, in the save and every log -- at the next Repair Saves & Logs, and a numbered name that would not fit the game's name limit is left for Repair Saves & Logs to show you. The game keeps both parents on the child's own record, and each Birth record reads them from there. VV2 keeps the father's name on the mother's record and no father id; his head and body are copied onto her at conception, so the log reads them from her record and they stay correct even after he dies or another villager takes his name. His age, which has no copy on her, is read from his own record -- every caller that holds it passes it, the Love Note included -- so a normal birth records his real age. **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which is installed automatically with it and adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens**: the loader trampoline lives in the page that base appends, because VV2's own code cave is occupied by the renamed-build crash guard and has no room for it.

**Needs Write Village Statistics to Text File or Show Cause of Death on Graves, and Log Every Death on for the village and savegame header at the top of the log, and for creating the log at a village's first save -- a new village, or one restarted with Start Over -- before anything is recorded (without either, records are still written correctly, just unlabelled, and the log first appears with its first record; Cause of Death names the village at each save itself). The Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically. Needed by Show Cause of Death on Graves, and Log Every Death for the Deaths and Unaccounted Villagers logs, which that patch's DLL writes (without it neither is written). Needed by Write Island Events Log to Text File for the Island Events log, which that patch's DLL writes (without it nothing is written).**

- Behavior changes: Keeps a plain-text log of the village's conceptions and births in 'Virtual Villagers 2 Births and Conceptions Log <n>.txt', in the save slot's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Births and Conceptions' folder beside the game's saves (Documents\LDW\<game executable name>\); a shared 'Births and Conceptions' folder an older patcher wrote is kept as it was and still read. Each Conception record gives both parents' names, both parents' ages at conception, both head and body values, both parents' likes and dislikes, and the number of babies; the mother's age determines the child's age. Each Birth record, numbered like the Conceptions ("Birth 1", "Birth 2", ...), gives the child's name, head, body, likes, dislikes and skills, and its mother's and father's names, heads and bodies; Repair Saves & Logs can number the Birth records an older patcher wrote without one. A new numbered file is started after every 256 Conception records; Birth records go into the file holding the latest conceptions and do not count toward that limit. Each Arrived record, numbered on its own, gives a villager who joined the village without being born into it -- a new village's founders, an island event's newcomers, the Barrel of Babies, the Custom Island Event's new villagers (never a birth): their name, age when they arrived, sex, head, body, likes, dislikes and skills, and how they came ("Founder", the event's title, "Barrel of Babies", "Custom Island Event", or "unknown"); villagers who arrived before this record existed get one, marked "Recorded afterwards", only once the player chooses Repair when the village is loaded. **The Arrived records are found by the Cause of Death patch ("Log Every Death ..."): with it off, none is written.** A baby born with the full name of a living villager is numbered at its birth, before its Birth record is written ("Chip Kenobi" is born "Chip Kenobi II"; a number a dead or gone namesake had is never given again), while the village's "Number villagers who share a name automatically" is on (Repair Saves & Logs; on by default); the villager who already had the name becomes "I" -- with the dead, in the save and every log -- at the next Repair Saves & Logs, and a numbered name that would not fit the game's name limit is left for Repair Saves & Logs to show you. The game keeps both parents on the child's own record, and each Birth record reads them from there. VV2 keeps the father's name on the mother's record and no father id; his head and body are copied onto her at conception, so the log reads them from her record and they stay correct even after he dies or another villager takes his name. His age, which has no copy on her, is read from his own record -- every caller that holds it passes it, the Love Note included -- so a normal birth records his real age. **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which is installed automatically with it and adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens**: the loader trampoline lives in the page that base appends, because VV2's own code cave is occupied by the renamed-build crash guard and has no room for it.

#### Write Island Events Log to Text File (`vv2_island_events`)

Every change an island event makes to a villager is written to a new log, the Island Events log ("Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Island Events\Virtual Villagers 2 Island Events Log 1.txt"): one numbered record per villager it changed, with the event's title as the game shows it, the answer you picked when it asked, and each change as old -> new -- health, age, sickness, pregnancy, head, body, name, likes, dislikes, every skill, parents, custom title, mask and Special villager title, Esteemed Elder and totem -- "Gone" for a villager the event took away, and the sex and age of a villager it brought. What an event changes in the village as a whole -- food, tech points, the coconut trees, fish, the field's protection from birds and the crops, puzzles solved or unsolved -- is one record of its own, a "Village:" list of old -> new, and an event that changes nothing still gets its record, "Changes: none". A villager whose head or body an event changed also gets an "Appearance changed" record naming the event, so the Family Tree Maker knows the old and the new look are the same villager. A branching Custom Island Event from the library (Story / Cheat Upgrades), whose effects come page by page, is ONE record: its title, the answer picked, then every change in page order as "<name>: <change> <old> -> <new>"; at every save during it the log already holds the entry so far, and later pages continue that same entry, across a quit too, nothing twice. The records are written when the game saves, like the other logs. **Needs Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File: that patch's DLL writes the records.**

**Needs Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File on for the Island Events log, which that patch's DLL writes (without it nothing is written).**

- Behavior changes: When an island event runs, every villager is copied just before the game applies it and compared just after; each difference is one line of the villager's "Island event <n>" record. The village's food, tech points, food stores, puzzles and (where the game has one) weather are read just before and just after too; what changed is one "Island event <n>" record with a "Village:" list, and an event that changes nothing is one record ending "Changes: none". A villager the event brings is named with its sex and its age, in game units and years ("Age: 340 (17 years old)"). A head or body change is also an "Appearance changed" record in the Births and Conceptions log, ending "Changed by: <event> (island event)". A new village gets its Island Events log when it is made, like the other logs. A branching Custom Island Event (Story / Cheat Upgrades, story_graph.inc) brackets each page's own effects through this comparison (VvfpIslandEventsGraphBegin / End) and hands the event's one entry so far to the log after each page (VvfpIslandEventsGraphWrite -> the Parentage Export's WriteVillageEventEntry): "Event:", "Choice:", then each change as "<name>: <Label> <old> -> <new>" in page order. Its held record is replaced each time and each save writes what it has gained onto the same entry, append-only (a numbered first part left open, then only new lines, or a marked "(continued) Island event <n>" when another record came between), closed when the event is over; the game's own bracket around its popups writes nothing for them (VvfpStoryGraphLogged).
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion detours the routines' first instructions at run time, after verifying them, and installs nothing if any differs. The game's own routine runs unchanged, with the same registers and stack; the events, their odds and their effects are the game's own. Nothing is written without Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static exact-build verification of the event routines and the villager records in each executable; live-tested per game before release
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Write Village Statistics to Text File (`vv2_write_village_statistics`)

After each successful save of slots 1 through 5, writes the save's local lifetime statistics to 'Village Statistics v2 - Save N.txt' in the save slot's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Village Statistics' folder beside the game's saves (an earlier 'Village Statistics - Save N.txt' is kept unchanged). Counts the game does not keep are stored in per-save .dat files in each save's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save N\Data' folder. Later games retain the inherited per-save statistics block even where no Statistics screen is reachable; omitted stock bookkeeping is restored by exact gameplay hooks. Puzzle totals are read from the current save state during export so existing saves are reported accurately. These files are checked against what the save and the patcher's own logs prove -- Villagers Buried below the Deaths log's burials or the graves, Twins Birthed below the Births log's twin pregnancies -- and are changed only when the player says so -- Repair Saves & Logs in the patcher window, or Repair when the game asks as it closes (with "Check logs automatically" on, and only if something is wrong); nothing is ever asked while the village is played. Each file is backed up first (a copy '<file>.before-v1.35.58-repair' in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Data\Copies Made Before Repairs', at the file's own place), every change is listed in the Repairs log ('Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Repairs Made'; the shared 'Repairs Made' or 'Repairs' folder an older version made is kept as it was: nothing is moved), and a count is only ever raised and an elder never removed. The original save result is preserved, and text-export failure does not turn a successful game save into a failure. Start Over wipes everything the Fun Patcher kept for that save: all its logs (the Village History too), all its data (ElderTotems.dat too) and its family tree files. It keeps Backups, Copies Made Before Repairs and exported family tree pictures. Other saves are not touched.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File for the village and savegame header at the top of the log, and for creating the log at a village's first save -- a new village, or one restarted with Start Over -- before anything is recorded (without either, records are still written correctly, just unlabelled, and the log first appears with its first record; Cause of Death names the village at each save itself).**

- Behavior changes: After each successful save of slots 1 through 5, writes the save's local lifetime statistics to 'Village Statistics v2 - Save N.txt' in the save slot's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Village Statistics' folder beside the game's saves (an earlier 'Village Statistics - Save N.txt' is kept unchanged). Counts the game does not keep are stored in per-save .dat files in each save's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save N\Data' folder. Later games retain the inherited per-save statistics block even where no Statistics screen is reachable; omitted stock bookkeeping is restored by exact gameplay hooks. Puzzle totals are read from the current save state during export so existing saves are reported accurately. These files are checked against what the save and the patcher's own logs prove -- Villagers Buried below the Deaths log's burials or the graves, Twins Birthed below the Births log's twin pregnancies -- and are changed only when the player says so -- Repair Saves & Logs in the patcher window, or Repair when the game asks as it closes (with "Check logs automatically" on, and only if something is wrong); nothing is ever asked while the village is played. Each file is backed up first (a copy '<file>.before-v1.35.58-repair' in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Data\Copies Made Before Repairs', at the file's own place), every change is listed in the Repairs log ('Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Repairs Made'; the shared 'Repairs Made' or 'Repairs' folder an older version made is kept as it was: nothing is moved), and a count is only ever raised and an elder never removed. The original save result is preserved, and text-export failure does not turn a successful game save into a failure. Start Over wipes everything the Fun Patcher kept for that save: all its logs (the Village History too), all its data (ElderTotems.dat too) and its family tree files. It keeps Backups, Copies Made Before Repairs and exported family tree pictures. Other saves are not touched.

## Virtual Villagers - The Secret City

### Automatic population and safety changes

Supported stock identity is the exact `Virtual Villagers - The Secret City.exe` build recorded in `data/builds.json`. The automatic edits are the selected population mode plus 22 guarded safety edits. The modified output retains the untouched stock executable beside the modified executable. Stock modes preserve vanilla save format; expanded modes use the documented guarded compatibility/conversion path.

### Optional features

#### 2-10x Sickness (`vv3_sickness_multiplier`)

**Needs no other patch.** Makes the game harder; off by default. Villagers fall sick 2 to 10 times as often as they would: you choose how many times with the 2-10x Sickness slider in the patcher window (a whole number, 2 unless you move it). Every natural chance of falling sick is multiplied, at every Medicine level and difficulty, the old villagers' extra chance included, and it stacks with the other patches. Medicine, the fire, Easy's cures, healers, island events and everything that cures are unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The natural sickness roll's four moduli (Medicine 1, 2, 3 and the old villagers' roll) become round(stock / N), N the slider (2 to 10): each chance about N times as large.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The roll's thresholds, Medicine, the fire, the difficulty, Easy's cures, healers, events, the Hospital and every other health rule are unchanged; four immediates in place, written when the build is published.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; every multiplier on every site, stock and with Sickness works like VV1-3, is checked in tests/test_sickness_patches.py; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### 2-10x Tech Cost (`vv3_tech_cost_multiplier`)

Every technology level on the Tech screen costs 2 to 10 times its normal price in tech points: you choose the multiplier with the 2-10x Tech Cost slider in the patcher window (a whole number, 3 unless you move it). The normal prices are: Science level 2 11,000, level 3 150,000; Medicine level 2 8,000, level 3 75,000; Alchemy level 2 5,000, level 3 55,000; Restoration level 2 7,000, level 3 85,000; Leadership level 2 7,000, level 3 125,000; Nature level 1 4,500, level 2 50,000, level 3 150,000; Magic level 1 4,500, level 2 50,000, level 3 150,000. At x 3, for example, a 5,000-point level costs 15,000. The Tech screen shows the multiplied price, a purchase is refused (and nothing is spent) with fewer tech points than that, and buying takes exactly that many. The two factions, Nature and Magic, are technologies too: choosing one costs that many times as much. Research, tech points from anywhere else, every other tech-point cost (such as clothes) and the patcher's own upgrades are unchanged. The higher you set it, the harder the game. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: Every non-zero entry of the technology price table 0x4A818C, x N (the slider, 2 to 10; 3 by default). Its only reader is the getter 0x427020, called by the Tech screen's hover label, information box and purchase (0x464C84, 0x464E47, 0x465706): the shown price, the purchase's refusal threshold and the amount it takes are the same multiplied number.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: Each price is changed in place, same length; no code is added and no executable space is claimed. Research, tech points from island events and duplicate collectibles, every other tech-point cost (such as 5,000 for clothes) and the patcher's Origins and Story / Cheat upgrades keep their stock numbers.

#### 256 Villagers (Experimental) (`vv3_population_256`)

EXPERIMENTAL. Gives The Secret City 256 villager slots (0 to 255) instead of 150. The game's villager table is moved to a new, larger place in memory and every part of the game that walks it -- births, island events, the Villager Details screen, saving and loading -- is widened to match. With Collection Progression Max Pop the cap becomes 221 plus the collection and Magic Level 3 bonuses (256 with everything); with Immediate Fixed Max Pop it is 256 at once; with No Population Increase the stock cap of 125 is unchanged, only the table is larger. The patched game is named "... - Modded 256" and keeps its saves, and the patcher's logs, in their own "Virtual Villagers - The Secret City - Modded 256" folder, so they never mix with 150-slot saves. The patcher does not copy saves into it: copy your save files from the "... - Modded" save folder yourself. An old save loads with all its villagers; the first time the game saves it, it is written in the longer 256 format, which only a 256 build can open, so keep the originals as a backup. **Needs Fix Vanilla Bugs on (it is on by default) to load a village that the base game's exactly-150-villager save bug has already damaged.** Off by default.

**Needs Fix Vanilla Bugs on for loading a village that the base game's exactly-150-villager save bug has already damaged (without it such a village does not load).**

- Behavior changes: The villager table has 256 slots; the population modes that raise the cap reach 256. Saves hold up to 256 villagers in a longer save file that only this build reads.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No Population Increase keeps the stock cap of 125. Nothing changes for a build that does not tick this patch.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static exact-build implementation with emulation of the replaced routines; live-tested with the game driven through its memory (an old save upgraded, filled to 256, triplets born into slots 200, 253 and 254 and a baby into slot 255, saved and reloaded); a hands-on live pass is pending
- Guarded executable edits: 570; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.
- Automatic safety edits: replaced, in every population mode, by its own 22 guarded safety edits for the 256-slot table.
- Population-mode edits: replaced by its own guarded rows, stock=0, collection_progression=1, immediate_fixed=1; only the selected mode's rows are applied.
- Guarded rewrites inside other selected patches' own code, applied only when that patch is also selected: Enable Origins-Exclusive Features (`vv3_enable_origins_exclusive_features`) 7, Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File (`vv3_write_parentage_log`) 2, Everyone Tries On the Robe (`vv3_everyone_tries_on_robe`) 3; each pattern must occur exactly that many times in the bytes that patch wrote, or nothing is written.
- Appends 4096 bytes of code (one page per population mode) as the new PE section `.vv256` at 0x7F0000, mapped as 0x23E000 bytes whose remainder is zero-fill for the relocated villager table, the Details list and the save buffers; when the image ends before 0x7F0000, a zero-fill `.vv256z` section maps the gap. It rewrites 3 guarded regions of the PE headers to map them: the new section headers (40 bytes each), NumberOfSections and SizeOfImage. The appended bytes and every header change carry an exact before/after guard.

#### All Fruit Trees Refill at the Same Time (`vv3_fruit_trees_refill_together`)

All the fruit trees refill at the same moment. In the stock game each tree has its own refill clock, started when it was planted, so the trees refill at different times. With this patch they share one: when the first tree is due to refill, every tree refills with it (a tree that was not due yet gets less fruit that once, for the shorter time), and from then on they refill together. A newly planted tree joins the others' schedule at their next refill. Each tree gets the stock amount of fruit for the time since its own last refill -- the game's own formula, with Nature level 1's bonus and "Nature Level 1 Actually Replenishes Food Sources Faster" when it is ticked -- so over time every tree gives exactly as much fruit as in the stock game; only when the fruit comes changes. A newly planted tree still starts full and is still ready to pick after 8 hours. The island event that refills the trees is unchanged, and catch-up (the time that passes while the game is closed) and Time Warp pay the same fruit as the stock game. The save keeps every tree's own stock refill time, so without this patch the trees simply go back to their own times, with nothing lost; the patch's schedule is kept in its own file in the save's folder (Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <S>\Data\Fruit Trees\Virtual Villagers 3 Fruit Tree Timers - Save <S>.dat) and Start Over deletes it. **With "All Fruit Trees Refill to Full" ticked too, each of this patch's refills fills the tree to 1,000 instead of adding the stock amount (a tree that refills early is filled early).** **Cannot be ticked together with "Fruit Trees Take Turns Refilling": the two give the trees different schedules, so tick only one; with both ticked the patcher builds nothing.** **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.** This patch needs no other row. It is on by default for The Secret City (Owner's Defaults ticks "Fruit Trees Take Turns Refilling" instead); untick it to keep the stock game. The companion is "VVFP VV3 Trees Refill Together.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock game runs.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The fruit trees' update 0x434760 (vtable 0x49D1D0 slot 8, run by the world objects' update 0x435880, live and after catch-up and Time Warp): its refill loop (0x43478A..0x43481A) is replaced by the companion's pass, which goes on to the stock tail at 0x43481B (the planting-puzzle check and the removal of dead trees, 0x43487F, unchanged). The pass keeps every tree's own stock timer (record +0x28) exactly as the stock loop moves it -- set to now whenever it is at least the interval old -- so the save holds the timers the game without this patch would hold. The fruit follows the patch's schedule: each tree has the time its fruit is paid up to and the moment of its next refill. At that moment it gains floor((now - paid up to) x factor / 3600), the stock formula with the stock factor (37, or the immediate at 0x4347CE at Nature 1 or more: 42, or 56 with the Nature patch), and both move on (paid up to = now, next = now + the interval: 10,800 s, or 8,100 s at Nature 1 or more with the Nature patch, whose test at 0x4347AA the companion recognises). Every tree's fruit is held to 1,000 on every pass, as the stock loop does. With "All Fruit Trees Refill to Full" (vv3_fruit_trees_refill_to_full) the 7 bytes at 0x4347EB are its mov eax,0x3E8 / nop / nop instead of the stock add, and the companion then sets the tree's fruit to 1,000 at each refill instead of adding the stock share. A tree the companion has not seen (newly planted, or every tree of a save without a matching entry) starts from its own stock timer and joins the schedule; a removed tree leaves it (trees are matched by position, planted time and kind, so the list closing up does not mix them). Saving (0x433EC0, before the stock saver): the schedule is written to "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <S>\Data\Fruit Trees\Virtual Villagers 3 Fruit Tree Timers - Save <S>.dat" with an FNV-1a 64 fingerprint of the trees' saved bytes (header, records, count), the last 16 saves kept, written atomically (a temporary file moved over it). Loading (0x433E40, after the stock loader): only the entry written with exactly these trees by this same patch is used; otherwise every tree starts from its stock timer. After every change the trees' next refills are laid out together: the earliest keeps its moment and every other tree's next refill is moved to it, so all refill in the same pass.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the companion verifies the stock bytes at its three sites (0x43478A, 0x433E40, 0x433EC0) and that the interval test and factors are the stock ones or the Nature patch's exactly and the refill's add (0x4347EB) the stock one or All Fruit Trees Refill to Full's exactly, and writes its detours at run time, all together or none; a different build of the game installs nothing. The save is stock: the trees' records, their stock timers included, are written by the stock saver; without the companion the stock loop continues from those timers. No tree earns fruit faster than the stock rate: the amount is the stock formula for the time since its own last refill (or, with All Fruit Trees Refill to Full, the tree filled to 1,000, as that patch's own refill does), and the 1,000 cap is unchanged. Planting (0x4349FD), the 8-hour growth (0x434030), the pickable checks, the island event refill (0x415AD0) and the fruit job are unchanged. Nothing is written to a villager record.
- Dependencies: none

#### All Fruit Trees Refill to Full (`vv3_fruit_trees_refill_to_full`)

Every fruit tree refill fills the tree to 1,000 fruit, instead of adding the stock share for the time since its last refill (111 fruit every 3 hours, 126 at Nature level 1 or more). The refill times are unchanged: a tree still refills 3 hours after its last refill (2 hours 15 minutes at Nature level 1 or more with "Nature Level 1 Actually Replenishes Food Sources Faster"), and after time away (catch-up or Time Warp) its next refill fills it too. **Works with "All Fruit Trees Refill at the Same Time" and "Fruit Trees Take Turns Refilling": their refills fill the trees to 1,000 too, on their own schedule (so a tree that refills early with the others is filled early).** Planting, the 8 hours before a new tree can be picked, picking, "Fruit Counts When It Reaches the Food Bin" and the island event that fills the trees are unchanged; the honey is not affected. Nothing new is saved, so without this patch the trees simply go back to the stock refills. Off by default; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The fruit trees' refill (0x434760, vtable 0x49D1D0 slot 8, run every frame by the world objects' update 0x435880, live and after catch-up and Time Warp): once a tree's timer is at least the interval old (0x2A30 = 10,800 game seconds; 8,100 at Nature 1 or more with vv3_nature_honey_refill, whose test at 0x4347AA jumps to its cave and back to 0x4347B7), the stock code computes floor((now - timer) x factor / 3600) in edx (0x4347DC..0x4347E9) and adds it to the tree's fruit (0x4347EB mov eax,[edi] / 0x4347ED shr edx,0xB / 0x4347F0 add eax,edx). Those 7 bytes become mov eax,0x3E8 and two NOPs, so the store at 0x4347F7 sets the fruit to 1,000; the timer is set to now (0x4347FE) and the stock 1,000 cap (0x434801) runs as before. "All Fruit Trees Refill at the Same Time" and "Fruit Trees Take Turns Refilling" replace the loop (0x43478A..0x43481A) with their companion's pass: the companion reads the 7 bytes at 0x4347EB and, when they are this patch's, fills each tree to 1,000 at its refill instead of adding the stock share.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The refill interval and its test (0x4347AA), the Nature factor immediates (0x4347BE, 0x4347CD), the timer update, the cap, planting (0x4349FD), the 8-hour growth (0x434030), the pickable checks, picking, the island event that fills grown trees (0x415AD0), the honey (0x4319B0) and the save format are unchanged. Nothing is written to a villager record or to the save beyond the stock fields the stock code writes.

#### Birth Control (`vv3_birth_control`)

Requires BOTH parenting skill and the checked preference before a villager will initiate Embracing. The native chooser's score floor remains in force and the scanned candidate stays in the stock internal-age 360..999 range, but the 25% non-preference fallback is removed: a roll that admitted one unchecked villager in four is the reported leak. The initiating villager has no extra upper-age rejection. Birth Control owns only the five ordinary initiator checks; the native manual category-1 carrier gate, conception, pregnancy, and delivery remain separate, while automatic physical-capacity safety applies in every public mode.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The five repeated candidate-selector blocks at file offsets 0x5CE74, 0x5CF35, 0x5CFFC, 0x5D0C0, and 0x5D187 retain each candidate's stock age<1000 check while removing only the initiator's duplicate age<1000 check. The chooser at 0x459730 no longer rolls RNG(100) for a villager whose parenting preference is unchecked. File offset 0x59890 replaces that roll with a jump to the routine's own reject epilogue at 0x4598B8. Stock tests the selected category at 0x459883 (cmp edi,1 / jne 0x4598AF) before this point, so Farming, Building, Research and Healing leave the routine with their selection intact and never reach the patched bytes. The ordinary action-13 autonomous/catch-up route therefore follows the VV4 reference boundary: the scanned candidate is capped at internal age 999, but the initiating villager has no male or female upper-age ceiling in this selector.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The native VV3 manual pairing handler at VA 0x4584B0 retains its category-1 carrier/female-only internal-age-1000 rejection for both participants. The native VV4/VV5-style chooser score floor, action selection, preference scoring, conception roll/writer, pending delivery, save format, RNG, health, fertility, messages, and statistics are unchanged by Birth Control; automatic physical-capacity safety remains separately owned and applies in every public mode. The 25% non-preference fallback is NOT among them: it is removed by this feature, and only for the Parenting category, which stock selects before the patched roll is reachable. Direct event-created births, Island Events, clone paths, and every route outside the ordinary action-13 mate selector are unchanged by Birth Control; automatic physical-capacity safety separately guards their physical allocation in every public mode.

#### Both Factions: Nature and Magic (`vv3_both_factions`)

Lets a tribe own BOTH the Faction of Nature and the Faction of Magic. Buy one faction on the Tech screen as usual, then click the other: instead of "You have already chosen your faction!" it is bought at its Tech screen price in tech points (its normal price, times the multiplier with the patcher's 2-10x Tech Cost). Buying level 1 of either faction asks Yes/No: "With the power of the Fun Patcher, you can now embrace both Nature and Magic Factions. Use this gift wisely." (No buys nothing); levels 2 and 3 are bought without a question, as before, and both Buy buttons stay as they always are. With both: every level of each works at the same time -- Nature's faster food refills (with the patcher's Nature Level 1 honey and fruit refill row), the Pitcher Plant and longer lives (with the patcher's Nature Level 3 row), and Magic's extra tech point from research, the Berry Plant and the population bonus (+10; the maximum stays 150, or 256 with 256 Villagers, and Immediate Fixed keeps its fixed maximum). Both herbs grow on the island and can be gathered and brewed. Both faction columns are lit on the Tech screen with their own floating petals and sparkles. Seven new potions need a Pitcher Plant and a Berry Plant together, with a Tiger Lily (a fun potion), Cactus (a trance), Lotus (crazy talk), Black Orchid (paralysis), Rose (lonely), a second Pitcher Plant (whoa!, the drinker moves) or a second Berry Plant (something smells yummy: free children under 14 run to the pot); they count toward "Alchemy R Us" and Stews Found. The sharks: the latest shark potion decides how they look -- Nature's stink bomb makes them go, Magic's Shark Charmer Vial brings them back charmed and sparkling -- and nothing else changes (the puzzle, its message and reward stay once). Save safety: the faction bought first stays in the save exactly as the unpatched game keeps it; the second, and which new potions were brewed, are kept in the save's own file (Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <S>\Data\Factions\Virtual Villagers 3 Second Faction - Save <S>.dat), so every save loads in the unpatched game (with the first faction only; putting the patch back brings the second back). Start Over deletes the file. **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.** **Needs no other patch.** It is on by default for The Secret City; untick it to keep the stock game. The companion is "VVFP VV3 Both Factions.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock game runs.

#### Builders and Healers Work First (`vv3_builders_and_healers_work_first`)

Builders and healers are more likely to do their own work first, at any food level -- about three times in four each time the game chooses what they do; the rest of the time the game chooses exactly as it always has, and the one roll is shared with Builders Fix Huts When Idle, so a choice is either all patched or all stock. When it steps in: whenever the game looks for something for a villager whose selected job is Building to do, it first tries building work (a project, or fixing a hut) while not every population hut is built -- and, in A New Home and The Lost Children below Building level 3, whenever any hut is built; for one whose selected job is Healing it always first tries healing and study, whenever there is a patient or they can study medicine (**in The Secret City, only once Medicine 2 has been researched**). This comes before idling, farming or gathering. When there is nothing of their own to do, they do whatever the game would have had them do. This also applies during catch-up -- the time that passes while the game is closed, and Time Warp: each time catch-up chooses work for a builder or healer, about three times in four they are first given their own job (a builder only while it has hut work, as above), so they keep gaining skill while you are away; the rest of the time, and whenever there is nothing of theirs to do, catch-up's own choice stands. Villagers with any other job are untouched. Catch-up's low-food rule still wins: at 250 food or less a villager with Farming 20 or more farms, whatever their job. An addendum to Builders Fix Huts When Idle. **Requires Builders Fix Huts When Idle**, whose DLL loads this one (in The Secret City, whose stub does); ticking this ticks it, and it brings with it the Origins-exclusive base, which adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens.

**Requires Builders Fix Huts When Idle: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this.**

- Behavior changes: Whenever the adult scheduler asks the work dispatcher to start a job for a villager whose selected job is Healing (job 2), or Building (job 4) while it has hut work (a population hut unbuilt, or in A New Home and The Lost Children below Building level 3 any hut built), the dispatcher is first asked for that villager's own job; if that starts something the scheduler sees it started, and if there is nothing of theirs to do the scheduler's own request runs unchanged. At any food level; at 250 food or less in The Secret City, The Tree of Life and New Believers this includes the scheduler's farming attempt. About three times in four, not always: the companion asks the decision's roll that Builders Fix Huts When Idle draws once per choice of the idle scheduler (VvfpFixHutsRoll, handed over through VvfpWorkFirstSetRoll, or looked up by module name in The Secret City); when it fails, the scheduler's own request runs alone, exactly as the stock game. Catch-up (time passed while the game was closed, and Time Warp) never runs the idle scheduler: the catch-up worker (0x45BF00) dispatches the stock picker's job itself. Its pick dispatch (0x45BFC0, returning to 0x45BFC5) is treated as the scheduler's calls are -- own job first, then the pick -- and its research pick (job 1), which never reaches the dispatcher, is tested at 0x45BF52: for a builder or healer the own job is dispatched first and, if it starts something, the worker's own finish (its queue processor) runs instead of the stock research step. One 75% roll per catch-up decision: Builders Fix Huts When Idle wraps the worker as one decision, so VvfpFixHutsRoll gives every patch that decision reaches the same roll; when it fails, or there is nothing of theirs to do, the worker's stock code runs. At 250 food or less a healer's pick is also dispatched at once instead of waiting behind a farming attempt, as Builders Fix Huts When Idle already does for builders.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: The Secret City's hooks are the dispatcher stub and the catch-up research-pick stub (0x45BF52) that Builders Fix Huts When Idle places in the page Origins appends, each of which resolves this DLL's VvfpWorkFirstFirst itself -- so the research pick is covered from the first catch-up decision, before any dispatch; without this row the DLL is not shipped and the stubs run the stock code. A builder or healer with nothing of their own to do does whatever the stock scheduler chose (farming, research, ...); the younger villagers' routine, every other caller of the dispatcher and every other selected job are untouched. A builder is put first only while it has hut work (a hut unbuilt, or in A New Home and The Lost Children below Building level 3 any hut built); a healer always. What the work does -- which project, which hut, which patient or study -- is the game's own dispatcher's choice. In catch-up, the worker's low-food Farming dispatch (0x45BFAB: 250 food or less and Farming 20 or more) is not one of the calls the hook acts on, so Farming wins exactly as in the stock game. Nothing is written to a villager record, the save or any file.

#### Builders Fix Huts When Idle (`vv3_builders_fix_huts`)

Builders fix huts when no building projects are present, and build first. This makes builders more likely to do their building work, not certain: each time the game chooses what a builder does, the patch steps in about three times in four, and the rest of the time the game chooses exactly as it always has. A villager whose job checkmark on the Villager Details screen is not Building (any other job, or none) but whom the game gives building work anyway gets all of this only on 14% of those choices; otherwise the game chooses exactly as it always has. When it steps in, construction always comes first -- a builder goes straight into a new hut or building project the game would let it build, even when the game's own random roll would have skipped it this time, and never fixes a hut while there is one. When no building project is available to be worked on and at least one population hut stands -- while another is unbuilt, and below Building level 3 even once every one is built -- a builder with nothing to do examines and fixes one of the huts that already stands, the game's own "Examining hut" / "Fixing hut" job, which trains Building. It only makes that job able to be chosen autonomously; the job itself, its chance of a repair and its skill roll are the game's own. Whenever there is hut work to do, a builder also does this regardless of the food supply: plentiful food no longer skips the builder's work attempt (A New Home, The Lost Children), and scarce food no longer sends the builder to farm or gather first (The Secret City, The Tree of Life, New Believers). Builders and Healers Work First uses the same roll when selected with it, so one choice is either all patched or all stock. The food bypass acts only while you play. During catch-up (time passing while the game was closed, and Time Warp) each villager does the job the stock game picks, and when that job is building, the same build-first and hut-fixing rules apply. **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. That base's companion loads this patch's DLL (in The Secret City, a small stub in the page the base appends does); if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock scheduler runs unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked; the Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically. Needed by Builders and Healers Work First: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: When the Building dispatcher finds no project to work on (every project check has failed) and at least one population hut is complete while another is not, the companion picks a random complete hut and starts the game's own 'Examining hut' job for it, in live play and in catch-up alike. Whenever a builder has hut work to do, its work attempt no longer depends on the food supply: at 250 food or less a picked Building job is dispatched at once instead of waiting behind a farming attempt and a 50% swap for a food action. Every other villager keeps the stock food behaviour. Construction always comes first: the stock 'fix a hut' option is taken out of any option list that also holds a hut to build or a project, so a builder fixes a hut only when there is no construction to choose. The Secret City's Building branch has no random roll that skips construction, so there is nothing to go straight into. Every change above happens about three times in four, not always: each time the game's idle scheduler chooses what a villager does (one run of 0x45BFE0, including the choose-the-next-job routine's retries of it for the same villager (0x45C388, up to ten)), one 75% roll from the companion's own generator -- never the game's random numbers -- decides whether the patches step in. If it passes, they act together; if it fails, every patched place runs the stock code for that choice, exactly as the unpatched game. The roll is drawn the first time a patched place asks and shared by every patch the choice reaches -- Builders and Healers Work First included. Catch-up -- time that passed while the game was closed, and Time Warp -- never runs the idle scheduler; its worker (0x45BF00) makes the choice instead, and one run of it is one decision too: the patches it reaches (this one's sites in the Building dispatcher, Builders and Healers Work First) share one 75% roll, never one each. Not checked on the job: everything this companion makes a villager do trains Building -- construction first and the hut fix inside the Building dispatcher; and the low-food bypass, which sends a builder or (with Builders and Healers Work First) a healer straight to their pick, asks the same of the picked job, Building or Healing -- and the dispatcher is reached for anyone the game gives that job. For a villager whose job preference (record + 0xEC0, Building 4, Healing 2; 0 or -1 is no checkmark) is not that job, the companion acts only when, after the decision's roll passes, one more roll of its own passes 14 times in 100 (NOT_PREFERRED_PERCENT, drawn once per decision like the decision's roll): about 10.5% of such decisions instead of 75%. A failed roll is the stock game's choice. A villager checked on the job is unchanged. 14 is the later games' own figure: their job chooser keeps a villager's checked job 86 times in 100.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The Secret City's row diverts one eight-byte test in the Building dispatcher, one nine-byte test in the idle scheduler's low-food path, the work dispatcher's ten-byte entry, the idle scheduler's six-byte entry, the catch-up worker's six-byte entry and its five-byte research-pick test into six stubs in the page Origins appends; each resolves its companion once and otherwise replays the stock bytes, so with the DLL missing the stock scheduler runs. The dispatcher and research-pick stubs serve the Builders and Healers Work First addendum and do nothing unless "VVFP Work First.dll" is shipped. Nothing about the examine/fix job itself changes: its route, its 70% repair chance, its Building practice roll and its messages are the game's own. A builder with a project available still takes the project. With no population hut built there is nothing to fix. With every hut built and no construction available, at Building level 3 or above (and in The Secret City, The Tree of Life and New Believers at any level) the hut choice is the stock fix-a-hut option; below level 3 in A New Home and The Lost Children a built population hut is fixed directly (never The Lost Children's building 5). Nothing is written to a villager record, the save or any file.

#### Checked Skill Preferences are listed as Jobs on Graves (`vv3_preferred_job_graves`)

A grave's Job line names the skill the villager had checked as their skill preference on the Villager Details screen (the one the game itself shows as their job there), with that skill's rank: "Untrained" below 20, else "Trainee", "Adept" or "Master" by the game's own values (and "Apprentice" for a child under 14 where Children's Graves Say Apprentice or the game does it). With no preference checked the grave shows the highest skill, as before. The epitaph follows the same job. Titles still win: the Tribal Chief still gets "Wise and Beloved Chief", an Esteemed Elder "Esteemed Elder", and a child the children's epitaphs. Only graves made from now on change; for older graves, Repair Saves & Logs rewrites the grave and its Deaths log lines where the save still holds the villager's preference at death. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

The epitaph is picked from that job.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The shared best-skill routine is not touched (its other callers, the Nursery lesson among them, are unchanged); only the burial writer's block is recoded in place, same length, no executable space claimed. Titles and the children's epitaphs are chosen before the job as stock; a grave already made is never changed by the exe (Repair Saves & Logs does it where the preference at death is known).

#### Copy and Paste in Text Boxes (`vv3_copy_paste`)

Lets you copy and paste in the game's text boxes (the tribe name when a new village starts and the villager names on the Details screen, and every other box you type in). While a box has typing focus: Ctrl+V or Shift+Insert pastes the text on the Windows clipboard where you type (the boxes have no movable caret, so at the end of the text); Ctrl+C or Ctrl+Insert copies the box's whole text; Ctrl+X cuts it (copies it, then empties the box). Pasted text keeps the box's own rules: its own character filter (a numbers-only box takes only digits), and its own length limit, cut before the first character that does not fit, never inside a character. Line breaks and tabs become spaces; other control characters are dropped, and so is every character the game cannot show (never turned into '?'): **with Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts or Use Unicode Font on, every character those patches let you type is pasted (at least every Windows-1252 character: accented letters, curly quotes, €, ...); with neither, plain English letters, digits and signs only.** The keys never reach the game as letters or shortcuts. Ctrl+A does nothing: the game's boxes have no selection. When the clipboard is busy or holds no text, nothing happens. **On by default.** **Needs no other patch; works with or without Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts and Use Unicode Font.** **Not yet seen in a running game** (checked by emulation of each stock executable). The companion is "VVFP Copy and Paste.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; saves are never written by it.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The event pump's SDL_KEYDOWN case (0x404286) first asks the companion about the key: Ctrl+V, Shift+Insert, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Insert and Ctrl+X (no Alt, no Windows key), while a text box has typing focus, are handled and the pump goes on with the next event; every other key, and these keys while no box has focus, go on to the stock case exactly as before. The focused box is found the way the game types into it: the game's own keyboard listeners (event manager 0x4B3088), in the game's order, the first whose keyboard handler is the text box's (0x40D4A0) that has focus ([box+0x25]) on a screen that takes input. Paste: the clipboard's CF_UNICODETEXT, composed (NFC) and split into whole characters, CR/LF/Tab as spaces, other control characters and lone surrogates dropped, each character turned into the box's bytes (UTF-8 when the loaded Unicode companion -- VVFP Unicode Text.dll, else VVFP Unicode Font.dll -- answers VvfpGlyphsUtf8() == 1; every printable Windows-1252 character when it answers 0; printable ASCII when neither is loaded), a character the game cannot show dropped, a numbers-only box's filter applied, and the whole cut before the first character that does not fit the box's byte limit ([box+0x28]). UTF-8 text goes in through that companion's VvfpBoxInsertUtf8 (it inserts as typing does); otherwise the bytes are typed into the box through its own handler, one character message each. Copy: the box's text bytes, read back by the same rule, put on the clipboard as CF_UNICODETEXT; Cut: the same, then (only when the copy succeeded) the box's own Backspace for each byte.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces the SDL_KEYDOWN case's first ten bytes at run time, only after verifying their stock bytes, and installs nothing on a different build. Nothing is written but a focused box's text, through the box's own handler and its own rules: opening and closing a box without these keys leaves its bytes exactly as they were. Saves, villager records and the patcher's files are never written. The clipboard is opened and closed on the game thread and never waited for; busy or empty means nothing happens. A fault is abandoned and the key goes on to the stock code. The SDL_TEXTINPUT case (detoured by Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts) is not touched; both patches work together or alone.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending

#### Everyone Tries On the Robe (`vv3_everyone_tries_on_robe`)

Dropping an active, living, non-nursing villager on the robe interrupts every other active, living, non-nursing villager and sends them to try on the robe too. Each villager receives the complete base-game success or failed-fit result, and the base game alone decides who becomes Tribal Chief.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: After the stock callback handles the dropped villager, every other active, living, non-nursing VV3 villager is interrupted into the robe action through the game's own action dispatcher, so they stop their current task and walk to the amphitheatre. The runtime loop accepts only the authenticated stock bounds 150 and 256.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: Dead, inactive, and nursing villagers are skipped. The unchanged stock callback remains responsible for success/failure, Chief clothing, Chief state, puzzle mutation, and candidate selection for every villager. The wrapper READS two candidate fields and writes neither: +0xE80 (the chief flag) so the ceremony is skipped entirely while the village already has a chief, and +0xE88 so each villager receives the same one of the two robe actions the stock code would have given it. The wrapper does not write +0xE80 or +0xE88, and does not change pregnancy/nursing state, health, age, skills, preferences, or saved record layout. It calls three stock routines per villager -- 0x460F70 to stop the villager's current work, 0x4611B0 to set the amphitheatre destination, and 0x455570 to assign the robe action -- which is the same sequence the game performs for a villager the player drops on the robe.
- Dependencies: none

#### Fix Vanilla Bugs (`vv3_fix_vanilla_bugs`)

Fixes bugs in the base game. The Royal Jelly: the dark vial now cures the villager's cold and raises their Healing, and the clear vial (whose text says the jelly turned bitter) changes nothing, so each vial does what its own text says. The Mysterious Vial (amber): the "flash of scientific insight" result now also gives the tribe 100 tech points, as its text promises, as well as the villager's Research gain. The Mysterious Vial (quartz): a villager who is exactly 14 now gets the text of what really happens to them (becoming an elder) instead of the text about becoming a little child. A village with exactly 150 villagers can be saved and loaded again: the base game, when it saves a full list of 150 villagers, writes past the end of that list and damages the next part of the save, so the village refused to load; now all 150 are kept and the village loads, and a village already saved that way is repaired when it is loaded. Every default name can be chosen: the game numbers its 125 male and 125 female names from 0 but picks a number from 1 (and never the last one), so Akivi and Yapili (male) and Aipi and Zucca (female) could never be given; now every name in each list can come up, for new villagers and twins alike. A "%" in a villager's name can no longer crash the game: the game showed some names by using them as formatting instructions; now it copies them as plain text, and its text boxes no longer accept a typed "%". A like or dislike holding a negative number other than the game's own "none" (-1) is left out of the Details screen instead of being shown as "ants". A villager's name is saved only to the villager it belongs to on the Details screen: the screen remembers which villager it filled the name box for, and Done or the arrows save the box only into that same villager; if the selected villager is not the one the box was filled for, the box is dropped and the right name is shown. A name you type is still saved to the villager shown. Builders build population huts while the game catches up: after a Time Warp, or when the game is opened after time away, the base game had builders work on a hut without walking there, so their work counted only if they already stood on that hut's site and the huts hardly grew; now each builder goes to the hut first, as in The Tree of Life and New Believers, so the work is added to that hut (each try still needs the builder's Building roll, as in the base game). Fixes the hospital tables' broken legs (art by Lorsieab2). Unpausing at a different speed now gives the campfire and the game's other timers the new speed's length, as a speed change while playing does (the base game kept the old one: a fire lit on Fast burned only 10 hours after unpausing on Normal). No crash from a raindrop of no length: the game draws each raindrop as a short line from where it is to where it was, and its line drawer divides by the line's length, so a line whose two ends are the same point stops the game (a divide by zero). A raindrop has no length when it starts at the screen's top left corner before it has moved, which can happen when rain starts. Now such a line is drawn as a single dot, and every other line is drawn exactly as before. Villagers keep what they carry when the way to where they are going is blocked: a villager with a mushroom or a collectible in its hands whose goal could not be reached (the spot was under a building or a tree) gave up the walk, the game dropped the item and it was never credited. Now the game's own route finder is asked for the nearest spot round the goal that it can reach (up to 64 pixels away, nearest first); the villager walks there, puts the item down and it is credited as for any delivery if it is in the right place. Only when no spot can be reached does the walk end as it always did. A villager carrying nothing (or a baby), a goal the game can reach, and every other walk are exactly as before. The Overview Map's water lines up with its riverbeds: the map shows the island at 424/2048 of its size (20.7%), but the game drew every picture on it (the rivers, waterfalls and every frame of their animations, and the rest) at 20%, its scale cut down to a whole percent, so each was too small from its top left corner and the water sat above and to the left of its bed. Now the scale is rounded to the nearest whole percent (21%), so the water fills its riverbeds. The village view is unchanged. A word too wide for its line (a long name or an unbroken word in a translation or a Custom Island Event) no longer freezes the game: the justified paragraph of island events, tips and notices dropped the word and tried it again for ever, and the tips' line fitter cut it into empty lines. Now such a word gets a line of its own, at its full width (wider than its box), and the text goes on; text without such a word is laid out exactly as before ("VVFP Long Words.dll"). **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by 256 Villagers (Experimental) for loading a village that the base game's exactly-150-villager save bug has already damaged (without it such a village does not load).**

- Behavior changes: The Royal Jelly: the dark vial (whose text says the cold is gone) clears the sick flag and adds 15-29 Healing (capped at 100); the clear vial (whose text says the jelly spoiled) changes nothing. The Mysterious Vial (amber), scientific insight: the tribe gains 100 tech points through the game's own tech adder, in addition to the stock 15-44 Research for the villager. The Mysterious Vial (quartz): the result text uses the same age test as the effect, so a villager aged exactly 14 (280 age units) is told they become an elder, which is what happens. Saving a village of exactly 150 villagers keeps all 150 and no longer writes past the saved villager list into the next block of the save; loading reads at most 150 saved villagers; a save already damaged this way (150 villagers, the next block's size 0x2AD stored as 0x200) loads with all 150. A villager's default first name is picked from the whole of the game's male or female list (125 names each): name numbers 0 to 124 instead of 1 to the base game's limit. A villager's name (and in The Lost Children a grave's epitaph and the parents' names) is copied as plain text, never used as a printf format, and every text box refuses a typed "%". Details screen Likes/Dislikes builders: a slot is skipped when it is negative (the stock test was 'equal to -1'); every word index from 0 up is shown exactly as before. Villager Details name box (The Secret City): the screen remembers which villager it filled the box for -- the villager-name pointer (+0xDD4) and a fingerprint: the name's first dword XOR its second, the low byte also XOR the sex byte (+0xDC8), kept in 8 new bytes at the end of the screen object (+0x33C) -- whenever the box is filled (setText 0x40D1A0 (shown 0x46E449, after an arrow 0x46E516)); every write-back (the record lookup 0x45C840 that gives each write-back its destination (arrow 0x46E492, Done 0x46E56D)) goes ahead only when its destination is that same name and that villager still has the same fingerprint, otherwise the box is not saved (the next fill shows the right name). This covers any way the selected record could stop holding the villager shown (two clicks in one frame, a record reused or moved while the screen is open). Population huts during catch-up (a Time Warp, or the time replayed when a village is opened): the hut-building action 0x453990 skips its walk steps while the catch-up flag [world+0x12FB4] is set, and the build-progress step (27, 0x4358B0 -> 0x432680) credits only the hut whose map area the builder stands in, so a builder anywhere else added nothing.  The last walk before the progress step (0x4610D0, step 3 to the chosen hut's area) is now queued in catch-up too, and the catch-up runner turns step 3 into a move (0x45B7D7 -> 0x455EB0), exactly as The Tree of Life and New Believers always do; the skill test before it and every other step are unchanged. The hospital (all three stages: straw beds, mats, sleeping bags) is drawn from Images\vvfp_hospitalFixed.png, the owner's redrawn sheet (art by Lorsieab2), instead of the stock Images\map_hospitalStates.png: the sprite table names the new file. It is the stock sheet with only the lower supply table's legs redrawn (frames 2 and 3; frame 1 is unchanged), same size (1071x280, three 357x280 frames) and format (RGBA PNG). Unpausing at another speed (the pause key or an Options speed button from a paused game): the game clock's set_speed 0x426630, whose branch from a paused clock (0x42669F) took the factor 1, now takes new / the speed before the pause (clock +0x24) applied around the wall clock at the pause (+0x28), exactly as its running branch applies new / old, through the routine's own rescale loop; every timer registered to the clock (the campfire's two among them) therefore gets the new speed's length. Unpausing at the same speed is byte for byte the base game's. Installed at run time by "VVFP Speed Change Timers.dll", which checks the whole routine (0x426630..0x426742), _ftol 0x46EF58 and the 2^32 constant 0x47F510 hold the stock bytes, or installs nothing. The line drawer (0x403D20) no longer divides by zero: a line whose two ends are the same point (2|dx| = 2|dy| = 0) keeps its undivided alpha step and is drawn as the one point; its callers are the rain (0x41F5F0: each drop is a line from its point to its previous point, and the rain initialiser sets a new point (rand(800), rand(600)) but not the previous one, so a drop whose new point is its previous point -- (0, 0) while the previous points are still the zeroed ones -- is a zero-length line until its first rain update). Keep what a villager carries ("VVFP Keep Carried.dll", started by "VVFP Startup.dll"): the route finder's call 0x4237C0 inside the walk step (at 0x458A80) goes to the companion, which asks the game's route finder first, exactly as before. Only when it answers "no route", the villager holds an item (not -1, not 3 the baby), the front step is the walk and another step is queued behind it, the route finder is asked about points on rings of 8, 16, 24, 32, 48 and 64 pixels round the goal (16 directions, nearest first) and the first it can route to becomes the walk's goal (step +4/+8); none: the answer stays "no route" and the stock give-up 0x460F70 (which releases the item with -1 through 0x455F30) runs. (Emulated: a mushroom walked to a blocked spot next to the food area is credited, 6 food.) Overview Map scale (0x46C360: origin (188, 61), scale 424/2048 = 0.20703125): the draw queue's origin routine 0x42E250 (queue 0x58F6F8) and the map's overlay list 0x428EF0 (list 0x582660, called at 0x46C343) turn the scale into the whole percent every picture is drawn at; they cut 20.703 to 20 with _ftol 0x46EF58, and now round it to 21 (push eax; fistp dword [esp]; pop eax: the FPU's round-to-nearest, which pops the value as _ftol does). Positions on the map are unchanged (world x 0.20703125 + 188, y + 61); every sprite, static or animated (each waterfall and river frame), is drawn 21% of its size instead of 20%, 0.30 points from the map's 20.70 instead of 0.70, so its far edges miss the riverbed by less than half as much as before. The village view's scale 1.0 still gives 100. The justified paragraph 0x40A0C0 (every island event, tip and notice body): at 0x40A2DC (`cmp ecx, eax`, deciding whether a line too wide drops its last word) VVFP Long Words.dll keeps a line's only word -- laid out on a line of its own at its full width -- where the stock code dropped it, drew an empty line and tried the same word again for ever; a line of two or more words is decided by the stock compare. The line fit 0x4022F0 (the tips' line loops and the wrapped-height measures): at 0x402425 (`cmp byte [esi], ' '`, where a line too wide backs off to its last space) a line with no space keeps its letters and takes the rest of the word (to the next space, line break or end, within the caller's letter limit less one), where the stock code backed off to nothing and returned one letter on, so the word lost its letters one empty line each until the rest fitted; a line with a space backs off as before.

No villager record layout is changed; saves with 0 to 149 villagers are written and read exactly as before, and the save file's size and format are unchanged. Turned off, the game draws the stock sheet again. #### Fruit Counts When It Reaches the Food Bin (`vv3_fruit_harvested_at_food_bin`)

Fruit picking works like honey gathering: the fruit leaves the tree, and the village gains its food, only when the villager puts it in the food bin. In the stock game both happened the moment the fruit was picked, before the walk to the bin. A villager who lets go of the fruit anywhere else -- the trip is interrupted, for example -- takes nothing from the tree and adds no food. Several villagers may pick the same tree at once: each delivery takes its own load off the tree, which never goes below zero, and a delivery that finds the tree already emptied by the others still adds its food, as honey does. The same goes for the fruit the rain lift brings down from the cliff tree once all three fruit trees are planted: a villager who picks it up and carries it to the food bin ("Depositing food") now adds its 4 food when it goes into the bin, not when it is picked up; dropped on the way, it adds nothing and is lost, as it is in the stock game. The food per load, the Tribal Chief's supervision bonus, the Food Gathered statistic and the trees' regrowth are unchanged, and catch-up (the time that passes while the game is closed) still gains the same food. **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested in the game.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: Fruit picking works like honey gathering: the fruit leaves the tree, and the village gains its food, only when the villager puts it in the food bin. In the stock game both happened the moment the fruit was picked, before the walk to the bin. Several villagers may pick the same tree at once: each delivery takes its own load off the tree, which never goes below zero, and a delivery that finds the tree already emptied by the others still adds its food, as honey does. The same goes for the fruit the rain lift brings down from the cliff tree once all three fruit trees are planted: a villager who picks it up and carries it to the food bin ("Depositing food") now adds its 4 food when it goes into the bin, not when it is picked up; dropped on the way, it adds nothing and is lost, as it is in the stock game. The food per load, the Tribal Chief's supervision bonus, the Food Gathered statistic and the trees' regrowth are unchanged, and catch-up (the time that passes while the game is closed) still gains the same food. **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested in the game.**

#### Fruit Trees Take Turns Refilling (`vv3_fruit_trees_take_turns`)

The fruit trees take turns to refill, evenly spread over the refill time: with three trees one tree refills every hour (every 45 minutes at Nature level 1 with "Nature Level 1 Actually Replenishes Food Sources Faster"), with two trees every hour and a half. In the stock game each tree's refill clock follows when it was planted, so trees planted close together refill close together and then leave a long wait. A village that lives on fruit therefore waits the shortest time with no tree to pick: in a simulation of a hungry village (12 villagers picking, three trees, Nature 0) the longest wait was 2 hours 46 minutes with trees planted at the same time and 55 minutes with this patch, for the same fruit per day. Planting or losing a tree rearranges the turns. Each tree gets the stock amount of fruit for the time since its own last refill -- the game's own formula, with Nature level 1's bonus and "Nature Level 1 Actually Replenishes Food Sources Faster" when it is ticked -- so over time every tree gives exactly as much fruit as in the stock game; only when the fruit comes changes. A newly planted tree still starts full and is still ready to pick after 8 hours. The island event that refills the trees is unchanged, and catch-up (the time that passes while the game is closed) and Time Warp pay the same fruit as the stock game. The save keeps every tree's own stock refill time, so without this patch the trees simply go back to their own times, with nothing lost; the patch's schedule is kept in its own file in the save's folder (Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <S>\Data\Fruit Trees\Virtual Villagers 3 Fruit Tree Timers - Save <S>.dat) and Start Over deletes it. **With "All Fruit Trees Refill to Full" ticked too, each of this patch's refills fills the tree to 1,000 instead of adding the stock amount (a tree that refills early is filled early).** **Cannot be ticked together with "All Fruit Trees Refill at the Same Time": the two give the trees different schedules, so tick only one; with both ticked the patcher builds nothing.** **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.** This patch needs no other row. It is off by default (and Select All Patches leaves it off), because "All Fruit Trees Refill at the Same Time" is on by default; untick that one first to tick this. Owner's Defaults ticks this one instead. The companion is "VVFP VV3 Trees Take Turns.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock game runs.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The fruit trees' update 0x434760 (vtable 0x49D1D0 slot 8, run by the world objects' update 0x435880, live and after catch-up and Time Warp): its refill loop (0x43478A..0x43481A) is replaced by the companion's pass, which goes on to the stock tail at 0x43481B (the planting-puzzle check and the removal of dead trees, 0x43487F, unchanged). The pass keeps every tree's own stock timer (record +0x28) exactly as the stock loop moves it -- set to now whenever it is at least the interval old -- so the save holds the timers the game without this patch would hold. The fruit follows the patch's schedule: each tree has the time its fruit is paid up to and the moment of its next refill. At that moment it gains floor((now - paid up to) x factor / 3600), the stock formula with the stock factor (37, or the immediate at 0x4347CE at Nature 1 or more: 42, or 56 with the Nature patch), and both move on (paid up to = now, next = now + the interval: 10,800 s, or 8,100 s at Nature 1 or more with the Nature patch, whose test at 0x4347AA the companion recognises). Every tree's fruit is held to 1,000 on every pass, as the stock loop does. With "All Fruit Trees Refill to Full" (vv3_fruit_trees_refill_to_full) the 7 bytes at 0x4347EB are its mov eax,0x3E8 / nop / nop instead of the stock add, and the companion then sets the tree's fruit to 1,000 at each refill instead of adding the stock share. A tree the companion has not seen (newly planted, or every tree of a save without a matching entry) starts from its own stock timer and joins the schedule; a removed tree leaves it (trees are matched by position, planted time and kind, so the list closing up does not mix them). Saving (0x433EC0, before the stock saver): the schedule is written to "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <S>\Data\Fruit Trees\Virtual Villagers 3 Fruit Tree Timers - Save <S>.dat" with an FNV-1a 64 fingerprint of the trees' saved bytes (header, records, count), the last 16 saves kept, written atomically (a temporary file moved over it). Loading (0x433E40, after the stock loader): only the entry written with exactly these trees by this same patch is used; otherwise every tree starts from its stock timer. After every change the trees' next refills are laid out in turns: the earliest keeps its moment and the others follow it, in the order they were due, by the interval divided by the number of trees (one hour apart with three trees and the stock interval).
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the companion verifies the stock bytes at its three sites (0x43478A, 0x433E40, 0x433EC0) and that the interval test and factors are the stock ones or the Nature patch's exactly and the refill's add (0x4347EB) the stock one or All Fruit Trees Refill to Full's exactly, and writes its detours at run time, all together or none; a different build of the game installs nothing. The save is stock: the trees' records, their stock timers included, are written by the stock saver; without the companion the stock loop continues from those timers. No tree earns fruit faster than the stock rate: the amount is the stock formula for the time since its own last refill (or, with All Fruit Trees Refill to Full, the tree filled to 1,000, as that patch's own refill does), and the 1,000 cap is unchanged. Planting (0x4349FD), the 8-hour growth (0x434030), the pickable checks, the island event refill (0x415AD0) and the fruit job are unchanged. Nothing is written to a villager record.

#### Full Names on the Details Screen (`vv3_details_full_names`)

The Villager Details screen keeps a villager's whole name. In the base game its name box holds only 18 characters (fewer for wide letters) and, when the screen closes, writes what it holds back to the villager, so a longer name -- a last name, a numbered namesake -- was cut short for good. Now the box holds the 23 characters the game's name field has room for, is wide enough to show them, and copies the whole name back; typing a new name there allows 23 characters too. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts): unticking this unticks it.**

- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The villager's name field is the base game's own 24-byte field; nothing is written past it, and the save's layout is unchanged. Names that already fitted are shown and kept exactly as before; no other screen changes.

#### Hungrier Villagers (2-10x Meals) (`vv3_hungrier_villagers`)

**Needs no other patch.** Makes the game harder; off by default. Every villager's meal takes 2 to 10 times the normal food: you choose how many times with the Hungrier Villagers slider in the patcher window (a whole number, 2 unless you move it). Normally a villager's meal takes 2 food, and 2 more three times in four at 8,000 food or more on Normal difficulty, at any food level on Hard, never on Easy; at x 2 that is 4 and 4 more. Food never goes below 0: when it runs out the game's own starvation rules take over, as without the patch. Skipped meals when food is low, the snack at the food bin, events that take food and everything that brings food in are unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The meal routine's two food amounts (0x460080, 0x4600C4), each -2, become -2 x N (the slider, 2 to 10; 2 by default); the stock clamp keeps food at 0 or more.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: When a villager eats, the low-food skip, starvation, the snack at the food bin, starting food, events and everything that brings food in are unchanged. Two one-byte edits in place; no code is added and no executable space is claimed.
