#### Keep the Game's Own Log (ldwLog.txt) (`vv3_game_log`)

Keeps the game's own log, 'ldwLog.txt' in the game's save folder (Documents\LDW\<game executable name>\). Every Virtual Villagers game has always had this log, but the base game starts the file afresh the first time it writes in each run (erasing the earlier runs' lines), holds what it writes in memory until the game closes (a crash loses it), and writes only when something goes wrong -- so most players never see the file. Now each time the game opens it adds a "---- Game started ----" line, and every line the game writes is added to the file at once and kept: a missing font picture, a missing picture, a missing sound, a text the game asks for that is missing from its text file (sm.xml), a text in sm.xml with no end, a healer who could not find anyone to heal and "Seconds Timer out of bounds!" (the computer's clock was set back, so the game's one-second timer is ahead of it). The Secret City's code contains no tip or path-finding line, so those cannot be logged (its villagers keep a pointer to the log, but no code writes through it). A line repeated without a break is written once a minute with how many times it repeated, at most 1,000 lines are written a minute, and when the file reaches 4 MB it is renamed 'ldwLog 1.txt' (then 2, 3, ...) and a new one is started, so no file grows without limit; nothing is ever deleted. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The game's log writer (0x40b800) is replaced at run time by the companion's: the same "<date and time>: <line>" text with CR-LF line ends, to the same file, Documents\LDW\<executable name up to its first dot>\ldwLog.txt. The file is appended to (the base game opens it with "wt", which erases the earlier runs' lines), and each line is written to the file at once (the base game buffers until a clean exit). Each run starts with one "---- Game started ----" line, which also creates the file. A line that exactly repeats the one before it is written again only after a minute, preceded by "(the line above was repeated <n> more times)". At most 1,000 lines are written in a minute; the next line written says how many were left out. When ldwLog.txt would pass 4 MiB it is renamed "ldwLog <n>.txt" (n one more than the highest already there) and a new ldwLog.txt is started. Call at 0x4025b7 writes "Font Image not found: %s": a font picture is missing (the game then closes). Call at 0x40b5b5 writes " Missing Graphic -> %s": a picture file is missing. Call at 0x40c5c7 writes "ldwSoundFx Missing File ->%s": a sound file is missing. Call at 0x42f635 writes "String Table (sm.xml) malformed near %s": a text id the game asks for is not in Assets\sm.xml. Call at 0x42f68e writes "String Table (sm.xml) malformed looking for </Text> after %s": a text in Assets\sm.xml has no </Text>. Call at 0x45b940 writes "%s could not find someone to heal.": a healer found nobody to heal. Call at 0x4688f9 writes "Seconds Timer out of bounds!": the game's one-second timer is more than 3 seconds ahead of the computer's clock, as when the clock is set back (checked every frame).
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces the writer's first instruction at run time, only after verifying its first 16 bytes, and installs nothing on a different build. Which lines the game writes, and when, is the game's own: every call site is unchanged, and no line the game's code does not contain is ever written (only the "Game started" line and the repeat and left-out counts are the companion's). No save, village or villager data is read or written; nothing else in the game changes. Older 'ldwLog <n>.txt' files and any other file in the folder are never changed or deleted.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static exact-build verification of the writer and every call to it in each executable (tests/test_game_log.py); the companion's writer is run by native/vvfp_game_log/game_log_harness.c
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

Villagers succeed every work-task skill roll for Farming, Building, Researching, Healing, and Parenting; the native skill gains and all non-skill outcomes remain unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: Removes only the five native work-task skill-failure branches in The Secret City, so each eligible work task reaches its stock skill-gain path. Does not alter pregnancy, food, tech-point, or other random outcomes.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The native skill increment code and skill caps remain stock. No save data, villager creation, or non-work-task RNG path is changed.

#### Log Every Death, Disappearance and Unaccounted Villager (`vv3_cause_of_death`)

Every death that leaves a body is written to the Deaths log ('Virtual Villagers 3 Deaths Log <n>.txt' in the save slot's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Deaths and Disappearances' folder beside the game's saves, or 'Deaths' in a save an older version made: nothing is moved) when it is final: when the body is buried, with the skill line and epitaph the grave was given, or when the game removes a body nobody buried ("no grave"). Each Death record gives the villager's name, head, body, likes and dislikes, their age at death in the game's own units (20 per year, as the Village Population log prints Age), the cause, the grave and the epitaph. A villager brought back to life gets no Death record. A villager taken with no skeleton (The Tsunami and The Low Tide, or the Custom Island Event's "Disappears") gets a "Disappeared" record saying what took them, and editing a grave's epitaph adds an "Epitaph changed" record with the old and new text. A grave the Deaths log has no record for -- dug before the log was kept, or while the game was catching up on time away -- is given a Death record only when the player says so -- Repair Logs in the patcher window, or Repair when the game asks as it closes (with "Check logs automatically" on, and only if something is wrong); nothing is ever asked while the village is played. The record is made from the grave (name, age at death, skill line, epitaph, and the cause where the game or this patch knows it) with the head, body, likes and dislikes of the villager's last Village History snapshot ("(unknown)" when that does not settle who it was), and marked "Recorded from the grave". Which graves have their record is kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Deaths\Virtual Villagers 3 Graves Logged - Save <n>.dat', so no grave is recorded twice; Start Over deletes it. Every villager who joins the village without being born into it -- a new village's founders, an island event's newcomer, the Barrel of Babies, the Custom Island Event's new villagers -- gets an "Arrived" record in the Births and Conceptions log ('Virtual Villagers 3 Births and Conceptions Log <n>.txt'), written at the next save: the name, the age when they arrived, sex, head, body, likes, dislikes, skills, and how they came ("Founder", the island event's title, "Barrel of Babies", "Custom Island Event", or "unknown"). A birth is never an arrival. A mother who dies or disappears while nursing (the game's own word for a mother whose babies are not yet born) loses them with her: they never become villagers and get no grave, so her Death or Disappeared record says "Nursing: yes, <n> babies (never born: lost with their mother)", and a "Lost before birth" record in the Births and Conceptions log closes her Conception (the mother, the expected father, the babies). Repair Saves & Logs adds both to older records where her Conception has no Birth and her one Death or Disappeared record came before the babies were due, and asks the player where the records cannot settle it. Villagers already in a village who arrived before this record existed (no Birth or Arrived record with their name, head and body) each get one the same way, only when the player says so, marked "Recorded afterwards (arrived before this log existed)", as "Founder" when the village's first Village History snapshot lists them and otherwise with how they came unknown -- exactly once: 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Data\Arrivals\Virtual Villagers 3 Arrivals Recorded - Save <n>.dat' then says it is done; Start Over deletes it. A villager the save says was born here (their record keeps their parents) who has no Birth or Arrived record -- born before the log existed -- gets, the same way and only when the player says so, a Birth record written from the save, with their parents as the save keeps them, marked "Recorded afterwards (born before this log existed)" -- exactly once: 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Births\Virtual Villagers 3 Births Recorded - Save <n>.dat' then says it is done; Start Over deletes it. At every save, the village is checked against the one saved before, villager by villager by who they are (name, sex, looks, likes and dislikes, and an age that fits; never by record number, which every load, a full village and the Elder Totems move change): a villager who left with no Death or Disappeared record, or arrived with no birth or known arrival, is written with everything known about them to the Unaccounted Villagers log ('Virtual Villagers 3 Unaccounted Villagers Log <n>.txt' in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Unaccounted Villagers'). Both logs are headed with the village and its save slot, are created when a village is started and again after Start Over (which deletes them with the village), only ever grow, and start a new numbered file after every 256 records. The village as it was at each save is kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Unaccounted Villagers\Virtual Villagers 3 Villagers at Last Save - Save <n>.dat' ('... Village Roster ...' in a save an older version made); Start Over deletes it. A villager who is in the village at both saves with another head or body (an island event the Island Events log did not see, or any other change the game made) is written to the Births and Conceptions log as an 'Appearance changed' record, 'Changed by: the game', unless Change Appearance or the Island Events log already wrote one for that look; a newcomer never is. The cause is the one The Secret City itself records and shows on the grave. **The first save after this patch is installed only starts the check: nothing is reported about anything that happened before it.** **The patch's DLL is loaded and its hooks installed as soon as the game is opened, before any village is loaded, so the deaths, burials, disappearances and arrivals of the catch-up on time away (and of a Time Warp) are recorded as they happen, like any others.** **The logs are written by Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File's DLL: with that patch off, none of them is written.** **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. That base's companion loads this patch's DLL; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the game runs unchanged.

**Needs Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File on for the Deaths and Unaccounted Villagers logs, which that patch's DLL writes (without it neither is written). The Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically.**

- Behavior changes: After the burial's Roster of the Dead write, the Death record is written with the cause, skill line and epitaph the game gave the grave; a body the game removes unburied gets "no grave". The listed removals of a living villager write a Disappeared record before the game takes them; the Custom Island Event's "Disappears" is reported by the Story / Cheat Upgrades DLL. Graves with no Death record: VvfpCauseScanGraves counts, writing nothing, the graves the village's Deaths log has no record for (the first-load check lists them for the player); VvfpCauseRepairGraves records the player's answer. Only after Repair, at each save of that village in the session, each such grave gets a Death record from the grave, filed by RecordGravesMissingFromLog in "VVFP Parentage Export.dll" (which counts the log's own and held records first, and takes the head, body, likes and dislikes from the Village History log); a villager the previous save held who was buried unseen is then not an Unaccounted record. The graves whose record is in the log are kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Deaths\Virtual Villagers 3 Graves Logged - Save <n>.dat' (written atomically; deleted by Start Over). The grave's Done writes an Epitaph changed record when the epitaph's text changed; spaces typed before or after the same words are not a change. Every villager the game's own creators make is noted as an arrival; after each save the village is compared with the roster kept at the save before, and any departure with no Death or Disappeared record, or arrival with no known arrival, is written to the Unaccounted Villagers log. The comparison follows each villager by identity, never by record number (v1.35.80): each villager of the last save is matched one to one to a villager now by name, sex, head, body, likes and dislikes with the age gone on by the time every matched villager aged, then by name, sex and looks, then -- only when one villager on each side is such -- through a changed head, a rename or a rejuvenation; a departure the game reported (a burial, a body's removal, a disappearance) accounts for the villager it names, by name, sex and looks, before any matching; a villager who only moved to another record is neither Left nor Arrived, and one with a Death or Disappeared record is never Left. Statues, totems and look-alikes are no villagers. The roster is kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Unaccounted Villagers\Virtual Villagers 3 Villagers at Last Save - Save <n>.dat', or '... Village Roster ...' in a save an older version made, never renamed; under both names the one written last (written atomically; deleted by Start Over). Arrivals: a villager a creator made that is neither a birth (the path's own return addresses, read at fixed places on the stack, or the Births and Conceptions log's note) nor a record the game takes away again is decided at the next tick, named by its path (Founder, the island event, Barrel of Babies, the developer F7 command in The Tree of Life), or "added outside a recorded event" when no listed path made it, and gets an Arrived record at the next save of that village (at its departure if it leaves first); the Story / Cheat Upgrades DLL names the Custom Island Event's (VvfpCauseArrivedBy). A founder is written only at a save with no village saved in the slot before. Arrivals before this record existed: VvfpCauseScanArrivals counts, writing nothing, the villagers (believers, with no parents on their record) the village's Births and Conceptions log has no Birth or Arrived record for (name, head and body), for the first-load check; VvfpCauseRepairArrivals records the answer. Only after Repair, at the next save, each gets an Arrived record filed by RecordArrivalsMissingFromLog in "VVFP Parentage Export.dll", and none is an Unaccounted record; once all are on disk 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Arrivals\Virtual Villagers 3 Arrivals Recorded - Save <n>.dat' (deleted by Start Over) ends the backfill for good. All records are written through WriteVillageRecord in "VVFP Parentage Export.dll".
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the Origins companion loads the DLL, which detours the listed sites at run time only after verifying every site's stock bytes; any other build installs nothing. No game value is changed: health, age, the graves, the Roster of the Dead and the save are only read; each detoured site's own instructions run unchanged after the check.
- Dependencies: vv3_enable_origins_exclusive_features
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Manual Drop-Breeding overrides Birth Control (`vv3_manual_drop_breeding_overrides_birth_control`)

**Works the same with or without Birth Control: the 50-and-over refusal it lifts is The Secret City's own, which Birth Control does not change.** When you drop an adult villager onto an adult of the opposite sex, a woman aged 50 or older is no longer refused. It is not a guarantee: the game's usual chances still decide whether the pair gets along and whether a baby is conceived, exactly as for any other couple, so a drop can still fail. Every other rule of the drop is unchanged: a man and a woman, both adults, both alive and well, the woman not already expecting or nursing, and the game's own food and population checks. The game never looks at the Parenting preference on a manual drop, and Parenting skill (the dropped villager's) only changes the chances without ever blocking a drop, so an unchecked preference or no skill never stopped one, with or without this patch. Only the manual drop is changed: villagers pairing up on their own, catch-up, events and Birth Control's own rules stay as they are. Off by default.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: After the stock conception roll succeeds, the pairing handler at VA 0x4584B0 (step 13) returns without calling the pregnancy writer when either participant is a woman at internal age 1000 (50) or older. The player's drop and villagers pairing up on their own both reach this handler through action 4 (0x44A680), so the refusal is skipped only for the drop: file 0x586F3 jumps to the unused padding at 0x458741, which continues at the stock writer call 0x45871C when the drop's return address 0x4669D6 sits at [esp+0x48] -- the depth the drop's own call chain (0x4669D1 -> 0x455570 -> 0x441170 -> 0x44A680 -> 0x461BF0 -> 0x4584B0) puts it, because the drop queues step 13 on an emptied queue and the handler runs inside that call -- so she conceives on a passing roll like any other woman. Every other entry returns to the stock check, re-encoded in place with the same comparisons. Autonomous pairing (0x45B674) queues a walk to the partner before step 13, so its handler runs later from the walk's arrival (0x460F20) and never with the drop's call on the stack: a woman of 50 or older is still refused after the stock roll, exactly as stock.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: Birth Control's five candidate-selector edits and its chooser change are not touched and do not overlap this patch. Every other stock manual-drop rule is unchanged and still refuses the drop: same sex, either villager under internal age 360 (18), either villager dead or ill, a woman already expecting or nursing, and the game's own food and population checks. The stock Parenting skill-attempt roll and the stock conception roll (RNG(300) against Parenting skill and technology) are unchanged and still decide; a drop can fail at either one. Autonomous pairing keeps the stock woman-aged-50-or-older refusal in the shared handler; the partner chooser and candidate scans, catch-up, Island Events and every other birth route, the conception and pregnancy writers, delivery, and automatic physical-capacity safety are unchanged.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the player's drop and autonomous pairing are each emulated from their real call sites through the game's own action table, step queue and dispatcher into the handler in tests/test_manual_drop_breeding.py; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 2; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### More Island Events (`vv3_more_island_events`)

Adds new island events, written by the owner, to the ones the game draws from (more come in later versions). Five here: The Aspiring Adventurer -- a villager who loves to explore sees something glinting off the safe path. "Go investigate!" finds a pile of dirt, a stack of meat (food) or a golden chest of artifacts (tech points); half the time the adventurer gets home (with the find, or with a friend's help), half the time a trap leads to death (a grave) or a disappearance (no grave). "Stay on the safe path" brings them home 9 times in 10; otherwise they are lost: hurt, healed or disabled, a skilled survivalist, killed, gone, or they join another tribe. The event is one more island event, listed and drawn like the game's own (1 in the number listed); it needs two villagers of 14 or more who are not nursing a baby and not the Tribal Chief, and the adventurer and the friend who may come to help are drawn from them. The reward is a random amount from the smallest to the largest food or tech-point gain of the game's own island events (200 to 600 food for the meat, 1,000 to 2,000 tech points for the chest) times the game's own multiplier for its events (the villagers it counts, divided by 20, plus 1). Deaths are the game's own ("Unknown causes", with a grave); a disappearance is logged as one in the Deaths log. The popups show the owner's text in pages that fit the screen (OK shows the next); the effects wait for the page that tells them, and the Island Events log keeps one entry for each event. And The Troubling Signs (The Secret City only): the Tribal Chief, wearing the chief's robe, asks one of four groups for advice in a popup with four buttons (the game's own look; the mouse, or the keys 1 to 4): the spiritual leaders (the village loses food), the magicians (gains tech points), the naturalists (gains food) or the scientists and healers (loses tech points) -- a random amount as the Aspiring Adventurer's, 200 to 600 food or 1,000 to 2,000 tech points, times the game's own multiplier; a loss never takes more than is stored. Each group's advisor speaks, the chief calls the tribe by its own name, and the decree sends five villagers of 18 or more away for good (no graves). It needs the robed chief, nine other villagers of 18 or more who are not nursing a baby (four advisors, who stay, and the five) and a population of 61 or more (The Lost Children's "A Dangerous Mission" rule: the living villagers plus the babies being carried); it has its own share of the draw. And Diving for Treasure (The Secret City only): a villager of 18 or more dives for something shimmering on the reef. "Swim deeper": 1 in 4 each, golden doubloons (tech points), a useless buoy, a container of exotic ingredients (food) -- a random amount as the Aspiring Adventurer's, 1,000 to 2,000 tech points or 200 to 600 food, times the game's own multiplier -- or an air tank pops: 75% the diver gets ashore and now dislikes swimming; 25% the diver sinks: dies (17%, a grave), is never found (17%, no grave) or is rescued (66%, +10 to 20 Healing, at most 100). "Better not": +10 to 20 Parenting, at most 100. It needs two villagers of 18 or more who are not nursing a baby and not the Tribal Chief (the diver, and another named as the head Doctor on the rescue page); it has its own share of the draw. And The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings (all five games; one popup each, OK only). The Remembrance Ceremony needs at least one grave: everyone joins in -- children, nursing mothers and fathers, everyone -- each at the graveyard, "Honoring the Dead" or "Reflecting" (half the time each), and the feast quietly uses 10 food for every villager (never below 0). The Rumblings needs every puzzle solved and a finished structure: an earthquake damages each of the three population huts and the clothing hut one time in four (at least one always), each losing 10 to 100% of its building work; the builders must build it again (at 100% it is unbuilt again, as in a new village). Nobody is hurt; a village over its limit keeps everyone and has no new births until it is rebuilt. Each has its own share of the draw and can come again. Off by default; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Needs no other patch.** **Unverified in play: the event has not been seen in a running game** (emulated on the stock executable). The companion is "VVFP More Island Events.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; nothing is saved by it.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The event is one more island event, listed and drawn like the game's own (1 in the number listed). It can happen only while at least two villagers may go: 14 or more (280 age units), alive and present, not carrying a baby, and not the Tribal Chief; the adventurer and the friend of ending A8 are drawn from them, the friend never the adventurer. Choice A, "Go investigate!": the find 50% a pile of dirt, 25% meat (a food award: 200 to 600 food), 25% a golden chest (a tech award: 1,000 to 2,000 tech points); then 50% a surviving ending (after the dirt A7 or A9; after a find A1, A5 or A8, which give the reward) and 50% a deadly one (A2 and A4 die, the game's own death with cause -1 and a grave; A3 and A6 disappear, no body), each equally likely within its half. Choice B, "Stay on the safe path": 90% home safe; 10% lost, then 1 in 6 each: the healers (1 in 3 each: dies; a full recovery; health set to 10-50 and running disliked), joins another tribe (gone for good, no grave), a survivalist (+20 to 30 in Farming, Building, Research or Healing, at most 100), dies under a fallen tree, dies at the bottom of a cliff, disappears. The reward is drawn, each amount equally likely, from the game's smallest to its largest stock island-event gain of that kind (src/vv_aspiring_adventurer.py AWARD_RANGES), and goes through the game's own food or tech writer, times the game's own multiplier for its events (the villagers it counts, divided by 20, plus 1). The effects wait for their own page (the page that ends the ending's text), and the event writes its own one Island Events log entry; a disappearance is told to the Cause of Death companion (VvfpCauseVanishedBy), so its Deaths log records it as one. The owner's words, by translation key (the event's popup shows the player's language when a translation has them), are laid out in pages that fit the game's popup -- whole paragraphs, else whole sentences -- each shown in turn with OK. The Troubling Signs (The Secret City): needs the Tribal Chief in the robe (+0xE80 and the robe's body +0xDF4 = 29, as the robing 0x45FBC0 writes them), nine other different villagers of 18 or more (360 age units) who are not protected (adv_is_protected: nursing +0xE8C, the chief +0xE80) -- four advisors (one per group, the same four for the event; they stay) and five travellers, any nine equally likely -- a population of 61 or more (The Lost Children's 0x425860 rule: the living villagers plus the babies carried, litter +0xE90) and the tribe's name (the game object [0x4B309C] +0x12ED4). It shares table slot 0 with The Aspiring Adventurer and Diving for Treasure but has its own share of the draw: the loop-end stub lists slot 0 once for each of them that can happen (never past the list's room) and puts one of their objects there, each equally likely. The popup is the game's own dialog 0x4192F0 with two more answer buttons made as its constructor makes its two (0x46EC93, picture 4 via 0x42E9D0 / 0x42E8A0, 0x4019F0 ids 4 and 5, labels 0x4185A0 / 0x401620, add-child 0x40C1F0), stacked and centred 1.5 button heights apart, room for them measured by the game's own paragraph 0x40A0C0; that dialog's virtual table is a copy of 0x47F28C with its own click (ids 4 and 5) and key handlers (Enter / Esc OK, 1-4 the answers); Scrolling Popups' reserve adds VvfpMoreIslandEventsButtonRoom. Each answer's award is a normal one (the game's range, then its multiplier); the effects -- the five removed as a living villager is (no body), told to Cause of Death, and the award through the game's own writer (a loss at most what is stored) -- are made when the decree's last page is shown, with the event's one Island Events log entry. No site of its own. Diving for Treasure (The Secret City): the diver and the rescue page's head Doctor are two different villagers of 18 or more (360 age units) who may be picked (vv3_eligible: alive +0xE78, present +0xF10, not a look-alike +0xE94, adv_is_protected: nursing +0xE8C, the chief +0xE80), each drawn among them. One more two-choice object with the Adventurer's virtual table and methods (adv_flow), its own entry in the draw (t_list: one entry for slot 0 per event that can happen, never past the list's room; the object put there drawn among them). "Swim deeper": rand(4) A / B / C / D; D: rand(100) < 75 survives -- swimming (preference 37 of the game's list at file 0x97488) taken from the likes +0xFB4 and added to the dislikes +0xFC0 -- else sinks: rand(100) < 17 the game's own death (0x462670, health 0, cause -1: a grave), < 34 removed as a living villager is (no body; told to Cause of Death), else +10 to 20 Healing (+0xEB4); A a normal tech award, C a normal food award (the game's range, then its multiplier, through 0x427130 / 0x4263F0). "Better not": +10 to 20 Parenting (+0xEB0). Skills at most 100 (the game's own adder 0x455740 caps at 0x64). The effects are made when the ending's last page is shown, with the event's one Island Events log entry. No site of its own. The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings (ceremony_core.inc, ceremony_games.inc): each its own entry in the draw (t_list), no site of its own; the game's own single-result popup shows the owner's words, the effects are made as it is built, with the event's one Island Events log entry. The Remembrance Ceremony: needs at least one grave (the game's own grave count); every living, present villager is started on its own through the game's own stop and action starter, as its Day of Honor starts each one (so no group filter leaves anyone out), at the graveyard, "Honoring the Dead" or "Reflecting" (half the time each); the feast uses 10 food for every villager the game counts, never below 0 (Blessings Day's own rule). The Rumblings: needs every puzzle of the game's Puzzles screen solved and one of the three population huts and the clothing hut finished; each finished one rand(100) < 25 (none: one of them at random), each losing 10 + rand(91) percent of its building work, written as the states the game's own construction passes through (at 100% the new village's state); the building's effect handle freed and set to -1.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion writes each site at run time, only after verifying every site's stock bytes (all of them, or none); without it the event does not exist. Every stock event, its odds, the island-event timer and counting, the rescue rules and Custom Island Events are unchanged; nothing is saved by the companion.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the draw, the popup pages, both choices' effects and the install with every other patch emulated on the stock executable in tests/test_aspiring_adventurer.py (The Troubling Signs: who, the draw, all four answers by mouse and key, the effects on the last page, the log entry, the words and the four buttons, in tests/test_troubling_signs.py; Diving for Treasure: who, every branch at its odds, every effect on the last page, the log entry, the words and the draw with 1, 2 and 3 events, in tests/test_diving_for_treasure.py); The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings: the conditions, the draw, everyone sent and where, the feast, the damage and its states, the log entry and the words, in tests/test_ceremony_and_rumblings.py; runtime/player confirmation pending

#### Nature Level 1 Actually Replenishes Food Sources Faster (`vv3_nature_honey_refill`)

Nature level 1 or higher reduces fruit-tree refills from 3 hours to 2 hours 15 minutes and honey refills from 1 hour to 45 minutes. Fruit trees retain their stock Nature quantity bonus, while honey gains the same proportional quantity bonus. Honey keeps the part of a refill too small to make a whole unit for the next refill, so playing with the game open gains the same honey as the same time away.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

#### Original Looks for Reset to Original (`vv3_original_look`)

Remembers each villager's original look -- the head, body and mask they had before any Change Appearance or island event changed them -- so Change Appearance and Change Appearance for All can put them back with Reset to original (the head look goes back to Auto too). A look the game itself gives a villager stays: The Secret City's robe for a new Tribal Chief, and the outfit the game's own clothing dialog puts on (The Lost Children to New Believers), become part of the original. Each villager's look is noted the first time the patcher sees them: when they are born or arrive, or, for a village you already have, the first time you play it with this patch; a look noted is never written over. For villagers changed before this patch, Repair Saves & Logs adds the original the patcher's logs prove -- the look before their earliest "Appearance changed" record -- and never guesses: when the logs cannot prove it, Change Appearance says the original look is not known. The looks are kept in the save's own Original Looks file, follow each villager (through deaths, reloads and renames) and are copied by Back Up Saves; Start Over clears them. **On by default.** Change Appearance is in the Origins upgrades: **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. **Works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Not yet seen in a running game.** The companion is "VVFP Original Look.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; it changes nothing the game does. If it cannot be loaded, Change Appearance says the original look is not known.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked; the Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically.**

- Behavior changes: Each villager's head, body and mask (the mask the Origins companion keeps, its VvfpMaskOf) are noted the first time the companion sees them, in the save's own "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <S>\Data\Original Looks\Original Looks - Save <S>.dat" (native/vvfp_original_look/original_look_store.inc), and never written over. The companion looks at the villager records from the game's own thread between frames (a WH_GETMESSAGE hook on that thread and a thread timer, at most every 250 ms): a villager present when a village is bound is a first-run original, one who appears after is a born / arrived one. A village is bound only once its records have held still for 1.5 s; one whose file is missing or belongs to another village is kept in memory only until the game itself saves that slot again (so the title screen's seeded records are never written into a slot's file). Repair Saves & Logs (game closed) adds the originals the logs prove (src/vv_original_look.py): the Old head and Old body of each villager's earliest "Appearance changed" record, the mask before it when logged; where a change is seen with no record, the original is marked not known. Change Appearance's Reset to original reads it through VvfpOriginalLookGet (native/shared/original_look.h). The game's own changes are kept: each instruction by which the game itself writes a villager's body outside Change Appearance and island events -- The Secret City's robe (0x45FBDE in the robing 0x45FBC0) and the clothing dialog's OK (The Lost Children 0x4228E4, The Secret City 0x41BF89, The Tree of Life 0x41961D, New Believers 0x419D68 and 0x419E8E) -- tells the companion the body first, which becomes part of that villager's original; the game's write then happens exactly as before. A New Home's stock game has no such writer.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the companion splices the game's own body writers listed above at run time, after checking their stock bytes, through the shared all-or-none writer (a different build installs none, and then the game's own changes are not kept); it writes no record byte of its own -- the splice makes the very write the game makes. Change Appearance and island events are never folded in: neither reaches those instructions. The save is never written; the Original Looks file is the patcher's own. A corrupt Original Looks file is moved aside intact and never read or written over; another village's file is never replaced on what is on screen alone.
- Dependencies: vv3_enable_origins_exclusive_features

#### Picked Up Collectibles Stay Collected When Dropped (`vv3_collectibles_stay_collected`)

A mushroom or collectible a child has picked up counts wherever the child puts it down -- dropped by you somewhere else, or set down when the child stops on the way: the mushroom's food, or the collection piece (tech points for a piece already found), with its tips and completion messages, exactly once. In the normal game it counts only where the game takes it (the food bin for a mushroom, the collection spot for a collectible) and is lost anywhere else. Nothing new is saved, so without the patch the game simply goes back to its own rule. **Needs no other patch.** Off by default; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The item listener's release (0x42DEB0, run once when a child's carried item is put down: 0x455F30 with -1 dispatches the old item and then empties the hands) no longer requires the place: the collectible's area test (area 25, 0x42DEEA jne) and the mushroom's (area 14, 0x42DF1A jne) become NOPs, so the stock award runs wherever the item is put down.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The awards (0x42DF32..0x42E056 collectibles, 0x42E064..0x42E095 mushrooms), the pickup, the spawn and the save are unchanged. A release with empty hands dispatches nothing (0x42CE50 refuses -1), so an item is credited once.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the release listener (every collectible kind and mushroom, at the food bin, the collection spot and elsewhere) is emulated on the stock and rendered executables in tests/test_collectibles_stay_collected.py; runtime/player confirmation pending

#### Pointing Out a Rare Collectible Always Works (`vv3_rare_collectible_retry`)

When the Tribal Chief completes Pointing out a rare collectible and the stock game rejects its random choice (a collectible a villager is already after, or a special one already collected), the whole stock selection is run again, up to 20 times in all, stopping as soon as a collectible is placed. In practice a collectible almost always appears instead of the stock cooldown being spent for nothing; if every attempt is refused (for example, when every special collectible has already been found), nothing is placed, exactly as in the stock game. The original rare categories, collectible IDs, collection rules and placement logic are unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

In practice a collectible almost always appears instead of the stock cooldown being spent for nothing; if every attempt is refused (for example, when every special collectible has already been found), nothing is placed, exactly as in the stock game. The original rare categories, collectible IDs, collection rules and placement logic are unchanged.

#### Push Clouds Away on the Overview Map (`vv3_push_overview_clouds`)

The clouds that drift over the island on the overview map (the Map button) move away from the mouse, exactly as in The Tree of Life: bring the cursor within about 80 pixels of a cloud's middle and it is pushed away from the cursor, sideways and up or down, faster the closer the cursor is (up to 5 pixels a frame, 10 when it is pushed the way the clouds drift), and it fades a little each time the mouse moves near it. It keeps going until the mouse moves again, and every cloud is back at full strength the next time the map is opened. The drift, and where a cloud comes back after leaving the map, are the game's own. **On by default.** **Needs no other patch.** **While Disable Clouds on the Overview Map is ticked the clouds are hidden, so this has no visible effect until Disable Clouds on the Overview Map is unticked.** **Not yet seen in a running game** (checked by emulation of the stock executable). The companion is "VVFP Push Clouds.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; saves are never written by it.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: Every mouse move (message 1 to the overview screen's event slot), for each of the five clouds at (x, y) (screen +8 + 12*i): dx = x - mouse x + 90, dy = y - mouse y + 50, distance = the float square root of dx*dx + dy*dy truncated, push = (100 - distance) / 20; push above 0: fade -= 0.01, vertical = push (dy >= 0) or -push, horizontal = -push (dx >= 0) or 2*push; otherwise both 0 -- The Tree of Life's event slot 0x444B70, number for number. Every frame the stock update moves the clouds (unless that frame ends the screen's leave, 0x46C0BC..0x46C0FB): x -= horizontal and y += vertical first, then the stock drift and wrap -- The Tree of Life's x -= horizontal + drift, y += vertical (0x444AE0). Each cloud is drawn at its fade instead of the stock 1.0 (the call 0x46C3D8 of the sprite draw 0x42EB90), as The Tree of Life draws each at its own alpha (0x4454B0); showing the screen (the activate slot) sets every fade back to 1.0, as The Tree of Life's activate 0x4447A0 does.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces three vtable slots of the overview screen and one call in its cloud loop at run time, only after verifying every stock value, all or none. The stock event slot runs for every message (it ignores mouse moves), and the stock update and activate run as before: the clouds' drift (1 or 2 a frame), their wrap at the left edge and where they come back are The Secret City's own; clicks, buttons and the map's markers are unchanged. Nothing is written to a save, a villager record or a file; no text is shown.
- Dependencies: none

#### Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts (`vv3_unicode_text`)

Lets the game draw, measure and accept ANY character -- accented letters, Greek, Cyrillic, Turkish, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic and Hebrew (joined and right to left), Indian scripts, cuneiform, symbols and colour emoji -- in the game's own two fonts (the big Burweed story font and the small Arial Bold font). The Secret City's fonts hold ASCII and the Latin-1 letters; every other Windows-1252 character is added to the fonts in their own style when the game starts (from the font's own plain letter with the accent added, or drawn by Windows in the font's own typeface: Arial Bold is part of Windows; **for Burweed, install the Burweed ICG font for the best-matching letters** -- the patcher never ships it -- otherwise Comic Sans MS stands in), and every other character is made the first time it is shown, in the font's size, baseline and weight, from the fonts Windows has (Segoe UI, Segoe UI Historic, Segoe UI Symbol, Segoe UI Emoji (in colour), the CJK fonts, Nirmala UI, Ebrima ..., Noto if installed, then the bundled open fonts: Noto Sans Cuneiform, Noto Serif Tangut, GNU Unifont and Unifont Upper, and last Last Resort, so every one of Unicode 18.0's assigned characters draws, even ones no Windows font has). Names, the Details screen, popups, dialogs and every other text use them with their real widths, so centring and line breaks stay right; Chinese and Japanese break between characters. **Text and translations never run off the screen:** a line this patch, a long name or a translation draws that would cross the edge of the game's 800-pixel-wide window is cut there with "…" (whole letters only; a justified paragraph wraps at the edge instead), and one that would start left of the window starts at its edge; it may still run past its own box. Without a translation, the game's own English is drawn exactly as before. This needs this row: with Translations alone (no Unicode row) the game draws by itself and nothing is fitted. Where Windows has no icu.dll (before Windows 10 1903), Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between words by ICU's own word lists (ICU 77.1, Unicode License; about 4.4 MB in "Word Lists", read only when such a line is broken). Typing: every text box -- the tribe name, villager names on the Details screen, epitaphs -- takes any character Windows sends (dead keys, Alt codes, the Windows emoji panel, an input method for Japanese or Chinese), each stored whole or not at all, and Backspace erases a whole character (a whole emoji, flag or accented letter). Long names, everywhere: every name box takes names up to 1,200 bytes (up to 1,200 plain letters; fewer when letters need more bytes): the tribe name, villager names on the Details screen, epitaphs; Rename Tribe takes the same. It is one limit, shared with the other Fun Patchers. Characters are counted as you see them (a letter with its accents, an emoji with its skin tone or a flag is one), and Backspace removes one whole character. A long name scrolls in its box while you type it. The save itself is not changed: a name that fits its field (a villager's name 23 bytes, the tribe name 19) is kept there exactly as before; a longer one is kept there as its short form (its start and a mark, with a number when two would start alike) and the whole name is kept beside the save, in Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Long Names. The game shows the whole name wherever it shows that name. Back Up Saves, Restore Saves and Copy Player Slot carry the Long Names files with the saves. With both settings off the game still loads and plays such a save and shows the short form. Characters are stored as UTF-8 (a Western European letter keeps its one Windows-1252 byte), so every older name reads as before; the base game and older patchers show other characters as odd letters but never break. **On by default and in Owner's Defaults.** **Cannot be used with "Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts)" (ticking one unticks the other).** **Needs "Full Names on the Details Screen" (ticked with it): its Details box keeps the whole stored name, so opening a villager's Details and closing it never changes a name.** **Not yet seen in a running game** (checked by emulation of each stock executable). The companion is "VVFP Unicode Text.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; the game's own pictures and saves are never changed. **Bundles four open fonts, loaded privately by the game (never installed in Windows): GNU Unifont 18.0.01 (GPL-2.0-or-later with the font exception, or OFL-1.1) and Unifont Upper for nearly every assigned character, Noto Sans Cuneiform and Noto Serif Tangut (OFL-1.1), and Last Resort 18.000 (OFL-1.1), a placeholder block for anything still without a glyph; about 14 MB of fonts (in the patcher's files folder, in "Unicode Fonts", with their licence texts and sources), copied once per game folder, and not again when the folder already has identical files.**

**Requires Full Names on the Details Screen: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this.**

- Behavior changes: The font constructor (0x402510) runs unchanged; for the game's two fonts -- ldwBurweed27 (stock glyph table 0x4A5B78) and ldwarialbold (0x4A6A80) -- the companion records the font's line height, baseline, capital height and pixel format, then adds every printable Windows-1252 character the font lacks (src/vv_font_glyphs.py, run in C by native/vvfp_unicode_text/glyphs.inc) as new rows under the loaded picture and new entries in a copy of the glyph table. Text is read by one rule (src/vv_game_text.py, native/vvfp_unicode_text/text_utf8.h): a well-formed UTF-8 sequence is its character, every other byte its Windows-1252 character, so every existing name reads as before. The width, draw, line-fitting, counted-draw and justified-paragraph routines are detoured: text without a multi-byte sequence goes to the game's own routine unchanged; other text is cut into whole units (grapheme clusters; shaped runs of Arabic, Hebrew, Indic and other scripts) and drawn in runs by the game's own draw and width routines, from the font's own letters or from pages of letters made at run time (Uniscribe shaping, GDI glyphs, COLR colour layers for emoji) in the font's size and baseline. Each detoured text routine first offers the text to VvfpTranslateText of "VVFP Translations.dll" when that companion is loaded (fails open), and shows a long name's short form as the whole name. Line breaking follows UAX #14 by Windows' own icu.dll (loaded from System32 only; a built-in table where Windows has none): a text with Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar or emoji breaks between whole characters where the rules allow (never before a closing mark or small kana, never after an opening one; Thai and the others at their words, inside a shaped run too), other text at spaces, and a word wider than the line after its longest start of whole characters that fits. Without icu.dll, Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between the words of ICU's own word lists ("Word Lists" beside the companion, read the first time a line of that script is broken; a missing list leaves the built-in table). The screen edge: a text drawn by the companion, expanded from a long name's short form, or drawn while a translation is in use is measured where the game draws it (x is its left edge after the game's own alignment); a line that would cross the right edge of the 800-pixel window (or of a narrower surface) is drawn as its longest start of whole units that fits with "…" after it, a text partly left of the window is drawn from its left edge, a justified paragraph is laid out no wider than the room to the edge, and when not even one unit fits the game's English is drawn. The widths the game is told are unchanged. The SDL_TEXTINPUT case (0x40444B) posts a typed ASCII character exactly as before; any other well-formed text is handed whole to the focused text box, which stores each character whole (a Windows-1252 character as its one byte, any other as UTF-8) while it fits the box's limit. Backspace erases a whole unit. A box never cuts its text by pixels. Every box's limit is 1200 bytes; a text longer than the field GetText copies it to leaves as a short form: its longest start of whole characters, then "..." ("2...", "3...", the number first, when another long name has it; the older short forms ending in … stay readable), whose whole text is appended to the save's Long Names file and given back when the game puts the short form into a box.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces each routine's first instructions at run time, all of them or none, only after verifying their stock bytes, and installs nothing on a different build. The game's pictures (Images\ldwBurweed27.png, Images\ldwarialbold.png) are never changed and nothing of the game's art is shipped; letters are made in memory from the player's own Windows fonts and, for what they lack, from the bundled open fonts (Unicode Fonts folder), which are added to the game's process only (FR_PRIVATE) and never installed in Windows; a missing or unreadable font file only leaves its step out. A save's records only ever hold what fits their fields: every stock copy of a name sees the short form, never more bytes than the stock game wrote. Nothing is cut inside a character. A fault in any detour falls back to the game's own routine with the game's own text.
- Dependencies: vv3_details_full_names
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Scrolling Popups (`vv3_scrolling_popups`)

Popups get scrollbars when their text does not fit: a popup is never taller or wider than the screen (its buttons stay at its bottom, where they always are), and when its text is taller than the room left, or wider than the box (a long line, or one very long word), a vertical and/or a horizontal scrollbar appears, drawn with the game's own scrollbar pictures. Scroll with the mouse wheel over the popup, the arrows, by dragging the knob or by clicking the bar; the text starts at the top and starts over when it changes. A popup whose text fits looks and works exactly as before. This covers the island-event popups (and Custom Island Events from Story / Cheat Upgrades, which use them), message boxes (tech and puzzle results, confirmations), tips (the tutorial and notices), the tombstone (a long name or cause of death scrolls sideways) and the Roster of the Dead and Create Nickname (a long translation or name scrolls sideways). The Options panel (each label sits beside its slider or button, which cannot scroll with it) and the panels with no text body (Change Player, the outfit chooser) are as the game draws them. There is no keyboard scrolling. Nothing is saved, so the patch can be ticked or unticked at any time. **Needs no other patch.** Off by default; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.** The companion is "VVFP Scrolling Popups.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if it cannot be loaded, the popups are as the game draws them.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The island-event dialog (constructor 0x4192F0): its `call 0x40DDD0` sizing the panel (0x41983F) calls VVFP Scrolling Popups.dll, which caps the height to the screen's (600 px, read from the drawing context) less 16 px above and below; the game then centres the panel and places its buttons from the bottom. Its draw's `call 0x40A0C0` drawing the body text (0x418591) calls the companion, which measures the text with that same routine (measure only) and its words with the game's counted draw; when the text fits the box (the panel's bottom less the room the dialog keeps for its buttons: 4 x a choice button's height with two choices, else 5/2 x the OK button's) it makes the stock call unchanged; otherwise it sets the drawing context's clip rectangle (+0x60) to the box, draws the text moved by the scroll position, restores the clip, and draws the scrollbars with the game's own pictures. A word wider than the text box (a long unbroken word) hangs the stock game: its justified paragraph backs off to an empty line and tries the same word again, for ever. The constructor's four measures of the dialog's texts (0x419611, 0x419648, 0x419681, 0x4197F7, `call 0x40A0C0`, measure only) call the companion, which gives the paragraph the width of the text's widest word when that is wider than the box (the words measured with the game's counted draw, cut where the paragraph cuts them); the draw wraps at that same width and the box scrolls sideways. The message box (vtable 0x47F3AC, laid out by 0x41C3A0): its `call 0x40DDD0` sizing the panel (0x41C53F) calls the companion, which keeps the size asked for and caps the width and the height to the screen's (800 x 600, read from the drawing context) less 16 px on each side; the game then centres the panel and places its text and buttons as always. The text control draw's `call 0x40A060` drawing a control's text (0x40D807) calls the companion: the text of a message box whose panel was capped (the control's parent has the message box's vtable and asked for more than the screen holds) is drawn under a clip rectangle set to the room the box keeps for it (0x14 below the panel's top, 0x1E from its sides, above its buttons), moved by the scroll position, with the scrollbars beside it; every other text, and a message box's text that fits, is the stock call unchanged. The tip (vtable 0x47F454): its `call 0x40DDD0` sizing the panel (0x41DFF1) is capped the same way. The frame draw's tail (0x40E013, `mov edx, [esi]` to the `jmp` into the dialog's body draw) jumps to the companion, which makes the same pops and calls the body draw: a tip that asked for more than the screen holds has its body drawn with its panel rectangle (+0x14..+0x20, which the body draw places everything by) moved by the scroll position and by what the capped panel moved its centred contents, under a clip set to the box (0x24 from the sides, 0x0A below the top, above twice the OK button's height), the rectangle put back after, with the scrollbars; every other dialog's body is called exactly as before. The tip's per-line `call 0x40A0C0` (0x41E433) is given the widest word's width when that is wider than the box, so the stock hang on a long word cannot happen there. The tombstone (vtable 0x47F498, a fixed panel): each line is a text control. At the text control draw's call (0x40D807) a line whose window is the tombstone is measured with all the tombstone's other lines (its window's text controls, as the text control draw places them); when one runs past the panel's sides (a long name, a long cause, a translation), each line is drawn moved by the scroll position under a clip 16 px in from the sides and above the Done button, with a horizontal bar below the lines; the editable epitaph and every tombstone that fits are drawn exactly as before. The same for the Roster of the Dead (vtable 0x47F2C0), Create Nickname (vtable 0x47F344): at the text control draw's call (0x40D807) a line of one of these panels is measured with all the panel's lines (its window's text controls); when one runs past the panel's sides, every line is drawn moved by the scroll position under a clip 16 px in from the sides, above the controls in the panel's lower half (its buttons, a text box), with a horizontal bar below the lines; text boxes, buttons and every panel that fits are drawn exactly as before. The event pump's `call 0x4020A0` handing a mouse event to the game (0x40451E) calls the companion first: a press on a scrollbar of the popup drawn this moment, a knob drag and its release are used by the companion and not passed on; every other event goes to the game unchanged. The wheel is read by an SDL event watch (SDL_AddEventWatch, SDL_MOUSEWHEEL). The scrollbars are the game's own pictures (image ids 0x1B-0x1E, 0x19, 0x1A): Up/DownArrowButton, VerticalScrollTrack fitted to the bar's height, VerticalScrollKnob; the horizontal bar is WideSlider2 fitted to the vertical track's width (18 px) with sliderhandle fitted to the knob's size turned sideways.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion writes its sites at run time, only after verifying their stock bytes and the instructions before them (all of them, or none). A popup whose text fits is drawn by the very same call as in the stock game; the popups' text fields keep their sizes; keys, the buttons, the events and the save are unchanged.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the companion emulated on the published executable's own popup code with the game's own fonts and pictures (tests/test_scrolling_popups.py: the panel capped, the clip set and restored, wheel, arrows, knob drag and track clicks moving the drawn lines, the buttons at the panel's bottom, a fitting text drawn exactly as the stock game draws it); runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Story / Cheat Upgrades (`vv3_story_cheat_upgrades`)

Adds optional tools intended for custom stories, experiments, sandbox play, and cheats. These features deliberately allow the player to bypass normal game progression and random-event behavior. When enabled, all Origins Upgrades cost 0 Tech Points. Also adds the following Origins Upgrades: Pick Island Event -- Allows the player to directly choose which stock Island Event occurs instead of relying on random selection. Opening this upgrade displays a list of the game's official Island Event titles, each with a brief description. Selecting an event causes that specific event to occur through the game's Island Event system. Custom Island Event -- Allows the player to create and trigger a custom Island Event for storytelling, testing, sandbox play, or cheats. The player may customize supported event properties, including: Title and description; Food gained or lost; Tech Points gained or lost; Villagers spawned; Spawned-villager details, including supported appearance, age, sex, name, likes/dislikes, skills, and other valid villager attributes; Villager behavior or state changes; Village-state changes; Puzzle-state changes; Other game-specific values that can be safely and reliably manipulated. Custom events should appear and behave as closely as practical to ordinary Island Events, while clearly allowing player-defined outcomes. Only what this game's own code supports is offered; the rest is shown as not available in this game. A custom title is kept per save slot in a file beside the saves and is removed by Start Over. Bought island events don't change when the game's own island events come. A Custom Island Event can also be bought and delivered when everyone in the village has died (the game's own island events wait for a living villager), so new villagers, food, Tech Points, refills and revived skeletons can bring the village back; what needs a living villager is simply not there to choose, and a question with two choices is refused until someone lives. In A New Home and The Lost Children a village that died before its first island event gets it too, uncounted, so its first island event is still the game's own visitor once someone lives. A custom event can also ask a question with two choices: the player writes the question, the two button labels and, for each button, one to four outcomes, each with its own chance, result text and changes (everything the event itself can change); clicking a button rolls one of its outcomes by those chances and makes only that outcome's changes. **A question with two choices can be queued only in a game whose own two-button island-event popup the companion hooks; in any other game the option is shown as not available yet.** Pick Island Event also lets the player set how the picked event turns out. Each setting starts at "Random (original game)" and offers only what that event's own code can produce in this game: its result (for a two-choice event, the result of each choice -- the popup still appears and the player still clicks), every amount it can roll, who a roll it makes for each villager hits (nobody, everyone, or the villagers chosen), which villager it is about, and each baby's details; in A New Home and The Lost Children also its strength (normally a third of the population, 1 to 10). A setting whose condition does not hold right now can not be bought. An event whose own condition is only a matter of timing or story can be picked anyway, and developer-dead events proven to work are offered as never happening in the original game; events that need something the village lacks, or room for new villagers, stay locked with the reason. On by default, with Story / Cheat Upgrades cost Tech Points ticked too, so the upgrades keep their normal tech-point prices until that row is unticked. **Requires Enable Origins Tech, Details, and Village-Wide Upgrades: ticking this ticks it, and without it there are no Origins Upgrades to make free and no Pick Island Event or Custom Island Event.** **A pregnancy a custom event starts is written to the Births and Conceptions log only with Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File ticked.** Also adds Choose Time Skip Amount (0 Tech Points, the same as Time Warp): the player types how many years to skip, from 1 to 72, and the village moves forward that many villager years as a run of the Time Warp upgrade's own advance -- one Time Warp at a time (3 years on slow, 6 on normal, 12 on fast, the last one only what is left), each caught up by the game before the next -- so villagers work, eat, have babies, grow up and die of old age through the skipped years just as after a Time Warp. **Keep the game running until the skip is done: it pauses while the game is paused, and loading another village, Start Over or deleting the tribe drops the rest.** Cancel charges nothing. Also adds Recharge Chief Powers (0 Tech Points, the same as Pick Island Event): the Tribal Chief's once-a-day powers (granting food, educating the children, pointing out a rare collectible) are ready to use at once, exactly as when a villager first becomes the chief; the next use rests the power for a day as usual. Refused, with nothing spent, when the village has no chief, the chief has no powers yet (Leadership level 0), or every power is ready already.

**Requires Enable Origins Tech, Details, and Village-Wide Upgrades: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this. Needed by Story / Cheat Upgrades cost Tech Points: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: Every Origins upgrade on the Tech screen and the Villager Details screen costs 0 tech points: each price the Origins payload compares, deducts, refunds or shows is set to 0 at run time, and the Origins companion shows and charges 0. Every existing refusal stays: one pending Island Event or Barrel of Babies at a time, room for the Barrel's children, and every "nothing to change" check. A bought island event (the Origins Island Event, Pick Island Event, Custom Island Event) counts as pending until the game's own island-event trigger runs it -- the Origins companion's keeper of the island timer knows it from the purchase's write until the trigger's own (native/shared/island_timer_keep.h) -- not only while the timer is due within the purchase's five seconds, which the paused Tech screen outlasts.  A Custom Island Event is never held by it: it is delivered first and the bought or picked event it went ahead of is made due again right after it, each charged once; a waiting Barrel of Babies is never replaced (it comes first).  With nobody the trigger accepts (a count of 0, or no villager its own draw takes), the custom event is delivered all the same, so its new villagers always arrive; changes for villagers who are not there are skipped and the popup says so.  It is never held for a new village's two opening island events: it comes first, uncounted, and they still come after it as the game makes them. Adds a Choose Time Skip Amount upgrade (the Time Warp's price: 0 tech points, or 50,000 with Story / Cheat Upgrades cost Tech Points) to the Origins Tech menu: a plain Windows dialog takes 1-72 years (20 age units a year), and the Origins companion's own Time Warp advance runs in steps of at most one Time Warp at the current speed, the next step only once the game's villager tick has replayed the last (its catch-up), so no jump is bigger than a Time Warp.  Charged once, when the first step is made; Cancel, a paused game or an empty village charge nothing. Adds a Pick Island Event upgrade (0 tech points) to the Origins Tech menu: a plain Windows list of this game's island events by their official titles, each with a one-line description.  The pick makes the island event due exactly as the Island Event upgrade does (the same pending lock), and when the game's own scheduler fires it, the game's own chooser runs the picked event -- only if that event's own condition holds -- with its own text, choices, random outcomes and amounts. Offers 57 island events; events that can never run in this game are not offered. Adds a Custom Island Event upgrade (0 tech points): plain Windows dialogs build an event (title, description, village changes, new villagers, per-villager changes for a list with extended selection and the group toggles All Adult Women, All Adult Men, All Females, All Males and All Children, plus in New Believers All Heathens and one toggle for each Heathen type; each villager's row names the role the game keeps for them, such as the Golden Child or the Tribal Chief).  It is queued exactly as the Island Event upgrade queues one (the same lock), and when the game's own scheduler fires it, the game's own island-event popup shows the custom title and description and the changes are made through the game's own routines. Its amounts list shows each amount the game keeps as it is now, below 0 included (The Lost Children's fish and the field's protection fall below 0 in the original game), and the event replaces it; only a store that is not there yet, such as a farm not yet built, reads "not there yet" and is refused. Villager Changes offers every villager action the game's own code can start for one villager, Celebrating included, grouped (work, leisure, celebration and dance, devotion, family, children, health, curiosity, moods, puzzles and story) and sorted, each labelled with the text the Details screen then shows; the villager is stopped first and the game's own starter runs.  An action that may harm the game or the save ends "(Unsafe)": choosing it shows the reason and advises backing up the save (OK / Cancel), and one that would need a missing object is refused when the event happens instead of crashing. New villagers and babies are made only while the game's own room predicate says the village has room, so the population cap of the installed mode is never passed. A new tribe's first two island events are always the game's own (each game's village start sets its island-event counter to 0): a custom event queued before the second of them stays queued -- the same lock, nothing charged again -- without making the island event due, and is made due exactly as the Island Event upgrade does once the game has made both, so it is the third. A village where everyone has died (the game's own population count is 0; in New Believers the believers): the game keeps running but its island-event trigger does nothing while that count is 0.  The trigger's call of the count is retargeted to a stub that runs it unchanged; only when it answers 0 and a plain Custom Island Event is queued for this village does the trigger go on past its villager draw (as if one had been drawn), so the game reschedules, plays its sound, counts the event, builds it and shows its own popup with the custom event.  New Believers' selector, when no stock event is possible, goes to its delivery site with the custom event the same way (its two stock trophy calls first).  The purchase allows an empty village (a question with two choices is refused: it needs a living villager), an empty village does not wait for the two opening island events.  A New Home's and The Lost Children's trigger makes a village's first island event the game's visitor: an empty village that has had none resumes past that check too, and the delivery takes the trigger's count of it back (as for the time skip's notice), so Island Events Seen stays 0 and the visitor is still its first island event once someone lives. Pick Island Event's settings: each offered event can carry its result, every amount it rolls, who a per-villager roll hits, which villager it is about and each baby's details (A New Home and The Lost Children: also its strength), each defaulting to Random (original game).  The companion points the event's own rand() calls at a stub that answers the chosen value only in that roll's phase (before the popup, the popup, or the event's apply), for the clicked choice, and -- in a routine other code shares -- only inside the event's own call to it; the outcome ends when the event's apply returns, on refusal and on lapse, so no chosen value reaches a natural event. Unlocked picks: an event whose own condition is only timing or story (proven by running its popup and apply with the condition false) can be picked anyway; its condition is passed for that one delivery only.  Developer-dead events proven to work are offered as never happening in the original game. A custom title replaces a villager's title in the villager panel and is printed in the Village Population and Village History logs; it is kept per save slot in Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save N\Data\Custom Titles\Custom Titles - Save N.dat and deleted by Start Over. Adds a Recharge Chief Powers upgrade (the Island Event upgrade's price: 0 tech points, or 30,000 with Story / Cheat Upgrades cost Tech Points) to the Origins Tech menu: each of the Tribal Chief's three once-a-day powers whose next-use time (world +0x12F00 food, +0x12EFC lessons, +0x12EF8 rare collectible) is still ahead of the game's clock gets the game's own ready value 0, which the robe's success writes when a villager becomes the chief.  Refused with nothing written or charged when there is no living chief (the game's own chief test 0x45FC00), at Leadership level 0, or when every power is ready already.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched; the companion writes the listed sites at run time after verifying every one of them, and writes nothing if any differs. No stock event is emulated: a picked event is created, shown and resolved by the game's own code; a custom event is shown by the game's own island-event popup. Pick Island Event adds no tech points and writes nothing to the save; a custom event changes only what the player chose, through the game's own routines and fields, and the game saves the village as usual. No custom title is written into a villager record. An empty village with nothing queued, and every village with anyone alive, runs the island-event trigger exactly as stock; the game's own "Your tribe has been lost! Game over." status line and its tips are left as they are.
- Dependencies: vv3_origins_village_wide_upgrades
- Evidence status: static exact-build verification and emulation of the rendered executables and the companion; runtime/player confirmation pending
