#### Translations (`vv3_translations`)

Plays the game in another language. Choose a language for each game in Tools > Translations... (or make your own there: the patcher writes a file with every English line of the game, its menus, events, tips, tech names and the patcher's own windows, and a built-in editor shows each line in the game's font). The game uses the chosen language from its next start, with no re-patching; lines a translation leaves out, or gets wrong, stay English. Gender and plural words follow the villager or the number (for example il / elle, 1 pomme / 2 pommes). **On by default, and English until you choose a language: with English chosen the game is exactly as without this patch.** **Letters beyond plain English (accents, Turkish ğ ş ı, Greek, Cyrillic, Chinese, Japanese, Cuneiform, emoji) need "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" or "Use Unicode Font"; without either, the game's own font draws only plain English letters and the rest show as "?".** **With one of those two rows a translated line never runs off the screen (it is cut with "…" at the window's edge, though it may run past its own box); without them the game draws it as it is.** **Words painted into pictures (buttons, the title screen, help pages) stay English.** **Every patch's own text is translated too: its windows and messages, Custom Island Event popups, Cause of Death words and epitaphs, Son/Daughter, and the text the exe patches write; log files stay English.** **Works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Not yet seen in a running game.** The companion is "VVFP Translations.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if it cannot be loaded, or the game's text is not the version a translation was made from, those lines stay English.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: At game start the companion reads "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Files\Translation\Translation.txt" (written by the patcher's Translations window; docs/translation-file-format.md). With no such file it returns at once and writes nothing. Each translated line replaces the English where the game looks it up: the string table at 0x4AB990: each translated entry's loaded-text pointer (+0xC), after the loader; the visible literals outside the table by the address their loading instruction pushes (data/translations/vv3_strings.json).  A line is used only when the English it was made from is the English this game shows (the key's SHA-256), its placeholders match and its selects are well formed. The patcher's own windows (Origins, Story / Cheat Upgrades, Custom Island Event) are translated as they open (a WH_CALLWNDPROCRET hook on the game's own thread, only when the file translates any of them); a message put together from several lines is translated line by line. The companions that build a text the game shows (Cause of Death's words and epitaphs, Story / Cheat Upgrades' island event lines and Time Skip notice, Show Parents' Son / Daughter, Storytelling, Both Factions) ask for it by its line's key (VvfpTranslateKey / VvfpTranslateKeyText, native/shared/vvfp_translate.h): the translation is used only when the English is the line's and it fits the companion's own buffer, else the English. Text an exe patch wrote ("patch/0x<va>" lines, data/translations/exe_patch_strings.json) is written over in place when the translation fits the English's own bytes (through the same all-or-none writer, after checking the live text is the line's English); a longer one is left English there. Without "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" or "Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts)" (their companion's VvfpGlyphsUtf8; Use Unicode Font's, which starts later, is loaded and started on first use), translations are given to the game in Windows-1252, '?' for what it cannot write.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the companion checks each site's stock bytes and writes them at run time through the shared all-or-none writer, and writes only the ones the chosen file needs; if any check fails it writes nothing, not even a table pointer, and the game stays English. No save, record or game file is written; the game's own English text stays in memory unchanged. With English chosen (no Translation.txt), nothing at all is written.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Tribal Chief Lessons Stop at 50 (`vv3_chief_lessons_cap_50`)

The Tribal Chief's lessons stop at 50. Each child who finishes a lesson still gains 7 to 9 points in one random skill, but only a skill still below 50 can be chosen, and the gain stops at exactly 50; a skill already at 50 or above is never chosen and never lowered. When every skill is at 50 the lesson awards nothing. This matches the Nursery Schools of the later games, which skip any skill at 50. The Secret City has no companion that runs every frame, so this row diverts the lesson award's first seven bytes into a small stub in the page Origins appends, which calls "VVFP Lesson Cap.dll"; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock lesson runs and trains to 100. **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked; the Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically.**

- Behavior changes: When a child finishes a Tribal Chief lesson (callback 42), the companion counts the skills below 50, asks the game's own RNG for one of them and for the stock 7 to 9 points, adds them and stops at exactly 50. With every skill at 50 or above the lesson awards nothing.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row diverts one seven-byte instruction pair in the lesson award into a stub in the page Origins appends; the stub resolves the companion once and otherwise replays the stock bytes, so with the DLL missing the stock lesson runs (capped at 100). A skill at or above 50 is never lowered; work-task training past 50 is untouched. The lesson itself -- who teaches, who attends, its length, its animation and its messages -- is the game's own; only the award at its end changes. Nothing is written to a villager record beyond the skill the lesson would have written, nor to the save or any file.
- Dependencies: vv3_enable_origins_exclusive_features
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 1; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.
- Appends 4096 bytes as 1 new PE section -- `.vv3lc` (executable code) -- and rewrites 3 guarded header regions (46 bytes) of the PE headers to map them; the appended bytes and every header change carry an exact before/after guard in the manifest.
- When vv3_enable_origins_exclusive_features is also selected it appends nothing, writing its payload into that feature's reserved zero range instead; the range is checked against a declared zero preimage before anything is written.

#### Tribal Chief Supervises the Hospital (`vv3_chief_hospital_supervision`)

Dropping the Tribal Chief on the Hospital hotspot (Medicine level 2 or more) makes him walk to the spot where he stands when he is "Concerned about the sick" and do the game's own "Directing work" action there; in the stock game he does nothing and picks another task. While he directs work there, a healer who finishes studying medicine at the hospital gains twice the usual Medicine skill points (at least 1); the chance to learn is not changed, so this does not stack with the Medicine technology's cure bonus. A healer whose cure roll fails also gets a second chance: the chief's supervision roll, which passes about 25% of the time per Leadership level, lets the cure go ahead as if the healer had passed. The stock game gives the chief that supervision bonus for fishing, fruit, honey, huts, research and puzzles, but never for a cure. **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.** This patch needs no other row and does not add the Origins Upgrades buttons. It is on by default for The Secret City; untick it to keep the stock game. The companion is "VVFP VV3 Chief Hospital.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock game runs.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The chief's site switch 0x458C70 gives site 9 (the Hospital, written by the drop handler 0x4215E0 at 0x4215F6) the stock Directing-work order (0x458D4C: action 0x81, handler 0x44B5F0, text 0x219 eSayDirectWork "Directing work") instead of clearing the site at 0x458D0B: the index byte at 0x458D94 becomes 0x0B, the index the other directed sites use. In the Directing-work handler, site 9 stands where "Concerned about the sick" stands (action 0x8A, handler 0x452540, text 0x1E4: (0x47B + rand(0x96), 0x665 + rand(0x32))): the handler's bases become 0x47B + rand(0x79) and 0x665 + rand(0x15), so its walks of base + rand(0x1E) stay inside that area, and the handler's own plain pose (0x44B86B) runs. Studying medicine (action 0xBD, handler 0x451890) ends with a Medicine practice step (script op 7, skill 2, run at 0x462051 as 0x45A2C0); when that step succeeds while the chief is alive, not sick, on site 9 and doing action 0x81, the Medicine points it adds (0x45A753, written by 0x455740, capped at 100) are doubled, and at least 1. When a healer's Healing roll in a cure fails (the roll at 0x457395), the game asks the chief's supervision roll 0x45FC60 for the Hospital site (9). That roll passes only when the Tribal Chief is alive, not sick, standing on the hospital hotspot (+0xEA0 = 9), and rand(100) < 25 x Leadership level; then the cure continues as a passed Healing roll does. A passed Healing roll is unchanged, and so is every cure when no chief is on the hospital: the supervision roll then draws nothing from the game's random generator.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: VVFP VV3 Chief Hospital.dll verifies the stock bytes at each place and writes its changes at run time; a different build of the game installs nothing. The Directing-work changes are installed all together or not at all. The chief's supervision is unchanged everywhere else: fishing, fruit, honey, huts, research and puzzles keep their stock bonuses, and the chief still never picks a job. Every other site's Directing work, the chief's other choices and their order are stock: when a villager is doing action 0x2D the chief still does "Concerned about the sick" (0x45BDED) before directing work, as in the stock game. The Medicine learning chance, cures, other skills and every other villager's study are unchanged; the bonus applies only to the study step of a villager on action 0xBD. A healer who dislikes medicine still fails half of their cures, as in the stock game; a chief's success is a pass of the Healing roll, not a guaranteed cure. Catch-up healing (the cure scan at 0x45B94A) is not changed by this row. Nothing is written to a villager record, the save or any file.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts) (`vv3_unicode_font`)

Draws ALL of the game's text in a Windows typeface instead of the game's own bitmap fonts: Segoe UI unless you choose another in the patcher (the Unicode Font box, or the Tools tab's Unicode Font... window: any installed family, or a .ttf, .otf or .ttc file; the choice is written next to the game as "VVFP Unicode Font.txt"), with Windows' fallback chain for every character it lacks (Segoe UI, Segoe UI Historic, Segoe UI Symbol, Segoe UI Emoji (in colour), the CJK fonts, Nirmala UI, Ebrima ..., Noto if installed, then the bundled open fonts: Noto Sans Cuneiform, Noto Serif Tangut, GNU Unifont, Unifont Upper and last Last Resort). Each of the game's two fonts keeps its line height, baseline and weight, and its size is fitted so a line is as wide as the game's own, so every screen keeps its layout; every character works, as with "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts". **Text and translations never run off the screen:** a line this patch, a long name or a translation draws that would cross the edge of the game's 800-pixel-wide window is cut there with "…" (whole letters only; a justified paragraph wraps at the edge instead), and one that would start left of the window starts at its edge; it may still run past its own box. Without a translation, the game's own English is drawn exactly as before. This needs this row: with Translations alone (no Unicode row) the game draws by itself and nothing is fitted. Where Windows has no icu.dll (before Windows 10 1903), Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between words by ICU's own word lists (ICU 77.1, Unicode License; about 4.4 MB in "Word Lists", read only when such a line is broken). Typing: every text box -- the tribe name, villager names on the Details screen, epitaphs -- takes any character Windows sends (dead keys, Alt codes, the Windows emoji panel, an input method for Japanese or Chinese), each stored whole or not at all, and Backspace erases a whole character (a whole emoji, flag or accented letter). Long names, everywhere: every name box takes names up to 1,200 bytes (up to 1,200 plain letters; fewer when letters need more bytes): the tribe name, villager names on the Details screen, epitaphs; Rename Tribe takes the same. It is one limit, shared with the other Fun Patchers. Characters are counted as you see them (a letter with its accents, an emoji with its skin tone or a flag is one), and Backspace removes one whole character. A long name scrolls in its box while you type it. The save itself is not changed: a name that fits its field (a villager's name 23 bytes, the tribe name 19) is kept there exactly as before; a longer one is kept there as its short form (its start and a mark, with a number when two would start alike) and the whole name is kept beside the save, in Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Long Names. The game shows the whole name wherever it shows that name. Back Up Saves, Restore Saves and Copy Player Slot carry the Long Names files with the saves. With both settings off the game still loads and plays such a save and shows the short form. Characters are stored as UTF-8 (a Western European letter keeps its one Windows-1252 byte), so every older name reads as before; the base game and older patchers show other characters as odd letters but never break. **Off by default and in Owner's Defaults.** **Cannot be used with "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" (ticking one unticks the other).** **Needs "Full Names on the Details Screen" (ticked with it): its Details box keeps the whole stored name, so opening a villager's Details and closing it never changes a name.** **Not yet seen in a running game** (checked by emulation of each stock executable). The companion is "VVFP Unicode Font.dll" (the same code as "VVFP Unicode Text.dll"), started by VVFP Startup.dll; the game's own pictures and saves are never changed, and no Windows font is shipped. **Bundles four open fonts, loaded privately by the game (never installed in Windows): GNU Unifont 18.0.01 (GPL-2.0-or-later with the font exception, or OFL-1.1) and Unifont Upper for nearly every assigned character, Noto Sans Cuneiform and Noto Serif Tangut (OFL-1.1), and Last Resort 18.000 (OFL-1.1), a placeholder block for anything still without a glyph; about 14 MB of fonts (in the patcher's files folder, in "Unicode Fonts", with their licence texts and sources), copied once per game folder, and not again when the folder already has identical files.**

**Requires Full Names on the Details Screen: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this.**

- Behavior changes: The font constructor (0x402510) runs unchanged; for the game's two fonts -- ldwBurweed27 (stock glyph table 0x4A5B78) and ldwarialbold (0x4A6A80) -- the companion records the font's line height, baseline, capital height and pixel format. Their own letters are not used: every letter is made from the chosen Windows typeface. Text is read by one rule (src/vv_game_text.py, native/vvfp_unicode_text/text_utf8.h): a well-formed UTF-8 sequence is its character, every other byte its Windows-1252 character, so every existing name reads as before. The width, draw, line-fitting, counted-draw and justified-paragraph routines are detoured: text without a multi-byte sequence goes to the game's own routine unchanged (with this patch, every text is drawn by the companion); other text is cut into whole units (grapheme clusters; shaped runs of Arabic, Hebrew, Indic and other scripts) and drawn in runs by the game's own draw and width routines, from the font's own letters or from pages of letters made at run time (Uniscribe shaping, GDI glyphs, COLR colour layers for emoji) in the font's size and baseline. Each detoured text routine first offers the text to VvfpTranslateText of "VVFP Translations.dll" when that companion is loaded (fails open), and shows a long name's short form as the whole name. Line breaking follows UAX #14 by Windows' own icu.dll (loaded from System32 only; a built-in table where Windows has none): a text with Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar or emoji breaks between whole characters where the rules allow (never before a closing mark or small kana, never after an opening one; Thai and the others at their words, inside a shaped run too), other text at spaces, and a word wider than the line after its longest start of whole characters that fits. Without icu.dll, Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between the words of ICU's own word lists ("Word Lists" beside the companion, read the first time a line of that script is broken; a missing list leaves the built-in table). The screen edge: a text drawn by the companion, expanded from a long name's short form, or drawn while a translation is in use is measured where the game draws it (x is its left edge after the game's own alignment); a line that would cross the right edge of the 800-pixel window (or of a narrower surface) is drawn as its longest start of whole units that fits with "…" after it, a text partly left of the window is drawn from its left edge, a justified paragraph is laid out no wider than the room to the edge, and when not even one unit fits the game's English is drawn. The widths the game is told are unchanged. The SDL_TEXTINPUT case (0x40444B) posts a typed ASCII character exactly as before; any other well-formed text is handed whole to the focused text box, which stores each character whole (a Windows-1252 character as its one byte, any other as UTF-8) while it fits the box's limit. Backspace erases a whole unit. A box never cuts its text by pixels. Every box's limit is 1200 bytes; a text longer than the field GetText copies it to leaves as a short form: its longest start of whole characters, then "..." ("2...", "3...", the number first, when another long name has it; the older short forms ending in … stay readable), whose whole text is appended to the save's Long Names file and given back when the game puts the short form into a box.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces each routine's first instructions at run time, all of them or none, only after verifying their stock bytes, and installs nothing on a different build. The game's pictures (Images\ldwBurweed27.png, Images\ldwarialbold.png) are never changed and nothing of the game's art is shipped; letters are made in memory from the player's own Windows fonts and, for what they lack, from the bundled open fonts (Unicode Fonts folder), which are added to the game's process only (FR_PRIVATE) and never installed in Windows; a missing or unreadable font file only leaves its step out. A save's records only ever hold what fits their fields: every stock copy of a name sees the short form, never more bytes than the stock game wrote. Nothing is cut inside a character. A fault in any detour falls back to the game's own routine with the game's own text.
- Dependencies: vv3_details_full_names
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Villagers Have Last Names (`vv3_last_names`)

Babies born in the village and the village's founders get a last name after their first name, from the game's own list of 50 last names (Akikai, Alosaka, Awanata ... Wikimak) -- a list the game has always carried but never used, and the one Virtual Villagers 6 and 7 later used for villagers' last names. A baby takes its father's or its mother's last name by the rule chosen in Repair Saves & Logs (Last names come from: from the father, from the mother, 50:50, or a random one of the last names the village has ever used); without a rule recorded, a baby takes its father's last name (the village's default is from the father). A villager can also have a rule of their own for their children (Each villager's own rule): from the father, from the mother, 50:50, a random last name from the list, which gives each child -- twins and triplets too -- its own random draw from the game's list, every name equally likely, or a random one of the village's existing last names. A villager's own rule always beats the village's; when both parents have one and they disagree, a coin toss for each child picks whose. Villagers who arrive through an island event get no last name, because theirs would not be their family's. Only villagers named from now on get one: villagers who already have names keep them. The last name is part of the name the game stores, so it shows wherever the name does and stays in the save even if this patch is later removed. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: A baby born in the village from now on (a mother's delivery: the first child, a twin or a triplet) and a new village's founders are called "<first name> <last name>": the first name is the game's own pick, and the last name is name number <family - 1> of the game's unused third list (0X49DFF8), read from the running executable. A villager the game creates any other way -- brought by an island event, a cheat or the Origins page -- keeps the game's own first name only: the companion tells a birth or a founder by the callers' return addresses on the stack, at fixed places. A villager whose family is outside 1-50 gets no last name. At a birth, the rule recorded by Repair Saves & Logs decides the last name (VvfpRuleLastName2): the father's, the mother's, either at random (50:50), or -- a parent's own rule "Random last name from the list" -- a name drawn at random from the game's list, or -- "Random from the existing Village Names", the village's rule or a parent's own -- one of the last names the village has ever used (the record's "used" lines, the villagers in the game at the birth, VvfpRuleLastName3, and the parents'; the game's list when there are none); every random draw is a fresh, unbiased one for each child. Each such birth adds the names it saw that the record lacks as "used" lines (only adding, through a temporary file, never for a slot it cannot tell), so a name stays ever used after its last bearer is gone. A parent's own rule always beats the village's; parents whose own rules disagree: a fresh coin toss for each child picks the father's or the mother's. The whole name always fits the game's own name field: the longest pairing is far below its 23 characters.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion detours the naming routine's first instruction at run time, after verifying it, the routine's push of the list and the creators' calls to it, and changes nothing if any differs. Villagers who already have names keep them; nothing is renamed when a village is loaded. The first names, sexes, looks and families are the game's own; the save format is unchanged.

#### Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File (`vv3_write_parentage_log`)

Keeps a plain-text log of the village's conceptions and births in 'Virtual Villagers 3 Births and Conceptions Log <n>.txt', in the save slot's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Births and Conceptions' folder beside the game's saves (Documents\LDW\<game executable name>\); a shared 'Births and Conceptions' folder an older patcher wrote is kept as it was and still read. Each Conception record gives both parents' names, both parents' ages at conception, both head and body values, both parents' likes and dislikes, and the number of babies; the mother's age determines the child's age. Each Birth record, numbered like the Conceptions ("Birth 1", "Birth 2", ...), gives the child's name, head, body, likes, dislikes and skills, and its mother's and father's names, heads and bodies; Repair Saves & Logs can number the Birth records an older patcher wrote without one. A new numbered file is started after every 256 Conception records; Birth records go into the file holding the latest conceptions and do not count toward that limit. Each Arrived record, numbered on its own, gives a villager who joined the village without being born into it -- a new village's founders, an island event's newcomers, the Barrel of Babies, the Custom Island Event's new villagers (never a birth): their name, age when they arrived, sex, head, body, likes, dislikes and skills, and how they came ("Founder", the event's title, "Barrel of Babies", "Custom Island Event", or "unknown"); villagers who arrived before this record existed get one, marked "Recorded afterwards", only once the player chooses Repair when the village is loaded. **The Arrived records are found by the Cause of Death patch ("Log Every Death ..."): with it off, none is written.** A baby born with the full name of a living villager is numbered at its birth, before its Birth record is written ("Chip Kenobi" is born "Chip Kenobi II"; a number a dead or gone namesake had is never given again), while the village's "Number villagers who share a name automatically" is on (Repair Saves & Logs; on by default); the villager who already had the name becomes "I" -- with the dead, in the save and every log -- at the next Repair Saves & Logs, and a numbered name that would not fit the game's name limit is left for Repair Saves & Logs to show you. The game keeps both parents on the child's own record, and each Birth record reads them from there. VV3 keeps the father's name on the mother's record and no father id. His HEAD and BODY are copied onto her at conception, so the log reads them from her record and they are correct even after he dies or another villager takes his name. His AGE, which has no copy on her, is read from his own record at conception -- the conception hook reads the other parent's saved record -- so a normal birth records his real age.

**Needs Write Village Statistics to Text File or Log Every Death, Disappearance and Unaccounted Villager on for the village and savegame header at the top of the log, and for creating the log at a village's first save -- a new village, or one restarted with Start Over -- before anything is recorded (without either, records are still written correctly, just unlabelled, and the log first appears with its first record; Cause of Death names the village at each save itself). Needed by Log Every Death, Disappearance and Unaccounted Villager for the Deaths and Unaccounted Villagers logs, which that patch's DLL writes (without it neither is written). Needed by Write Island Events Log to Text File for the Island Events log, which that patch's DLL writes (without it nothing is written).**

#### Write Island Events Log to Text File (`vv3_island_events`)

Every change an island event makes to a villager is written to a new log, the Island Events log ("Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Island Events\Virtual Villagers 3 Island Events Log 1.txt"): one numbered record per villager it changed, with the event's title as the game shows it, the answer you picked when it asked, and each change as old -> new -- health, age, sickness, pregnancy, head, body, name, likes, dislikes, every skill, parents, custom title, mask and Special villager title, and Tribal Chief -- "Gone" for a villager the event took away, and the sex and age of a villager it brought. What an event changes in the village as a whole -- food, tech points, the fruit trees and honey, puzzles solved or unsolved and the weather -- is one record of its own, a "Village:" list of old -> new, and an event that changes nothing still gets its record, "Changes: none". A villager whose head or body an event changed also gets an "Appearance changed" record naming the event, so the Family Tree Maker knows the old and the new look are the same villager. A branching Custom Island Event from the library (Story / Cheat Upgrades), whose effects come page by page, is ONE record: its title, the answer picked, then every change in page order as "<name>: <change> <old> -> <new>"; at every save during it the log already holds the entry so far, and later pages continue that same entry, across a quit too, nothing twice. The records are written when the game saves, like the other logs. **Needs Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File: that patch's DLL writes the records.**

**Needs Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File on for the Island Events log, which that patch's DLL writes (without it nothing is written).**

- Behavior changes: When an island event runs, every villager is copied just before the game applies it and compared just after; each difference is one line of the villager's "Island event <n>" record. The village's food, tech points, food stores, puzzles and (where the game has one) weather are read just before and just after too; what changed is one "Island event <n>" record with a "Village:" list, and an event that changes nothing is one record ending "Changes: none". A villager the event brings is named with its sex and its age, in game units and years ("Age: 340 (17 years old)"). A head or body change is also an "Appearance changed" record in the Births and Conceptions log, ending "Changed by: <event> (island event)". A new village gets its Island Events log when it is made, like the other logs. A branching Custom Island Event (Story / Cheat Upgrades, story_graph.inc) brackets each page's own effects through this comparison (VvfpIslandEventsGraphBegin / End) and hands the event's one entry so far to the log after each page (VvfpIslandEventsGraphWrite -> the Parentage Export's WriteVillageEventEntry): "Event:", "Choice:", then each change as "<name>: <Label> <old> -> <new>" in page order. Its held record is replaced each time and each save writes what it has gained onto the same entry, append-only (a numbered first part left open, then only new lines, or a marked "(continued) Island event <n>" when another record came between), closed when the event is over; the game's own bracket around its popups writes nothing for them (VvfpStoryGraphLogged).
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion detours the routines' first instructions at run time, after verifying them, and installs nothing if any differs. The game's own routine runs unchanged, with the same registers and stack; the events, their odds and their effects are the game's own. Nothing is written without Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static exact-build verification of the event routines and the villager records in each executable; live-tested per game before release
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Write Village Statistics to Text File (`vv3_write_village_statistics`)

After each successful save of slots 1 through 5, writes the save's local lifetime statistics to 'Village Statistics v2 - Save N.txt' in the save slot's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Village Statistics' folder beside the game's saves (an earlier 'Village Statistics - Save N.txt' is kept unchanged). Counts the game does not keep are stored in per-save .dat files in each save's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save N\Data' folder. Later games retain the inherited per-save statistics block even where no Statistics screen is reachable; omitted stock bookkeeping is restored by exact gameplay hooks. Puzzle totals are read from the current save state during export so existing saves are reported accurately. These files are checked against what the save and the patcher's own logs prove -- Village Elders the Village History log shows with Master in three or more skills who are missing from the list, Villagers Buried below the Deaths log's burials or the graves, Chiefs Robed at 0 while a robed Tribal Chief lives -- and are changed only when the player says so -- Repair Saves & Logs in the patcher window, or Repair when the game asks as it closes (with "Check logs automatically" on, and only if something is wrong); nothing is ever asked while the village is played. Each file is backed up first (a copy '<file>.before-v1.35.58-repair' in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Data\Copies Made Before Repairs', at the file's own place), every change is listed in the Repairs log ('Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Repairs Made'; the shared 'Repairs Made' or 'Repairs' folder an older version made is kept as it was: nothing is moved), and a count is only ever raised and an elder never removed. The original save result is preserved, and text-export failure does not turn a successful game save into a failure. Start Over wipes everything the Fun Patcher kept for that save: all its logs (the Village History too), all its data (ElderTotems.dat too) and its family tree files. It keeps Backups, Copies Made Before Repairs and exported family tree pictures. Other saves are not touched.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File for the village and savegame header at the top of the log, and for creating the log at a village's first save -- a new village, or one restarted with Start Over -- before anything is recorded (without either, records are still written correctly, just unlabelled, and the log first appears with its first record; Cause of Death names the village at each save itself).**

## Virtual Villagers - The Tree of Life

### Automatic population and safety changes

Supported stock identity is the exact `Virtual Villagers - The Tree of Life.exe` build recorded in `data/builds.json`. The automatic edits are the selected population mode plus 18 guarded safety edits. The modified output retains the untouched stock executable beside the modified executable. Stock modes preserve vanilla save format; expanded modes use the documented guarded compatibility/conversion path.

### Optional features

#### 2-10x Sickness (`vv4_sickness_multiplier`)

**Needs no other patch.** Makes the game harder; off by default. Villagers fall sick 2 to 10 times as often as they would: you choose how many times with the 2-10x Sickness slider in the patcher window (a whole number, 2 unless you move it). Every natural chance of falling sick is multiplied, at every Medicine level and difficulty, the old villagers' extra chance included, and it stacks with the other patches (with Sickness works like VV1-3 it multiplies that rule's chances). Medicine, the fire, Easy's cures, healers, island events and everything that cures are unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The natural sickness roll's four moduli (Medicine 1, 2, 3 and the old villagers' roll) become round(stock / N), N the slider (2 to 10): each chance about N times as large.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The roll's thresholds, Medicine, the fire, the difficulty, Easy's cures, healers, events, the Hospital and every other health rule are unchanged; four immediates in place, written when the build is published.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; every multiplier on every site, stock and with Sickness works like VV1-3, is checked in tests/test_sickness_patches.py; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### 2-10x Tech Cost (`vv4_tech_cost_multiplier`)

Every technology level on the Tech screen costs 2 to 10 times its normal price in tech points: you choose the multiplier with the 2-10x Tech Cost slider in the patcher window (a whole number, 3 unless you move it). The normal prices are: Science level 2 8,000, level 3 70,000; Medicine level 2 5,000, level 3 50,000; Learning level 2 4,000, level 3 35,000; Construction level 2 5,000, level 3 65,000; Food Mastery level 2 3,000, level 3 40,000; Dendrology level 2 3,000, level 3 60,000. At x 3, for example, a 5,000-point level costs 15,000. The Tech screen shows the multiplied price, a purchase is refused (and nothing is spent) with fewer tech points than that, and buying takes exactly that many. Research, tech points from anywhere else, every other tech-point cost (such as clothes) and the patcher's own upgrades are unchanged. The higher you set it, the harder the game. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Classic VV Difficulty: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: Every non-zero entry of the technology price table 0x4BC18C, x N (the slider, 2 to 10; 3 by default). Its only reader is the getter 0x41E220, called by the Tech screen's hover label, information box and purchase (0x43E57D, 0x43E900, 0x43EA76): the shown price, the purchase's refusal threshold and the amount it takes are the same multiplied number.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: Each price is changed in place, same length; no code is added and no executable space is claimed. Research, tech points from island events and duplicate collectibles, every other tech-point cost (such as 5,000 for clothes) and the patcher's Origins and Story / Cheat upgrades keep their stock numbers.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 12; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### 256 Villagers (Experimental) (`vv4_population_256`)

EXPERIMENTAL. Gives The Tree of Life 256 villager slots (0 to 255) instead of 150. The game's villager table is moved to a new, larger place in memory and every part of the game that walks it -- births, island events, the Villager Details screen, saving and loading -- is widened to match. With Collection Progression Max Pop the cap becomes 231 plus the collection bonus (256 with everything); with Immediate Fixed Max Pop it is 256 at once; with No Population Increase the stock cap of 115 is unchanged, only the table is larger. The patched game is named "... - Modded 256" and keeps its saves, and the patcher's logs, in their own "Virtual Villagers - The Tree of Life - Modded 256" folder, so they never mix with 150-slot saves. The patcher does not copy saves into it: copy your save files from the "... - Modded" save folder yourself. An old save loads with all its villagers; the first time the game saves it, it is written in the longer 256 format, which only a 256 build can open, so keep the originals as a backup. **Needs Fix Vanilla Bugs on (it is on by default) to load a village that the base game's exactly-150-villager save bug has already damaged.** Off by default.

**Needs Fix Vanilla Bugs on for loading a village that the base game's exactly-150-villager save bug has already damaged (without it such a village does not load).**

- Behavior changes: The villager table has 256 slots; the population modes that raise the cap reach 256. Saves hold up to 256 villagers in a longer save file that only this build reads.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No Population Increase keeps the stock cap of 115. Nothing changes for a build that does not tick this patch.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static exact-build implementation with emulation of the replaced routines; live-tested with the game driven through its memory (an old save upgraded, filled to 256, triplets born into slots 253, 254 and 255, saved and reloaded); a hands-on live pass is pending
- Guarded executable edits: 453; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.
- Of those, 1 stands aside when Enable Origins-Exclusive Features (with Heathen Mask mod) (`vv4_enable_origins_exclusive_features`) is also selected: that patch already replaced the same stock bytes with its own detour, and the rewrite inside its code (counted below) covers the instruction it moved.
- Automatic safety edits: replaced, in every population mode, by its own 18 guarded safety edits for the 256-slot table.
- Population-mode edits: replaced by its own guarded rows, stock=0, collection_progression=1, immediate_fixed=1; only the selected mode's rows are applied.
- Guarded rewrites inside other selected patches' own code, applied only when that patch is also selected: Enable Origins-Exclusive Features (with Heathen Mask mod) (`vv4_enable_origins_exclusive_features`) 10, Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File (`vv4_write_parentage_log`) 2; each pattern must occur exactly that many times in the bytes that patch wrote, or nothing is written.
- Appends 4096 bytes of code (one page per population mode) as the new PE section `.vv256` at 0x7F0000, mapped as 0x323000 bytes whose remainder is zero-fill for the relocated villager table, the Details list and the save buffers; when the image ends before 0x7F0000, a zero-fill `.vv256z` section maps the gap. It rewrites 3 guarded regions of the PE headers to map them: the new section headers (40 bytes each), NumberOfSections and SizeOfImage. The appended bytes and every header change carry an exact before/after guard.

#### Builders and Healers Work First (`vv4_builders_and_healers_work_first`)

Builders and healers are more likely to do their own work first, at any food level -- about three times in four each time the game chooses what they do; the rest of the time the game chooses exactly as it always has, and the one roll is shared with Builders Fix Huts When Idle, so a choice is either all patched or all stock. When it steps in: whenever the game looks for something for a villager whose selected job is Building to do, it first tries building work (a project, or fixing a hut) while not every population hut is built -- and, in A New Home and The Lost Children below Building level 3, whenever any hut is built; for one whose selected job is Healing it always first tries healing and study, whenever there is a patient or they can study medicine (**in The Tree of Life, only once the Hospital has been built**). This comes before idling, farming or gathering. When there is nothing of their own to do, they do whatever the game would have had them do. This also applies during catch-up -- the time that passes while the game is closed, and Time Warp: each time catch-up chooses work for a builder or healer, about three times in four they are first given their own job (a builder only while it has hut work, as above), so they keep gaining skill while you are away; the rest of the time, and whenever there is nothing of theirs to do, catch-up's own choice stands. Villagers with any other job are untouched. Catch-up's low-food rule still wins: at 250 food or less a villager with Farming 20 or more farms, whatever their job. An addendum to Builders Fix Huts When Idle. **Requires Builders Fix Huts When Idle**, whose DLL loads this one (in The Secret City, whose stub does); ticking this ticks it, and it brings with it the Origins-exclusive base, which adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens.

**Requires Builders Fix Huts When Idle: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this.**

- Behavior changes: Whenever the adult scheduler asks the work dispatcher to start a job for a villager whose selected job is Healing (job 2), or Building (job 4) while it has hut work (a population hut unbuilt, or in A New Home and The Lost Children below Building level 3 any hut built), the dispatcher is first asked for that villager's own job; if that starts something the scheduler sees it started, and if there is nothing of theirs to do the scheduler's own request runs unchanged. At any food level; at 250 food or less in The Secret City, The Tree of Life and New Believers this includes the scheduler's farming attempt. About three times in four, not always: the companion asks the decision's roll that Builders Fix Huts When Idle draws once per choice of the idle scheduler (VvfpFixHutsRoll, handed over through VvfpWorkFirstSetRoll, or looked up by module name in The Secret City); when it fails, the scheduler's own request runs alone, exactly as the stock game. Catch-up (time passed while the game was closed, and Time Warp) never runs the idle scheduler: the catch-up worker (0x465750) dispatches the stock picker's job itself. Its pick dispatch (0x465827, returning to 0x46582C) is treated as the scheduler's calls are -- own job first, then the pick -- and its research pick (job 1), which never reaches the dispatcher, is tested at 0x46579F: for a builder or healer the own job is dispatched first and, if it starts something, the worker's own finish (its queue processor) runs instead of the stock research step. One 75% roll per catch-up decision: Builders Fix Huts When Idle wraps the worker as one decision, so VvfpFixHutsRoll gives every patch that decision reaches the same roll; when it fails, or there is nothing of theirs to do, the worker's stock code runs. At 250 food or less a healer's pick is also dispatched at once instead of waiting behind a farming attempt, as Builders Fix Huts When Idle already does for builders.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the fix-huts companion loads the DLL, which detours the work dispatcher and the catch-up worker's research-pick test at run time only after verifying the stock bytes; a different build of the game installs nothing. A builder or healer with nothing of their own to do does whatever the stock scheduler chose (farming, research, ...); the younger villagers' routine, every other caller of the dispatcher and every other selected job are untouched. A builder is put first only while it has hut work (a hut unbuilt, or in A New Home and The Lost Children below Building level 3 any hut built); a healer always. What the work does -- which project, which hut, which patient or study -- is the game's own dispatcher's choice. In catch-up, the worker's low-food Farming dispatch (0x46580A: 250 food or less and Farming 20 or more) is not one of the calls the hook acts on, so Farming wins exactly as in the stock game. Nothing is written to a villager record, the save or any file.

#### Builders Fix Huts When Idle (`vv4_builders_fix_huts`)

Builders fix huts when no building projects are present, and build first. This makes builders more likely to do their building work, not certain: each time the game chooses what a builder does, the patch steps in about three times in four, and the rest of the time the game chooses exactly as it always has. A villager whose job checkmark on the Villager Details screen is not Building (any other job, or none) but whom the game gives building work anyway gets all of this only on 14% of those choices; otherwise the game chooses exactly as it always has. When it steps in, construction always comes first -- a builder goes straight into a new hut or building project the game would let it build, even when the game's own random roll would have skipped it this time, and never fixes a hut while there is one. When no building project is available to be worked on and at least one population hut stands -- while another is unbuilt, and below Building level 3 even once every one is built -- a builder with nothing to do examines and fixes one of the huts that already stands, the game's own "Examining hut" / "Fixing hut" job, which trains Building. It only makes that job able to be chosen autonomously; the job itself, its chance of a repair and its skill roll are the game's own. Whenever there is hut work to do, a builder also does this regardless of the food supply: plentiful food no longer skips the builder's work attempt (A New Home, The Lost Children), and scarce food no longer sends the builder to farm or gather first (The Secret City, The Tree of Life, New Believers). Builders and Healers Work First uses the same roll when selected with it, so one choice is either all patched or all stock. The food bypass acts only while you play. During catch-up (time passing while the game was closed, and Time Warp) each villager does the job the stock game picks, and when that job is building, the same build-first and hut-fixing rules apply. **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. That base's companion loads this patch's DLL (in The Secret City, a small stub in the page the base appends does); if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock scheduler runs unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked; the Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically. Needed by Builders and Healers Work First: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: When the Building dispatcher finds no project to work on (every project check has failed) and at least one population hut is complete while another is not, the companion picks a random complete hut and starts the game's own 'Examining hut' job for it, in live play and in catch-up alike. Whenever a builder has hut work to do, its work attempt no longer depends on the food supply: at 250 food or less a picked Building job is dispatched at once instead of waiting behind a farming attempt and a 50% swap for a food action. Every other villager keeps the stock food behaviour. Construction always comes first: the stock 'fix a hut' option is taken out of any option list that also holds a hut to build or a project, and when the stock dislike roll takes a builder's construction options away (a builder with a certain dislike keeps each option only 16% of the time, rand(100) <= 15), the options it took are put back, by the branch's own tests and in its own order, and the stock pick goes straight into one of them; a hut is fixed only when there is no construction at all. Every change above happens about three times in four, not always: each time the game's idle scheduler chooses what a villager does (one run of 0x465840, including the choose-the-next-job routine's retries of it for the same villager (0x465B1A, up to ten)), one 75% roll from the companion's own generator -- never the game's random numbers -- decides whether the patches step in. If it passes, they act together; if it fails, every patched place runs the stock code for that choice, exactly as the unpatched game. The roll is drawn the first time a patched place asks and shared by every patch the choice reaches -- Builders and Healers Work First included. Catch-up -- time that passed while the game was closed, and Time Warp -- never runs the idle scheduler; its worker (0x465750) makes the choice instead, and one run of it is one decision too: the patches it reaches (this one's sites in the Building dispatcher, Builders and Healers Work First) share one 75% roll, never one each. Not checked on the job: everything this companion makes a villager do trains Building -- construction first and the hut fix inside the Building dispatcher; and the low-food bypass, which sends a builder or (with Builders and Healers Work First) a healer straight to their pick, asks the same of the picked job, Building or Healing -- and the dispatcher is reached for anyone the game gives that job. For a villager whose job preference ([object + 0x1B88] + 0x1C70, Building 4, Healing 2; 0 or -1 is no checkmark) is not that job, the companion acts only when, after the decision's roll passes, one more roll of its own passes 14 times in 100 (NOT_PREFERRED_PERCENT, drawn once per decision like the decision's roll): about 10.5% of such decisions instead of 75%. A failed roll is the stock game's choice. A villager checked on the job is unchanged. 14 is the later games' own figure: their job chooser keeps a villager's checked job 86 times in 100.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: a companion that already runs every frame loads the DLL, which detours the dispatcher at run time only after verifying the stock bytes; a different build of the game installs nothing. Nothing about the examine/fix job itself changes: its route, its 70% repair chance, its Building practice roll and its messages are the game's own. A builder with a project available still takes the project. With no population hut built there is nothing to fix. With every hut built and no construction available, at Building level 3 or above (and in The Secret City, The Tree of Life and New Believers at any level) the hut choice is the stock fix-a-hut option; below level 3 in A New Home and The Lost Children a built population hut is fixed directly (never The Lost Children's building 5). Nothing is written to a villager record, the save or any file.
- Dependencies: vv4_enable_origins_exclusive_features

#### Checked Skill Preferences are listed as Jobs on Graves (`vv4_preferred_job_graves`)

A grave's Job line names the skill the villager had checked as their skill preference on the Villager Details screen (the one the game itself shows as their job there), with that skill's rank: "Untrained" below 20, else "Trainee", "Adept" or "Master" by the game's own values (and "Apprentice" for a child under 14 where Children's Graves Say Apprentice or the game does it). With no preference checked the grave shows the highest skill, as before. The epitaph follows the same job. Titles still win: a Scholar still gets "Scholar", and a child the children's epitaphs. Only graves made from now on change; for older graves, Repair Saves & Logs rewrites the grave and its Deaths log lines where the save still holds the villager's preference at death. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The Tree of Life's burial writer gives a villager with a skill preference checked the grave job of that preference and that skill's value (the grave dialog draws the rank, or Apprentice, from it as for any grave); without one the best-skill routine's job and value, as stock. The epitaph is picked from that job.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The shared best-skill routine is not touched (its other callers, the Nursery lesson among them, are unchanged); only the burial writer's block is recoded in place, same length, no executable space claimed. Titles and the children's epitaphs are chosen before the job as stock; a grave already made is never changed by the exe (Repair Saves & Logs does it where the preference at death is known).

#### Copy and Paste in Text Boxes (`vv4_copy_paste`)

Lets you copy and paste in the game's text boxes (the tribe name when a new village starts and the villager names on the Details screen, and every other box you type in). While a box has typing focus: Ctrl+V or Shift+Insert pastes the text on the Windows clipboard where you type (the boxes have no movable caret, so at the end of the text); Ctrl+C or Ctrl+Insert copies the box's whole text; Ctrl+X cuts it (copies it, then empties the box). Pasted text keeps the box's own rules: its own character filter (a numbers-only box takes only digits), and its own length limit, cut before the first character that does not fit, never inside a character. Line breaks and tabs become spaces; other control characters are dropped, and so is every character the game cannot show (never turned into '?'): **with Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts or Use Unicode Font on, every character those patches let you type is pasted (at least every Windows-1252 character: accented letters, curly quotes, €, ...); with neither, plain English letters, digits and signs only.** The keys never reach the game as letters or shortcuts. Ctrl+A does nothing: the game's boxes have no selection. When the clipboard is busy or holds no text, nothing happens. **On by default.** **Needs no other patch; works with or without Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts and Use Unicode Font.** **Not yet seen in a running game** (checked by emulation of each stock executable). The companion is "VVFP Copy and Paste.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; saves are never written by it.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The event pump's SDL_KEYDOWN case (0x4048A6) first asks the companion about the key: Ctrl+V, Shift+Insert, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Insert and Ctrl+X (no Alt, no Windows key), while a text box has typing focus, are handled and the pump goes on with the next event; every other key, and these keys while no box has focus, go on to the stock case exactly as before. The focused box is found the way the game types into it: the game's own keyboard listeners (event manager 0x4CB508), in the game's order, the first whose keyboard handler is the text box's (0x40D750) that has focus ([box+0x25]) on a screen that takes input. Paste: the clipboard's CF_UNICODETEXT, composed (NFC) and split into whole characters, CR/LF/Tab as spaces, other control characters and lone surrogates dropped, each character turned into the box's bytes (UTF-8 when the loaded Unicode companion -- VVFP Unicode Text.dll, else VVFP Unicode Font.dll -- answers VvfpGlyphsUtf8() == 1; every printable Windows-1252 character when it answers 0; printable ASCII when neither is loaded), a character the game cannot show dropped, a numbers-only box's filter applied, and the whole cut before the first character that does not fit the box's byte limit ([box+0x28]). UTF-8 text goes in through that companion's VvfpBoxInsertUtf8 (it inserts as typing does); otherwise the bytes are typed into the box through its own handler, one character message each. Copy: the box's text bytes, read back by the same rule, put on the clipboard as CF_UNICODETEXT; Cut: the same, then (only when the copy succeeded) the box's own Backspace for each byte.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces the SDL_KEYDOWN case's first ten bytes at run time, only after verifying their stock bytes, and installs nothing on a different build. Nothing is written but a focused box's text, through the box's own handler and its own rules: opening and closing a box without these keys leaves its bytes exactly as they were. Saves, villager records and the patcher's files are never written. The clipboard is opened and closed on the game thread and never waited for; busy or empty means nothing happens. A fault is abandoned and the key goes on to the stock code. The SDL_TEXTINPUT case (detoured by Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts) is not touched; both patches work together or alone.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Difficulty Settings (`vv4_difficulty_settings`)

Puts back the Options dialog's Difficulty choice -- Easy, Normal or Hard -- as A New Home, The Lost Children and The Secret City have it. The Tree of Life already plays by a difficulty level, saved with each village (a village starts on Normal), and its rules are The Secret City's, but its Options dialog never shows the choice. With this patch the Difficulty row is drawn where The Secret City has it, directly above Game Speed, with the game's own radio buttons, words and font; Game Speed moves down a row and the dialog's frame grows by whole tiles, so the whole dialog stays on the screen with everything in it where it was. The choice is saved with the village. Easy: a new village starts with 300 more food; villagers never eat the extra food the other levels take; a fed, healthy villager tries to regain health on every check instead of about half of them; and villagers fall sick about a quarter as often. Normal (a village's level until you change it): above 8,000 food each villager's meal takes 2 more food three times in four; a starving villager loses health on about three checks in four. Hard: a new village starts with 99 less food; each villager's meal takes 2 more food three times in four at any food level; a starving villager loses health on every check. **The starting food only changes for a village made after you pick the level; the other rules follow the level at once.** **Needs no other patch; it works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Checked in a live game, windowed: the row's layout, every button, and the chosen level after a save and reload. Clicks in fullscreen have not been tried in a live game.** It is on by default; untick it to keep the stock dialog (a village then keeps the level it has). The companion is "VVFP Difficulty.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock dialog is shown.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Classic VV Difficulty: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: The Options dialog (drawing 0x41A5A0, clicks 0x41AD60) shows a Difficulty row at y+0x145: the heading and three radio buttons with Easy, Normal and Hard (strings 0x534 Difficulty, 0x535 Easy, 0x53A Normal (Game Speed's own), 0x537 Hard), the selected one the village's level (game-state field +0x170F4). Game Speed's buttons, heading, labels and click areas move down 0x40 (64 pixels, the one tile the frame grows by; Difficulty sits 0x48 below Fullscreen and Game Speed 0x48 below Difficulty, as the stock 0x50 spacing does not fit the 600-pixel screen), to y+0x18D; the dialog's height becomes 0x23C, so its frame is one 64-pixel tile taller (576 pixels on the 800 x 600 screen); the frame, the Done button and the Music Tracks checkboxes are placed by the game from the frame, and the rows from the frame's top + 2 as in the stock dialog, so nothing else moves against them. The stock handler's own three Difficulty click areas (0x41B159 / 0x41B187 / 0x41B1B9 write 0, 1, 2) move onto the new row's buttons, with the Game Speed buttons' insets; no click near Game Speed changes the level any more. The level's effects are the stock game's own (starting food 0x41F3A3; food use, starvation and healing 0x4684E5..0x4686B0; sickness 0x4686B0 and 0x45E938): Easy: a new village starts with 300 more food; villagers never eat the extra food the other levels take; a fed, healthy villager tries to regain health on every check instead of about half of them; and villagers fall sick about a quarter as often. Normal (a village's level until you change it): above 8,000 food each villager's meal takes 2 more food three times in four; a starving villager loses health on about three checks in four. Hard: a new village starts with 99 less food; each villager's meal takes 2 more food three times in four at any food level; a starving villager loses health on every check.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: VVFP Difficulty.dll verifies every stock byte it rewrites and writes them at run time; a different build of the game installs nothing. No save byte, file or villager is written by the companion: the level is the stock field, written only by the game's own click handler and saved by the game's own save. What each level does is unchanged: these are the stock rules, which already run on Normal in every village. Every other row of the dialog (sound, music, voiceovers, music tracks, fullscreen) is drawn and clicked exactly as before.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending

#### Enable Origins-Exclusive Features (with Heathen Mask mod) (`vv4_enable_origins_exclusive_features`)

Adds Origins-style Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. The Tech menu offers Time Warp, Island Event, Barrel of Babies, Food and Tech Point Doublers for 500,000 tech points each (eligible positive gains are doubled after native Food Mastery, while Island Events and Duplicate Collectibles remain unchanged), Full Heal/Cure All, Complete and Reset All Collections, Equal Division of Labor with and without Parenting, Clear All Skill Preferences, and Check Highest Skill with and without Parenting. Clear All Skill Preferences (500,000 tech points): unchecks every villager's skill preference (job checkmark) so each villager is free to choose their own work, as in the stock game. Skills themselves are not changed. Check Highest Skill (Includes Parenting) / (No Parenting) (1,000,000 tech points each): sets each villager's skill preference (job checkmark) to the skill they have the most progress in; the No Parenting version ignores Parenting. Ties go to the first skill in the Skills list order (Farming, Building, Research, Healing, Parenting). Villagers with no progress in any skill yet keep their preference. The Village-Wide menu adds Running, Full Mastery, and Make Villagers Young Adults. Island Event and Barrel of Babies are queued rather than fired at once: each waits a few real seconds after the Tech screen closes, so the purchase confirmation is readable first and a natural island event falling due at the same moment cannot consume the purchased one. While either is still pending its row reads 'Why not?' instead of offering a second purchase; clicking it explains that one is already on its way and closes nothing, so it cannot be bought twice or charged for twice. The same applies when the village has no room for the children a barrel would bring, where the message says so and notes that a villager who has died still occupies a slot until buried. The Villager Details menu grants Youth, Full Mastery, Running, Set Age to 18, and Change Appearance. This patch also includes the Heathen Mask mod: a cosmetic head-mask overlay (Blue/Orange/Red/Purple/Chief) selectable per villager in Change Appearance and en masse via the Change Appearance for All tech upgrade, rendered over the villager's head in both the village and the Details screen. Inspired by the Virtual Villagers 1 mobile port, where selected Origins-exclusive upgrades originated; this wording does not claim unsupported mobile parity.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Enable Origins Tech, Details, and Village-Wide Upgrades: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Builders Fix Huts When Idle: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Original Looks for Reset to Original: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Log Every Death, Disappearance and Unaccounted Villager: unticking this unticks it.**
