#### Fix Vanilla Bugs (`vv4_fix_vanilla_bugs`)

Fixes bugs in the base game. A village with exactly 150 villagers can be saved and loaded again: the base game, when it saves a full list of 150 villagers, writes past the end of that list and damages the next part of the save, so the village then refuses to load and the game offers to start a new tribe. Now all 150 villagers are kept and the village loads. A village that was already saved with 150 villagers and would not load is repaired when it is loaded. Only a village with 150 villagers is affected; the base game cannot reach 150 on its own, but the Collection Progression and Immediate Fixed population modes can. Every default name can be chosen: the game numbers its 185 male and 185 female names from 0 but picks a number from 1 (and never the last one), so Ago and Yapili (male) and Aipi and Zucca (female) could never be given; now every name in each list can come up, for new villagers and twins alike. A "%" in a villager's name can no longer crash the game: the game showed some names by using them as formatting instructions; now it copies them as plain text, and its text boxes no longer accept a typed "%". A like or dislike holding a negative number other than the game's own "none" (-1) is left out of the Details screen instead of being shown as "ants". A villager's name is saved only to the villager it belongs to on the Details screen: the screen remembers which villager it filled the name box for, and Done or the arrows save the box only into that same villager; if the selected villager is not the one the box was filled for, the box is dropped and the right name is shown. A name you type is still saved to the villager shown. Unpausing at a different speed now gives the Fire Pit the new speed's length, as a speed change while playing does (the base game kept the old one: a fire lit on Fast burned only 10 hours after unpausing on Normal). Every body can be given: the game rolled a new villager's body from 0 to 28 only, so body 29, the last of its 30 bodies for each sex, was never given to a newborn, a twin, a Barrel of Babies baby, an arrival or a new village's villager; now each of the 30 is equally likely. No crash from a raindrop of no length: the game draws each raindrop as a short line from where it is to where it was, and its line drawer divides by the line's length, so a line whose two ends are the same point stops the game (a divide by zero). A raindrop has no length when it starts at the screen's top left corner before it has moved, which can happen when rain starts. Now such a line is drawn as a single dot, and every other line is drawn exactly as before. Villagers keep what they carry when the way to where they are going is blocked: a villager with a mushroom or a collectible in its hands whose goal could not be reached (the spot was under a building or a tree) gave up the walk, the game dropped the item and it was never credited. Now the game's own route finder is asked for the nearest spot round the goal that it can reach (up to 64 pixels away, nearest first); the villager walks there, puts the item down and it is credited as for any delivery if it is in the right place. Only when no spot can be reached does the walk end as it always did. A villager carrying nothing (or a baby), a goal the game can reach, and every other walk are exactly as before. The Overview Map's water lines up with its riverbeds: the map shows the island at 424/2048 of its size (20.7%), but the game drew every picture on it (the rivers, waterfalls and every frame of their animations, and the rest) at 20%, its scale cut down to a whole percent, so each was too small from its top left corner and the water sat above and to the left of its bed. Now the scale is rounded to the nearest whole percent (21%), so the water fills its riverbeds. The village view is unchanged. A child's Nursery School lesson no longer nearly always goes to Building: the whole lesson goes to the child's highest skill, but the game counted a skill with any fraction above the whole number of an earlier one as higher, so among skills with the same whole number the last in the list, Building, always won, and a child whose skills are all below 1 (every newborn) was taught Building almost every time. Now skills with the same whole number tie, and a tie is broken at random (each tied skill equally likely). The 50 limit, the 50-in-100 choice between one skill and all of them, and the amounts are the base game's own. After The Frog Rescue, the frogs leap all along the straight bottom stretch of the river (the owner, 2026-11-12), not only its right part: each leap was placed in a small fixed box (about 240 pixels wide); the boxes now span the whole straight stretch (about 440 pixels), the same height on the water, the same 1 to 3 leaps every refresh. Their splash ripples also play to the end: the game gave each frog leap 9 frames of the 12 its picture draws, so the ripple stopped at its first dot. A word too wide for its line (a long name or an unbroken word in a translation or a Custom Island Event) no longer freezes the game: the justified paragraph of island events, tips and notices dropped the word and tried it again for ever, and the tips' line fitter cut it into empty lines. Now such a word gets a line of its own, at its full width (wider than its box), and the text goes on; text without such a word is laid out exactly as before ("VVFP Long Words.dll"). **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by 256 Villagers (Experimental) for loading a village that the base game's exactly-150-villager save bug has already damaged (without it such a village does not load).**

- Behavior changes: Saving a village of exactly 150 villagers keeps all 150 and no longer writes past the saved villager list into the next block of the save, so the village loads again. Loading reads at most the 150 saved villagers, never anything after the list. A save already damaged this way (150 saved villagers and the next block's size with its low byte zeroed) is accepted and loads with all 150 villagers; the next save writes it correctly. A villager's default first name is picked from the whole of the game's male or female list (185 names each): name numbers 0 to 184 instead of 1 to the base game's limit. A villager's name (and in The Lost Children a grave's epitaph and the parents' names) is copied as plain text, never used as a printf format, and every text box refuses a typed "%". Details screen Likes/Dislikes builders: a slot is skipped when it is negative (the stock test was 'equal to -1'); every word index from 0 up is shown exactly as before. Villager Details name box (The Tree of Life): the screen remembers which villager it filled the box for -- the villager-name pointer (+0x1B9C) and a fingerprint: the name's first dword XOR its second, the low byte also XOR the sex byte (+0x1B90), kept in 8 new bytes at the end of the screen object (+0xD8) -- whenever the box is filled (setText 0x40D3E0 (shown 0x448516, after an arrow 0x4485F3)); every write-back (the record lookup 0x466040 that gives each write-back its destination (arrow 0x44856C, Done 0x448653)) goes ahead only when its destination is that same name and that villager still has the same fingerprint, otherwise the box is not saved (the next fill shows the right name). This covers any way the selected record could stop holding the villager shown (two clicks in one frame, a record reused or moved while the screen is open). Unpausing at another speed (the pause key or an Options speed button from a paused game): the game clock's set_speed 0x41DBE0, whose branch from a paused clock (0x41DC4E) took the factor 1, now takes new / the speed before the pause (clock +0x24) applied around the wall clock at the pause (+0x28), exactly as its running branch applies new / old, through the routine's own rescale loop; every timer registered to the clock (the Fire Pit's two) therefore gets the new speed's length. Unpausing at the same speed is byte for byte the base game's. Installed at run time by "VVFP Speed Change Timers.dll", which checks the whole routine (0x41DBE0..0x41DD0F) and the 2^32 constant 0x48C4C0 hold the stock bytes, or installs nothing. The villager creator's body roll (0x45F2AE) is rand(30), bodies 0 to 29 each 1 in 30, instead of rand(29): births, twins and triplets (copies of the first baby), Barrel of Babies, the canoe, island-event arrivals and a new village's villagers all get it. The line drawer (0x404280) no longer divides by zero: a line whose two ends are the same point (2|dx| = 2|dy| = 0) keeps its undivided alpha step and is drawn as the one point; its callers are the rain (0x46B6D0: each drop is a line from its point to its previous point, and the rain initialiser sets a new point (rand(800), rand(600)) but not the previous one, so a drop whose new point is its previous point -- (0, 0) while the previous points are still the zeroed ones -- is a zero-length line until its first rain update). Keep what a villager carries ("VVFP Keep Carried.dll", started by "VVFP Startup.dll"): the route finder's call 0x4706B0 inside the walk step (at 0x4612F8) goes to the companion, which asks the game's route finder first, exactly as before. Only when it answers "no route", the villager holds an item (not -1, not 3 the baby), the front step is the walk and another step is queued behind it, the route finder is asked about points on rings of 8, 16, 24, 32, 48 and 64 pixels round the goal (16 directions, nearest first) and the first it can route to becomes the walk's goal (step +4/+8); none: the answer stays "no route" and the stock give-up 0x468C60 (which releases the item with -1 through 0x45ED50) runs. (Emulated: a mushroom walked to a blocked spot in the food bin is released inside the bin.) Overview Map scale (0x44544B: origin (188, 61), scale 424/2048 = 0.20703125): the draw queue's origin routine 0x44C3E0 (queue 0x4DB9F8) and the map's overlay list 0x41C5B0 (list 0x4CCB20, called at 0x44542B) turn the scale into the whole percent every picture is drawn at; they cut 20.703 to 20 with _ftol 0x471630, and now round it to 21 (push eax; fistp dword [esp]; pop eax: the FPU's round-to-nearest, which pops the value as _ftol does). Positions on the map are unchanged (world x 0.20703125 + 188, y + 61); every sprite, static or animated (each waterfall and river frame), is drawn 21% of its size instead of 20%, 0.30 points from the map's 20.70 instead of 0.70, so its far edges miss the riverbed by less than half as much as before. The village view's scale 1.0 still gives 100. Nursery School top skill (the lesson 0x4203F3-0x420521): its one call of the shared top-skill routine 0x46AC20 (at 0x4204A8) goes to a tie-breaker, 14 pieces in the int3 padding between functions (0x420313-0x42397B), chained by jumps. It calls 0x46AC20 first and returns its -1 (no skill above 0) unchanged, so the lesson's own rand(5) still draws; otherwise the pick's whole number is the highest among the 5 skills, and it returns one of the skills with that whole number, each equally likely (reservoir sampling with the game's RNG 0x4036D0: the k-th tied skill replaces the pick when rand(k) is 0). Frogs after The Frog Rescue (puzzle 5; the world refresh 0x46D090, gate 0x46D3BF: puzzle 5 solved and the stream flowing): the leap effects' x ranges are widened to the straight bottom stretch of the river: the right-leaping frog (0x1B) from 1029..1182 to 784..1182 (0x46D3F8, 0x46D406), each left-leaping frog (0x1C, two 50% chances) from 950..1133 to 744..1133 (0x46D440/0x46D44E, 0x46D488/0x46D496); y, the count and the chances are unchanged. The two frog effects (0x4B9F0C, 0x4B9F1C) get 12 frames instead of 9, the frames frogstrip1/2.png draw, so the ripple frames 9-11 play. The justified paragraph 0x409C30 (every island event, tip and notice body): at 0x409E4D (`cmp ecx, eax`, deciding whether a line too wide drops its last word) VVFP Long Words.dll keeps a line's only word -- laid out on a line of its own at its full width -- where the stock code dropped it, drew an empty line and tried the same word again for ever; a line of two or more words is decided by the stock compare. The line fit 0x402550 (the tips' line loops and the wrapped-height measures): at 0x402686 (`cmp byte [esi], ' '`, where a line too wide backs off to its last space) a line with no space keeps its letters and takes the rest of the word (to the next space, line break or end, within the caller's letter limit less one), where the stock code backed off to nothing and returned one letter on, so the word lost its letters one empty line each until the rest fitted; a line with a space backs off as before.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The population cap, births, events and every population mode are unchanged; no villager is removed or added. Saves with 0 to 149 villagers are written and read exactly as before, byte for byte; the save file's size and format are unchanged. A save whose size check fails for any other reason is still refused, as in the base game. Which words a villager likes or dislikes, and how likes and dislikes affect behaviour, are the base game's own; only the Details screen's text changes. Renaming on the Details screen works as before: a typed name is saved to the villager shown by Done and the arrows; which villager the arrows select, the box's length and every other Details control are unchanged. The speed-change timers fix changes no executable bytes and nothing in the save's layout: the clock and its timers are saved exactly as before; only the values the game computes when it is unpaused at another speed differ. Every head roll and the head's inheritance are the base game's own; only the pushed bound changes, and the call to the game's rand routine after it is not touched. Every line with any length is drawn exactly as before: the same divisor, the same rounding and the same pixels; the rain, its drop count, speed and colour, and the lightning are the base game's own. A villager holding nothing or the baby, a goal the route finder reaches (the same answer, the same walk), a walk with no step behind it, the walk's follower and its map-edge give-ups, and what the release step credits (it still needs the villager to stand in the item's delivery place) are the base game's own. The village view (scale 1.0, 100%), every position on the Overview Map, the map's picture, its clouds, frame and buttons, where a click on the map zooms to, and which water shows (the river puzzle's state) are the base game's own; only the size of the pictures drawn on the map changes. The top-skill routine 0x46AC20 itself and its other callers (0x4402EA, 0x448341, 0x448351, 0x45D4EF, 0x4609B5, 0x4609C4, 0x465069, 0x465078 and 0x465A43) are the base game's own; in the Nursery lesson the 50 test on the top skill, the 50-in-100 roll, the spread to every skill below 50, the amounts, the teacher and which children learn are unchanged. No save data changes.
- Dependencies: none

with this fix (test build, 2026-10-03) that damaged save loaded with all 150 villagers, a clean quit wrote 150 villagers with the size intact (0x250) and the village loaded again, and 149 still saved and loaded; #### Food Gains are Flat, like VV1-3 (Harder Games) (`vv4_food_pays_like_earlier_games`)

Changes the food sources that scale to a flat gain. A blackberry pick (stock: the berries ÷ 100, at least 2, up to 10) now pays 7, 3 or 2 food on Fast, Normal or Slow and 4 while catching up, as The Secret City's fruit and honey do, and takes as many berries from the bush. Cooking Pit fruit (3), the blackberry harvest with a cutting tool (up to 30 at once), fish from the net (4) and the Golden Fish (8) already pay a fixed amount and are unchanged. Food Mastery still multiplies every gain. A harder setting: a well-stocked bush no longer pays more.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Classic VV Difficulty: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: The blackberry pick (job event 13, 0x464464) pays 7 food on Fast, 3 on Normal and 2 on Slow (the speed value game+0x17110: 3, 6 or 10), and 4 while the game catches up time away (the catch-up flag game+0x171A4), instead of the berries ÷ 100 (at least 2). The bush loses what the pick paid, as before; the stock clamp at 0 and the end of the bush task below 3 berries are unchanged.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: Food Mastery (0x41D920) still boosts the amount; the Farming check, the trips, the regrowth, the blackberry harvest with a cutting tool (job event 14), the fruit, the fish (4) and the Golden Fish (8, job event 17, on its stock (2 x fish scales + 1)% chance), the crabs and the mushrooms are stock. Tech points are unchanged. No save data is written.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static exact-build evidence; the pick step emulated on the stock and rendered executables; runtime/player confirmation pending

#### Full Names on the Details Screen (`vv4_details_full_names`)

The Villager Details screen keeps a villager's whole name. In the base game its name box holds only 18 characters (fewer for wide letters) and, when the screen closes, writes what it holds back to the villager, so a longer name -- a last name, a numbered namesake -- was cut short for good. Now the box holds the 23 characters the game's name field has room for, is wide enough to show them, and copies the whole name back; typing a new name there allows 23 characters too. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts: unticking this unticks it. Needed by Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts): unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: Villager Detail name box: SetEditable max characters 18 -> 23 five-villager naming screen name box: SetEditable max characters 18 -> 23 Villager Detail name box initial text: 15 'w' -> existing 26 'W' string at 0x0048EDD0 so the box is wide enough that the draw routine never NUL-truncates a 23-character name Villager Detail next/previous villager: GetText(rec+0x1B9C, 0x18) straight into the record instead of via the 20-byte stack local + strncpy(0x18); keeps 23 characters + NUL, no stack buffer involved Villager Detail OK: GetText(rec+0x1B9C, 0x18) straight into the record instead of via the 20-byte stack local + strncpy(0x18); keeps 23 characters + NUL, no stack buffer involved five-villager naming screen: GetText(rec+0x1B9C, 0x18) straight into the record instead of the 20-byte stack local + setter strncpy(+0x10, 0x18)
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The villager's name field is the base game's own 24-byte field; nothing is written past it, and the save's layout is unchanged. Names that already fitted are shown and kept exactly as before; no other screen changes.
- Dependencies: none

#### Harder Fishing Unlock in VV4 (`vv4_harder_fishing_unlock`)

**Needs no other patch.** Makes fishing come later, so the game is harder; off by default. Fish need the fishing nets, and the nets need the piers fixed and cloth to mend them. With this patch cloth waits for Science level 3 (70,000 tech points) and fixing the piers waits for Construction level 3 (65,000 tech points). The Clothing Hut still appears at Science level 2 as normal, but until Science 3 a villager dropped on the vines says "Don't know what to do with these tough vines!" and makes no cloth. Until Construction 3 a villager dropped on the broken piers says "Additional research may be necessary." (as on a hut that needs more Construction), builders do not go to fix them on their own, and a villager who was fixing them stops. Piers already fixed stay fixed, work already done on them is kept for Construction 3, and cloth the village already has can still be used: the nets are mended with it and the Clothing Hut gives clothes as before. Nothing else changes.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Classic VV Difficulty: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: The vines' drop handler 0x436D40: with the Clothing Hut finished and Science below 3, the stock refusal "Don't know what to do with these tough vines!" (0x249) instead of the cloth start (action 0x7A); at Science 3 the stock cloth start. The Fishing Nets drop handler 0x433440 (case 0, project 11 unfinished): with the piers unfixed (stage [0x4D86AC] < 2) and Construction ([0x4D6F68], tech 3) below 3, the villager says "Additional research may be necessary." (0x75, the game's refusal on Hut 2 / Hut 3 below their Construction level) instead of starting the pier fix (action 0x80, task 30); at Construction 3 the stock pier start. The nets' branch is unchanged. Below Construction 3 the Building dispatcher never lists "Fixing the piers" (option 6, 0x463DD8), live or while catching up, and a villager on task 30 (fixing the piers, saved mid-fix) has the task cleared (0x46385B) instead of resuming it; at Construction 3 both are stock.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The Clothing Hut's site (Science 2), its building, cloth bolts already in the store, the fishing nets' use of them, clothes and every other drop are unchanged; nothing but the vines' drop starts cloth-making. The piers' stage and counter are never written by the patch: fixed piers stay fixed and a part-done counter is kept; mending the nets, catching fish, the tech prices and every other building job are unchanged. Guarded in-place edits: one jump and int3 padding after the vines' handler, and three stock routines' own bytes rewritten to the same length (the nets' drop tail, the dispatcher's pier test, the task-30 continuation); no executable tail space is claimed.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the vines' drop at Science 1, 2 and 3, and the piers' drop, the dispatcher's pier offer and the task-30 continuation at Construction 1, 2 and 3 with the piers unfixed, part-done and fixed (and the nets' branch with the Clothing Hut finished and unfinished) are emulated stock and patched in tests/test_vv4_harder_fishing_unlock.py; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 5; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Hungrier Villagers (2-10x Meals) (`vv4_hungrier_villagers`)

**Needs no other patch.** Makes the game harder; off by default. Every villager's meal takes 2 to 10 times the normal food: you choose how many times with the Hungrier Villagers slider in the patcher window (a whole number, 2 unless you move it). Normally a villager's meal takes 2 food, and 2 more three times in four at 8,000 food or more on Normal difficulty, at any food level on Hard, never on Easy; at x 2 that is 4 and 4 more. Food never goes below 0: when it runs out the game's own starvation rules take over, as without the patch. Skipped meals when food is low, the snack at the food bin, events that take food and everything that brings food in are unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Classic VV Difficulty: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: The meal routine's two food amounts (0x4684C8, 0x46850B), each -2, become -2 x N (the slider, 2 to 10; 2 by default); the stock clamp keeps food at 0 or more.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: When a villager eats, the low-food skip, starvation, the snack at the food bin, starting food, events and everything that brings food in are unchanged. Two one-byte edits in place; no code is added and no executable space is claimed.

#### Island Events Scale With Population (like The Lost Children) (`vv4_island_events_scale_with_population`)

Island events' food and tech-point gains and losses grow with the village, as in The Lost Children: each amount is multiplied by 1 with up to 25 villagers, by 2 with 26 to 50 and by 3 with more than 50 (living villagers plus the babies being carried, as the game counts its population). The 14 amounts of 9 events are scaled: The Creeping Mold, The Mysterious Footprints (all four), The Arc of Brilliant Colors, The Calabash Instrument, The Climber, The Mosquito Larvae, Faces in the Night, The Sealed Box and The Aspiring Scientist. A loss still takes no more than there is, and Food Mastery still raises a food gain as the game does. A single-result event's popup shows the scaled amount (it prints the amount the game set); a two-choice event's result text is fixed (for example "Your tribe gains 5000 tech points."), so it still names the game's own amount while the scaled amount is what is given. Custom Island Events (Story / Cheat Upgrades) keep their own amounts. Nothing is saved, so the patch can be ticked or unticked at any time. **Needs no other patch.** **Cannot be ticked together with "Island Events Scale With Stored Food and Tech Points": the two scale the same amounts in different ways, so tick only one; with both ticked the patcher builds nothing.** Off by default; part of Classic VV Difficulty; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.** The companion is "VVFP Island Events Scale.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if it cannot be loaded, the stock amounts are given.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Classic VV Difficulty: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: Each site below calls VVFP Island Events Scale.dll, which counts the population with the population routine 0x467610 on the villager manager (0x50E568, or where 256 Villagers moves it: the manager's static initialiser's own `mov ecx`, 0x488D70) and puts the stock amount x k in place of the stock amount, k = 3 above 50, 2 above 25, else 1 (The Lost Children's 0x41F720: cmp 0x32 / jle, cmp 0x19 / jle). A gain stays a gain and a loss a loss. A single-result loss (The Creeping Mold, The Mysterious Footprints' food and tech lost) is then clamped to what is stored by the companion, by the setter's own rule (stored below the amount: the amount is what is stored), because the setter itself tests the store against its stock amount (cmp eax, imm / jge); the setter's test then runs as in the stock game, and the {award} its popup shows is what is taken. The two-choice food and tech writers' floor at 0 runs after it, as in the stock game. The Creeping Mold: -100 food (0x414730). The Mysterious Footprints (food gained): +300 food (0x414930). The Mysterious Footprints (food lost): -300 food (0x414980). The Mysterious Footprints (tech gained): +2,000 tech points (0x414A00). The Mysterious Footprints (tech lost): -2,000 tech points (0x414A50). The Arc of Brilliant Colors, "Run to the right side" (rare mushrooms): +300 food (0x415201). The Calabash Instrument, "Fill it up to the first notch": +3,000 tech points (0x41585A). The Calabash Instrument, "Fill it to the top": -2,000 tech points (0x415867). The Climber, "Start yelling for help": -500 tech points (0x415942). The Mosquito Larvae, "Pour oil in the pond": +500 tech points (0x415A74). Faces in the Night, "Inform the tribe": +1,000 tech points (0x415B39). The Sealed Box, "Swim back with the box": +5,000 tech points (0x415D7F). The Aspiring Scientist, "Try the salts": +2,000 tech points (0x416715). The Aspiring Scientist, "Use algae": -1,000 tech points (0x416728).
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion writes each site at run time, only after verifying every site's stock bytes (all of them, or none). The game's rolls, its food and tech writers (Food Mastery's raise included), the clamps, every other event, the popups' and buttons' texts, Custom Island Events and the save are unchanged.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; every site emulated on the stock executable with the shipped companion (k = 1, 2, 3 at 25, 26, 50 and 51 villagers, gains, losses and the loss clamp, the 256 Villagers manager) in tests/test_island_events_scale.py; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Island Events Scale With Stored Food and Tech Points (`vv4_island_events_scale_with_stored_amounts`)

Island events' food and tech-point gains and losses grow with what the village has stored: each amount becomes the game's own amount plus a tenth of the food (for a food amount) or of the tech points (for a tech amount) stored at that moment, rounded down, and never less than the game's own amount. For example, with 5,000 food stored a gain of 300 food becomes 800, and a loss of 300 food becomes a loss of 800. The 14 amounts of 9 events are scaled: The Creeping Mold, The Mysterious Footprints (all four), The Arc of Brilliant Colors, The Calabash Instrument, The Climber, The Mosquito Larvae, Faces in the Night, The Sealed Box and The Aspiring Scientist. A loss still takes no more than there is, and Food Mastery still raises a food gain as the game does. A single-result event's popup shows the scaled amount (it prints the amount the game set); a two-choice event's result text is fixed (for example "Your tribe gains 5000 tech points."), so it still names the game's own amount while the scaled amount is what is given. Custom Island Events (Story / Cheat Upgrades) keep their own amounts. Nothing is saved, so the patch can be ticked or unticked at any time. **Needs no other patch.** **Cannot be ticked together with "Island Events Scale With Population (like The Lost Children)": the two scale the same amounts in different ways, so tick only one; with both ticked the patcher builds nothing.** Classic VV Difficulty scales by the population instead, so it cannot be ticked with this one either. Off by default, and off in Owner's Defaults and Select All (it is the alternative). **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.** The patch adds one small file, "VVFP Island Events Scale Stored.txt", to the patcher's folder, which tells "VVFP Island Events Scale.dll" (started by VVFP Startup.dll) to scale this way.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

When it is, each site below puts the stock amount plus floor(stored / 10) -- the food (0x4D6DD0) or tech points (0x4D6F88), read at that moment, 0 when below 0 -- with the amount's own sign in place of the stock amount (a loss grows by the same tenth). A single-result loss (The Creeping Mold, The Mysterious Footprints' food and tech lost) is then clamped to what is stored by the companion, by the setter's own rule (stored below the amount: the amount is what is stored), because the setter itself tests the store against its stock amount (cmp eax, imm / jge); the setter's test then runs as in the stock game, and the {award} its popup shows is what is taken. The two-choice food and tech writers' floor at 0 runs after it, as in the stock game. The Creeping Mold: -100 food (0x414730). The Mysterious Footprints (food gained): +300 food (0x414930). The Mysterious Footprints (food lost): -300 food (0x414980). The Mysterious Footprints (tech gained): +2,000 tech points (0x414A00). The Mysterious Footprints (tech lost): -2,000 tech points (0x414A50). The Arc of Brilliant Colors, "Run to the right side" (rare mushrooms): +300 food (0x415201). The Calabash Instrument, "Fill it up to the first notch": +3,000 tech points (0x41585A). The Calabash Instrument, "Fill it to the top": -2,000 tech points (0x415867). The Climber, "Start yelling for help": -500 tech points (0x415942). The Mosquito Larvae, "Pour oil in the pond": +500 tech points (0x415A74). Faces in the Night, "Inform the tribe": +1,000 tech points (0x415B39). The Sealed Box, "Swim back with the box": +5,000 tech points (0x415D7F). The Aspiring Scientist, "Try the salts": +2,000 tech points (0x416715). The Aspiring Scientist, "Use algae": -1,000 tech points (0x416728).
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the row's own file is the flag; the companion writes each site at run time, only after verifying every site's stock bytes (all of them, or none). The game's rolls, its food and tech writers (Food Mastery's raise included), the clamps, every other event, the popups' and buttons' texts, Custom Island Events and the save are unchanged.

#### Keep the Game's Own Log (ldwLog.txt) (`vv4_game_log`)

Keeps the game's own log, 'ldwLog.txt' in the game's save folder (Documents\LDW\<game executable name>\). Every Virtual Villagers game has always had this log, but the base game starts the file afresh the first time it writes in each run (erasing the earlier runs' lines), holds what it writes in memory until the game closes (a crash loses it), and writes only when something goes wrong -- so most players never see the file. Now each time the game opens it adds a "---- Game started ----" line, and every line the game writes is added to the file at once and kept: a missing font picture, a missing picture, a missing sound, "Seconds Timer out of bounds!" (the computer's clock was set back, so the game's one-second timer is ahead of it), a text the game asks for that is missing from its text file (sm.xml), a text in sm.xml with no end and a healer who could not find anyone to heal. The Tree of Life's code contains no tip or path-finding line, so those cannot be logged (its villagers keep a pointer to the log, but no code writes through it). A line repeated without a break is written once a minute with how many times it repeated, at most 1,000 lines are written a minute, and when the file reaches 4 MB it is renamed 'ldwLog 1.txt' (then 2, 3, ...) and a new one is started, so no file grows without limit; nothing is ever deleted. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The game's log writer (0x40b6c0) is replaced at run time by the companion's: the same "<date and time>: <line>" text with CR-LF line ends, to the same file, Documents\LDW\<executable name up to its first dot>\ldwLog.txt. The file is appended to (the base game opens it with "wt", which erases the earlier runs' lines), and each line is written to the file at once (the base game buffers until a clean exit). Each run starts with one "---- Game started ----" line, which also creates the file. A line that exactly repeats the one before it is written again only after a minute, preceded by "(the line above was repeated <n> more times)". At most 1,000 lines are written in a minute; the next line written says how many were left out. When ldwLog.txt would pass 4 MiB it is renamed "ldwLog <n>.txt" (n one more than the highest already there) and a new ldwLog.txt is started. Call at 0x402875 writes "Font Image not found: %s": a font picture is missing (the game then closes). Call at 0x40b248 writes " Missing Graphic -> %s": a picture file is missing. Call at 0x40c4f8 writes "ldwSoundFx Missing File ->%s": a sound file is missing. Call at 0x43fc28 writes "Seconds Timer out of bounds!": the game's one-second timer is more than 3 seconds ahead of the computer's clock, as when the clock is set back (checked every frame). Call at 0x44d8b7 writes "String Table (sm.xml) malformed near %s": a text id the game asks for is not in Assets\sm.xml. Call at 0x44d90e writes "String Table (sm.xml) malformed looking for </Text> after %s": a text in Assets\sm.xml has no </Text>. Call at 0x465149 writes "%s could not find someone to heal.": a healer found nobody to heal.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces the writer's first instruction at run time, only after verifying its first 16 bytes, and installs nothing on a different build. Which lines the game writes, and when, is the game's own: every call site is unchanged, and no line the game's code does not contain is ever written (only the "Game started" line and the repeat and left-out counts are the companion's). No save, village or villager data is read or written; nothing else in the game changes. Older 'ldwLog <n>.txt' files and any other file in the folder are never changed or deleted.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static exact-build verification of the writer and every call to it in each executable (tests/test_game_log.py); the companion's writer is run by native/vvfp_game_log/game_log_harness.c
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Log Every Death, Disappearance and Unaccounted Villager (`vv4_cause_of_death`)

Every death that leaves a body is written to the Deaths log ('Virtual Villagers 4 Deaths Log <n>.txt' in the save slot's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Deaths and Disappearances' folder beside the game's saves, or 'Deaths' in a save an older version made: nothing is moved) when it is final: when the body is buried, with the skill line and epitaph the grave was given, or when the game removes a body nobody buried ("no grave"). Each Death record gives the villager's name, head, body, likes and dislikes, their age at death in the game's own units (20 per year, as the Village Population log prints Age), the cause, the grave and the epitaph. A villager brought back to life gets no Death record. A villager taken with no skeleton (The Sealed Box, or the Custom Island Event's "Disappears") gets a "Disappeared" record saying what took them, and editing a grave's epitaph adds an "Epitaph changed" record with the old and new text. A grave the Deaths log has no record for -- dug before the log was kept, or while the game was catching up on time away -- is given a Death record only when the player says so -- Repair Logs in the patcher window, or Repair when the game asks as it closes (with "Check logs automatically" on, and only if something is wrong); nothing is ever asked while the village is played. The record is made from the grave (name, age at death, skill line, epitaph, and the cause where the game or this patch knows it) with the head, body, likes and dislikes of the villager's last Village History snapshot ("(unknown)" when that does not settle who it was), and marked "Recorded from the grave". Which graves have their record is kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Deaths\Virtual Villagers 4 Graves Logged - Save <n>.dat', so no grave is recorded twice; Start Over deletes it. Every villager who joins the village without being born into it -- a new village's founders, an island event's newcomer, the Barrel of Babies, the Custom Island Event's new villagers -- gets an "Arrived" record in the Births and Conceptions log ('Virtual Villagers 4 Births and Conceptions Log <n>.txt'), written at the next save: the name, the age when they arrived, sex, head, body, likes, dislikes, skills, and how they came ("Founder", the island event's title, "Barrel of Babies", "Custom Island Event", or "unknown"). A birth is never an arrival. A mother who dies or disappears while nursing (the game's own word for a mother whose babies are not yet born) loses them with her: they never become villagers and get no grave, so her Death or Disappeared record says "Nursing: yes, <n> babies (never born: lost with their mother)", and a "Lost before birth" record in the Births and Conceptions log closes her Conception (the mother, the expected father, the babies). Repair Saves & Logs adds both to older records where her Conception has no Birth and her one Death or Disappeared record came before the babies were due, and asks the player where the records cannot settle it. Villagers already in a village who arrived before this record existed (no Birth or Arrived record with their name, head and body) each get one the same way, only when the player says so, marked "Recorded afterwards (arrived before this log existed)", as "Founder" when the village's first Village History snapshot lists them and otherwise with how they came unknown -- exactly once: 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Data\Arrivals\Virtual Villagers 4 Arrivals Recorded - Save <n>.dat' then says it is done; Start Over deletes it. A villager the save says was born here (their record keeps their parents) who has no Birth or Arrived record -- born before the log existed -- gets, the same way and only when the player says so, a Birth record written from the save, with their parents as the save keeps them, marked "Recorded afterwards (born before this log existed)" -- exactly once: 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Births\Virtual Villagers 4 Births Recorded - Save <n>.dat' then says it is done; Start Over deletes it. At every save, the village is checked against the one saved before, villager by villager by who they are (name, sex, looks, likes and dislikes, and an age that fits; never by record number, which every load, a full village and the Elder Totems move change): a villager who left with no Death or Disappeared record, or arrived with no birth or known arrival, is written with everything known about them to the Unaccounted Villagers log ('Virtual Villagers 4 Unaccounted Villagers Log <n>.txt' in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Unaccounted Villagers'). Both logs are headed with the village and its save slot, are created when a village is started and again after Start Over (which deletes them with the village), only ever grow, and start a new numbered file after every 256 records. The village as it was at each save is kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Unaccounted Villagers\Virtual Villagers 4 Villagers at Last Save - Save <n>.dat' ('... Village Roster ...' in a save an older version made); Start Over deletes it. A villager who is in the village at both saves with another head or body (an island event the Island Events log did not see, or any other change the game made) is written to the Births and Conceptions log as an 'Appearance changed' record, 'Changed by: the game', unless Change Appearance or the Island Events log already wrote one for that look; a newcomer never is. The cause is the one The Tree of Life itself records and shows on the grave. **The first save after this patch is installed only starts the check: nothing is reported about anything that happened before it.** **The patch's DLL is loaded and its hooks installed as soon as the game is opened, before any village is loaded, so the deaths, burials, disappearances and arrivals of the catch-up on time away (and of a Time Warp) are recorded as they happen, like any others.** **The logs are written by Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File's DLL: with that patch off, none of them is written.** **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. That base's companion loads this patch's DLL; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the game runs unchanged.

**Needs Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File on for the Deaths and Unaccounted Villagers logs, which that patch's DLL writes (without it neither is written). The Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically.**

- Behavior changes: After the burial's Roster of the Dead write, the Death record is written with the cause, skill line and epitaph the game gave the grave; a body the game removes unburied gets "no grave". The listed removals of a living villager write a Disappeared record before the game takes them; the Custom Island Event's "Disappears" is reported by the Story / Cheat Upgrades DLL. Graves with no Death record: VvfpCauseScanGraves counts, writing nothing, the graves the village's Deaths log has no record for (the first-load check lists them for the player); VvfpCauseRepairGraves records the player's answer. Only after Repair, at each save of that village in the session, each such grave gets a Death record from the grave, filed by RecordGravesMissingFromLog in "VVFP Parentage Export.dll" (which counts the log's own and held records first, and takes the head, body, likes and dislikes from the Village History log); a villager the previous save held who was buried unseen is then not an Unaccounted record. The graves whose record is in the log are kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Deaths\Virtual Villagers 4 Graves Logged - Save <n>.dat' (written atomically; deleted by Start Over). The grave's Done writes an Epitaph changed record when the epitaph's text changed; spaces typed before or after the same words are not a change. Every villager the game's own creators make is noted as an arrival; after each save the village is compared with the roster kept at the save before, and any departure with no Death or Disappeared record, or arrival with no known arrival, is written to the Unaccounted Villagers log. The comparison follows each villager by identity, never by record number (v1.35.80): each villager of the last save is matched one to one to a villager now by name, sex, head, body, likes and dislikes with the age gone on by the time every matched villager aged, then by name, sex and looks, then -- only when one villager on each side is such -- through a changed head, a rename or a rejuvenation; a departure the game reported (a burial, a body's removal, a disappearance) accounts for the villager it names, by name, sex and looks, before any matching; a villager who only moved to another record is neither Left nor Arrived, and one with a Death or Disappeared record is never Left. Statues, totems and look-alikes are no villagers. The roster is kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Unaccounted Villagers\Virtual Villagers 4 Villagers at Last Save - Save <n>.dat', or '... Village Roster ...' in a save an older version made, never renamed; under both names the one written last (written atomically; deleted by Start Over). Arrivals: a villager a creator made that is neither a birth (the path's own return addresses, read at fixed places on the stack, or the Births and Conceptions log's note) nor a record the game takes away again is decided at the next tick, named by its path (Founder, the island event, Barrel of Babies, the developer F7 command in The Tree of Life), or "added outside a recorded event" when no listed path made it, and gets an Arrived record at the next save of that village (at its departure if it leaves first); the Story / Cheat Upgrades DLL names the Custom Island Event's (VvfpCauseArrivedBy). A founder is written only at a save with no village saved in the slot before. Arrivals before this record existed: VvfpCauseScanArrivals counts, writing nothing, the villagers (believers, with no parents on their record) the village's Births and Conceptions log has no Birth or Arrived record for (name, head and body), for the first-load check; VvfpCauseRepairArrivals records the answer. Only after Repair, at the next save, each gets an Arrived record filed by RecordArrivalsMissingFromLog in "VVFP Parentage Export.dll", and none is an Unaccounted record; once all are on disk 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Arrivals\Virtual Villagers 4 Arrivals Recorded - Save <n>.dat' (deleted by Start Over) ends the backfill for good. All records are written through WriteVillageRecord in "VVFP Parentage Export.dll".
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the Origins companion loads the DLL, which detours the listed sites at run time only after verifying every site's stock bytes; any other build installs nothing. No game value is changed: health, age, the graves, the Roster of the Dead and the save are only read; each detoured site's own instructions run unchanged after the check.
- Dependencies: vv4_enable_origins_exclusive_features
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Louder Wind Flutes (`vv4_louder_wind_flutes`)

The wind flutes that play in fog once you have found a Wind Flute (every 60 to 89 seconds of the game's clock while the fog lasts: Flute1 with 1 to 4 flutes found, Flute3 with 5 to 9, Flute5 with 10 to 12) are 2.5 times louder, so they are heard clearly over the music. The game's own flute recordings are much quieter than its music, and the game already plays them at full volume, so the sounds themselves are made louder as the game loads them, without any distortion. Every other sound, the music, the Sound and Music sliders and when the flutes play are unchanged; the game's sound files are never changed. **On by default.** **Needs no other patch.** **Works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Not yet heard in a running game** (checked with the game's own sound library and by emulation of the stock executable). The companion is "VVFP VV4 Louder Flutes.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; saves are never written by it.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The sound loader's call of FSOUND_Sample_Load (0x40C4E1 in 0x40C490, every sound effect the game loads) goes to the companion, which makes the same call; when the file is Flute1.ogg, Flute3.ogg or Flute5.ogg and FMOD made a 16-bit signed PCM sample, it locks the whole sample (FSOUND_Sample_Lock), multiplies every sample by 5/2, kept within -32768..32767, and unlocks it: the flutes 2.5 times (+8 dB) louder. Peaks become -1.2, -3.8 and -3.5 dBFS; nothing is clipped.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces the one call at run time, only after verifying its stock bytes; FMOD functions missing from the game's fmod.dll mean nothing is installed. Every other sound and the music are loaded exactly as before; the volume the game asks for (3.0 x the Sound slider, 0x4AB3A8), when the flutes play (the weather update 0x46BE10) and which flute plays are the game's own. A sample that is not 16-bit signed PCM, or that FMOD does not hand back whole, is left as it is. The game's sound files are never changed; nothing is written to a save, a villager record or a file; no text is shown.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: the real fmod.dll 3.74 loads each flute as 16-bit stereo signed PCM (mode 0x151) and hands back the whole sample from FSOUND_Sample_Lock, equal within 1 to a decode of the .ogg (a scratch 32-bit probe, 2026-11-10); the companion's install and its scaling are emulated on the rendered executable in tests/test_vv4_louder_wind_flutes.py; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Manual Drop-Breeding overrides Birth Control (`vv4_manual_drop_breeding_overrides_birth_control`)

**Needs no other patch: the 50-and-over refusal it lifts is The Tree of Life's own; this game has no Birth Control patch.** When you drop an adult villager onto an adult of the opposite sex, a woman aged 50 or older is no longer refused. It is not a guarantee: the game's usual chances still decide whether the pair gets along and whether a baby is conceived, exactly as for any other couple, so a drop can still fail. Every other rule of the drop is unchanged: a man and a woman, both adults, both alive and well, the woman not already expecting or nursing, and the game's own food, love-shack and population checks. The game never looks at the Parenting preference on a manual drop, and Parenting skill (the dropped villager's) only changes the chances without ever blocking a drop, so an unchecked preference or no skill never stopped one, with or without this patch. Only the manual drop is changed: villagers pairing up on their own, catch-up, events and Birth Control's own rules stay as they are. Off by default.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: After the stock conception roll succeeds, the pairing handler at VA 0x460C10 (step 15 of the dispatcher 0x46A030) returns without calling the pregnancy writer when either participant is a woman at internal age 1000 (50) or older. The player's drop and villagers pairing up on their own (the live Embracing route) both reach this handler through action 3 (0x455420), so the refusal is skipped only for the drop: file 0x60E67 jumps to the unused padding at 0x460EB3, which continues at the stock writer call 0x460E8E when the drop's return address 0x440EF2 sits at [esp+0x40] -- the depth the drop's own call chain (0x440EED -> 0x45DEC0 -> 0x44F720 -> 0x455420 -> 0x46A030 -> 0x460C10) puts it, because the drop queues step 15 on an emptied queue and the handler runs inside that call -- so she conceives on a passing roll like any other woman. Every other entry runs the stock check unchanged (its first instruction, mov eax,0x3E8, is replayed in the padding at 0x460EC5). Autonomous pairing (0x463FC3, from the category chooser 0x4639B0) queues a walk to the partner before step 15, so its handler runs later from the walk's arrival (0x468C10) and never with the drop's call on the stack: an initiating woman of 50 or older is still refused after the stock roll, exactly as stock. Catch-up conceives through its own step executor (0x464FA0) and never reaches this handler.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: Every other stock manual-drop rule is unchanged and still refuses the drop: same sex, either villager under internal age 360 (18), either villager dead or ill, a woman already expecting or nursing, and the game's own food, love-shack and population checks. The stock Parenting skill-attempt roll and the stock conception roll (RNG(300) against Parenting skill and technology) are unchanged and still decide; a drop can fail at either one. Autonomous pairing keeps the stock woman-aged-50-or-older refusal in the shared handler; the partner chooser and candidate scans, catch-up, Island Events and every other birth route, the conception and pregnancy writers, delivery, and automatic physical-capacity safety are unchanged.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the player's drop and autonomous pairing are each emulated from their real call sites through the game's own action table, step queue and dispatcher into the handler in tests/test_manual_drop_breeding.py; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 3; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### More Island Events (`vv4_more_island_events`)

Adds new island events, written by the owner, to the ones the game draws from (more come in later versions). Five here: The Aspiring Adventurer -- a villager who loves to explore sees something glinting off the safe path. "Go investigate!" finds a pile of dirt, a stack of meat (food) or a golden chest of artifacts (tech points); half the time the adventurer gets home (with the find, or with a friend's help), half the time a trap leads to death (a grave) or a disappearance (no grave). "Stay on the safe path" brings them home 9 times in 10; otherwise they are lost: hurt, healed or disabled, a skilled survivalist, killed, gone, or they join another tribe. The event is one more island event, listed and drawn like the game's own (1 in the number listed); it needs two villagers of 14 or more who are not nursing a baby and not a body or a ghost, and the adventurer and the friend who may come to help are drawn from them. The reward is a random amount from the smallest to the largest food or tech-point gain of the game's own island events (300 food for the meat, 500 to 5,000 tech points for the chest); with Island Events Scale With Population or With Stored Food and Tech Points ticked, the amount scales as that patch scales the game's own events. Deaths are the game's own ("Unknown causes", with a grave); a disappearance is logged as one in the Deaths log. The popups show the owner's text in pages that fit the screen (OK shows the next); the effects wait for the page that tells them, and the Island Events log keeps one entry for each event. And The Playful Dolphins (The Tree of Life only): a villager of 14 or more, swimming underwater, spots a pod of dolphins. "Swim towards the dolphins": half the time the swimmer watches them hunt -- Farming becomes 100 (the game's maximum) and the village gains a large food award (twice a normal one: 600 food before the scaling); half the time a tail slaps the swimmer, who loses 30 to 50 health but never dies of it (at least 1 is left). "Hang back": a small food award (half a normal one: 150 food before the scaling). It needs two villagers of 14 or more who are not nursing a baby and not a body or a ghost; it needs no puzzle (not the Fishing Nets); it has its own share of the draw. And The Mysterious Mask (The Tree of Life only): a group of 2 to 4 children under 14 finds a strange carved mask at the edge of the forest, and the player picks one of four answers: "Wait for their parents to come" or "Cry for help" (the children are safe), "Walk towards the clearing" or "Walk towards the forest" (the same odds: home safe 50%, else lost -- then rescued 75% or captured 25%, when every child of the group is gone for good, no graves). The elders' speech tells what happened, and in every ending five volunteers of 18 or more leave on an expedition for good (no graves). It needs a population of 61 or more (the living plus the babies carried), two children under 14 and five villagers of 18 or more who are not nursing a baby and not a body or a ghost; it has its own share of the draw. And The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings (all five games; one popup each, OK only). The Remembrance Ceremony needs at least one grave: everyone joins in -- children, nursing mothers and fathers, everyone -- each at the graveyard, "Honoring the Dead", and the feast quietly uses 10 food for every villager (never below 0). The Rumblings needs every puzzle solved and a finished structure: an earthquake damages each of the three population huts, the clothing hut, the love shack, the nursery school and the hospital one time in four (at least one always), each losing 10 to 100% of its building work; the builders must build it again (at 100% it is unbuilt again, as in a new village; an unbuilt one can be moved). Nobody is hurt; a village over its limit keeps everyone and has no new births until it is rebuilt. Each has its own share of the draw and can come again. Off by default; part of Classic VV Difficulty; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Needs no other patch.** **Unverified in play: the event has not been seen in a running game** (emulated on the stock executable). The companion is "VVFP More Island Events.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; nothing is saved by it.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Classic VV Difficulty: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: The event is one more island event, listed and drawn like the game's own (1 in the number listed). It can happen only while at least two villagers may go: 14 or more (280 age units), alive and present, not carrying a baby, and not a body or a ghost; the adventurer and the friend of ending A8 are drawn from them, the friend never the adventurer. Choice A, "Go investigate!": the find 50% a pile of dirt, 25% meat (a food award: 300 food), 25% a golden chest (a tech award: 500 to 5,000 tech points); then 50% a surviving ending (after the dirt A7 or A9; after a find A1, A5 or A8, which give the reward) and 50% a deadly one (A2 and A4 die, the game's own death with cause -1 and a grave; A3 and A6 disappear, no body), each equally likely within its half. Choice B, "Stay on the safe path": 90% home safe; 10% lost, then 1 in 6 each: the healers (1 in 3 each: dies; a full recovery; health set to 10-50 and running disliked), joins another tribe (gone for good, no grave), a survivalist (+20 to 30 in Farming, Building, Research or Healing, at most 100), dies under a fallen tree, dies at the bottom of a cliff, disappears. The reward is drawn, each amount equally likely, from the game's smallest to its largest stock island-event gain of that kind (src/vv_aspiring_adventurer.py AWARD_RANGES), and goes through the game's own food or tech writer; with Island Events Scale With Population or With Stored Food and Tech Points ticked, the amount scales as that patch scales the game's own events. The effects wait for their own page (the page that ends the ending's text), and the event writes its own one Island Events log entry; a disappearance is told to the Cause of Death companion (VvfpCauseVanishedBy), so its Deaths log records it as one. The owner's words, by translation key (the event's popup shows the player's language when a translation has them), are laid out in pages that fit the game's popup -- whole paragraphs, else whole sentences -- each shown in turn with OK. The Playful Dolphins (The Tree of Life): the swimmer is a villager who may be picked (vv4_eligible: present +0x1CC4, alive +0x1C40, 14 or more +0x1B8C, adv_is_protected: nursing +0x1C4C, a body or ghost +0x1CC7), drawn among them; it can happen while two such villagers live, with no puzzle (not the Fishing Nets). One more two-choice object with the Adventurer's virtual table and methods (adv_flow), its own entry in the draw (t_list). "Swim towards the dolphins": rand(100) < 50 the hunt -- Farming (float +0x1C5C) +200 capped at 100.0, as the game's own skill adder 0x46AD80 caps (the double 100.0 at 0x48A7C0) -- and a large food award (the game's range x 2, then Island Events Scale, through 0x41D920), else the tail slap: health (+0x1C40, 0..100, in the block +0x1C34) minus 30 to 50, never below 1, through the game's own setter 0x46AF00 (value, cause -1: never its death path). "Hang back": a small food award (the range x 1 / 2, then Island Events Scale). The effects are made when the ending's last page is shown, with the event's one Island Events log entry. No site of its own. The Mysterious Mask (The Tree of Life): the group is 4 children under 14 (+0x1B8C < 280), or all of them when fewer (at least 2), the expedition 5 villagers of 18 or more (vv4_eligible and +0x1B8C >= 360), each drawn among those left; everyone passes adv_is_protected (nursing +0x1C4C, a body or ghost +0x1CC7); the population 61 or more counted as the game's own 0x467610 counts (present +0x1CC4, not a body +0x1CC7, health +0x1C40 > 0, plus the babies +0x1C50 while carrying +0x1C4C). One more object with the Adventurer's virtual table and methods (adv_flow, answers 4: the shared multi-answer popup native/shared/vvfp_multi_answer.h, ids 4 and 5 and the keys 1 to 4), its own entry in the draw (t_list). A walk: rand(100) < 50 home safe, else lost: rand(100) < 25 captured, else rescued. Its pages are laid out 6 lines shorter (3 for each answer past two) so the popup is no taller than a two-answer one. The five volunteers, and when captured every child of the group, are removed as a living villager is (adv_vv345.inc t_vanish: no body, no grave; told to Cause of Death) when the elders' last page is shown, with the event's one Island Events log entry. No site of its own. The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings (ceremony_core.inc, ceremony_games.inc): each its own entry in the draw (t_list), no site of its own; the game's own single-result popup shows the owner's words, the effects are made as it is built, with the event's one Island Events log entry. The Remembrance Ceremony: needs at least one grave (the game's own grave count); every living, present villager is started on its own through the game's own stop and action starter, as its Day of Honor starts each one (so no group filter leaves anyone out), at the graveyard, "Honoring the Dead"; the feast uses 10 food for every villager the game counts, never below 0 (Blessings Day's own rule). The Rumblings: needs every puzzle of the game's Puzzles screen solved and one of the three population huts, the clothing hut, the love shack, the nursery school and the hospital finished; each finished one rand(100) < 25 (none: one of them at random), each losing 10 + rand(91) percent of its building work, written as the states the game's own construction passes through (at 100% the new village's state); the building's effect handle freed and set to -1; the nursery school's teacher let go; a damaged population hut's count of the still-locked "3 huts" trophy taken back (saved with the village at the state's +0x328), so it still needs three different huts.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion writes each site at run time, only after verifying every site's stock bytes (all of them, or none); without it the event does not exist. Every stock event, its odds, the island-event timer and counting, the rescue rules and Custom Island Events are unchanged; nothing is saved by the companion.
- Dependencies: none
