#### Log Every Death, Disappearance and Unaccounted Villager (`vv5_cause_of_death`)

Every death that leaves a body is written to the Deaths log ('Virtual Villagers 5 Deaths Log <n>.txt' in the save slot's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Deaths and Disappearances' folder beside the game's saves, or 'Deaths' in a save an older version made: nothing is moved) when it is final: when the body is buried, with the skill line and epitaph the grave was given, or when the game removes a body nobody buried ("no grave"). Each Death record gives the villager's name, head, body, likes and dislikes, their age at death in the game's own units (20 per year, as the Village Population log prints Age), the cause, the grave and the epitaph. A villager brought back to life gets no Death record. A villager taken by the Custom Island Event's "Disappears" gets a "Disappeared" record (the game itself has no such event), and a believer who goes over to the Heathens (faith falling to 0, in play or while the game catches up on time away or a Time Warp; The Spa; The Cracked Mask; or the Custom Island Event's "Becomes a Heathen") leaves the tribe with a "Disappeared" record, "Left the tribe: became a Heathen", written the moment it happens (a Heathen is never a villager; converted back, they get an "Arrived" record again), and editing a grave's epitaph adds an "Epitaph changed" record with the old and new text. A grave the Deaths log has no record for -- dug before the log was kept, or while the game was catching up on time away -- is given a Death record only when the player says so -- Repair Logs in the patcher window, or Repair when the game asks as it closes (with "Check logs automatically" on, and only if something is wrong); nothing is ever asked while the village is played. The record is made from the grave (name, age at death, skill line, epitaph, and the cause where the game or this patch knows it) with the head, body, likes and dislikes of the villager's last Village History snapshot ("(unknown)" when that does not settle who it was), and marked "Recorded from the grave". Which graves have their record is kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Deaths\Virtual Villagers 5 Graves Logged - Save <n>.dat', so no grave is recorded twice; Start Over deletes it. Every villager who joins the village without being born into it -- a new village's founders, an island event's newcomer, the Barrel of Babies, the Custom Island Event's new villagers, a Heathen converted to a believer (a Heathen is never a villager) -- gets an "Arrived" record in the Births and Conceptions log ('Virtual Villagers 5 Births and Conceptions Log <n>.txt'), written at the next save: the name, the age when they arrived, sex, head, body, likes, dislikes, skills, and how they came ("Founder", the island event's title, "Barrel of Babies", "Custom Island Event", "Converted from the Heathens", or "unknown"). A birth is never an arrival. A mother who dies or disappears while nursing (the game's own word for a mother whose babies are not yet born) loses them with her: they never become villagers and get no grave, so her Death or Disappeared record says "Nursing: yes, <n> babies (never born: lost with their mother)", and a "Lost before birth" record in the Births and Conceptions log closes her Conception (the mother, the expected father, the babies). Repair Saves & Logs adds both to older records where her Conception has no Birth and her one Death or Disappeared record came before the babies were due, and asks the player where the records cannot settle it. Villagers already in a village who arrived before this record existed (no Birth or Arrived record with their name, head and body) each get one the same way, only when the player says so, marked "Recorded afterwards (arrived before this log existed)", as "Founder" when the village's first Village History snapshot lists them and otherwise with how they came unknown -- exactly once: 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Data\Arrivals\Virtual Villagers 5 Arrivals Recorded - Save <n>.dat' then says it is done; Start Over deletes it. A villager the save says was born here (their record keeps their parents) who has no Birth or Arrived record -- born before the log existed -- gets, the same way and only when the player says so, a Birth record written from the save, with their parents as the save keeps them, marked "Recorded afterwards (born before this log existed)" -- exactly once: 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Births\Virtual Villagers 5 Births Recorded - Save <n>.dat' then says it is done; Start Over deletes it. At every save, the village is checked against the one saved before, villager by villager by who they are (name, sex, looks, likes and dislikes, and an age that fits; never by record number, which every load, a full village and the Elder Totems move change): a villager who left with no Death or Disappeared record, or arrived with no birth or known arrival, is written with everything known about them to the Unaccounted Villagers log ('Virtual Villagers 5 Unaccounted Villagers Log <n>.txt' in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Unaccounted Villagers'). Both logs are headed with the village and its save slot, are created when a village is started and again after Start Over (which deletes them with the village), only ever grow, and start a new numbered file after every 256 records. The village as it was at each save is kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Unaccounted Villagers\Virtual Villagers 5 Villagers at Last Save - Save <n>.dat' ('... Village Roster ...' in a save an older version made); Start Over deletes it. A villager who is in the village at both saves with another head or body (an island event the Island Events log did not see, or any other change the game made) is written to the Births and Conceptions log as an 'Appearance changed' record, 'Changed by: the game', unless Change Appearance or the Island Events log already wrote one for that look; a newcomer never is. The cause is the one New Believers itself records and shows on the grave. **The first save after this patch is installed only starts the check: nothing is reported about anything that happened before it.** **The patch's DLL is loaded and its hooks installed as soon as the game is opened, before any village is loaded, so the deaths, burials, disappearances and arrivals of the catch-up on time away (and of a Time Warp) are recorded as they happen, like any others.** **The logs are written by Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File's DLL: with that patch off, none of them is written.** **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. That base's companion loads this patch's DLL; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the game runs unchanged.

**Needs Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File on for the Deaths and Unaccounted Villagers logs, which that patch's DLL writes (without it neither is written). The Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically.**

- Behavior changes: After the burial's Roster of the Dead write, the Death record is written with the cause, skill line and epitaph the game gave the grave; a body the game removes unburied gets "no grave". The listed removals of a living villager write a Disappeared record before the game takes them; the Custom Island Event's "Disappears" is reported by the Story / Cheat Upgrades DLL. Graves with no Death record: VvfpCauseScanGraves counts, writing nothing, the graves the village's Deaths log has no record for (the first-load check lists them for the player); VvfpCauseRepairGraves records the player's answer. Only after Repair, at each save of that village in the session, each such grave gets a Death record from the grave, filed by RecordGravesMissingFromLog in "VVFP Parentage Export.dll" (which counts the log's own and held records first, and takes the head, body, likes and dislikes from the Village History log); a villager the previous save held who was buried unseen is then not an Unaccounted record. The graves whose record is in the log are kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Deaths\Virtual Villagers 5 Graves Logged - Save <n>.dat' (written atomically; deleted by Start Over). The grave's Done writes an Epitaph changed record when the epitaph's text changed; spaces typed before or after the same words are not a change. Every villager the game's own creators make is noted as an arrival; after each save the village is compared with the roster kept at the save before, and any departure with no Death or Disappeared record, or arrival with no known arrival, is written to the Unaccounted Villagers log. The comparison follows each villager by identity, never by record number (v1.35.80): each villager of the last save is matched one to one to a villager now by name, sex, head, body, likes and dislikes with the age gone on by the time every matched villager aged, then by name, sex and looks, then -- only when one villager on each side is such -- through a changed head, a rename or a rejuvenation; a departure the game reported (a burial, a body's removal, a disappearance) accounts for the villager it names, by name, sex and looks, before any matching; a villager who only moved to another record is neither Left nor Arrived, and one with a Death or Disappeared record is never Left. Statues, totems and look-alikes are no villagers. The roster is kept in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Unaccounted Villagers\Virtual Villagers 5 Villagers at Last Save - Save <n>.dat', or '... Village Roster ...' in a save an older version made, never renamed; under both names the one written last (written atomically; deleted by Start Over). Arrivals: a villager a creator made that is neither a birth (the path's own return addresses, read at fixed places on the stack, or the Births and Conceptions log's note) nor a record the game takes away again is decided at the next tick, named by its path (Founder, the island event, Barrel of Babies, the developer F7 command in The Tree of Life), or "added outside a recorded event" when no listed path made it, and gets an Arrived record at the next save of that village (at its departure if it leaves first); the Story / Cheat Upgrades DLL names the Custom Island Event's (VvfpCauseArrivedBy); a Heathen made by a creator is not one, and a Heathen whose faction byte +0x1CEC the tick sees cleared is ("Converted from the Heathens"). A founder is written only at a save with no village saved in the slot before. A believer made a Heathen leaves the tribe, seen at the faction setter's entry (0x466880, called to set +0x1CEC from the conversion 0x4669E0 -- faith 0 or below, live or in the catch-up -- The Spa or The Cracked Mask), or else by the tick seeing the byte set: a Disappeared record ("Left the tribe: became a Heathen") written then, with no departure reported to the roster, which keeps Heathens, so never an Unaccounted record; an Arrived record not yet written is written first. Arrivals before this record existed: VvfpCauseScanArrivals counts, writing nothing, the villagers (believers, with no parents on their record) the village's Births and Conceptions log has no Birth or Arrived record for (name, head and body), for the first-load check; VvfpCauseRepairArrivals records the answer. Only after Repair, at the next save, each gets an Arrived record filed by RecordArrivalsMissingFromLog in "VVFP Parentage Export.dll", and none is an Unaccounted record; once all are on disk 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Arrivals\Virtual Villagers 5 Arrivals Recorded - Save <n>.dat' (deleted by Start Over) ends the backfill for good. All records are written through WriteVillageRecord in "VVFP Parentage Export.dll".
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the Origins companion loads the DLL, which detours the listed sites at run time only after verifying every site's stock bytes; any other build installs nothing. No game value is changed: health, age, the graves, the Roster of the Dead and the save are only read; each detoured site's own instructions run unchanged after the check.
- Dependencies: vv5_enable_origins_exclusive_features
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Manual Drop-Breeding overrides Birth Control (`vv5_manual_drop_breeding_overrides_birth_control`)

**Needs no other patch: the 50-and-over refusal it lifts is New Believers' own; this game has no Birth Control patch.** When you drop an adult villager onto an adult of the opposite sex, a woman aged 50 or older is no longer refused. It is not a guarantee: the game's usual chances still decide whether the pair gets along and whether a baby is conceived, exactly as for any other couple, so a drop can still fail. Every other rule of the drop is unchanged: a man and a woman, both adults, both alive and well, the woman not already expecting or nursing, and the game's own food, love-shack and population checks. The game never looks at the Parenting preference on a manual drop, and Parenting skill (the dropped villager's) only changes the chances without ever blocking a drop, so an unchecked preference or no skill never stopped one, with or without this patch. Only the manual drop is changed: villagers pairing up on their own, catch-up, events and Birth Control's own rules stay as they are. Off by default.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: After the stock conception roll succeeds, the pairing handler at VA 0x4689A0 (step 16 of the dispatcher 0x473590) returns without calling the pregnancy writer when either participant is a woman at internal age 1000 (50) or older. The player's drop and villagers pairing up on their own (the live Embracing route) both reach this handler through action 5 (0x45D010), so the refusal is skipped only for the drop: file 0x68BC4 jumps to unused .text padding at 0x494BC0, which continues at the stock writer call 0x468BEB when the drop's return address 0x44402D sits at [esp+0x4C] -- the depth the drop's own call chain (0x444028 -> 0x465580 -> 0x452BD0 -> 0x45D010 -> 0x473590 -> 0x4689A0) puts it, because the drop queues step 16 on an emptied queue and the handler runs inside that call -- so she conceives on a passing roll like any other woman. Every other entry replays the displaced mov eax,0x3E8 and returns to the stock check at 0x468BC9, unchanged. Autonomous pairing (0x46CB1E) queues a walk to the partner before step 16, so its handler runs later from the walk's arrival (0x4733F0) and never with the drop's call on the stack: an initiating woman of 50 or older is still refused after the stock roll, exactly as stock. Catch-up conceives through its own step executor (0x46E020) and never reaches this handler.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: Every other stock manual-drop rule is unchanged and still refuses the drop: same sex, either villager under internal age 360 (18), either villager dead or ill, a woman already expecting or nursing, and the game's own food, love-shack and population checks. The stock Parenting skill-attempt roll and the stock conception roll (RNG(300) against Parenting skill and technology) are unchanged and still decide; a drop can fail at either one. Autonomous pairing keeps the stock woman-aged-50-or-older refusal in the shared handler; the partner chooser and candidate scans, catch-up, Island Events and every other birth route, the conception and pregnancy writers, delivery, and automatic physical-capacity safety are unchanged.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the player's drop and autonomous pairing are each emulated from their real call sites through the game's own action table, step queue and dispatcher into the handler in tests/test_manual_drop_breeding.py; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 2; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Memorial Actions Can Also Occur at the Heathen Hovel (`vv5_hovel_memorial_actions`)

Best paired with "Shrine to the Ancestors". Villagers will sometimes come here to pay their respects to those that passed on, and others that guide their fate. **Needs no other patch.** Once every Heathen has been converted and the villagers have fixed up the old Heathen hovel (the game's own moment: The Last Heathen is solved and the hovel's flower cover appears), the hovel becomes a memorial for good, even if Heathens come back later. From then on, a villager who goes "Honoring the dead" on an ordinary day honors at the hovel a quarter of the time: they still go for their flowers first, then lay them in front of the hovel instead of at the graves. A villager "Reflecting" also reflects in front of the hovel a quarter of the time instead of in the usual spot. Each walk goes to a random point of the open ground just in front of the hovel. The Day of Honor island event's honoring, every other action and every other place are unchanged, and before the memorial nothing changes. Nothing is saved: the game's own puzzle progress decides it. **New Believers never sends villagers "Reflecting" by itself: only a Custom Island Event (Story / Cheat Upgrades) does, so the Reflecting part shows only then.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Respecting the Legacy of Isola: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: The hovel is a memorial once The Last Heathen (project 25) is done (0x43AE80 on 0x51E008): the game solves it when no Heathen is left and the villagers have fixed up the mud hut (0x437120, behaviour 0xD8, 0x46D487), and draws the hovel's flower cover from then on (0x4370E0). Project progress is saved and never goes back, so the hovel stays a memorial even when Heathens appear again. The everyday "Honoring the dead" (behaviour 17, 0x4595B0) started by its chooser 0x46B0F0 (0x46B145): with the memorial, rand(100) < 25 sends its three walks to the graves (area 0x7B) to random points in front of the hovel instead, x = 2176 + rand(97), y = 1576 + rand(25) (the feet's point; 2176..2272 by 1576..1600); its walk for the flowers (area 0x7A) is unchanged. "Reflecting" (behaviour 29, 0x457E90; registered at 0x46409E, so every start of it): with the memorial, rand(100) < 25 sends its five go-tos to random points in front of the hovel instead of 1530..1803 by 1606..1805.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The Day of Honor island event's honoring (behaviour 17 for everyone, 0x414DDA -> 0x470C60) and the Custom Island Event's "Honoring the dead [Day of Honor]" are as stock; so are "Honoring the dead (another way)" (behaviour 46, 0x4567C0) and every other action. Before The Last Heathen is solved everything is as stock. The actions' text, gestures, speeds, flags and length are their own. No save, sidecar or villager-record byte is written.

#### More Island Events (`vv5_more_island_events`)

Adds new island events, written by the owner, to the ones the game draws from (more come in later versions). Three here: The Aspiring Adventurer -- a villager who loves to explore sees something glinting off the safe path. "Go investigate!" finds a pile of dirt, a stack of meat (food) or a golden chest of artifacts (tech points); half the time the adventurer gets home (with the find, or with a friend's help), half the time a trap leads to death (a grave) or a disappearance (no grave). "Stay on the safe path" brings them home 9 times in 10; otherwise they are lost: hurt, healed or disabled, a skilled survivalist, killed, gone, or they become a Heathen. The event is one more island event, listed and drawn like the game's own (1 in the number listed); it needs two villagers of 14 or more who are not nursing a baby and not a Heathen, the chief, the Retired Chief or another of the special roles the game's own picker skips, or a Reanimated spirit, and the adventurer and the friend who may come to help are drawn from them. The reward is a random amount from the smallest to the largest food or tech-point gain of the game's own island events (50 to 300 food for the meat, 500 to 3,000 tech points for the chest); with Island Events Scale With Population or With Stored Food and Tech Points ticked, the amount scales as that patch scales the game's own events. Deaths are the game's own ("Unknown causes", with a grave); a disappearance is logged as one in the Deaths log. The popups show the owner's text in pages that fit the screen (OK shows the next); the effects wait for the page that tells them, and the Island Events log keeps one entry for each event. And The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings (all five games; one popup each, OK only). The Remembrance Ceremony needs at least one grave and The Last Heathen done (every Heathen converted and the hovel fixed up): everyone joins in -- children, nursing mothers and fathers, everyone who believes -- each at the mausoleum, "Honoring" -- or, with "Memorial Actions Can Also Occur at the Heathen Hovel" installed, half of them at the old Heathen hovel instead, "Honoring" or "Reflecting" (half the time each), and the feast quietly uses 10 food for every villager (never below 0). The Rumblings needs every puzzle solved and a finished structure: an earthquake damages each of the three population huts, the clothing hut and the love shack (the nursery school is left out) one time in four (at least one always), each losing 10 to 100% of its building work; the builders must build it again (at 100% it is unbuilt again, as in a new village; an unbuilt one can be moved). Nobody is hurt; a village over its limit keeps everyone and has no new births until it is rebuilt. Each has its own share of the draw and can come again. Off by default; part of Classic VV Difficulty; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Needs no other patch.** **Unverified in play: the event has not been seen in a running game** (emulated on the stock executable). The companion is "VVFP More Island Events.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; nothing is saved by it.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Classic VV Difficulty: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: The event is one more island event, listed and drawn like the game's own (1 in the number listed). It can happen only while at least two villagers may go: 14 or more (280 age units), alive and present, not carrying a baby, and not a Heathen, the chief, the Retired Chief or another of the special roles the game's own picker skips, or a Reanimated spirit; the adventurer and the friend of ending A8 are drawn from them, the friend never the adventurer. Choice A, "Go investigate!": the find 50% a pile of dirt, 25% meat (a food award: 50 to 300 food), 25% a golden chest (a tech award: 500 to 3,000 tech points); then 50% a surviving ending (after the dirt A7 or A9; after a find A1, A5 or A8, which give the reward) and 50% a deadly one (A2 and A4 die, the game's own death with cause -1 and a grave; A3 and A6 disappear, no body), each equally likely within its half. Choice B, "Stay on the safe path": 90% home safe; 10% lost, then 1 in 6 each: the healers (1 in 3 each: dies; a full recovery; health set to 10-50 and running disliked), becomes a Heathen, the game's own conversion ("the Isolans' tribe" with Guardians of Isola, else "the heathens' tribe"), a survivalist (+20 to 30 in Farming, Building, Research or Healing, at most 100), dies under a fallen tree, dies at the bottom of a cliff, disappears. The reward is drawn, each amount equally likely, from the game's smallest to its largest stock island-event gain of that kind (src/vv_aspiring_adventurer.py AWARD_RANGES), and goes through the game's own food or tech writer; with Island Events Scale With Population or With Stored Food and Tech Points ticked, the amount scales as that patch scales the game's own events. The effects wait for their own page (the page that ends the ending's text), and the event writes its own one Island Events log entry; a disappearance is told to the Cause of Death companion (VvfpCauseVanishedBy), so its Deaths log records it as one. The owner's words, by translation key (the event's popup shows the player's language when a translation has them), are laid out in pages that fit the game's popup -- whole paragraphs, else whole sentences -- each shown in turn with OK. The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings (ceremony_core.inc, ceremony_games.inc): each its own entry in the draw (t_list), no site of its own; the game's own single-result popup shows the owner's words, the effects are made as it is built, with the event's one Island Events log entry. The Remembrance Ceremony: needs at least one grave and The Last Heathen done (every Heathen converted and the hovel fixed up) (the game's own grave count); every living, present villager who is a believer is started on its own through the game's own stop and action starter, as its Day of Honor starts each one (so no group filter leaves anyone out), at the mausoleum, "Honoring" -- or, with "Memorial Actions Can Also Occur at the Heathen Hovel" installed, half of them at the old Heathen hovel instead, "Honoring" or "Reflecting" (half the time each); the feast uses 10 food for every villager the game counts, never below 0 (Blessings Day's own rule). The Rumblings: needs every puzzle of the game's Puzzles screen solved and one of the three population huts, the clothing hut and the love shack (the nursery school is left out) finished; each finished one rand(100) < 25 (none: one of them at random), each losing 10 + rand(91) percent of its building work, written as the states the game's own construction passes through (at 100% the new village's state); the building's effect handle freed and set to -1; a damaged population hut's count of the still-locked "3 huts" trophy taken back (saved with the village at the state's +0x328), so it still needs three different huts.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion writes each site at run time, only after verifying every site's stock bytes (all of them, or none); without it the event does not exist. Every stock event, its odds, the island-event timer and counting, the rescue rules and Custom Island Events are unchanged; nothing is saved by the companion.

#### New Heathens Get a Heathen's Faith (`vv5_new_heathens_get_heathen_faith`)

In New Believers a believer whose Faith drifts down to 0 (low food, sickness, too few believers) becomes a Heathen with Faith 0 or just below it, so one preaching brought them straight back. Every ordinary blue-mask Heathen the game makes has far less: a new village's get -67 to -38, Barrel O' Babies' -55. With this patch a believer the Faith drift turns Heathen (with or without Faith Loss is Doubled/Gains Halved) becomes an ordinary blue-mask Heathen with a random Faith from -67 to -38, drawn exactly as the game draws a new village's ordinary Heathens, and needs as much preaching as any blue Heathen to be won back. A Heathen's Faith never moves on its own in New Believers, so this is the Faith they keep until preached to. The game's own message "A villager has stopped believing in you!" is still shown. Island events that make a Heathen (The Spa, The Cracked Mask, the Custom Island Event) keep their own Faith (-10).

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The Faith setter 0x467F90: a believer whose new Faith is 0 or less becomes a Heathen (0x4669E0, called at 0x467FDF, as stock: the role +0x1CFC set to 0 at 0x4669F5, the bottom bar's eSayStoppedBelieving, string 0x48, at 0x4669EC). When the setter was called by FAITH_ADD 0x468020 for the Faith drift 0x468040 (its return 0x4681E3, or Faith Loss's tail cave 0x494F21), the cave 0x494F80 also clears the orange and red mask bytes (+0x1CED, +0x1CEE) and sets the Faith to be stored to -38 - rand(30). Stock stored the drift's Faith as it was (0 to -3). The mask a Heathen wears is chosen by the game's draw 0x4728C6..0x472919 from the role +0x1CFC (12 and 14-16 the purple Masters' and the Doctor's, 13 the Chief's, through the table 0x472B60) and then the kind bytes +0x1CED (orange, the chasers) and +0x1CEE (red, the scary ones); anything else is the blue mask. Faith plays no part in it. So a drift convert is made role 0 (0x4669E0's own) with neither kind byte: a blue-mask Heathen. -67 to -38 is the ordinary Heathens' Faith: the new village's Heathens are made at -1 (the creator 0x46FD20's last argument at 0x424AC0's calls) and every one still at -1 is then set to -38 - rand(30) (0x471050..0x471099) -- but five blue ones, set to -5, -9, -16, -23 and -30 (0x470F1F..0x471037); Barrel O' Babies! (heathens) makes its at -55 (push -0x37 at 0x4152B0, stored by 0x46FC31). No Heathen's Faith drifts: the life tick skips Heathens (0x472CB7).
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: Only the Faith drift's conversions change. The Spa (0x415D02) and The Cracked Mask (0x416C51) keep their -10 and their villager's mask; the Custom Island Event's "Becomes a Heathen" (which calls 0x4669E0 itself) and every Heathen the game makes are unchanged. Preaching, Spreading the Word and every conversion back to a believer (0x4668B0, Faith 55 below 5) are unchanged. One 5-byte call and one cave in the .text tail; no save byte is written.

#### Original Looks for Reset to Original (`vv5_original_look`)

Remembers each villager's original look -- the head, body and mask they had before any Change Appearance or island event changed them -- so Change Appearance and Change Appearance for All can put them back with Reset to original (the head look goes back to Auto too). A look the game itself gives a villager stays: The Secret City's robe for a new Tribal Chief, and the outfit the game's own clothing dialog puts on (The Lost Children to New Believers), become part of the original. Each villager's look is noted the first time the patcher sees them: when they are born or arrive, or, for a village you already have, the first time you play it with this patch; a look noted is never written over. For villagers changed before this patch, Repair Saves & Logs adds the original the patcher's logs prove -- the look before their earliest "Appearance changed" record -- and never guesses: when the logs cannot prove it, Change Appearance says the original look is not known. The looks are kept in the save's own Original Looks file, follow each villager (through deaths, reloads and renames) and are copied by Back Up Saves; Start Over clears them. **On by default.** Change Appearance is in the Origins upgrades: **Runs on the Origins-exclusive base, which the patcher installs automatically with it**, so selecting this patch also adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens. **Works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Not yet seen in a running game.** The companion is "VVFP Original Look.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; it changes nothing the game does. If it cannot be loaded, Change Appearance says the original look is not known.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked; the Origins-exclusive base it runs on is included automatically.**

- Behavior changes: Each villager's head, body and mask (the mask the Origins companion keeps, its VvfpMaskOf) are noted the first time the companion sees them, in the save's own "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <S>\Data\Original Looks\Original Looks - Save <S>.dat" (native/vvfp_original_look/original_look_store.inc), and never written over. The companion looks at the villager records from the game's own thread between frames (a WH_GETMESSAGE hook on that thread and a thread timer, at most every 250 ms): a villager present when a village is bound is a first-run original, one who appears after is a born / arrived one. A village is bound only once its records have held still for 1.5 s; one whose file is missing or belongs to another village is kept in memory only until the game itself saves that slot again (so the title screen's seeded records are never written into a slot's file). Repair Saves & Logs (game closed) adds the originals the logs prove (src/vv_original_look.py): the Old head and Old body of each villager's earliest "Appearance changed" record, the mask before it when logged; where a change is seen with no record, the original is marked not known. Change Appearance's Reset to original reads it through VvfpOriginalLookGet (native/shared/original_look.h). The game's own changes are kept: each instruction by which the game itself writes a villager's body outside Change Appearance and island events -- The Secret City's robe (0x45FBDE in the robing 0x45FBC0) and the clothing dialog's OK (The Lost Children 0x4228E4, The Secret City 0x41BF89, The Tree of Life 0x41961D, New Believers 0x419D68 and 0x419E8E) -- tells the companion the body first, which becomes part of that villager's original; the game's write then happens exactly as before. A New Home's stock game has no such writer. New Believers, with Heathens Keep Their Masks When Converted: a Heathen who joins the tribe keeping their mask (VvfpOriginalLookConverted) has the mask put on the original kept while they were a Heathen with no mask, so Reset to original gives it back; an original kept while they were a believer (one who left for the Heathens and came back) or one with a mask of its own stays. Each original notes whether its villager has been seen a believer since (the entry's last byte).
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the companion splices the game's own body writers listed above at run time, after checking their stock bytes, through the shared all-or-none writer (a different build installs none, and then the game's own changes are not kept); it writes no record byte of its own -- the splice makes the very write the game makes. Change Appearance and island events are never folded in: neither reaches those instructions. The save is never written; the Original Looks file is the patcher's own. A corrupt Original Looks file is moved aside intact and never read or written over; another village's file is never replaced on what is on screen alone.

#### Picked Up Collectibles Stay Collected When Dropped (`vv5_collectibles_stay_collected`)

A mushroom, relic or lab gear piece a child has picked up counts wherever the child puts it down -- dropped by you somewhere else, or set down when the child stops on the way: the mushroom's food and Mushrooms Found, or the collection piece (the reward for a piece already found) with its tips and completion messages, exactly once. In the normal game each counts only at its own place (the food bin, the relic spot, the lab) and is lost anywhere else. Nothing new is saved, so without the patch the game simply goes back to its own rule. **Needs no other patch.** Off by default; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The item listener's release (0x4146B0, run once when a child's carried item is put down: 0x466420 with -1 empties the hands and then dispatches) skips its three place tests (relics area 54, lab gear area 13, mushrooms area 5): 0x4146E6 ja becomes jmp 0x414713, so the stock award runs wherever the item is put down.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The awards (0x414713..0x414970), the pickup, the spawn and the save are unchanged. A release with empty hands dispatches nothing, so an item is credited once.

#### Popup When Believers Become Heathens (`vv5_heathen_conversion_notice`)

Meant to make VV5 harder and push players to take care of their tribe. When New Believers' own Faith drift turns believers into Heathens, the game says "A villager has stopped believing in you!" on the bottom bar for each one (that is the game's own line; with Guardians of Isola it is "A villager has left the tribe!"), but after a catch-up, a Time Warp or a time skip nothing told you how many left or why. With this patch a popup in the game's own island-event window sums them up: "The Breaking Point: Several of your villagers have lost faith due to the dire conditions amongst the tribe and have decided to join the heathens." and, below it, "3 villagers have left due to starvation, 1 due to sickness and 2 due to too few believers." With Guardians of Isola it says the villagers have lost trust in the village's ability to provide for their needs and have decided to join the Isolans, and lists the circumstances one a line ("Starvation: 3 villagers", "Food shortages", "Sickness", "Desire for a larger community"). Each believer is counted once, under the Faith roll that took their Faith: starvation (food under 10), hunger (food 10 to 250), sickness, or too few believers (fewer than 12). It comes once no believer has left for a few seconds, so a whole catch-up or time skip is one popup; it waits until no other island event is showing or on its way and the game is running, and like every island event it needs a living adult to show it to. It is not an island event: it does not move the next island event, is not counted in Island Events Seen and is not written to the Island Events log. It counts only believers the Faith drift turns Heathen: a believer an island event makes a Heathen, and Heathens island events or the Story / Cheat Upgrades make, never bring it. A popup still waiting when you quit is kept and comes after you load that save again, once; it goes with the village on Start Over or a deleted tribe and never shows in another save. Nothing in the game is changed by it. **On by default.** **Needs Story / Cheat Upgrades (on by default) for the popup: that patch's DLL shows it.** The companion is "VVFP Faith Notice.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; saves are never written by it (the waiting popup is kept in its own file in the patcher's save folder).

**Needs Story / Cheat Upgrades on for the popup, which that patch's DLL shows (without it only the game's own bottom-bar line is shown). Needed by Respecting the Legacy of Isola: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: Every believer the Faith drift 0x468040 turns Heathen (the life tick's call at 0x472D17; live, in the load-time catch-up, a Time Warp and Choose Time Skip Amount) is counted once, under the first loss roll that hit, by the executable's own thresholds: starvation -- food under 10 (rand(100) < [0x46805B], or the next roll < [0x46807B] with food under 10); hunger -- food 10 to 250 (< [0x46807B]); sickness (< [0x4680B8]); too few believers (fewer than 12: < 12 - n, or 2 x (12 - n) with Faith Loss is Doubled/Gains Halved, by the bytes at 0x468179); otherwise "a loss of faith". Once no conversion has come for 3 seconds, no time skip is under way, no island event popup is open, no pick, custom or island event is on its way and the game is running, VVFP Story Upgrades.dll arms one popup with its island-event notice (as the Time Skip's closing popup; the next island event keeps its time, the trigger's count is taken back, the Island Events log writes nothing): title FAITH_NOTICE_TITLE ("The Breaking Point"), "Several of your villagers have lost faith due to the dire conditions amongst the tribe and have decided to join the heathens." ("One of your villagers has ..." for one) and, in a paragraph of its own, "N villagers have left due to <reason>, M due to <reason> and K due to <reason>."; when the game's own string 0x48 (eSayStoppedBelieving, read at [0x5240A8 + 0x120] as 0x4506D0 reads it) says "left the tribe" (the Guardians of Isola rewrite), "Conditions have been dire amongst the tribe, and several villagers have been struggling to cope. They have lost trust in the village's ability to provide for their needs. Citing personal reasons, they have decided to join the Isolans." and "The following circumstances contributed to their decisions:" with one line a reason that came ("Starvation", "Food shortages", "Sickness", "Desire for a larger community", "Loss of trust": N villagers). The count starts again when it is armed. The bottom bar's line for each conversion is the game's own: 0x4669E0 says string 0x48 through the say bar 0x520F68 / 0x44EF60 (0x4669EC) on every conversion, with or without this patch. The batch still waiting for its popup (the total and each reason's count) is kept per save slot in <save folder>\Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <S>\Data\Faith Notice\Waiting Popup - Save <S>.dat (native/shared/sidecar_io.h: atomic writes; a locked or unreadable file is never replaced and is read again on the gate's throttle): written when the batch changes (at most every half second, from VvfpFaithNoticeKeep, which VVFP Story Upgrades.dll calls every frame, never from inside the life tick) and deleted the moment the popup is armed, when the Story queue's own file takes it over, so a quit after the arm never shows it twice. It is read when the game's save slot is first seen and added to what the load-time catch-up has turned since, then shown by the rules above. Start Over or a deleted tribe (VvfpFaithNoticeVillageReset) forgets it in memory, and native/shared/save_reset.c deletes the slot's folder with the file; a batch is only written to, and a file only read for, its own slot.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched and no Faith, villager record or save byte is written: the companion redirects five calls at run time, only after verifying every stock call and the thresholds' instructions, all or none; the drift runs exactly as before and draws the same random numbers. Island events that make a believer a Heathen (The Spa, The Cracked Mask, the Custom Island Event) show their own popup and are not counted. The popup is not an island event: it is not counted in Island Events Seen and the Island Events log writes nothing for it.
- Dependencies: none

#### Puddle Play Moves to the Lake Shore (`vv5_puddles_by_the_lake`)

When it rains, children in New Believers go "Playing in puddles" in the dry lake bed. Once The Lake holds water the game never starts that action again, because they cannot swim. With this patch, after The Lake has water, children still go "Playing in puddles" when it rains, on the north-west sandy shore of the lake (between the lake's west tip and the rocks with the red flower), never in the water: each of the action's five walks goes to a random point along that shore. Before The Lake has water nothing changes. Children "Playing in the dirt" play on that same sandy shore, always, before and after The Lake has water: each of the action's six steps goes to a random point along it. The actions, their text and their length are the game's own; "Excited about the puddles", "Chasing fish" and every other action are not changed. **Cannot be used with Move the "Playing in the dirt" Spot, which moves "Playing in the dirt" to the flower patch instead (ticking one unticks the other).**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The chooser of "Playing in puddles" (behaviour 0x5E, routine 0x45FFF0), 0x46E4F7, starts it when the rain level [0x718EB8] is 50 or more, rand(100) < 75 and it is raining (0x477040), as stock; stock also needed the lake to hold no water (0x43C5D0). 0x5E's walk (0x46003B, five times): with water in the lake (0x43C5D0), a walk (0x4745A0) to a random point of the north-west sandy shore, x = 1348 + r, y = 2116 - (17r >> 6), r = rand(252) (world pixels, the feet's point: 1348..1599 by 2116..2050); without, the stock walk to a random point of the lake bed (area 0x6A, 0x4744C0). "Playing in the dirt" (routine 0x45ED40, say-event 504), with the lake dry or full: each of its six go-tos (0x4745A0 at 0x45ED99) goes to a random point of the same shore line, x = 1348 + r, y = 2116 - (17r >> 6), r = rand(252) (the cave 0x494E44 replaces the routine's own x and y and jumps on to 0x4745A0); stock: 236..453 by 442..475, a strip from the rainbow totem's side across the river.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: Before the lake holds water "Playing in puddles" is as stock. Its text (string 0x229), its gestures, speed and length are unchanged; so are "Playing in the dirt"'s text, sound, six steps, speed and gestures (only the points it walks to change). "Excited about the puddles" (0xEB, 0x454200) and "Chasing fish" (0xEA) and their choosers (0x469E4B, 0x46EFB2) are exactly as stock. Behaviour 0x5F (0x4600D0, the waterfall pool), started only by The Missing Kids island event (0x4161AA), is unchanged. No save or villager-record byte is written.

#### Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts (`vv5_unicode_text`)

Lets the game draw, measure and accept ANY character -- accented letters, Greek, Cyrillic, Turkish, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic and Hebrew (joined and right to left), Indian scripts, cuneiform, symbols and colour emoji -- in the game's own two fonts (the big Burweed story font and the small Arial Bold font). New Believers' fonts hold ASCII and the Latin-1 letters; every other Windows-1252 character is added to the fonts in their own style when the game starts (from the font's own plain letter with the accent added, or drawn by Windows in the font's own typeface: Arial Bold is part of Windows; **for Burweed, install the Burweed ICG font for the best-matching letters** -- the patcher never ships it -- otherwise Comic Sans MS stands in), and every other character is made the first time it is shown, in the font's size, baseline and weight, from the fonts Windows has (Segoe UI, Segoe UI Historic, Segoe UI Symbol, Segoe UI Emoji (in colour), the CJK fonts, Nirmala UI, Ebrima ..., Noto if installed, then the bundled open fonts: Noto Sans Cuneiform, Noto Serif Tangut, GNU Unifont and Unifont Upper, and last Last Resort, so every one of Unicode 18.0's assigned characters draws, even ones no Windows font has). Names, the Details screen, popups, dialogs and every other text use them with their real widths, so centring and line breaks stay right; Chinese and Japanese break between characters. **Text and translations never run off the screen:** a line this patch, a long name or a translation draws that would cross the edge of the game's 800-pixel-wide window is cut there with "…" (whole letters only; a justified paragraph wraps at the edge instead), and one that would start left of the window starts at its edge; it may still run past its own box. Without a translation, the game's own English is drawn exactly as before. This needs this row: with Translations alone (no Unicode row) the game draws by itself and nothing is fitted. Where Windows has no icu.dll (before Windows 10 1903), Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between words by ICU's own word lists (ICU 77.1, Unicode License; about 4.4 MB in "Word Lists", read only when such a line is broken). Typing: every text box -- the tribe name, villager names on the Details screen, epitaphs -- takes any character Windows sends (dead keys, Alt codes, the Windows emoji panel, an input method for Japanese or Chinese), each stored whole or not at all, and Backspace erases a whole character (a whole emoji, flag or accented letter). Long names, everywhere: every name box takes names up to 1,200 bytes (up to 1,200 plain letters; fewer when letters need more bytes): the tribe name, villager names on the Details screen, epitaphs; Rename Tribe takes the same. It is one limit, shared with the other Fun Patchers. Characters are counted as you see them (a letter with its accents, an emoji with its skin tone or a flag is one), and Backspace removes one whole character. A long name scrolls in its box while you type it. The save itself is not changed: a name that fits its field (a villager's name 23 bytes, the tribe name 19) is kept there exactly as before; a longer one is kept there as its short form (its start and a mark, with a number when two would start alike) and the whole name is kept beside the save, in Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Long Names. The game shows the whole name wherever it shows that name. Back Up Saves, Restore Saves and Copy Player Slot carry the Long Names files with the saves. With both settings off the game still loads and plays such a save and shows the short form. Characters are stored as UTF-8 (a Western European letter keeps its one Windows-1252 byte), so every older name reads as before; the base game and older patchers show other characters as odd letters but never break. **On by default and in Owner's Defaults.** **Cannot be used with "Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts)" (ticking one unticks the other).** **Needs "Full Names on the Details Screen" (ticked with it): its Details box keeps the whole stored name, so opening a villager's Details and closing it never changes a name.** **Not yet seen in a running game** (checked by emulation of each stock executable). The companion is "VVFP Unicode Text.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; the game's own pictures and saves are never changed. **Bundles four open fonts, loaded privately by the game (never installed in Windows): GNU Unifont 18.0.01 (GPL-2.0-or-later with the font exception, or OFL-1.1) and Unifont Upper for nearly every assigned character, Noto Sans Cuneiform and Noto Serif Tangut (OFL-1.1), and Last Resort 18.000 (OFL-1.1), a placeholder block for anything still without a glyph; about 14 MB of fonts (in the patcher's files folder, in "Unicode Fonts", with their licence texts and sources), copied once per game folder, and not again when the folder already has identical files.**

**Requires Full Names on the Details Screen: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this.**

- Behavior changes: The font constructor (0x402730) runs unchanged; for the game's two fonts -- ldwBurweed27 (stock glyph table 0x4C8F08) and ldwarialbold (0x4C7FE0) -- the companion records the font's line height, baseline, capital height and pixel format, then adds every printable Windows-1252 character the font lacks (src/vv_font_glyphs.py, run in C by native/vvfp_unicode_text/glyphs.inc) as new rows under the loaded picture and new entries in a copy of the glyph table. Text is read by one rule (src/vv_game_text.py, native/vvfp_unicode_text/text_utf8.h): a well-formed UTF-8 sequence is its character, every other byte its Windows-1252 character, so every existing name reads as before. The width, draw, line-fitting, counted-draw and justified-paragraph routines are detoured: text without a multi-byte sequence goes to the game's own routine unchanged; other text is cut into whole units (grapheme clusters; shaped runs of Arabic, Hebrew, Indic and other scripts) and drawn in runs by the game's own draw and width routines, from the font's own letters or from pages of letters made at run time (Uniscribe shaping, GDI glyphs, COLR colour layers for emoji) in the font's size and baseline. Each detoured text routine first offers the text to VvfpTranslateText of "VVFP Translations.dll" when that companion is loaded (fails open), and shows a long name's short form as the whole name. Line breaking follows UAX #14 by Windows' own icu.dll (loaded from System32 only; a built-in table where Windows has none): a text with Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar or emoji breaks between whole characters where the rules allow (never before a closing mark or small kana, never after an opening one; Thai and the others at their words, inside a shaped run too), other text at spaces, and a word wider than the line after its longest start of whole characters that fits. Without icu.dll, Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between the words of ICU's own word lists ("Word Lists" beside the companion, read the first time a line of that script is broken; a missing list leaves the built-in table). The screen edge: a text drawn by the companion, expanded from a long name's short form, or drawn while a translation is in use is measured where the game draws it (x is its left edge after the game's own alignment); a line that would cross the right edge of the 800-pixel window (or of a narrower surface) is drawn as its longest start of whole units that fits with "…" after it, a text partly left of the window is drawn from its left edge, a justified paragraph is laid out no wider than the room to the edge, and when not even one unit fits the game's English is drawn. The widths the game is told are unchanged. The SDL_TEXTINPUT case (0x4049B5) posts a typed ASCII character exactly as before; any other well-formed text is handed whole to the focused text box, which stores each character whole (a Windows-1252 character as its one byte, any other as UTF-8) while it fits the box's limit. Backspace erases a whole unit. A box never cuts its text by pixels. Every box's limit is 1200 bytes; a text longer than the field GetText copies it to leaves as a short form: its longest start of whole characters, then "..." ("2...", "3...", the number first, when another long name has it; the older short forms ending in … stay readable), whose whole text is appended to the save's Long Names file and given back when the game puts the short form into a box.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces each routine's first instructions at run time, all of them or none, only after verifying their stock bytes, and installs nothing on a different build. The game's pictures (Images\ldwBurweed27.png, Images\ldwarialbold.png) are never changed and nothing of the game's art is shipped; letters are made in memory from the player's own Windows fonts and, for what they lack, from the bundled open fonts (Unicode Fonts folder), which are added to the game's process only (FR_PRIVATE) and never installed in Windows; a missing or unreadable font file only leaves its step out. A save's records only ever hold what fits their fields: every stock copy of a name sees the short form, never more bytes than the stock game wrote. Nothing is cut inside a character. A fault in any detour falls back to the game's own routine with the game's own text.
- Dependencies: vv5_details_full_names
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

Unticking any of them unticks this row too, and then the rest stay as they are. This row changes nothing by itself. Off by default; Owner's Defaults and Select All tick it.

Requires Popup When Believers Become Heathens: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this.**

#### Science Collectibles Only Count When Complete (`vv5_science_collectibles_complete`)

**Needs no other patch.** Makes tech points come slower, so the game is harder; off by default. In the base game every piece of the second collectible set (24 pieces, the one whose duplicates pay tech points) you find makes research bring more tech points: each successful research adds a random 0 to (half the pieces found - 1) more. With this patch those pieces add nothing until the collection is complete: with all 24 found, research gets the normal bonus (0 to 11 more). The researcher's own points, the Purify Tree's glow, the fire's extra point, the tech points a duplicate piece pays and everything else the collection does are unchanged.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Classic VV Difficulty: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: The research bonus (0x46DE4D..0x46DE77): the second set's count 0x413F50(0x50) becomes 12 when all 24 pieces are found and 0 otherwise (stock: the count / 2), so the bonus rand(...) is 0 to 11 with the set complete and the stock rand(0), 0, before.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: The researcher's points, the Purify Tree's glow, the fire's +1, catch-up's research, the duplicates' tech points, the population room and the collections screens are unchanged. One guarded in-place edit of 9 bytes; no code is added and no executable space is claimed.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the bonus for every piece count is emulated stock and patched in tests/test_science_collectibles_complete.py; runtime/player confirmation pending

#### Scrolling Popups (`vv5_scrolling_popups`)

Popups get scrollbars when their text does not fit: a popup is never taller or wider than the screen (its buttons stay at its bottom, where they always are), and when its text is taller than the room left, or wider than the box (a long line, or one very long word), a vertical and/or a horizontal scrollbar appears, drawn with the game's own scrollbar pictures. Scroll with the mouse wheel over the popup, the arrows, by dragging the knob or by clicking the bar; the text starts at the top and starts over when it changes. A popup whose text fits looks and works exactly as before. This covers the island-event popups (and Custom Island Events from Story / Cheat Upgrades, which use them), message boxes (tech and puzzle results, confirmations), tips (the tutorial and notices), the tombstone (a long name or cause of death scrolls sideways) and Create Nickname (a long translation or name scrolls sideways). The Options panel (each label sits beside its slider or button, which cannot scroll with it) and the panels with no text body (Change Player, the outfit chooser) are as the game draws them. There is no keyboard scrolling. Nothing is saved, so the patch can be ticked or unticked at any time. **Needs no other patch.** Off by default; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.** The companion is "VVFP Scrolling Popups.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if it cannot be loaded, the popups are as the game draws them.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: The island-event dialog (constructor 0x418020): its `call 0x40E310` sizing the panel (0x418573) calls VVFP Scrolling Popups.dll, which caps the height to the screen's (768 px, read from the drawing context) less 16 px above and below; the game then centres the panel and places its buttons from the bottom. Its draw's `call 0x409F00` drawing the body text (0x4176E9) calls the companion, which measures the text with that same routine (measure only) and its words with the game's counted draw; when the text fits the box (the panel's bottom less the room the dialog keeps for its buttons: 4 x a choice button's height with two choices, else 5/2 x the OK button's) it makes the stock call unchanged; otherwise it sets the drawing context's clip rectangle (+0x60) to the box, draws the text moved by the scroll position, restores the clip, and draws the scrollbars with the game's own pictures. A word wider than the text box (a long unbroken word) hangs the stock game: its justified paragraph backs off to an empty line and tries the same word again, for ever. The constructor's four measures of the dialog's texts (0x41834E, 0x418387, 0x4183C2, 0x41852B, `call 0x409F00`, measure only) call the companion, which gives the paragraph the width of the text's widest word when that is wider than the box (the words measured with the game's counted draw, cut where the paragraph cuts them); the draw wraps at that same width and the box scrolls sideways. The message box (vtable 0x4985D4, laid out by 0x41A2D0): its `call 0x40E310` sizing the panel (0x41A47B) calls the companion, which keeps the size asked for and caps the width and the height to the screen's (1024 x 768, read from the drawing context) less 16 px on each side; the game then centres the panel and places its text and buttons as always. The text control draw's `call 0x409EA0` drawing a control's text (0x40D4B9) calls the companion: the text of a message box whose panel was capped (the control's parent has the message box's vtable and asked for more than the screen holds) is drawn under a clip rectangle set to the room the box keeps for it (0x14 below the panel's top, 0x1E from its sides, above its buttons), moved by the scroll position, with the scrollbars beside it; every other text, and a message box's text that fits, is the stock call unchanged. The tip (vtable 0x49868C): its `call 0x40E310` sizing the panel (0x41BD13) is capped the same way. The frame draw's tail (0x40E56C, `mov edx, [esi]` to the `jmp` into the dialog's body draw) jumps to the companion, which makes the same pops and calls the body draw: a tip that asked for more than the screen holds has its body drawn with its panel rectangle (+0x14..+0x20, which the body draw places everything by) moved by the scroll position and by what the capped panel moved its centred contents, under a clip set to the box (0x24 from the sides, 0x0A below the top, above twice the OK button's height), the rectangle put back after, with the scrollbars; every other dialog's body is called exactly as before. The tip's per-line `call 0x409F00` (0x41C200) is given the widest word's width when that is wider than the box, so the stock hang on a long word cannot happen there. The tombstone (vtable 0x4986E8, a fixed panel): each line is a text control. At the text control draw's call (0x40D4B9) a line whose window is the tombstone is measured with all the tombstone's other lines (its window's text controls, as the text control draw places them); when one runs past the panel's sides (a long name, a long cause, a translation), each line is drawn moved by the scroll position under a clip 16 px in from the sides and above the Done button, with a horizontal bar below the lines; the editable epitaph and every tombstone that fits are drawn exactly as before. The same for Create Nickname (vtable 0x498564): at the text control draw's call (0x40D4B9) a line of one of these panels is measured with all the panel's lines (its window's text controls); when one runs past the panel's sides, every line is drawn moved by the scroll position under a clip 16 px in from the sides, above the controls in the panel's lower half (its buttons, a text box), with a horizontal bar below the lines; text boxes, buttons and every panel that fits are drawn exactly as before. The event pump's `call 0x4022D0` handing a mouse event to the game (0x404A92) calls the companion first: a press on a scrollbar of the popup drawn this moment, a knob drag and its release are used by the companion and not passed on; every other event goes to the game unchanged. The wheel is read by an SDL event watch (SDL_AddEventWatch, SDL_MOUSEWHEEL). The scrollbars are the game's own pictures (image ids 0x81-0x84, 0x7F, 0x80): Up/DownArrowButton, VerticalScrollTrack fitted to the bar's height, VerticalScrollKnob; the horizontal bar is WideSlider2 fitted to the vertical track's width (18 px) with sliderhandle fitted to the knob's size turned sideways.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion writes its sites at run time, only after verifying their stock bytes and the instructions before them (all of them, or none). A popup whose text fits is drawn by the very same call as in the stock game; the popups' text fields keep their sizes; keys, the buttons, the events and the save are unchanged.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the companion emulated on the published executable's own popup code with the game's own fonts and pictures (tests/test_scrolling_popups.py: the panel capped, the clip set and restored, wheel, arrows, knob drag and track clicks moving the drawn lines, the buttons at the panel's bottom, a fitting text drawn exactly as the stock game draws it); runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Shrine to the Ancestors (`vv5_respectful_hovel_cover`)

Turns the restored hovel into an ancestral shrine. A sacred, peaceful place where villagers can honor the ancestral spirits that guide them. Best paired with "Memorial Actions Can Also Occur at the Heathen Hovel". Once The Last Heathen is converted, the game covers the old Heathen camp with a picture of the empty hovel among flowers. With this patch that picture is the owner's more respectful one (art by Lorsieab2): the same hovel, with graves and flowers round the camp. Its bottom and left edges sit on the old picture's, so it rises above and reaches right of where the old one ended. It is drawn wherever the game draws the cover, the village and the Overview Map alike, and replaces both the game's own picture and Fix Vanilla Bugs' redrawn one; it sits where Fix Vanilla Bugs puts the hovel (on the map's own tiles), with Fix Vanilla Bugs on or off. The patcher puts it in the game's Images folder as vvfp_respectful_hovel.png; the game's own hovel_cover.png is never changed. When the cover appears and every other picture are the base game's own. Off by default; Owner's Defaults and Select All tick it. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Respecting the Legacy of Isola: unticking this unticks it.**

The image table entry 0x1B (0x4CF768) names "vvfp_respectful_hovel.png" (a new string at 0x4C5FD0, in the zero tail of .rdata's last page) instead of 0x49D5E0. With Fix Vanilla Bugs too: its hovel bytes (the name at 0x49D5E0, the x and y immediates at 0x4370F5 and 0x4370FF) are still written but no longer used for the cover; this row writes none of its bytes.

#### Sickness works like VV1-3 (`vv5_sickness_like_vv3`)

**Needs no other patch.** Makes the game harder; off by default. #### Statue Drops: Normal Action or Honoring (`vv5_statue_polishing_or_honoring`)

Dropping a villager on a completed statue gives Polishing the Statue or Honoring on a 50/50 choice, regardless of that villager's skills. When a villager later carries that statue job on by themselves (the game's own choice), the 50/50 pick is kept only for a villager checked on its skill -- Honoring on Devotion, Polishing on Building -- and for anyone else 14% of the time; otherwise they do neither and the game gives them something else to do. Your own drop is never restricted. Only the completed statue is affected: building an unfinished statue, the upgradeable statue's Honoring, and the Confused result when the technology is missing all keep their stock behaviour.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**
