#### Story / Cheat Upgrades (`vv5_story_cheat_upgrades`)

Adds optional tools intended for custom stories, experiments, sandbox play, and cheats. These features deliberately allow the player to bypass normal game progression and random-event behavior. When enabled, all Origins Upgrades cost 0 Tech Points. Also adds the following Origins Upgrades: Pick Island Event -- Allows the player to directly choose which stock Island Event occurs instead of relying on random selection. Opening this upgrade displays a list of the game's official Island Event titles, each with a brief description. Selecting an event causes that specific event to occur through the game's Island Event system. Custom Island Event -- Allows the player to create and trigger a custom Island Event for storytelling, testing, sandbox play, or cheats. The player may customize supported event properties, including: Title and description; Food gained or lost; Tech Points gained or lost; Villagers spawned; Spawned-villager details, including supported appearance, age, sex, name, likes/dislikes, skills, and other valid villager attributes; Villager behavior or state changes; Village-state changes; Puzzle-state changes; Other game-specific values that can be safely and reliably manipulated. Custom events should appear and behave as closely as practical to ordinary Island Events, while clearly allowing player-defined outcomes. Only what this game's own code supports is offered; the rest is shown as not available in this game. A custom title is kept per save slot in a file beside the saves and is removed by Start Over. Bought island events don't change when the game's own island events come. A Custom Island Event can also be bought and delivered when everyone in the village has died (the game's own island events wait for a living villager), so new villagers, food, Tech Points, refills and revived skeletons can bring the village back; what needs a living villager is simply not there to choose, and a question with two choices is refused until someone lives. In A New Home and The Lost Children a village that died before its first island event gets it too, uncounted, so its first island event is still the game's own visitor once someone lives. A custom event can also ask a question with two choices: the player writes the question, the two button labels and, for each button, one to four outcomes, each with its own chance, result text and changes (everything the event itself can change); clicking a button rolls one of its outcomes by those chances and makes only that outcome's changes. **A question with two choices can be queued only in a game whose own two-button island-event popup the companion hooks; in any other game the option is shown as not available yet.** Pick Island Event also lets the player set how the picked event turns out. Each setting starts at "Random (original game)" and offers only what that event's own code can produce in this game: its result (for a two-choice event, the result of each choice -- the popup still appears and the player still clicks), every amount it can roll, who a roll it makes for each villager hits (nobody, everyone, or the villagers chosen), which villager it is about, and each baby's details; in A New Home and The Lost Children also its strength (normally a third of the population, 1 to 10). A setting whose condition does not hold right now can not be bought. An event whose own condition is only a matter of timing or story can be picked anyway, and developer-dead events proven to work are offered as never happening in the original game; events that need something the village lacks, or room for new villagers, stay locked with the reason. On by default, with Story / Cheat Upgrades cost Tech Points ticked too, so the upgrades keep their normal tech-point prices until that row is unticked. **Requires Enable Origins Tech, Details, and Village-Wide Upgrades: ticking this ticks it, and without it there are no Origins Upgrades to make free and no Pick Island Event or Custom Island Event.** **A pregnancy a custom event starts is written to the Births and Conceptions log only with Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File ticked.** Also adds Choose Time Skip Amount (0 Tech Points, the same as Time Warp): the player types how many years to skip, from 1 to 72, and the village moves forward that many villager years as a run of the Time Warp upgrade's own advance -- one Time Warp at a time (3 years on slow, 6 on normal, 12 on fast, the last one only what is left), each caught up by the game before the next -- so villagers work, eat, have babies, grow up and die of old age through the skipped years just as after a Time Warp. **Keep the game running until the skip is done: it pauses while the game is paused, and loading another village, Start Over or deleting the tribe drops the rest.** Cancel charges nothing.

**Requires Enable Origins Tech, Details, and Village-Wide Upgrades: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this. Needed by Popup When Believers Become Heathens for the popup, which that patch's DLL shows (without it only the game's own bottom-bar line is shown). Needed by Story / Cheat Upgrades cost Tech Points: unticking this unticks it.**

- Behavior changes: Every Origins upgrade on the Tech screen and the Villager Details screen costs 0 tech points: each price the Origins payload compares, deducts, refunds or shows is set to 0 at run time, and the Origins companion shows and charges 0. Every existing refusal stays: one pending Island Event or Barrel of Babies at a time, room for the Barrel's children, and every "nothing to change" check. A bought island event (the Origins Island Event, Pick Island Event, Custom Island Event) counts as pending until the game's own island-event trigger runs it -- the Origins companion's keeper of the island timer knows it from the purchase's write until the trigger's own (native/shared/island_timer_keep.h) -- not only while the timer is due within the purchase's five seconds, which the paused Tech screen outlasts.  A Custom Island Event is never held by it: it is delivered first and the bought or picked event it went ahead of is made due again right after it, each charged once; a waiting Barrel of Babies is never replaced (it comes first).  With nobody the trigger accepts (a count of 0, or no villager its own draw takes), the custom event is delivered all the same, so its new villagers always arrive; changes for villagers who are not there are skipped and the popup says so.  It is never held for a new village's two opening island events: it comes first, uncounted, and they still come after it as the game makes them. Adds a Choose Time Skip Amount upgrade (the Time Warp's price: 0 tech points, or 50,000 with Story / Cheat Upgrades cost Tech Points) to the Origins Tech menu: a plain Windows dialog takes 1-72 years (20 age units a year), and the Origins companion's own Time Warp advance runs in steps of at most one Time Warp at the current speed, the next step only once the game's villager tick has replayed the last (its catch-up), so no jump is bigger than a Time Warp.  Charged once, when the first step is made; Cancel, a paused game or an empty village charge nothing. Adds a Pick Island Event upgrade (0 tech points) to the Origins Tech menu: a plain Windows list of this game's island events by their official titles, each with a one-line description.  The pick makes the island event due exactly as the Island Event upgrade does (the same pending lock), and when the game's own scheduler fires it, the game's own chooser runs the picked event -- only if that event's own condition holds -- with its own text, choices, random outcomes and amounts. Offers 47 island events; events that can never run in this game are not offered. Adds a Custom Island Event upgrade (0 tech points): plain Windows dialogs build an event (title, description, village changes, new villagers, per-villager changes for a list with extended selection and the group toggles All Adult Women, All Adult Men, All Females, All Males and All Children, plus in New Believers All Heathens and one toggle for each Heathen type; each villager's row names the role the game keeps for them, such as the Golden Child or the Tribal Chief).  It is queued exactly as the Island Event upgrade queues one (the same lock), and when the game's own scheduler fires it, the game's own island-event popup shows the custom title and description and the changes are made through the game's own routines. Its amounts list shows each amount the game keeps as it is now, below 0 included (The Lost Children's fish and the field's protection fall below 0 in the original game), and the event replaces it; only a store that is not there yet, such as a farm not yet built, reads "not there yet" and is refused. Villager Changes offers every villager action the game's own code can start for one villager, Celebrating included, grouped (work, leisure, celebration and dance, devotion, family, children, health, curiosity, moods, puzzles and story) and sorted, each labelled with the text the Details screen then shows; the villager is stopped first and the game's own starter runs.  An action that may harm the game or the save ends "(Unsafe)": choosing it shows the reason and advises backing up the save (OK / Cancel), and one that would need a missing object is refused when the event happens instead of crashing. New villagers and babies are made only while the game's own room predicate says the village has room, so the population cap of the installed mode is never passed. A new tribe's first two island events are always the game's own (each game's village start sets its island-event counter to 0): a custom event queued before the second of them stays queued -- the same lock, nothing charged again -- without making the island event due, and is made due exactly as the Island Event upgrade does once the game has made both, so it is the third. A village where everyone has died (the game's own population count is 0; in New Believers the believers): the game keeps running but its island-event trigger does nothing while that count is 0.  The trigger's call of the count is retargeted to a stub that runs it unchanged; only when it answers 0 and a plain Custom Island Event is queued for this village does the trigger go on past its villager draw (as if one had been drawn), so the game reschedules, plays its sound, counts the event, builds it and shows its own popup with the custom event.  New Believers' selector, when no stock event is possible, goes to its delivery site with the custom event the same way (its two stock trophy calls first).  The purchase allows an empty village (a question with two choices is refused: it needs a living villager), an empty village does not wait for the two opening island events.  A New Home's and The Lost Children's trigger makes a village's first island event the game's visitor: an empty village that has had none resumes past that check too, and the delivery takes the trigger's count of it back (as for the time skip's notice), so Island Events Seen stays 0 and the visitor is still its first island event once someone lives. Pick Island Event's settings: each offered event can carry its result, every amount it rolls, who a per-villager roll hits, which villager it is about and each baby's details (A New Home and The Lost Children: also its strength), each defaulting to Random (original game).  The companion points the event's own rand() calls at a stub that answers the chosen value only in that roll's phase (before the popup, the popup, or the event's apply), for the clicked choice, and -- in a routine other code shares -- only inside the event's own call to it; the outcome ends when the event's apply returns, on refusal and on lapse, so no chosen value reaches a natural event. Unlocked picks: an event whose own condition is only timing or story (proven by running its popup and apply with the condition false) can be picked anyway; its condition is passed for that one delivery only.  Developer-dead events proven to work are offered as never happening in the original game. A custom title replaces a villager's title in the villager panel and is printed in the Village Population and Village History logs; it is kept per save slot in Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save N\Data\Custom Titles\Custom Titles - Save N.dat and deleted by Start Over.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched; the companion writes the listed sites at run time after verifying every one of them, and writes nothing if any differs. No stock event is emulated: a picked event is created, shown and resolved by the game's own code; a custom event is shown by the game's own island-event popup. Pick Island Event adds no tech points and writes nothing to the save; a custom event changes only what the player chose, through the game's own routines and fields, and the game saves the village as usual. No custom title is written into a villager record. An empty village with nothing queued, and every village with anyone alive, runs the island-event trigger exactly as stock; the game's own "Your tribe has been lost! Game over." status line and its tips are left as they are.
- Dependencies: vv5_origins_village_wide_upgrades
- Evidence status: static exact-build verification and emulation of the rendered executables and the companion; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Translations (`vv5_translations`)

Plays the game in another language. Choose a language for each game in Tools > Translations... (or make your own there: the patcher writes a file with every English line of the game, its menus, events, tips, tech names and the patcher's own windows, and a built-in editor shows each line in the game's font). The game uses the chosen language from its next start, with no re-patching; lines a translation leaves out, or gets wrong, stay English. Gender and plural words follow the villager or the number (for example il / elle, 1 pomme / 2 pommes). **On by default, and English until you choose a language: with English chosen the game is exactly as without this patch.** **Letters beyond plain English (accents, Turkish ğ ş ı, Greek, Cyrillic, Chinese, Japanese, Cuneiform, emoji) need "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" or "Use Unicode Font"; without either, the game's own font draws only plain English letters and the rest show as "?".** **With one of those two rows a translated line never runs off the screen (it is cut with "…" at the window's edge, though it may run past its own box); without them the game draws it as it is.** **Words painted into pictures (buttons, the title screen, help pages) stay English.** **Every patch's own text is translated too: its windows and messages, Custom Island Event popups, Cause of Death words and epitaphs, Son/Daughter, and the text the exe patches write; log files stay English.** **Works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Not yet seen in a running game.** The companion is "VVFP Translations.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if it cannot be loaded, or the game's text is not the version a translation was made from, those lines stay English.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: At game start the companion reads "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Files\Translation\Translation.txt" (written by the patcher's Translations window; docs/translation-file-format.md). With no such file it returns at once and writes nothing. Each translated line replaces the English where the game looks it up: the string table at 0x4D31F0: each translated entry's loaded-text pointer (+0xC), after the loader; the visible literals outside the table by the address their loading instruction pushes (data/translations/vv5_strings.json).  A line is used only when the English it was made from is the English this game shows (the key's SHA-256), its placeholders match and its selects are well formed. The patcher's own windows (Origins, Story / Cheat Upgrades, Custom Island Event) are translated as they open (a WH_CALLWNDPROCRET hook on the game's own thread, only when the file translates any of them); a message put together from several lines is translated line by line. The companions that build a text the game shows (Cause of Death's words and epitaphs, Story / Cheat Upgrades' island event lines and Time Skip notice, Show Parents' Son / Daughter, Storytelling, Both Factions) ask for it by its line's key (VvfpTranslateKey / VvfpTranslateKeyText, native/shared/vvfp_translate.h): the translation is used only when the English is the line's and it fits the companion's own buffer, else the English. Text an exe patch wrote ("patch/0x<va>" lines, data/translations/exe_patch_strings.json) is written over in place when the translation fits the English's own bytes (through the same all-or-none writer, after checking the live text is the line's English); a longer one is left English there. Without "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" or "Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts)" (their companion's VvfpGlyphsUtf8; Use Unicode Font's, which starts later, is loaded and started on first use), translations are given to the game in Windows-1252, '?' for what it cannot write.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: This row changes no executable bytes: the companion checks each site's stock bytes and writes them at run time through the shared all-or-none writer, and writes only the ones the chosen file needs; if any check fails it writes nothing, not even a table pointer, and the game stays English. No save, record or game file is written; the game's own English text stays in memory unchanged. With English chosen (no Translation.txt), nothing at all is written.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Use Unicode Font (overrides in-game fonts) (`vv5_unicode_font`)

Draws ALL of the game's text in a Windows typeface instead of the game's own bitmap fonts: Segoe UI unless you choose another in the patcher (the Unicode Font box, or the Tools tab's Unicode Font... window: any installed family, or a .ttf, .otf or .ttc file; the choice is written next to the game as "VVFP Unicode Font.txt"), with Windows' fallback chain for every character it lacks (Segoe UI, Segoe UI Historic, Segoe UI Symbol, Segoe UI Emoji (in colour), the CJK fonts, Nirmala UI, Ebrima ..., Noto if installed, then the bundled open fonts: Noto Sans Cuneiform, Noto Serif Tangut, GNU Unifont, Unifont Upper and last Last Resort). Each of the game's two fonts keeps its line height, baseline and weight, and its size is fitted so a line is as wide as the game's own, so every screen keeps its layout; every character works, as with "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts". **Text and translations never run off the screen:** a line this patch, a long name or a translation draws that would cross the edge of the game's 800-pixel-wide window is cut there with "…" (whole letters only; a justified paragraph wraps at the edge instead), and one that would start left of the window starts at its edge; it may still run past its own box. Without a translation, the game's own English is drawn exactly as before. This needs this row: with Translations alone (no Unicode row) the game draws by itself and nothing is fitted. Where Windows has no icu.dll (before Windows 10 1903), Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between words by ICU's own word lists (ICU 77.1, Unicode License; about 4.4 MB in "Word Lists", read only when such a line is broken). Typing: every text box -- the tribe name, villager names on the Details screen, epitaphs -- takes any character Windows sends (dead keys, Alt codes, the Windows emoji panel, an input method for Japanese or Chinese), each stored whole or not at all, and Backspace erases a whole character (a whole emoji, flag or accented letter). Long names, everywhere: every name box takes names up to 1,200 bytes (up to 1,200 plain letters; fewer when letters need more bytes): the tribe name, villager names on the Details screen, epitaphs; Rename Tribe takes the same. It is one limit, shared with the other Fun Patchers. Characters are counted as you see them (a letter with its accents, an emoji with its skin tone or a flag is one), and Backspace removes one whole character. A long name scrolls in its box while you type it. The save itself is not changed: a name that fits its field (a villager's name 23 bytes, the tribe name 19) is kept there exactly as before; a longer one is kept there as its short form (its start and a mark, with a number when two would start alike) and the whole name is kept beside the save, in Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <n>\Data\Long Names. The game shows the whole name wherever it shows that name. Back Up Saves, Restore Saves and Copy Player Slot carry the Long Names files with the saves. With both settings off the game still loads and plays such a save and shows the short form. Characters are stored as UTF-8 (a Western European letter keeps its one Windows-1252 byte), so every older name reads as before; the base game and older patchers show other characters as odd letters but never break. **Off by default and in Owner's Defaults.** **Cannot be used with "Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts" (ticking one unticks the other).** **Needs "Full Names on the Details Screen" (ticked with it): its Details box keeps the whole stored name, so opening a villager's Details and closing it never changes a name.** **Not yet seen in a running game** (checked by emulation of each stock executable). The companion is "VVFP Unicode Font.dll" (the same code as "VVFP Unicode Text.dll"), started by VVFP Startup.dll; the game's own pictures and saves are never changed, and no Windows font is shipped. **Bundles four open fonts, loaded privately by the game (never installed in Windows): GNU Unifont 18.0.01 (GPL-2.0-or-later with the font exception, or OFL-1.1) and Unifont Upper for nearly every assigned character, Noto Sans Cuneiform and Noto Serif Tangut (OFL-1.1), and Last Resort 18.000 (OFL-1.1), a placeholder block for anything still without a glyph; about 14 MB of fonts (in the patcher's files folder, in "Unicode Fonts", with their licence texts and sources), copied once per game folder, and not again when the folder already has identical files.**

**Requires Full Names on the Details Screen: ticking this ticks it, and unticking it unticks this.**

- Behavior changes: The font constructor (0x402730) runs unchanged; for the game's two fonts -- ldwBurweed27 (stock glyph table 0x4C8F08) and ldwarialbold (0x4C7FE0) -- the companion records the font's line height, baseline, capital height and pixel format. Their own letters are not used: every letter is made from the chosen Windows typeface. Text is read by one rule (src/vv_game_text.py, native/vvfp_unicode_text/text_utf8.h): a well-formed UTF-8 sequence is its character, every other byte its Windows-1252 character, so every existing name reads as before. The width, draw, line-fitting, counted-draw and justified-paragraph routines are detoured: text without a multi-byte sequence goes to the game's own routine unchanged (with this patch, every text is drawn by the companion); other text is cut into whole units (grapheme clusters; shaped runs of Arabic, Hebrew, Indic and other scripts) and drawn in runs by the game's own draw and width routines, from the font's own letters or from pages of letters made at run time (Uniscribe shaping, GDI glyphs, COLR colour layers for emoji) in the font's size and baseline. Each detoured text routine first offers the text to VvfpTranslateText of "VVFP Translations.dll" when that companion is loaded (fails open), and shows a long name's short form as the whole name. Line breaking follows UAX #14 by Windows' own icu.dll (loaded from System32 only; a built-in table where Windows has none): a text with Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar or emoji breaks between whole characters where the rules allow (never before a closing mark or small kana, never after an opening one; Thai and the others at their words, inside a shaped run too), other text at spaces, and a word wider than the line after its longest start of whole characters that fits. Without icu.dll, Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between the words of ICU's own word lists ("Word Lists" beside the companion, read the first time a line of that script is broken; a missing list leaves the built-in table). The screen edge: a text drawn by the companion, expanded from a long name's short form, or drawn while a translation is in use is measured where the game draws it (x is its left edge after the game's own alignment); a line that would cross the right edge of the 800-pixel window (or of a narrower surface) is drawn as its longest start of whole units that fits with "…" after it, a text partly left of the window is drawn from its left edge, a justified paragraph is laid out no wider than the room to the edge, and when not even one unit fits the game's English is drawn. The widths the game is told are unchanged. The SDL_TEXTINPUT case (0x4049B5) posts a typed ASCII character exactly as before; any other well-formed text is handed whole to the focused text box, which stores each character whole (a Windows-1252 character as its one byte, any other as UTF-8) while it fits the box's limit. Backspace erases a whole unit. A box never cuts its text by pixels. Every box's limit is 1200 bytes; a text longer than the field GetText copies it to leaves as a short form: its longest start of whole characters, then "..." ("2...", "3...", the number first, when another long name has it; the older short forms ending in … stay readable), whose whole text is appended to the save's Long Names file and given back when the game puts the short form into a box.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces each routine's first instructions at run time, all of them or none, only after verifying their stock bytes, and installs nothing on a different build. The game's pictures (Images\ldwBurweed27.png, Images\ldwarialbold.png) are never changed and nothing of the game's art is shipped; letters are made in memory from the player's own Windows fonts and, for what they lack, from the bundled open fonts (Unicode Fonts folder), which are added to the game's process only (FR_PRIVATE) and never installed in Windows; a missing or unreadable font file only leaves its step out. A save's records only ever hold what fits their fields: every stock copy of a name sees the short form, never more bytes than the stock game wrote. Nothing is cut inside a character. A fault in any detour falls back to the game's own routine with the game's own text.
- Dependencies: vv5_details_full_names
- Evidence status: static source/manifest verification performed; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Villagers Have Last Names (`vv5_last_names`)

Babies born in the village and the village's founders get a last name after their first name, from the game's own list of 50 last names (Akikai, Alosaka, Awanata ... Wikimak) -- a list the game has always carried but never used, and the one Virtual Villagers 6 and 7 later used for villagers' last names. A baby takes its father's or its mother's last name by the rule chosen in Repair Saves & Logs (Last names come from: from the father, from the mother, 50:50, or a random one of the last names the village has ever used); without a rule recorded, a baby takes its father's last name (the village's default is from the father). A villager can also have a rule of their own for their children (Each villager's own rule): from the father, from the mother, 50:50, a random last name from the list, which gives each child -- twins and triplets too -- its own random draw from the game's list, every name equally likely, or a random one of the village's existing last names. A villager's own rule always beats the village's; when both parents have one and they disagree, a coin toss for each child picks whose. Villagers who arrive through an island event get no last name, because theirs would not be their family's. Only villagers named from now on get one: villagers who already have names keep them. The last name is part of the name the game stores, so it shows wherever the name does and stays in the save even if this patch is later removed. Heathens get last names too: each village's Heathen tribe has four family names of its own, chosen once at random from the same list among the names none of the village's villagers have ever used, and the same after every reload. Each Heathen gets one of the four at random, kept roughly even so no family is empty or huge: a new Heathen as the game makes them, and a Heathen with none the first time the patched game loads the village. Heathens who share a family name are not related. A Heathen who converts keeps their last name. While they are Heathens their last names are not counted among the village's existing names (Random from the existing Village Names); once converted, theirs counts like any other. Start Over gives the new village four of its own. **Needs no other patch.**

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

- Behavior changes: A baby born in the village from now on (a mother's delivery: the first child, a twin or a triplet) and a new village's founders are called "<first name> <last name>": the first name is the game's own pick, and the last name is name number <family - 1> of the game's unused third list (0X4B8450), read from the running executable. A villager the game creates any other way -- brought by an island event, a cheat or the Origins page -- keeps the game's own first name only: the companion tells a birth or a founder by the callers' return addresses on the stack, at fixed places. A villager whose family is outside 1-50 gets no last name. At a birth, the rule recorded by Repair Saves & Logs decides the last name (VvfpRuleLastName2): the father's, the mother's, either at random (50:50), or -- a parent's own rule "Random last name from the list" -- a name drawn at random from the game's list, or -- "Random from the existing Village Names", the village's rule or a parent's own -- one of the last names the village has ever used (the record's "used" lines, the villagers in the game at the birth, VvfpRuleLastName3, and the parents'; the game's list when there are none); every random draw is a fresh, unbiased one for each child. Each such birth adds the names it saw that the record lacks as "used" lines (only adding, through a temporary file, never for a slot it cannot tell), so a name stays ever used after its last bearer is gone. A parent's own rule always beats the village's; parents whose own rules disagree: a fresh coin toss for each child picks the father's or the mother's. The whole name always fits the game's own name field: the longest pairing is far below its 23 characters. Each village's Heathens have FOUR family names: chosen once, the first time one of its Heathens is named, at random from the game's list among the names no believer in the game (converts included) and no "used" line of the village's Last Names record has (every last name the tribe has ever had, living or dead); with fewer than four such names the rest are any others of the list. Kept as four "family" lines of the record, so a reload gives the same four; Start Over deletes the record with the village. A record with no "family" lines while living Heathens already carry last names (a session that ended before its four were written, a record lost) takes their names as the four, the most carried first, before choosing any anew; four chosen while the village's slot was not known yet are written at the first naming or birth after it is. A Heathen (the Heathen allocator 0x46FB80, every Heathen the game makes: a new village's 28, Barrel O' Babies' Heathen babies, the Story / Cheat Upgrades' and the Custom Island Event's Heathens, the Heathen Mommy) is called "<first name> <family name>": one of the four that fits, at random, each weighted by how far it is behind the most-carried one among the living Heathens (1, and 4 more for each Heathen behind), so the four stay roughly even. Sharing one never makes Heathens related: the name is drawn, never inherited. Right after the villager table's load (0x46FA20), each living Heathen whose name carries no last name gets one the same way (a numeral is kept after it), and a "Name changed" record (Old name, Age) goes to the Births and Conceptions log at the next save, so the logs, the Family Tree Maker and Check Saves & Logs follow them as one villager. Each is kept as a "heathen" line with the name, head and body they had, so a session that ends without a save gives them the same name again; never written for a slot that cannot be told (a village whose slot is not known yet keeps its four in memory, and writes them once it is). Whatever the patcher keeps for a Heathen by their name -- a custom title, a mask, a head look, an original look, a Former Heathens entry -- stays theirs: right after the load the renamed are handed, as one batch, to each of those companions that is loaded (its export VvfpVillagersRenamed), which carries its own records to the new name and writes its own file; a name two renamed Heathens shared, or one a villager outside the batch still has, is carried to nobody (a custom title is then told apart by the looks it was kept with), and the batch is handed over again at later loads for a file a session never rewrote. A Heathen's own rule for their children's last names (a "villager" line of the Last Names record, keyed by the whole name, head, body and sex) is carried to the new name the same moment -- never a line a villager outside the batch still is, or two of the batch were -- and Repair's editor follows the "Name changed" record to it. "Random from the existing Village Names" never counts a current Heathen's last name (the villagers in the game at a birth, and Repair's names of the village); a converted Heathen keeps their name and it counts from then on.
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion detours the naming routine's first instruction at run time (and the villager table's load, 0x46FA20), after verifying it, the routine's push of the list and the creators' calls to it, and changes nothing if any differs. Villagers who already have names keep them; when a village is loaded, only a Heathen whose name carries no last name is given one. The first names, sexes, looks and families are the game's own; the save format is unchanged. Heathens still never count in the statistics, and a Heathen's last name never makes them anyone's relative: it is drawn, never inherited, and no parent is recorded for it.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static exact-build verification of the naming routines, their callers and the unused list in each executable; runtime/player confirmation pending
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### VV4 Nursery School Divisor Parity (`vv5_vv4_nursery_divisor_parity`)

For parity with Virtual Villagers 4, changes VV5's six-skill spread lesson divisor from five to six. VV5 normally distributes one-fifth of a lesson to each of six skills, an arithmetic inconsistency that awards six-fifths in total; this patch distributes exactly one-sixth to each skill without claiming whether the original inconsistency was intentional.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked.**

#### Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File (`vv5_write_parentage_log`)

Keeps a plain-text log of the village's conceptions and births in 'Virtual Villagers 5 Births and Conceptions Log <n>.txt', in the save slot's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Births and Conceptions' folder beside the game's saves (Documents\LDW\<game executable name>\); a shared 'Births and Conceptions' folder an older patcher wrote is kept as it was and still read. Each Conception record gives both parents' names, both parents' ages at conception, both head and body values, both parents' likes and dislikes, and the number of babies; the mother's age determines the child's age. Each Birth record, numbered like the Conceptions ("Birth 1", "Birth 2", ...), gives the child's name, head, body, likes, dislikes and skills, and its mother's and father's names, heads and bodies; Repair Saves & Logs can number the Birth records an older patcher wrote without one. A new numbered file is started after every 256 Conception records; Birth records go into the file holding the latest conceptions and do not count toward that limit. Each Arrived record, numbered on its own, gives a villager who joined the village without being born into it -- a new village's founders, an island event's newcomers, the Barrel of Babies, the Custom Island Event's new villagers (never a birth): their name, age when they arrived, sex, head, body, likes, dislikes and skills, and how they came ("Founder", the event's title, "Barrel of Babies", "Custom Island Event", or "unknown"); villagers who arrived before this record existed get one, marked "Recorded afterwards", only once the player chooses Repair when the village is loaded. **The Arrived records are found by the Cause of Death patch ("Log Every Death ..."): with it off, none is written.** A baby born with the full name of a living villager is numbered at its birth, before its Birth record is written ("Chip Kenobi" is born "Chip Kenobi II"; a number a dead or gone namesake had is never given again), while the village's "Number villagers who share a name automatically" is on (Repair Saves & Logs; on by default); the villager who already had the name becomes "I" -- with the dead, in the save and every log -- at the next Repair Saves & Logs, and a numbered name that would not fit the game's name limit is left for Repair Saves & Logs to show you. The game keeps both parents on the child's own record, and each Birth record reads them from there. Village seeding is excluded, so a new village does not write a record for every starting villager. The game keeps only the father's name on the mother's record. His HEAD and BODY are copied onto her at conception, so the log reads them from her record and they stay correct even after he dies or another villager takes his name. His AGE, which has no copy on her, is read from his own record at conception -- the moment the engine hands both parents to the hook -- so a normal birth records his real age.

**Needs Write Village Statistics to Text File or Log Every Death, Disappearance and Unaccounted Villager on for the village and savegame header at the top of the log, and for creating the log at a village's first save -- a new village, or one restarted with Start Over -- before anything is recorded (without either, records are still written correctly, just unlabelled, and the log first appears with its first record; Cause of Death names the village at each save itself). Needed by Log Every Death, Disappearance and Unaccounted Villager for the Deaths and Unaccounted Villagers logs, which that patch's DLL writes (without it neither is written). Needed by Write Island Events Log to Text File for the Island Events log, which that patch's DLL writes (without it nothing is written).**

Each Conception record gives both parents' names, both parents' ages at conception, both head and body values, both parents' likes and dislikes, and the number of babies; the mother's age determines the child's age. Each Birth record, numbered like the Conceptions ("Birth 1", "Birth 2", ...), gives the child's name, head, body, likes, dislikes and skills, and its mother's and father's names, heads and bodies; Repair Saves & Logs can number the Birth records an older patcher wrote without one. #### Write Island Events Log to Text File (`vv5_island_events`)

Every change an island event makes to a villager is written to a new log, the Island Events log ("Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Island Events\Virtual Villagers 5 Island Events Log 1.txt"): one numbered record per villager it changed, with the event's title as the game shows it, the answer you picked when it asked, and each change as old -> new -- health, age, sickness, pregnancy, head, body, name, likes, dislikes, every skill, parents, custom title, mask and Special villager title, faith and Heathen -- "Gone" for a villager the event took away, and the sex and age of a villager it brought. What an event changes in the village as a whole -- food, tech points, the noni and crops, puzzles solved or unsolved and the weather -- is one record of its own, a "Village:" list of old -> new, and an event that changes nothing still gets its record, "Changes: none". A villager whose head or body an event changed also gets an "Appearance changed" record naming the event, so the Family Tree Maker knows the old and the new look are the same villager. A branching Custom Island Event from the library (Story / Cheat Upgrades), whose effects come page by page, is ONE record: its title, the answer picked, then every change in page order as "<name>: <change> <old> -> <new>"; at every save during it the log already holds the entry so far, and later pages continue that same entry, across a quit too, nothing twice. The records are written when the game saves, like the other logs. **Needs Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File: that patch's DLL writes the records.**

**Needs Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File on for the Island Events log, which that patch's DLL writes (without it nothing is written).**

- Behavior changes: When an island event runs, every villager is copied just before the game applies it and compared just after; each difference is one line of the villager's "Island event <n>" record. The village's food, tech points, food stores, puzzles and (where the game has one) weather are read just before and just after too; what changed is one "Island event <n>" record with a "Village:" list, and an event that changes nothing is one record ending "Changes: none". A villager the event brings is named with its sex and its age, in game units and years ("Age: 340 (17 years old)"). A head or body change is also an "Appearance changed" record in the Births and Conceptions log, ending "Changed by: <event> (island event)". A new village gets its Island Events log when it is made, like the other logs. A branching Custom Island Event (Story / Cheat Upgrades, story_graph.inc) brackets each page's own effects through this comparison (VvfpIslandEventsGraphBegin / End) and hands the event's one entry so far to the log after each page (VvfpIslandEventsGraphWrite -> the Parentage Export's WriteVillageEventEntry): "Event:", "Choice:", then each change as "<name>: <Label> <old> -> <new>" in page order. Its held record is replaced each time and each save writes what it has gained onto the same entry, append-only (a numbered first part left open, then only new lines, or a marked "(continued) Island event <n>" when another record came between), closed when the event is over; the game's own bracket around its popups writes nothing for them (VvfpStoryGraphLogged).
- Explicit non-changes/exclusions: No executable byte is patched: the companion detours the routines' first instructions at run time, after verifying them, and installs nothing if any differs. The game's own routine runs unchanged, with the same registers and stack; the events, their odds and their effects are the game's own. Nothing is written without Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File.
- Dependencies: none
- Evidence status: static exact-build verification of the event routines and the villager records in each executable; live-tested per game before release
- Guarded executable edits: 0; every edit has an exact purpose and before/after guard in the manifest.

#### Write Village Statistics to Text File (`vv5_write_village_statistics`)

After each successful save of slots 1 through 5, writes the save's local lifetime statistics to 'Village Statistics v2 - Save N.txt' in the save slot's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Village Statistics' folder beside the game's saves (an earlier 'Village Statistics - Save N.txt' is kept unchanged). Counts the game does not keep are stored in per-save .dat files in each save's own 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save N\Data' folder. Later games retain the inherited per-save statistics block even where no Statistics screen is reachable; omitted stock bookkeeping is restored by exact gameplay hooks. Puzzle totals are read from the current save state during export, including an already-completed VV5 Puzzle 17 save. These files are checked against what the save and the patcher's own logs prove -- Villagers Buried below the Deaths log's burials or the graves -- and are changed only when the player says so -- Repair Saves & Logs in the patcher window, or Repair when the game asks as it closes (with "Check logs automatically" on, and only if something is wrong); nothing is ever asked while the village is played. Each file is backed up first (a copy '<file>.before-v1.35.58-repair' in 'Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Data\Copies Made Before Repairs', at the file's own place), every change is listed in the Repairs log ('Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <slot>\Logs\Repairs Made'; the shared 'Repairs Made' or 'Repairs' folder an older version made is kept as it was: nothing is moved), and a count is only ever raised and an elder never removed. The original save result is preserved, and text-export failure does not turn a successful game save into a failure. Start Over wipes everything the Fun Patcher kept for that save: all its logs (the Village History too), all its data (ElderTotems.dat too) and its family tree files. It keeps Backups, Copies Made Before Repairs and exported family tree pictures. Other saves are not touched.

**Requires no other patch to be ticked. Needed by Write Births and Conceptions Log to Text File for the village and savegame header at the top of the log, and for creating the log at a village's first save -- a new village, or one restarted with Start Over -- before anything is recorded (without either, records are still written correctly, just unlabelled, and the log first appears with its first record; Cause of Death names the village at each save itself).**

## Transparency and validation boundaries

Each successful output writes `VVFP Transparency Log.txt` and the machine-readable patch log `VVFP Patch Log.json` (older versions named it `<game> - Modded.patch-log.json`; a re-patch replaces it, and the readers find either name) in the `Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher Files` folder beside the modified executable, where every other file the patcher adds also goes (except the few the game itself opens from its own folders by name; see README). Both logs, the hidden staging/backup/recovery folders beside the output and the files a re-patch carries over are read and written with Windows' long-path form (the '\\?\' prefix), so their length never stops a patch; the output folder is refused, before anything is written, only when a file the game itself opens (the executable, its own files, a companion or an asset the companions read) would pass the games' 259-character limit, and the refusal names that file and how much shorter the folder must be. The text report is written through a temporary file only after the executable, companions, and source/output tree have been verified; its SHA-256 is recorded in JSON without self-hashing the JSON. The report lists the stock and modified hashes, every applied edit grouped by owner, PE layout/checksum differences, file additions/modifications/removals, save handling, selected feature predicates/costs/exclusions, static checks, and the explicit runtime/player-confirmation-pending status.

Historical counters that are not persisted in a save cannot be reconstructed from a current save. The statistics exporter therefore reports persisted per-save counters and derives current puzzle completion (including VV5 Puzzle 17 when the save records it) at export time.
